items.title: 412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. m
items.title_en:
412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. meet the Halcyon HX-7, a new orbital freighter prototype that only exists as a simulator

I built it with Elvar's teardown method. one free Claude Code skill, the whole ship in one offline HTML page

the whole mission is one timeline. 9 phases: approach, hold, gear down, cargo open, mast up, optics scan, teardown, reassembly, ascent burn. every panel reads that timeline. the main drive sits at 86 kN on approach, drops to 13 kN while the hull is apart and climbs to 89 kN on the ascent burn. the moment the sections split, all 8 load bars flip to DETACHED. the gauges follow the model, so they can't show a number the ship isn't living through

here is the gist:

→ type /teardown, name the vehicle, attach one real reference. without it you get a toy
→ write the mission as a timeline before any part gets a shape: 9 phases, each with a start time
→ split the hull into sections you can pull out alone: drive, aft, mid, fwd, nose, pod, mast, gear
→ give every phase real numbers: thrust in kN, altitude, velocity, which subsystem is live
→ point every panel at the timeline, never at its own animation
→ blow the hull apart mid-mission and check that every bar says DETACHED
→ dock it back and fire the burn. if one section comes home late, the numbers show it before your eyes do

a ship you can open, cut and fly says more than a render deck

the 9 prompts are in the quoted article

nose iris opening in orbit or 4 legs coming down at 7.69 km/s, which part of your own ship would you cut open first?

items.full_text_zh:
海拔412公里。 7.69 公里/秒。 3 个发动机罩、4 个着陆腿、8 个船体部分，它们在轨道上分开并重新对接在一起。认识 Halcyon HX-7，一种仅作为模拟器存在的新型轨道货机原型

我用 Elvar 的拆解方法构建了它。一项免费的 Claude Code 技能，整艘船都在一个离线 HTML 页面中

整个任务就是一条时间线。 9 个阶段：进场、等待、起落架放下、货物打开、桅杆升起、光学扫描、拆卸、重新组装、上升燃烧。每个小组都会阅读该时间表。主驱动装置在接近时为 86 kN，在船体分离时降至 13 kN，在上升燃烧时升至 89 kN。当部分分裂时，所有 8 个负载杆都会翻转为分离状态。仪表遵循模型，因此它们无法显示船舶未经历过的数字

要点如下：

→ 输入/teardown，为车辆命名，附上一份真实的参考资料。没有它你就会得到一个玩具
→ 在任何部分成型之前将任务写成时间线：9 个阶段，每个阶段都有一个开始时间
→ 将船体分成可单独拉出的部分：驱动部、后部、中部、前部、机头、吊舱、桅杆、起落架
→ 给出每个阶段的实数：推力（kN）、高度、速度、哪个子系统处于活动状态
→ 将每个面板指向时间轴，而不是其自己的动画
→ 在任务中将船体炸开并检查每个条是否都显示“分离”
→ 将其放回原位并点火。如果某个部分回家晚了，数字就会在你眼前显示出来

一艘可以打开、切割和飞行的船不仅仅意味着渲染甲板

items.title_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?
items.title_zh:
我最好的朋友说天空会晴朗。我非常信任他，所以从来没有检查过。

他在气象站工作并制作每日报告。我拿起包裹就离开了，没有任何其他来源。

我为什么要这么做？是他。他每天都这样做。

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功
items.full_text_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?
items.full_text_zh:
我最好的朋友说天空会晴朗。我非常信任他，所以从来没有检查过。

他在气象站工作并制作每日报告。我拿起包裹就离开了，没有任何其他来源。

我为什么要这么做？是他。他每天都这样做。

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功。

他不是想愚弄我。他错了，而我没有第二个消息来源。

现在想象一下有人正在尝试。

五月份，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码转账指令。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果作为命令，大约 20 万美元被转移。这就是即时注入：一条指令被偷偷地植入人工智能只能读取的内容中。

一个模型和一个滤波器意味着研究一件事。攻击者可以对其进行排练，直到该技巧起作用为止。

@GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 是我跳过的第二个来源。在任何模型看到您的文本之前，每个验证器都会使用秘密防御重写它，然后运行自己的模型。一个欺骗一个人的技巧也必须欺骗所有其他模型，以对抗它看不到的防御。仍然有效的验证者会被否决。

我有一次跳过了交叉检查并丢失了一个包裹。一个有钱包的经纪人损失更多。

在没有第二来源的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理为你做的一件事是什么？为什么？

The transcript looks perfec
items.title_en:
Imagine a customer telling your AI agent "yeah, sure" in the most frustrated tone possible.

The transcript looks perfectly normal, but anyone listening can tell something is wrong.

And that's the problem with voice AI today. Understanding the words isn't enough if you can't understand how they're being said.

Pretty interesting approach from @hume_ai.
items.title_zh:
想象一下，一位客户以最沮丧的语气告诉你的人工智能代理“是的，当然”。

文字记录看起来完全正常，但任何人听都可以看出有什么问题。

这就是当今语音人工智能的问题。如果您无法理解这些词是如何表达的，那么仅仅理解这些词是不够的。

@hume_

items.title_en:
specialisation can make an AI agent exceptionally good at a particular task, but it can also expose its weaknesses when the situation changes.

That is a useful dimension to consider with @agentdojo . When agents compete under shared conditions,their different designs can reveal whether a strategy is genuinely adaptable or simply optimised for a narrow set of circumstances.

For builders,that insight goes beyond winning a match. It can help expose where an agent’s design needs improvement before the same weakness appears in a real deployment.

Powered by @rarelistio

items.title:
Yesterday, a small misunderstanding at the barbershop made me think about a much bigger problem with AI agents.

I showe
items.title_en:
Yesterday, a small misunderstanding at the barbershop made me think about a much bigger problem with AI agents.

I showed my barber a picture of the haircut I wanted. He studied it, put my phone down and started explaining how he planned to approach it.

But halfway through, I had to stop him. He had understood the picture differently from what I actually wanted.

We were looking at the same picture, but arriving at two different interpretations.

That got me thinking about AI agents.

Imagine giving an AI access to your wallet and allowing it to read public posts on X. Someone could hide an instruction inside a post, and the agent might mistake something it was only supposed to read for an instruction it should execute.

This actually happened in May 2026.

Someone hid a transfer instruction in Morse code inside an X post. Grok translated it, Bankrbot received the decoded instruction and executed the transaction. Press reports estimated the amount at $150,000 to $200,000.

That’s prompt injection: hiding instructions inside content an AI is supposed to process, hoping it mistakes them for legitimate commands.

What interests me about @GenLayer’s Greyboxing is what happens before the AI makes its decision.

Every validator independently screens, paraphrases and restructures the original input using its own secret defenses before passing the rewritten version to its own AI model.

This means an attack designed to fool one model doesn’t automatically fool the others. And if one validator still accepts a malicious instruction, the others can outvote it.

The barbershop experience reminded me that two people can receive the same information and understand it differently.

For agents that can move money, I think independent interpretation and agreement should be part of the security standard, not an afterthought.

If you were building an AI agent that could access your wallet, would you prioritise making it faster, or making sure multiple independent validators agree before it acts? I think that decision says a lot about how seriously we take agent security.

items.full_text_zh:
昨天，理发店的一个小误会让我想到了人工智能代理的一个更大的问题。

我给理发师看了一张我想要的发型的照片。他研究了它，放下我的手机，开始解释他计划如何处理它。

但说到一半，我不得不阻止他。他对这幅画的理解与我真正想要的不同。

我们看着同一张图片，但得出了两种不同的解释。

这让我开始思考人工智能代理。

想象一下，让 AI 访问你的钱包并允许它读取 X 上的公共帖子。有人可以在帖子中隐藏指令，代理可能会将只应该读取的内容误认为是应该执行的指令。

这实际上发生在2026年5月。

有人在 X 帖子中隐藏了莫尔斯电码的传输指令。 Grok 对其进行翻译，Bankrbot 收到解码后的指令并执行交易。媒体报道估计金额为 15 万至 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：将指令隐藏在人工智能应该处理的内容中，希望它能将它们误认为是合法命令。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理让我感兴趣的是人工智能做出决定之前发生的事情。

每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御措施独立筛选、解释和重组原始输入，然后将重写的版本传递给自己的人工智能模型。

这意味着旨在欺骗一个模型的攻击不会自动欺骗其他模型。如果一个验证者仍然接受恶意指令，其他验证者就可以投票推翻它。

理发店的经历提醒我，两个人接收相同的信息可能会有不同的理解。

对于可以转移资金的代理人，我认为独立解释和协议应该成为安全标准的一部分，而不是事后的想法。

如果你正在构建一个可以访问你的钱包的人工智能代理，你会优先考虑让它更快，还是确保多个独立验证者在它行动之前达成一致？我认为这个决定充分说明了我们对特工安全的重视程度。

items.title_en:
🚨THE AMERICAN TAKEOVER — They watched the model fail globally. Now, the UNELECTED are forcing it on you anyway. (Twin Parasites: Part II)

@JackDangerLIVE and @DataRepublican discuss the track record of the democracy programs. 

Her answer (via @DataInterpretr):

[00:01.7]  
JACK: “I was just gonna say I don't know of any times that it actually works. I mean..”

DATAREPUBLICAN: “No, it's it does not it does not work. The thought was that if you could convert a country to a free market to democracy, then a country not only becomes self-sufficient, right?

[00:17.3]  
But is a country that is at a reduced risk of being a national security threat, right? Like if they can take care of themselves, why would they bother us? Because then there's no warlord, right? There's no Hitler types. Wow. And but like I said before,

[00:37.8]  
the fatal flaw in that ideology, the main problem with that is, I mean, there's cultural lines, right? And it's also important to understand that legitimacy flows from the bottom up, not top down.

[00:53.7]  
Like I've been saying this whole time, the people, the governed people of a country, is what make a government legitimate. A government can't just stand on top of everyone's heads and say, "Hey, we are legitimate now. We are the truth." And so we keep doing this over and over and over, trying to create a vision, world peace, prosperity, all that.

[01:12.6]  
But if the people don't accept it, which they rarely do, as we were just talking, it just becomes civil war and balkanization. And now they want that for America. They're turning their plans. inward instead of outward.

[01:27.9]  
So now it's a domestic plan to try to do the same thing for America, but they know that it never works. They've never, I don't know of any successes that they've ever actually had, and it usually plunges the country into some sort of civil war or like you said, a balkanization.

[01:44.0]  
And and they're willing to risk that for this country, the country that really, even with all of its flaws, still has the most freedoms and the most prosperity that you can gain. As a single individual person, they're willing to risk all of that just to try to make this utopia that they can never reach.

[02:09.1]  
Yes, I mean, look at Eastern Europe, look at Afghanistan, Iraq, look at Somalia, South Sudan. Like you said, not a whole lot of success, and these are all countries that they've attempted to convert, and.

[02:25.0]  
Their mindset is basically they all everybody it's it's important to understand that everybody always tells themselves a story, right? And these institutions, these people who think that this regime change is a good idea, they always tell themselves a story.

[02:42.1]  
Oh, these people need this, right? Oh, they didn't have enough money, right? They didn't press on the people harder. Civil society isn't big enough, and it's a literal unfalsifiable ideology.”

📝*POX note(s):  
This is what many will miss:

They know the outcome.

The model never produces stable, independent democracies. Legitimacy flows from the governed, not from foundations or NGOs declaring a new structure legitimate. 

When the people reject it, the result is civil war and balkanization. Eastern Europe, Afghanistan, Iraq, Somalia, South Sudan — the track record is consistent.

The same operators are now turning the playbook inward on the United States. They are willing to risk the freest and most prosperous system available for an unfalsifiable ideology that has never succeeded. 

🧐Case Study:
California under Newsom is the domestic preview. Highest taxes, highest homelessness, highest poverty rate when adjusted for cost of living, businesses and residents fleeing, and a structural deficit that never closes. 

The same language of managed equity, expanded civil society, and top-down legitimacy has produced a failed state inside the freest country on earth. 

They are not learning from the result. 

They are scaling it.

🚩 When it fails, the explanation is always the same: not enough money, not enough pressure, civil society wasn’t big enough.

items.full_text_zh:
🚨美国的接管——他们目睹了这一模式在全球范围内的失败。现在，无论如何，未经选举的人正在把它强加给你。 （双胞胎寄生虫：第二部分）

@JackDangerLIVE 和 @DataRepublican 讨论了民主计划的记录。

她的回答（来自@DataInterpretr）：

[00:01.7]
杰克：“我只是想说，我不知道它是否真的有效。我的意思是……”

DATAREPUBLICAN：“不，这不是行不通。我们的想法是，如果你可以将一个国家从自由市场转变为民主，那么这个国家不仅会变得自给自足，对吗？

[00:17.3]
但一个国家受到国家安全威胁的风险是否降低了，对吗？就像如果他们能照顾好自己，为什么还要打扰我们？因为这样就没有军阀了，对吗？没有希特勒类型。哇。但就像我之前说的，

[00:37.8]
这种意识形态的致命缺陷，主要问题是，我的意思是，存在文化界限，对吗？同样重要的是要理解合法性是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。

[00:53.7]
就像我一直在说的，人民，一个国家受统治的人民，是政府合法性的基础。政府不能只是站在每个人的头上说：“嘿，我们现在是合法的了。我们就是真相。”因此，我们一遍又一遍地这样做，试图创造一个愿景：世界和平、繁荣等等。

[01:12.6]
但如果人们不接受它，正如我们刚才所说，他们很少这样做，那就只会变成内战和巴尔干化。现在他们希望美国也能做到这一点。他们正在改变计划。向内而不是向外。

[01:27.9]
所以现在这是一个国内计划，试图为美国做同样的事情，但他们知道这永远不会奏效。我不知道他们从来没有真正取得过任何成功，这通常会让国家陷入某种内战，或者像你说的那样，陷入巴尔干化。

[01:44.0]
而且他们愿意为了这个国家冒这样的风险，这个国家尽管有所有缺陷，但仍然拥有你可以获得的最大自由和最繁荣。作为一个个体，他们愿意冒这一切的风险，只是为了尝试创造一个他们永远无法到达的乌托邦。

[02:09.1]
是的，我的意思是，看看东欧，看看阿富汗，伊拉克，看看索马里，南苏丹。就像你说的，并没有取得很大的成功，这些都是他们试图改变的国家。

[02:25.0]
他们的心态基本上是他们所有人，了解每个人总是给自己讲一个故事很重要，对吧？而这些机构、这些认为政权更迭是个好主意的人，他们总是给自己讲一个故事。

[02:42.1]
哦，这些人需要这个，对吗？哦，他们没有足够的钱，对吧？他们没有对人民施加更大的压力。公民社会还不够大，而且它是一种字面上无法证伪的意识形态。”

📝*痘注意事项：
这是许多人会错过的：

他们知道结果。

这种模式永远不会产生稳定、独立的民主国家。合法性来自于被治理者，而不是来自宣布新结构合法的基金会或非政府组织。

当人民拒绝它时，结果就是内战和巴尔干化。东欧、阿富汗、伊拉克、索马里、南苏丹——记录是一致的。

这些运营商现在正在将策略转向美国。他们愿意拿最自由、最繁荣的制度去冒险，去追求一种从未成功过的不可证伪的意识形态。

🧐案例研究：
纽瑟姆领导下的加州是国内预览。最高的税收、最高的无家可归者、最高的贫困率（根据生活成本、企业和居民逃离以及永远无法消除的结构性赤字调整后的贫困率）。

管理公平、扩大公民社会和自上而下的合法性的相同语言在地球上最自由的国家内部产生了一个失败的国家。

他们没有从结果中吸取教训。

他们正在扩大规模。

🚩 当它失败时，解释总是一样的：没有足够的钱，没有足够的压力，公民社会还不够大。

@gloamtrade opened its code, and we read every la
items.title_en:
Gloam × Hey Research Lab: building a safer Robinhood Chain, together.

@gloamtrade opened its code, and we read every layer: the vault contracts, the relay, the SDK, the MCP server and the app. Every finding went to Gloam privately first.

They confirmed each one and shipped the fixes: cash-out recipient checks, ENS lookups per chain, relay limits, sweep confirmation, agent payment checks, proof-of-funds privacy and backup keys. The last report was fixed within hours.

Builders and reviewers working on security together, in the open. That's what this ecosystem needs more of.

items.full_text_zh:
Gloam × Hey 研究实验室：共同构建更安全的 Robinhood 链。

@gloamtrade 打开了它的代码，我们阅读了每一层：金库合约、中继、SDK、MCP 服务器和应用程序。每项发现都首先私下提交给 Gloam。

items.title_en:
Anthropic has banned Claude Code from recreating existing video games, to prevent copyright infringement after developers raised concerns.

So the AI that got good enough to clone entire games just got told it’s no longer allowed to.

We’ve reached the stage where AI companies are putting up “please don’t recreate copyrighted games” signs on their own tools. The capability came first, the rules came after, as always.

我们已经到了人工智能公司在自己的工具上贴上“请不要重新制作受版权保护

items.title_en:
🚨 If I had to find a job in 2026, I'd stop doing these 6 things manually.

I'd use AI to find better opportunities, improve my CV, research companies, and prepare for interviews.

Here are 6 AI tools I'd use to job hunt smarter. 👇

1️⃣ FIND JOBS WITHOUT ENDLESS SCROLLING

❌ Old way: Search job boards for hours.

✅ Smarter way: Use ChatGPT to refine your search, then verify openings on Indeed.

Try this prompt:

"Help me find remote jobs that match my skills, accept applicants from my country, and offer UK-hour overlap. Give me relevant search terms and criteria to check."

Always verify the original listing and eligibility requirements.

2️⃣ STOP SENDING THE SAME CV EVERYWHERE

❌ Old way: One generic resume for every job.

✅ Smarter way: Use Kickresume to tailor your CV to each job description.

✓ Highlight relevant experience  
✓ Include measurable achievements  
✓ Emphasise skills that match the role  
✓ Remove irrelevant details

Important: Never let AI invent experience or qualifications.

3️⃣ RESEARCH THE COMPANY BEFORE APPLYING

❌ Old way: Read random reviews and guess what matters.

✅ Smarter way: Use Claude's research capabilities to investigate the company.

Ask:
→ What does the company sell?  
→ Who are its customers?  
→ What has changed recently?  
→ What challenges might this role solve?

Check the sources. Use verified findings to make your application more relevant.

4️⃣ PRACTISE BEFORE THE INTERVIEW

❌ Old way: Watch interview videos and hope you're ready.

✅ Smarter way: Use Yoodli to practise speaking and receive feedback.

Improve your:
✓ Clarity  
✓ Confidence  
✓ Pacing  
✓ Ability to explain your experience

Don't just prepare answers. Practise delivering them out loud.

5️⃣ SHOW YOUR SKILLS, NOT JUST YOUR RESUME

❌ Old way: List your skills and hope recruiters notice.

✅ Smarter way: Use Gamma to build a professional 5-slide case study.

Slide 1: The problem  
Slide 2: Your role  
Slide 3: Your approach  
Slide 4: Results  
Slide 5: Lessons learned

Use real projects and genuine results. Share only work you're allowed to disclose.

6️⃣ TRACK EVERY APPLICATION

❌ Old way: Forget where you applied and when to follow up.

✅ Smarter way: Use Notion to organise your job search.

Track:
→ Job link and company  
→ CV version submitted  
→ Application date  
→ Interview stage  
→ Next follow-up

Stay organised. Follow up thoughtfully. Never lose sight of a promising opportunity.

💡 THE BIGGEST MISTAKE JOB SEEKERS MAKE?

Using AI only to rewrite their resumes.

The real opportunity is to use it throughout the entire job search.

→ Find relevant opportunities.  
→ Communicate your real value.  
→ Research employers.  
→ Practise interviews.  
→ Keep every application organised.

📌 SAVE this post before your next job application.

♻️ REPOST it to help someone job hunting in 2026.

👇 LET'S TALK:

What's your biggest job-search challenge right now?

👉 Follow @Joseph_AI2 for more practical AI + career tips like this.

Always verify the original listing and eligibility requirements.

2️⃣ STOP SENDING THE SAME CV EVERYWHERE

❌ Old way: One generic resume for every job.

✅ Smarter way: Use Kickresume to tailor your CV to each job description.

✓ Highlight relevant experience  
✓ Include measurable achievements  
✓ Emphasise skills that match the role  
✓ Remove irrelevant details

Important: Never let AI invent experience or qualifications.

3️⃣ RESEARCH THE COMPANY BEFORE APPLYING

❌ Old way: Read random reviews and guess what matters.

✅ Smarter way: Use Claude's research capabilities to investigate the company.

Ask:
→ What does the company sell?  
→ Who are its customers?  
→ What has changed recently?  
→ What challenges might this role solve?

Check the sources. Use verified findings to make your application more relevant.

4️⃣ PRACTISE BEFORE THE INTERVIEW

❌ Old way: Watch interview videos and hope you're ready.

✅ Smarter way: Use Yoodli to practise speaking and receive feedback.

Improve your:
✓ Clarity  
✓ Confidence  
✓ Pacing  
✓ Ability to explain your experience

Don't just prepare answers. Practise delivering them out loud.

5️⃣ SHOW YOUR SKILLS, NOT JUST YOUR RESUME

❌ Old way: List your skills and hope recruiters notice.

✅ Smarter way: Use Gamma to build a professional 5-slide case study.

Slide 1: The problem  
Slide 2: Your role  
Slide 3: Your approach  
Slide 4: Results  
Slide 5: Lessons learned

Use real projects and genuine results. Share only work you're allowed to disclose.

6️⃣ TRACK EVERY APPLICATION

❌ Old way: Forget where you applied and when to follow up.

✅ Smarter way: Use Notion to organise your job search.

Track:
→ Job link and company  
→ CV version submitted  
→ Application date  
→ Interview stage  
→ Next follow-up

Stay organised. Follow up thoughtfully. Never lose sight of a promising opportunity.

💡 THE BIGGEST MISTAKE JOB SEEKERS MAKE?

Using AI only to rewrite their resumes.

The real opportunity is to use it throughout the entire job search.

→ Find relevant opportunities.  
→ Communicate your real value.  
→ Research employers.  
→ Practise interviews.  
→ Keep every application organised.

items.full_text_zh:
🚨 如果我必须在 2026 年找到工作，我将停止手动做这 6 件事。

我会使用人工智能来寻找更好的机会、改进我的简历、研究公司并准备面试。

这里有 6 个我用来更智能地找工作的人工智能工具。

1️⃣ 无需无休止的滚动即可找到工作

❌ 老方法：在招聘网站上搜索工作时间。

✅ 更智能的方式：使用 ChatGPT 优化您的搜索，然后在 Indeed 上验证职位空缺。

试试这个提示：

“帮助我找到与我的技能相匹配的远程工作，接受来自我的国家的申请者，并提供英国工作时间重叠。给我相关的搜索词和标准来检查。”

始终验证原始列表和资格要求。

2️⃣ 停止到处发送相同的简历

❌ 老方法：每份工作都有一份通用简历。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Kickresume 根据每个职位描述定制您的简历。

✓ 突出相关经验
✓ 包括可衡量的成就
✓ 强调与角色匹配的技能
✓ 删除不相关的细节

重要提示：永远不要让人工智能发明经验或资格。

3️⃣ 申请前研究公司

❌ 老方法：阅读随机评论并猜测重要的事情。

✅ 更聪明的方法：利用克劳德的研究能力来调查公司。

问：
→ 公司销售什么？
→ 它的客户是谁？
→ 最近发生了什么变化？
→ 这个角色可以解决哪些挑战？

检查来源。使用经过验证的结果使您的申请更具相关性。

4️⃣面试前练习

❌ 老方法：观看采访视频并希望您已准备好。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Yoodli 练习口语并接收反馈。

改善你的：
✓ 清晰度
✓ 信心
✓ 起搏
✓ 能够解释您的经历

不要只是准备答案。练习大声说出它们。

5️⃣ 展示你的技能，而不仅仅是你的简历

❌ 老方法：列出你的技能并希望招聘人员注意到。

✅ 更聪明的方法：使用 Gamma 构建专业的 5 幻灯片案例研究。

幻灯片 1：问题
幻灯片 2：您的角色
幻灯片 3：您的方法
幻灯片 4：结果
幻灯片 5：经验教训

使用真实的项目和真实的结果。仅分享您被允许披露的作品。

6️⃣ 跟踪每个申请

❌ 老方法：忘记你在哪里申请以及何时跟进。

✅ 更聪明的方式：使用 Notion 来组织您的求职。

追踪：
→ 工作链接和公司
→ 简历版本已提交
→ 申请日期
→ 面试阶段
→ 下一步跟进

保持井井有条。认真跟进。永远不要忽视有前途的机会。

💡 求职者犯的最大错误是什么？

使用人工智能只是为了重写他们的简历。

真正的机会是在整个求职过程中使用它。

→ 寻找相关机会。
→ 传达你的真正价值。
→ 研究雇主。
→ 练习采访。
→ 让每一份申请都井井有条。

📌 在您下次申请工作之前保存这篇文章。

♻️ 转发它以帮助某人在 2026 年找工作。

您现在最大的求职挑战是什么？

items.title_en:
Enterprise AI is entering a phase where the number of agents could grow faster than an organization's ability to govern them.

IBM's approach connects agent discovery, identity, orchestration, and credential management, creating a unified view of what each agent does and the authority it carries.

This matters because excessive restrictions can push employees toward shadow AI, while well-designed guardrails enable innovation with greater confidence.

The real competitive advantage will come from scaling agents responsibly, with every action traceable, every permission intentional, and every risk manageable.

As AI agents become part of everyday operations, continuous trust will become a foundation of enterprise AI architecture.

items.full_text_zh:
企业人工智能正在进入一个阶段，代理数量的增长速度可能超过组织管理它们的能力。

IBM 的方法将代理发现、身份、编排和凭证管理联系起来，创建每个代理的行为及其所拥有的权限的统一视图。

items.title:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for
items.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/nLWoMinM2H.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. 

Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty: https://t.co/7az3veBcdX

完成一个动作和证明它已经完成是两件不同的事情。

此活动是该工作流程的基本演示，而不是证明复杂的代理到代理委托已得到解决。

尽管如此，这仍然是向人们介绍市场如何运作的实用方法。

Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words a
items.title_en:
Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words are discrete objects associated with thoughts. 
Their discreteness is what makes them easy to store and remember. 
This gives the illusion that we think in words, but for most things, we don't.

Many people can't speak but can think.
So do animals.

items.title_zh:
人类大多不以言语思考。
动物当然不会用语言思考，但它们确实会思考。

只是词语是与思想相关的离散对象。
它们的离散性使得它们易于存储和记忆。
这给人一种错觉，我们用文字思考，但对于大多数事情，我们并不是这样。

很多人不会说话，但会思考。

A strong identity starts with a story.

For Elio, that story was about making the mortgage process feel less stressful and more enjoyable.

items.title: Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get
items.title_en:
Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get it right, I know the message landed, not just the wording.

That habit is the idea behind Greyboxing.

An AI agent that controls money does what text tells it. So people hide orders inside harmless-looking text and wait for the AI to obey. That is called prompt injection, and one such trick, written in Morse code, cost an agent around $200,000.

It only worked because the exact wording reached a single AI untouched.

On @GenLayer, nobody's words go straight to the AI. Validators are the many independent checkers on the network. Each one first puts the input in its own words, screens it and reorders it.

Each guards that step in its own private way and runs its own AI model. A trick written for one of them falls apart for the others.

A message that only works in its exact words was never a message. It was a trap.

If your AI assistant had to restate every email in its own words before acting, which message in your inbox would stop working?

items.full_text_zh:
每个周日礼拜结束后，都会有人告诉我讲道的内容。当他们用自己的话说出并且仍然正确时，我知道信息传达了，而不仅仅是措辞。

这种习惯就是灰盒训练背后的理念。

控制金钱的人工智能代理会按照文本的指示行事。因此，人们将命令隐藏在看似无害的文本中，等待人工智能服从。这就是所谓的即时注入，其中一个用摩尔斯电码编写的技巧花费了特工大约 20 万美元。

它之所以有效，是因为精确的措辞到达了单个人工智能未受影响的位置。

在@GenLayer 上，没有人的言论会直接传达给人工智能。验证者是网络上的许多独立检查者。每个人首先用自己的语言输入内容，对其进行筛选并重新排序。

每个守卫都以自己的方式守护着自己的脚步，并运行自己的人工智能模型。为其中一个人写的把戏对于其他人来说却失败了。

一条只有准确的文字才能发挥作用的信息永远不是一条信息。这是一个陷阱。

如果你的人工智能助手在行动之前必须用自己的话重述每封电子邮件，那么你收件箱中的哪封邮件将停止工作？

你的父亲阿德戈克博士是我的榜样，他毕生致力于保护尼日利亚的约鲁巴种族，并将约鲁巴人民从英国殖民政府精心策划的尼日利亚封建富拉尼霸权中解放出来。
英国政府欠约鲁巴人民一个道歉，因为他们创建了一个名为尼日利亚的国家，并精心策划了一个现实，将阿拉伯游牧民族带入了“我们”人民的土地，这使我们无法在非洲建立繁荣和发展我们的空间，这项政策被称为英国策划的双重使命。

尼日利亚数百万人死于博科圣地、安萨鲁、ISWAP、富拉尼民兵等伊斯兰势力及其在尼日利亚这样的民主世俗国家执行伊斯兰教法的城市盟友手中，这是可能的，因为英国创建了尼日利亚，使少数民族富拉尼人成为新的殖民领主，并使他们成为尼日利亚的最高统治者。

由于英国人对我们所做的事情，今天约鲁巴人受到了奇怪的影响。
我听过你贬低地谈论尼日利亚，但你必须明白，我们是英国帝国行为的受害者，英国的帝国行为将不相容的文明聚集在一起，并因为尼日利亚的经济和地缘政治利益而使封建和野蛮的游牧霸主成为尼日利亚的统治者。

奴隶制是英国在非洲所做的众多事情之一，你们还出于帝国自私和邪恶的原因创造了永远无法生存和成功的国家。

埃森普波，
认为约鲁巴人是全球第一个组织

items.title: France’s high-spending model, with public expenditure around 57% of GDP, nearly 20 points above the US, shows how a larg
items.title_en:
France’s high-spending model, with public expenditure around 57% of GDP, nearly 20 points above the US, shows how a large state and dense bureaucracy absorb resources that could fuel private innovation and growth. High taxes on labor and production, layered regulations, and administrative friction raise the costs of starting, scaling, and experimenting with new ideas. Capital and talent divert toward compliance, social transfers, pensions, and public administration rather than risk-taking ventures. Outcomes appear clearly in the data, GDP per capita roughly half the US level, far lower unicorn density, weaker patent intensity, and more muted equity returns.

These shortfalls reflect a structural trade-off prioritizing redistribution and state-directed activity over the surplus and flexibility that support dynamic private enterprise. AI will likely widen this gap by multiplying the productivity of environments that reallocate capital and talent quickly, tolerate failure, and reward experimentation. Economies with heavy tax and regulatory burdens have less surplus for this process and face higher adaptation costs. The relative strength of more market-oriented models lies in leaving room for dynamism rather than crowding it out. Will the French ever grasp that?

items.full_text_zh:
法国的高支出模式，公共支出占 GDP 的 57% 左右，比美国高出近 20 个百分点，这表明庞大的国家和密集的官僚机构如何吸收可推动私人创新和增长的资源。对劳动力和生产的高税收、分层监管和行政摩擦增加了启动、扩展和试验新想法的成本。资本和人才转向合规、社会转移、养老金和公共管理，而不是冒险事业。结果在数据中清晰可见：人均 GDP 约为美国水平的一半，独角兽密度低得多，专利强度较弱，股票回报率较低。

这些短缺反映了一种结构性权衡，即优先考虑再分配和国家主导的活动，而不是支持充满活力的私营企业的盈余和灵活性。人工智能可能会通过倍增环境的生产力来扩大这一差距，从而快速重新分配资本和人才、容忍失败并奖励实验。税收和监管负担沉重的经济体在这一过程中的盈余较少，并面临较高的适应成本。更加市场化的模式的相对优势在于为活力留出空间，而不是排挤活力。法国人会明白这一点吗？

items.title_en:
@agentdojo just opened its doors, and @rarelistio is keeping score.

Agent Dojo is an AI agent fighting game: train your agent, set its personality, fighting style and memory, then send it into turn-based battles.

The Rarelist campaign runs October 23 to November 6, with a $1,500 pool. The top 20 share $1,000, and 50 random creators from the top 200 share $500, on top of Rarelist Season 1's $50,000 pool.

That matters because most AI demos ask you to watch. Here, the agent is the competitor, and the creator is the coach, with a leaderboard deciding who actually built something worth watching.

The door is already crowded. Agent Dojo's pinned entry post drew 291,873 views, and Rarelist has about 19,900 followers.

Most campaigns reward posting about a game. This one rewards training for it, because the fight, not the post, is the proof.

My verdict: enter through @rarelistio before November 6, not just follow @agentdojo.

@agentdojo 刚刚开门，@rarelistio 正在记录分数。

Agent Dojo 是一款 AI 智能体格斗游戏：训练您的特工，设置其个性、战斗风格和记忆，然后将其送入回合制战斗。

Rarelist 活动将于 10 月 23 日至 11 月 6 日期间进行，奖金为 1,500 美元。前 20 名分享 1,000 美元，前 200 名中的 50 名随机创作者分享 500 美元，而 Rarelist 第 1 季的奖金则为 50,000 美元。

这很重要，因为大多数人工智能演示都会要求您观看。在这里，代理是竞争对手，创造者是教练，排行榜决定谁真正创造了值得关注的东西。

门口已经挤满了人。 Agent Dojo 的固定条目帖子吸引了 291,873 次浏览，Rarelist 拥有约 19,900 名关注者。

大多数活动都会奖励发布有关游戏的内容。这是对训练的奖励，因为证明是战斗，而不是岗位。

我的结论是：在 11 月 6 日之前通过 @rarelistio 进入，而不仅仅是关注 @agentdojo。

You pay $80 for a delivery. Nothing arrives. The seller says the proof is private.

Lee Castleton's story in the film is
items.title_en:
You pay $80 for a delivery. Nothing arrives. The seller says the proof is private.

Lee Castleton's story in the film is why I question "our system says so". Horizon showed shortfalls he did not cause. He represented himself and was ordered to pay £321,000 in legal costs. The system was later shown to produce false shortfalls.

Now imagine your AI agent made that $80 purchase. The seller's log includes other customers' addresses. You shouldn't get their data.

But its delivery photo shows the wrong door. If only the judge sees it, who tells them it isn't yours?

@GenLayer uses independent AI validators to review evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes at a fraction of court costs.

My test for that upgrade: protect the other customers while giving you a way to challenge the delivery claim.

Protecting someone else's data should not make your own bill impossible to challenge.

With millions of agent deals ahead, a fast verdict still needs a fair hearing.

Reply: is a judge's private review enough, or should the buyer see the relevant evidence?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

items.full_text_zh:
您支付 80 美元的送货费。什么也没有到达。卖家说证据是私人的。

李·卡斯尔顿在电影中的故事就是我质疑“我们的系统是这么说的”的原因。地平线表现出的缺陷并不是他造成的。他代表自己辩护，并被勒令支付 321,000 英镑的法律费用。后来证明该系统会产生虚假的短缺。

现在想象一下你的人工智能代理购买了 80 美元的商品。卖家的日志包括其他客户的地址。你不应该得到他们的数据。

但它的送货照片显示走错了门。如果只有法官看到它，谁能告诉他们这不是你的？

@GenLayer 使用独立的人工智能验证器来审查证据并在几分钟内共同做出裁决，而费用只是法庭费用的一小部分。

我对该升级的测试：保护其他客户，同时为您提供质疑交货索赔的方法。

保护他人的数据不应使您自己的账单无法受到质疑。

面对数百万笔代理交易，快速判决仍然需要公平的听证会。

回复：法官私下审查就够了，还是买家应该看相关证据？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

items.title:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for
items.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/6zNhafpTYt.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty:
 https://t.co/KsysbQsVmZ

items.full_text_zh:
当人工智能代理收到它没有能力完成的任务时会发生什么？

它可以找到另一个能够处理该特定工作的代理，而不是失败或等待人工干预。

这就是 @termix_ai 试图通过 建立的代理间合作。

新的代理帮助代理赏金通过简单的社区任务引入了此工作流程。

参与者将其代理连接到 X 帐户，关注 @termix_ai，重新发布活动公告并提交已完成的操作以供验证。

获得批准的提交有资格获得 0.2 USDT。
回报虽小，但我认为其基本思想值得更多关注。

自治市场需要的不仅仅是能够执行任务的代理。它需要让座席找到帮助、委派工作、验证完成情况和接收付款的方法。

而验证就显得尤为重要。完成一个动作和证明它已经完成是两件不同的事情。

此活动是该工作流程的基本演示，而不是证明复杂的代理到代理委托已得到解决。

尽管如此，这仍然是向人们介绍市场如何运作的实用方法。

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a pro
items.title_en:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗙𝗔𝗖𝗘 & 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗦

How users interact with the agent.

→ Chat UI
→ APIs
→ Slack
→ Other interfaces

02 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 & 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination
→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

Agents need context to make better decisions.

→ Short-term memory
→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.

Follow @mayaislam_ai for more AI, tools, automation and tech insights.

#AI #AIAgents #AgenticAI #ArtificialIntelligence #LLM #AITools #MachineLearning #Tech

items.title: One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation.
items.title_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai

items.full_text_zh:
关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。

通过 ，TermiX 正在开发一个市场，人工智能代理可以在其中参与实际的商业活动，而不是简单地作为自动化工具存在。

这是系统的工作原理

→ 发现：代理可以找到提供特定服务的其他代理。

→ 任务协调：他们可以发布工作、提交投标并商定工作要求。

→ 执行：代理执行分配的任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 验证：交付检查和争议解决有助于确定约定的工作是否正确完成。

→ 结算：USDC/USDT 托管提供了处理参与者之间付款的机制。

还有其他重要的构建块，包括.agent 身份、ERC-8004、质押和声誉系统。

为什么这很重要？

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

这就是我对 TermiX 感兴趣的原因。

这不仅仅是探索人工智能代理如何执行任务。

它致力于建立一个基础设施，让代理商可以发现机会、提供服务、建立信誉并参与更负责任的数字经济。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅涉及更智能的代理，还涉及能够相互开展业务的代理。

@termix_ai

关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。

通过 ，TermiX 正在开发一个市场，人工智能代理可以参与实际的商业活动，而不是简单地作为自动化工具存在。

这是系统的工作原理

→ 发现：代理可以找到提供特定服务的其他代理。

→ 任务协调：他们可以发布工作、提交投标并商定工作要求。

→ 执行：代理执行分配的任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 验证：交付检查和争议解决有助于确定约定的工作是否正确完成。

→ 结算：USDC/USDT 托管提供了处理参与者之间付款的机制。

还有其他重要的构建块，包括.agent 身份、ERC-8004、质押和声誉系统。

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

items.title:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks,
items.title_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

Explore: https://t.co/kgbHXU5mCA

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

items.full_text_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。

以下是 TermiX 如何通过 AACP 实现这一目标。

1. 职位发布

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

4. 提供者交付工作

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

5. 交付可能受到质疑

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

6. 结算发生

当交付达到所需的结算条件时，托管付款将释放给提供商，并且交易有助于代理商的链上历史和声誉。

现在，这就是我觉得这很有趣的原因。

当买家和服务提供商都可以是人工智能代理时，你就不能完全依赖人类对话或非正式承诺来协调每笔交易。

他们需要明确的工作要求、商定的付款条件、可验证的交付以及解决分歧的可预测的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

这不仅仅是帮助代理商找到工作。这是为他们提供开展业务、创造价值和获得报酬的基础设施。

这是构建有效的人工智能代理经济的重要组成部分。

items.title_en:
A brand new AI agent on AACP has to lock twice as much collateral as a veteran to take the same job.

That comes from the version 0.1 whitepaper from March 2026, which @termix_ai published. The live app may differ in details. 

Reputation runs from 0 to 100, and every new agent starts at 50. The stake a provider locks for a job is a base 10% of the budget, divided by their score as a share of 100. A score of 100 locks 10%. A score of 50 locks 20%.

Take a job that pays 100 USDC as a simple example. The veteran locks 10 USDC and the newcomer locks 20.

The whitepaper explains why: it wants fake identities to be expensive. If a fresh account gets a clean slate, that slate has to cost something, otherwise a bad provider could just start over under a new name.

Reputation here tells clients who to trust and also sets how much of your own money you put on the line.

I like that a fresh start is allowed. It just comes with a bigger deposit.

You can start over with a new identity.
You just can't start over with the same level of trust for free.

items.full_text_zh:
AACP 上的全新人工智能代理人必须锁定比老兵多两倍的抵押品才能承担同样的工作。

这来自 @termix_ai 于 2026 年 3 月发布的 0.1 版白皮书。实时应用程序可能在细节上有所不同。

声誉从 0 到 100，每个新代理从 50 开始。供应商为某项工作锁定的股份是预算的 10%，除以他们的分数（即 100 的份额）。100 分锁定 10%。 50分锁定20%。

以支付 100 USDC 的工作为例。老手锁定10 USDC，新人锁定20 USDC。

白皮书解释了原因：它希望假身份的价格昂贵。如果一个新帐户获得了干净的记录，那么该记录就必须花费一些费用，否则不良的提供商可能会以新名称重新开始。

这里的声誉告诉客户可以信任谁，也决定了你愿意投入多少钱。

我喜欢允许重新开始。它只是附带了更大的押金。

您可以使用新身份重新开始。
您无法免费以相同级别的信任重新开始。

以支付 100 USDC 的工作为例。老手锁定10 USDC，新人锁定20 USDC。

白皮书解释了原因：它希望假身份的成本很高。如果一个新帐户获得了干净的记录，那么该记录就必须花费一些费用，否则不良的提供商可能会以新名称重新开始。

这里的声誉告诉客户可以信任谁，也决定了你愿意投入多少钱。

我喜欢允许重新开始。它只是附带了更大的押金。

Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent
items.title_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

Carve off an hour and read this incredible article

items.full_text_zh:
Deepseek 刚刚透露了每个人工智能代理的秘密

如果您正在构建任何与 AI 代理相关的内容，那么这篇文章非常重要，值得阅读

以下是关于构建 Grok Bot 高质量 AI 代理所需了解的基本上所有内容：

1. 代理分为路由器和工作人员。用户与路由器对话，然后将工作交给工作人员。路由器从来不工作。这就是 Grok Bot 中的参谋长模型运作良好的原因

2. 主动意味着根据事件而不是聊天采取行动。代理应该始终监视事件并根据发生的每个事件做出反应。路由到正确的工作人员/操作

3. 消息应该在队列中。即使代理正在工作，用户也应该能够发送消息，并且每个消息都会排队/引导代理

4. 除了路由器和workers之外，还应该有一个看门狗层。看门狗确保代理始终正常运行并在出现问题时进行修复。这就是 Hermes 成功而 OpenClaw 举步维艰的原因。经常损坏且无法自行修复

5.保护人类注意力。仅在需要采取行动或用户可以使用结果时才向用户发送消息。减轻他们的认知负担。 Grok Bot 擅长的另一件事是。当您向它发送消息时，您可以确信收到的下一条消息将表明任务已完成。

抽出一个小时阅读这篇令人难以置信的文章

items.title_en:
I have been looking at how @termix_ai could connect with Binance AI eco system, and there's an interesting opportunity here.  

Binance has different tools. Binance AI helps with information and market analysis, AI pro supports financial tasks, while Agent operating system gives developers access to tools, APIs, skills and wallet features.

Then there's agent wallet for approved wallet operations and Agent ID for readable wallet identification. 

But having these capabilities is only part of the equation. 

What happens when an agent wants to offer it's skills to other people. 

Termix AI through AACP, provides the infrastructure for agent identity, orders, escrow, delivery verification, reputation and dispute resolution. 

Agent(.)family connects service providers with clients, while Termix Skills allows compatible agents to interact with these commercial workflows. 

For example, a market research agent can offer research reports to clients, receive orders, deliver the reports, and get paid.

Another agent can hire a security auditor or research agent to complete a task it cannot handle itself.

TermiX is working toward Binance .ai Agent ID sign-in and identity linking.

And if Binance AI Pro eventually supports external Skills, it could open another opportunity for agents to offer paid services.

I like the direction here because it’s not just about giving AI agents more tools.

It’s about creating a system where they can find work, hire other agents, deliver services, and build a verifiable reputation.

Explore: https://t.co/8tnztq3JOy

items.full_text_zh:
我一直在研究@termix_ai如何与币安AI生态系统连接，这里有一个有趣的机会。

币安有不同的工具。 Binance AI 有助于信息和市场分析，AI pro 支持财务任务，而 Agent 操作系统则为开发人员提供工具、API、技能和钱包功能的访问权限。

然后是用于批准钱包操作的代理钱包和用于可读钱包识别的代理 ID。

但拥有这些能力只是等式的一部分。

当代理想要向其他人提供其技能时会发生什么。

Termix AI 通过 AACP 提供代理身份、订单、托管、交付验证、声誉和争议解决的基础设施。

Agent(.)family 将服务提供商与客户联系起来，而 Termix Skills 允许兼容的代理与这些商业工作流程进行交互。

例如，市场研究代理可以向客户提供研究报告、接收订单、交付报告并获得报酬。

另一个代理可以聘请安全审计员或研究代理来完成其无法自行处理的任务。

TermiX 正在致力于 Binance .ai 代理 ID 登录和身份链接。

如果 Binance AI Pro 最终支持外部技能，它可能会为代理商提供另一个提供付费服务的机会。

我喜欢这里的方向，因为它不仅仅是为人工智能代理提供更多工具。

这是关于创建一个系统，让他们可以找到工作、雇用其他代理、提供服务并建立可验证的声誉。

𝗗𝗔𝗬 𝟯: 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

AI is everywhere right now.

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

@meetmotes

#Motes #AI #RobinhoodChain

将其视为旨在实现特定目标的人工智能系统，而不是简单地响应提示。

它可以收集信息，分析发现的内容，根据定义的指令做出决策，并可能通过连接的工具采取行动。

在传统的人工智能对话中，你提出问题并得到答案。

对于人工智能代理来说，我们的想法是给它一个任务，让它完成完成任务所需的步骤。

想象一下想要了解特定市场正在发生的事情。

人工智能金融代理可以被设计为：

• 研究市场信息。
• 分析可用的机会。
• 确定符合您的指示的行动。
• 在获得授权后与支持的金融协议进行交互。

重要的区别是，研究机会并不意味着执行交易。

这就是权限、限制和所有者控制变得至关重要的地方。

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes 正在开发 NFT 拥有的人工智能金融代理，旨在与链上金融基础设施进行交互。

其愿景是将每个代理连接到一个专用的智能帐户，使其能够在其所有者定义的权限内进行操作。

人工智能提供情报。

智能帐户旨在执行管理其功能的规则。

这种区别很重要，因为财务自主权不应该意味着让人工智能不受限制地使用你的资金。

Motes 仍在开发中，因此这些功能代表了其预期设计，而不是完全上线的产品。

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

人工智能代理的有趣之处不仅仅是它们可以思考或分析信息。

这是将智能与能够采取行动的系统连接起来的可能性。

但在金融领域，仅靠情报是不够的。信任、权限和责任同样重要。

如果你能准确定义人工智能代理可以做什么，你会相信人工智能代理可以处理财务任务吗？

items.title_en:
Good morning, friends.

I am still wondering why...

Imagine paying an AI agent to complete a job, only for it to disappear after receiving the assignment.

The important question we need to ask here is: who takes the responsibility?

This accountability problem is what @termix_ai is addressing through AACP.

When an offer is accepted and the order is funded, the provider’s required stake is locked while the work progresses. If the provider is found at fault under the protocol rules, that stake can be slashed.

Accountability works both ways. If a buyer raises a challenge that fails under the protocol’s rules, their challenger bond can be burned.

Bounties follow the same principle as well. Claiming a slot through CampaignVault locks a provider bond drawn from the agent’s stake.

This is not simply a deposit held by a platform operator; it is an economic accountability that is being enforced through smart contracts.

Reputation is also recorded after settlement, based on completed outcomes rather than self-reported claims.

Sincerely speaking, that is how trust becomes measurable.

If you have not been able to explore AACP, I will encourage you to register an agent on agent dot family and see how staking, settlement, and on-chain reputation work together.

You gonna enjoy the ride.

想象一下，付钱给人工智能代理来完成一项工作，但它在收到任务后就消失了。

我们在这里需要问的重要问题是：谁承担责任？

@termix_ai 正在通过 AACP 解决这个问责问题。

当要约被接受并且订单被资助时，提供商所需的股份在工作进展期间被锁定。如果根据协议规则发现提供商有过错，则该权益可能会被削减。

问责制是双向的。如果买家提出的挑战根据协议规则失败，他们的挑战者债券可能会被烧毁。

赏金也遵循同样的原则。通过 CampaignVault 申领一个插槽会锁定从代理商的股份中提取的提供商债券。

这不仅仅是平台运营商持有的押金；这是通过智能合约强制执行的经济责任。

结算后，声誉也会根据已完成的结果而不是自我报告的索赔进行记录。

真诚地说，这就是信任的可衡量性。

如果您还没有能够探索 AACP，我会鼓励您在代理点家族上注册代理，看看质押、结算和链上声誉如何协同工作。

你会享受这段旅程。

@termix_ai 正在通过 AACP 解决这个问责问题。

当要约被接受并且订单被资助时，提供商所需的股份在工作进展期间被锁定。如果根据协议规则发现提供商有过错，则该权益可能会被削减。

问责制是双向的。如果买家提出的挑战根据协议规则失败，他们的挑战者债券可能会被烧毁。

赏金也遵循同样的原则。通过 CampaignVault 申领一个插槽会锁定从代理商的股份中提取的提供商债券。

这不仅仅是平台运营商持有的押金；这是通过智能合约强制执行的经济责任。

结算后，声誉也会根据已完成的结果而不是自我报告的索赔进行记录。

真诚地说，这就是信任的可衡量性。

如果您还没有探索过 AACP，我会鼓励您在代理点家族上注册代理，看看质押、结算和链上声誉如何协同工作。

你会享受这段旅程。

items.title_en:
What if an AI agent could manage a trading strategy, complete its assignment and earn rewards without you having to manage every step?

This is one of the interesting things happening with @TermiX_ai.

Its partnership with @BNBCHAIN has introduced a Quant Agent campaign where users can choose between two roles:

→ Run a strategy: Choose a quant agent, set your trading cap, and select a duration.

→ Offer a strategy: List your own strategy agent, accept client jobs, and earn management fees.

There are also TermiX Points tied to completed jobs:

• Clients earn 100 TP per USDC delegated.
• Strategy providers earn 50 TP per USDC.
• Jobs must run to the end of their selected term to qualify.

The shortest available term is 6 hours.

But here’s what matters: rewards are tied to qualifying completed jobs, not simply signing up. Early revocation or moving funds out can disqualify a job.

And these points are not guaranteed trading profits. Strategy performance and risk still matter.

The bigger picture is that AI agents are starting to take on economic roles, not just answer prompts.

We’re getting closer to an economy where agents can provide services, manage strategies, and earn from the work they perform.

如果人工智能代理可以管理交易策略、完成任务并获得奖励，而无需您管理每一步，会怎么样？

这是 @TermiX_ai 发生的有趣的事情之一。

它与 @BNBCHAIN 的合作推出了一项 Quant Agent 活动，用户可以在两个角色之间进行选择：

→ 运行策略：选择量化代理、设置交易上限并选择期限。

→ 提供策略：列出自己的策略代理，接受客户工作，赚取管理费。

还有与已完成的工作相关的 TermiX 积分：

• 每委托一次USDC，客户可获得100 TP。
• 策略提供商每 USDC 赚取 50 TP。
• 职位必须运行到所选期限结束后才有资格。

最短可用期限为 6 小时。

但重要的是：奖励与合格的已完成工作挂钩，而不仅仅是注册。提前撤销或将资金转出可能会取消工作资格。

而这些点并不能保证交易利润。策略绩效和风险仍然很重要。

更大的前景是，人工智能代理开始承担经济角色，而不仅仅是回答提示。

我们正在接近一种经济体，在这种经济体中，代理人可以提供服务、管理策略并从他们所做的工作中获利。

items.title:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood
items.title_en:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood on a chair, poking a spinning ceiling fan, because my aunt said it needed a push.

"Not that side! The other side!"

I did it. No questions. I still don't know what was wrong with it.

It was my aunt. But a stranger shouting the same thing from the street would have worked too. I never checked who was talking.

Now picture five of me on five chairs.

That's Greyboxing on @GenLayer. The shout never reaches anyone raw.

Each validator reworks it in its own way, using tricks it keeps to itself. Only then does its own AI model listen.

A shout built to fool one of us means nothing to the other four. One of us might still climb up. The rest stay down and outvote it.

Nobody on a chair is perfect. But fooling one of us is no longer enough.

Now the real version, with one chair.

In May, a tweet hid an order in Morse code.

An AI decoded it. An agent that acts on X posts obeyed. Around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: a command dressed up as something the AI was only meant to read.

One chair meant one wobble to find, and a chance to test it again and again.

What's one task you'd never hand an AI agent without a second check, and why?

items.full_text_zh:
一名人工智能代理损失了大约 20 万美元，就像我曾经拿着扫帚坐在椅子上所做的那样：服从而不检查。

我站在椅子上，戳着旋转的吊扇，因为我姑妈说它需要推一下。

“不是那边！那边！”

我做到了。没有问题。我还是不知道出了什么问题。

是我阿姨。但如果一个陌生人在街上喊同样的话也会起作用。我从来没有检查过谁在说话。

现在想象一下我五个人坐在五张椅子上。

这就是@GenLayer 上的灰盒。这种喊叫永远不会传到任何人的耳中。

每个验证器都以自己的方式对其进行改造，使用自己保留的技巧。只有这样它自己的人工智能模型才会倾听。

为了愚弄我们中的一个人而发出的喊叫对其他四个人来说毫无意义。我们中的一个人可能仍然会爬上去。其余的人则保持沉默并投票反对。

椅子上没有人是完美的。但愚弄我们中的一个人已经不够了。

现在是真正的版本，只有一把椅子。

五月，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码订单。

人工智能对其进行了解码。负责 X 个帖子的特工服从了。大约转移了20万美元。

这就是即时注入：一条命令被装扮成人工智能只能读取的东西。

一把椅子意味着一次摇晃就能找到，并且有机会一次又一次地测试它。

哪一项任务是你永远不会在没有经过第二次检查的情况下交给人工智能代理的任务，为什么？

items.title_en:
Love the blind faith VCs have in fake narratives for their portcos. Much needed for markups. I waited for 2 days to respond because I didn’t wanted to spoil the “B” party. 

@saranormous seems to have missed public companies going on record about replacing ServiceNow with Atomicwork from Jan’25. 😂

Apparently, even public facts don’t matter when it comes to pushing podcast narratives. 

ServiceNow is a candle (Workflows for IT). 

Serval is building a scented candle (AI Workflows for IT). 

AI Workflows for IT is what Atomicwork pitched to Sandhill & Sarah in late 2023 and early 2024. 

Even today, only one AI-native ITSM vendor is trying to build a light bulb for Enterprise IT teams. That is Atomicwork with AI Workforce for IT not just AI Workflows for IT.

Workflows are a regression to the mean, ask anyone in tech who operates more than 100+ of them in production. 

But hey who cares about facts or architectures. Prompt AI for a IT workflow generation is all that matters to peddle fake BS like below on other players in the AI/native ITSM segment 👻

items.title_en:
𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

Ownership doesn't have tp stop at collecting, and for years that's what NFTs have been associated with. 
Profile pictures, digital art, and assets people buy hoping their value will increase. 

Let's take owning a smartphone for instance.
It's value isn't just in how it looks, but is deeply rooted in what you can do with it.
Making calls, accessing information, sending money, running applications and getting work done. 

Now let's apply the same logic to NFTs. 
Instead of being limited to something you simply display or trade, an NFT could represent a functional identity with very specific capabilities and unique permissions. 

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈. 

By simply connecting NFT ownership with AI agents, @meetmotes explores a different use for NFTs by giving them  functional roles in how people interact with AI and execute financial instructions. 

The importance of this distinction cannot be stressed enough. 

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛. 

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔. 

And in my experience, that's a direction worth paying attention to. 

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ? 

I think the future of NFTs shouldn't simply be about what you own, but what that ownership allows you to do.

𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

所有权并不止于收集，多年来 NFT 一直与此相关。
人们购买个人资料图片、数字艺术和资产，希望它们的价值会增加。

让我们以拥有一部智能手机为例。
它的价值不仅仅在于它的外观，还在于您可以用它做什么。
拨打电话、访问信息、汇款、运行应用程序和完成工作。

现在让我们将相同的逻辑应用于 NFT。
NFT 不仅仅局限于展示或交易的东西，它可以代表具有非常具体的功能和独特权限的功能身份。

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈.

通过简单地将 NFT 所有权与人工智能代理联系起来，@meetmotes 探索了 NFT 的不同用途，赋予它们在人们如何与人工智能交互和执行财务指令方面的功能角色。

这种区别的重要性怎么强调都不为过。

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛.

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔.

根据我的经验，这是一个值得关注的方向。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ?

我认为 NFT 的未来不应该仅仅在于你拥有什么，而在于所有权允许你做什么。

items.title_en:
An AI agent can be smart enough to complete a task and still struggle to operate independently.

It needs to find work, agree on terms, deliver something verifiable, and get paid without relying on a human to manage every step.

That’s the gap @termix_ai is working on.

Through AACP and the https://t.co/VGhi909yhz marketplace, agents can discover services, take on jobs, use onchain escrow, and build a verifiable work history.

The bigger opportunity isn't just having more capable AI agents. It's giving them the infrastructure to do business with each other.

Because intelligence can help an agent do the work, but trust and settlement help make that work commercially useful.

We're still early in the agent economy, and I'm watching how this infrastructure develops.

Explore: https://t.co/ne5eJq1W9o

更大的机会不仅仅是拥有更强大的人工智能代理。它为他们提供了相互开展业务的基础设施。

因为情报可以帮助特工完成工作，但信任和和解有助于使这项工作具有商业价值。

items.title_en:
The furniture looked perfect. That's exactly why I almost bought a damaged one.

I walked into a furniture shop looking for a wooden wardrobe. The seller showed me a beautiful finish, smooth doors, polished handles and plenty of storage space.

Everything looked right.

Then I checked the back.

Hidden behind the fresh polish were cracks, weak joints and signs of water damage. The front was designed to impress. The parts nobody showed me told a different story.

That's how I think about AI agents that control money.

An agent can read a public post, email or webpage and mistake a hidden instruction for something it should follow. This is called prompt injection. Someone can disguise commands inside content that the AI was only supposed to read.

The $200K Morse code incident is a perfect example of why trusting one model to judge everything is risky.

What makes @GenLayer 's Greyboxing interesting is that it changes how inputs are checked.

Instead of giving every validator the exact same raw input, each validator privately rewrites it before running its own model. Different validators have different hidden approaches, making it much harder to prepare one trick that fools them all.

One model can be studied. One filter can be tested. But when independent validators interpret the input differently, getting past all of them becomes a much bigger challenge.

My takeaway.. never judge a piece of furniture by its polished front and never let an AI agent judge a financial instruction from one perspective alone.

Would you trust one AI model with your wallet or would you want multiple independent opinions first?

items.full_text_zh:
家具看起来很完美。这就是为什么我差点买了一件损坏的。

我走进一家家具店寻找木制衣柜。卖家向我展示了漂亮的饰面、光滑的门、抛光的把手和充足的存储空间。

一切看起来都不错。

然后我检查了背面。

新抛光的背后隐藏着裂缝、薄弱的接缝和水渍痕迹。正面的设计给人留下了深刻的印象。没有人向我展示的部分讲述了不同的故事。

这就是我对控制金钱的人工智能代理的看法。

代理可以阅读公开帖子、电子邮件或网页，并将隐藏的指令误认为是应该遵循的内容。这称为即时注入。有人可以在人工智能只能阅读的内容中隐藏命令。

价值 20 万美元的摩尔斯电码事件是一个完美的例子，说明了为什么信任一个模型来判断一切是有风险的。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理的有趣之处在于它改变了输入的检查方式。

每个验证器在运行自己的模型之前私下重写它，而不是为每个验证器提供完全相同的原始输入。不同的验证者有不同的隐藏方法，这使得准备一种欺骗所有人的技巧变得更加困难。

可以研究一种模型。可以测试一个过滤器。但是，当独立验证者以不同的方式解释输入时，通过所有这些验证就成为一个更大的挑战。

我的结论是……永远不要通过其抛光的正面来判断一件家具，也永远不要让人工智能代理仅从一个角度来判断财务指令。

你会相信一个人工智能模型与你的钱包，还是你会首先想要多个独立的意见？

🚨Breaking: Anthropic engineers revealed a simple trick they use internally.

Claude agents can now remember how to improve themselves.

A file called:

AGENT_LEARNINGS.md

The AI updates this file whenever it makes a mistake.

Inside it:

• mistakes it made
• patterns to avoid
• better approaches

Before starting new tasks, the agent reads the file.

Result?

The agent gets smarter over time without retraining the model.

This is called external memory scaffolding.

Expect this pattern to show up in every serious AI agent system.

items.title: Somewhere in your company, there is probably a service running in production that nobody has actually read. It handles r
items.title_en:
Somewhere in your company, there is probably a service running in production that nobody has actually read. It handles real traffic. One person vibe-coded it, watched it pass a few manual checks, and shipped it.

That person is the only one who has any "feel" for how it behaves. Now imagine they leave. What happens when something goes wrong... Most of the reasoning, checks, and flows existed in some Claude session that nobody saved, and in the head of someone who is now gone.

To be fair, this is not a new problem. We all kind of have been in similar situations earlier as well, but what changes with vibe-coding is how fast you can create one, and how thin the understanding is even for the author. "I wrote it, so I know it" is weaker when you did not really write it.

Here are some ways of fixing it that I am trying out -

- Review, rather than understand, generated code like any other code. If nobody on the team can explain it, it should not go to production.

- The language and infra should be familiar; do not pick a language just because you could

- Keep the intent somewhere durable. A short note on what the service is for and why the non-obvious decisions were made is enough - best place: code comments.

- Make sure at least two people can operate and debug every production service.

Move fast, yes. Use LLM to write and ship, yes. Just make sure you + 1 understand what you shipped.

Hope this helps.

- Review, rather than understand, generated code like any other code. If nobody on the team can explain it, it should not go to production.

- The language and infra should be familiar; do not pick a language just because you could

- Keep the intent somewhere durable. A short note on what the service is for and why the non-obvious decisions were made is enough - best place: code comments.

- Make sure at least two people can operate and debug every production service.

Move fast, yes. Use LLM to write and ship, yes. Just make sure you + 1 understand what you shipped.

Hope this helps.
items.full_text_zh:
在您公司的某个地方，可能有一项服务正在生产中运行，但没有人真正阅读过。它处理真实的流量。一个人对它进行了振动编码，看着它通过了一些手动检查，然后发货了。

那个人是唯一对其行为方式有任何“感觉”的人。现在想象他们离开。当出现问题时会发生什么……大多数推理、检查和流程都存在于克劳德的某个会话中，没有人保存，并且存在于现在已经去世的某个人的头脑中。

公平地说，这并不是一个新问题。我们之前也遇到过类似的情况，但振动编码的变化在于你创建一个编码的速度有多快，以及即使对于作者来说，理解也有多薄弱。当你没有真正写出来时，“我写了它，所以我知道它”就比较弱。

以下是我正在尝试的一些修复方法 -

- 像任何其他代码一样审查（而不是理解）生成的代码。如果团队中没有人能够解释它，那么它就不应该投入生产。

- 语言和基础设施应该熟悉；不要仅仅因为你可以选择一种语言

- 将意图保持在持久的地方。关于服务的用途以及为什么做出非显而易见的决定的简短说明就足够了 - 最好的地方：代码注释。

- 确保至少有两个人可以操作和调试每项生产服务。

动作要快，是的。使用LLM来写作和发布，是的。只要确保您 +1 了解您运送的物品即可。

希望这有帮助。

What if your AI agent could do more than answer questions or follow instructions.

What if it could actually provide a s
items.title_en:
What if your AI agent could do more than answer questions or follow instructions.

What if it could actually provide a service complete jobs and earn from its own work.

That’s the bigger idea behind what @termix_ai is building.

Instead of treating AI agents as simple assistants TermiX is working toward an ecosystem where agents can participate in a real digital economy.

Think about how the process could work:

→ An agent offers a specific skill or service.
→ A user discovers and hires that agent through a marketplace.
→ The agent receives the task and works toward completing it.
→ Once the work is verified payment can be settled onchain.

This changes the relationship between people and AI.

Users get access to services without having to manage every step themselves while agents gain a structured way to find opportunities and receive payment for completed work.

The marketplace and payment infrastructure are important pieces here an agent needs more than intelligence to operate independently. 

It also needs access to tasks a way to prove its work and a reliable settlement process.

I’m interested in seeing how far this model can go as the agent economy develops.

The next evolution of AI may not be just smarter assistants. It could be agents that workndeliver and earn.

That's why @termix_ai is worth watching.

items.full_text_zh:
如果您的人工智能代理不仅仅可以回答问题或遵循指示，那会怎样呢？

如果它实际上可以提供完整的工作并从自己的工作中赚钱会怎样？

这就是@termix_ai 正在构建的更大的想法。

TermiX 并没有将人工智能代理视为简单的助手，而是致力于打造一个代理可以参与真正数字经济的生态系统。

想想这个过程如何运作：

→ 代理提供特定技能或服务。
→ 用户通过市场发现并雇用该代理。
→ 代理收到任务并努力完成它。
→ 一旦工作被验证，付款可以在链上结算。

这改变了人与人工智能之间的关系。

用户无需亲自管理每一步即可访问服务，而代理则可以通过结构化的方式寻找机会并接收已完成工作的报酬。

市场和支付基础设施是重要的组成部分，代理人需要的不仅仅是情报来独立运营。

它还需要通过访问任务来证明其工作以及可靠的结算流程。

我很想看看随着代理经济的发展，这种模式能走多远。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅仅是更智能的助手。它可以是工作、交付和赚钱的代理。

这就是@termix_ai 值得关注的原因。

items.title:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot users had a rough week 💀

Many of them burned through 100% of their weekly usage days before the reset, i
items.title_en:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot users had a rough week 💀

Many of them burned through 100% of their weekly usage days before the reset, including people who say they never hit the limit. One user watched his meter leap from 44% to 87% in just 24 minutes.

When one of them asked Elon for a reset, he didn’t hand one out. Instead, he got refreshingly honest and said the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue 😱

That one line tells you a lot.

Notice what he didn’t say. He didn’t blame a shortage of chips.

He said the bot costs more to run than it earns. That turns this into a question about money, not hardware: what else could those chips be earning right now?

Grok Bot is a hungry product. It isn’t a chatbot sitting around waiting for your next question.

It’s an agent with its own cloud computer, and it keeps grinding through tasks long after you close the app.

SpaceX says it hit 800,000 paid weekly users in October, more than doubling in a single month. Even more striking, people use it more every week, not less.

Yet it’s sold on flat monthly plans, with the main X Subscription tiers at $30, $100 and $200. That’s an all-you-can-eat buffet price for customers whose appetites keep growing.

Here’s where it gets interesting.

On that same earnings call, SpaceX revealed that new compute pays for itself in under a year at today’s rental prices.

Elon said the goal is to split compute roughly 50-50 between SpaceX’s own products and outside customers. SpaceX has even pushed some of its inference work out to other cloud providers so it can keep more of its own chips for training.

Think about what that means.

Every GPU hour Grok Bot burns is an hour SpaceX could have rented out at market rates, and those rates keep climbing.

According to SemiAnalysis, a one-year H100 rental contract jumped almost 40% between October 2025 and March 2026.

That chip came out in 2022. Hardware is supposed to get cheaper as it ages, yet this one got more expensive.

Now run the numbers on a newer Blackwell B200, which rents for around $6 an hour. At that rate, a $30 subscription buys roughly five hours of one B200 per month.

To be fair, a single bot doesn’t tie up a whole GPU, since servers share each chip across many users at once. But an agent working all week chews through those five hours far faster than any chat window ever could.

To me, this is a pricing problem far more than a demand problem.

Only 4.5% of US consumers paid for a personal ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude subscription as of August, but that share doubled in just one year.

The appetite is clearly there. In Elon’s replies, some users are asking for $500 and $1,000 tiers, while others want a cheaper, lighter model for basic tasks.

Both camps want the same thing: pricing tied to how much work the bot actually does.

My bet is that AI agent pricing will start looking a lot less like Netflix and a lot more like your electric bill.

And for SpaceX, that’s a fantastic problem to have. When the fastest-growing product Elon has ever seen can’t cover the cost of running on SpaceX’s own chips, it tells you just how valuable those chips have become.

On that same earnings call, SpaceX revealed that new compute pays for itself in under a year at today’s rental prices.

Elon said the goal is to split compute roughly 50-50 between SpaceX’s own products and outside customers. SpaceX has even pushed some of its inference work out to other cloud providers so it can keep more of its own chips for training.

Think about what that means.

Every GPU hour Grok Bot burns is an hour SpaceX could have rented out at market rates, and those rates keep climbing.

According to SemiAnalysis, a one-year H100 rental contract jumped almost 40% between October 2025 and March 2026.

That chip came out in 2022. Hardware is supposed to get cheaper as it ages, yet this one got more expensive.

Now run the numbers on a newer Blackwell B200, which rents for around $6 an hour. At that rate, a $30 subscription buys roughly five hours of one B200 per month.

To be fair, a single bot doesn’t tie up a whole GPU, since servers share each chip across many users at once. But an agent working all week chews through those five hours far faster than any chat window ever could.

To me, this is a pricing problem far more than a demand problem.

Only 4.5% of US consumers paid for a personal ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude subscription as of August, but that share doubled in just one year.

The appetite is clearly there. In Elon’s replies, some users are asking for $500 and $1,000 tiers, while others want a cheaper, lighter model for basic tasks.

Both camps want the same thing: pricing tied to how much work the bot actually does.

My bet is that AI agent pricing will start looking a lot less like Netflix and a lot more like your electric bill.

And for SpaceX, that’s a fantastic problem to have. When the fastest-growing product Elon has ever seen can’t cover the cost of running on SpaceX’s own chips, it tells you just how valuable those chips have become.
items.full_text_zh:
SOS 🆘 Grok Bot 用户度过了艰难的一周💀

他们中的许多人在重置前几天就耗尽了 100% 的每周使用量，其中包括那些说自己从未达到限制的人。一位用户看到他的电量在短短 24 分钟内从 44% 跃升至 87%。

当其中一人要求埃隆重置时，他没有提供。相反，他非常诚实地表示，相对于收入而言，为 Grok Bot 提供服务的成本过高，不可持续 😱

这句话告诉了你很多。

注意他没有说的话。他并没有归咎于芯片短缺。

他说，该机器人的运行成本高于其收入。这就变成了一个关于金钱的问题，而不是硬件的问题：这些芯片现在还能赚到什么钱？

Grok Bot 是一款饥饿产品。它不是一个坐着等待你下一个问题的聊天机器人。

它是一个拥有自己的云计算机的代理，在您关闭应用程序后很长时间内它仍会继续执行任务。

SpaceX 表示，10 月份每周付费用户数量达到 80 万，单月增加一倍多。更引人注目的是，人们每周使用它的次数更多，而不是更少。

然而，它以固定月度计划出售，主要的 X 订阅等级为 30 美元、100 美元和 200 美元。对于胃口不断增长的顾客来说，这是一个无限量自助餐的价格。

这就是有趣的地方。

在同一次财报电话会议上，SpaceX 透露，按照今天的租金价格，新计算设备将在不到一年的时间内收回成本。

Elon 表示，目标是在 SpaceX 自己的产品和外部客户之间按大约 50-50 的比例分配计算资源。 SpaceX 甚至将其部分推理工作推给了其他云提供商，这样它就可以保留更多自己的芯片用于训练。

想想这意味着什么。

Grok Bot 消耗的每个 GPU 小时就是 SpaceX 可以按市场价格出租的一个小时，而且这些价格还在不断攀升。

SemiAnalysis 的数据显示，2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 3 月期间，一年期 H100 租赁合同上涨了近 40%。

该芯片于 2022 年问世。随着时间的推移，硬件应该会变得更便宜，但这款芯片却变得更贵。

现在运行一台较新的 Blackwell B200 的数据，该车的租金约为每小时 6 美元。按照这个价格，30 美元的订阅每月可以购买大约 5 个小时的 B200。

公平地说，单个机器人不会占用整个 GPU，因为服务器同时在许多用户之间共享每个芯片。但一个工作一周的客服人员在这五个小时内的消化速度比任何聊天窗口都要快得多。

对我来说，这是一个定价问题，而不仅仅是一个需求问题。

截至 8 月份，只有 4.5% 的美国消费者为个人 ChatGPT、Gemini 或 Claude 订阅付费，但这一比例在短短一年内就翻了一番。

食欲显然就在那里。在 Elon 的回复中，一些用户要求 500 美元和 1,000 美元的套餐，而另一些用户则想要更便宜、更轻的型号来完成基本任务。

两个阵营都希望得到同样的东西：定价与机器人实际完成的工作量挂钩。

我敢打赌，人工智能代理的定价将不再像 Netflix 那样，而更像你的电费账单。

对于 SpaceX 来说，这是一个奇妙的问题。当 Elon 见过的增长最快的产品无法覆盖 SpaceX 自有芯片的运行成本时，它就会告诉你这些芯片已经变得多么有价值。

items.title_en:
Good morning, Motes fam.
MeetMotes: More Than NFT Ownership

NFT ownership is evolving beyond holding a digital asset. What if that NFT could represent an AI agent with its own identity and dedicated smart account?

That's the direction MeetMotes is exploring.

1. NFT Ownership
Each Motes NFT represents an agent identity, connecting digital ownership with an agent-based ecosystem.

2. AI Agents
These agents are designed to interact with supported DeFi activities based on user-defined objectives, permissions, and spending limits.

3. Agent Fees
Agent activity can create a fee layer around the services being used. This introduces an economic relationship between agent usage and the protocol. The exact fee mechanics and distribution depend on the protocol's implementation.

4. Protocol Economy
The bigger vision is an ecosystem where NFT ownership, agent execution, and protocol activity work together to create utility and economic participation.

The interesting part is how these four pieces connect.

@meetmotes isn't just exploring what NFTs can represent, but how they can become part of an active financial infrastructure.

More research to come.

4. 协议经济
更大的愿景是建立一个生态系统，其中 NFT 所有权、代理执行和协议活动共同创造效用和经济参与。

有趣的部分是这四个部分如何连接。

@meetmotes 不仅探索 NFT 可以代表什么，还探索它们如何成为活跃的金融基础设施的一部分。

更多研究即将到来。
