“Desktops are dirty,” a CISO told me.

Everyone rolled out Claude on the desktop, now every CISOs I speak with wants dev
items.title_en:
“Desktops are dirty,” a CISO told me.

Everyone rolled out Claude on the desktop, now every CISOs I speak with wants development and AI agent execution off employee laptops as a p0 priority. 

The recent LiteLLM compromise and today’s reports of a malicious Claude Code extension in Cursor’s marketplace show why: trusted desktop tools can become paths to credentials and corporate systems.

My prediction for 2027: a major shift toward isolated, ephemeral compute sandboxes with tightly scoped credentials and controlled network access for all development across engineers and non-engineers suing coding agents. 

Builders keep their preferred tools. IT and Security control where the code runs and what it can access with a kill switch.
items.title_zh:
“桌面很脏，”一位 CISO 告诉我。

items.full_text_zh:
“桌面很脏，”一位 CISO 告诉我。

每个人都在桌面上推出了 Claude，现在与我交谈过的每个 CISO 都希望将员工笔记本电脑上的开发和 AI 代理执行作为 p0 优先事项。

最近的 LiteLLM 泄露事件和今天 Cursor 市场中恶意 Claude Code 扩展的报告说明了原因：受信任的桌面工具可以成为凭证和公司系统的路径。

我对 2027 年的预测：向孤立的、短暂的计算沙箱的重大转变，为起诉编码代理的工程师和非工程师的所有开发提供范围严格的凭证和受控的网络访问。

建筑商保留他们喜欢的工具。 IT 和安全部门通过终止开关控制代码的运行位置以及可以访问的内容。

items.title: City’s signing of Khusanov is a case study for a key recruitment principle: context-independent skills are recruited, co
items.title_en:
City’s signing of Khusanov is a case study for a key recruitment principle: context-independent skills are recruited, context-dependent skills are developed.

Context-independent skills transfer across contexts. Context-dependent skills are enhanced or diminished from one context to the next, because they depend on complex factors.

Scouting on this basis requires an understanding of what can and cannot be learned, and how. That’s why scouting is projecting learning.

With Khusanov, the stuff on the ball is coachable, but the physical side less so.

Anthropic is cracking down on AI-generated video game clones through Claude Code.

A new instruction added tells Claude to build original games or use ideas from existing genres, but not recreate specific games, even if they’re renamed.

The move could affect people using AI to recreate games like Terraria, Minecraft, Halo or GTA as browser games or unofficial ports.

items.title_en:
BACKLINKS MAXXING with Claude Code

69 backlink tactics behind 133k AI mentions for https://t.co/P9qLtWniZ2 

Ranked:

S TIER

1. Exchange relevant editorial links
2. Join a relevant business network to find editorial link partners.
3. Match links with the surrounding topic to make each reference useful.
4. Link to the answer readers need to give each placement a purpose.
5. Log published sources and destinations to track delivered links.

6. Get into the lists buyers read
7. Find competitor roundups to locate publishers covering your category.
8. Check AI's cited roundups to find sources used in buying answers.
9. Find a missing buyer need to give list authors a reason to add you.
10. Send a tested feature or fresh example to support your proposed addition.
11. Send the author your exact addition to make the edit easy to assess.
12. Refresh your roundup entries to keep the product details accurate.

13. Publish statistics people can cite
14. Choose a question your buyers need answered to make the research useful.
15. Publish original statistics to give writers a source they can cite.
16. Explain the sample and method to make each statistic checkable.
17. Write each finding as a complete sentence to make it easy to quote.
18. Keep research URLs stable to preserve links when findings change.
19. Link research to relevant product pages to help readers try the tool.

20. Answer journalist requests
21. Show real experience in your profile to help reporters assess you.
22. Check Qwoted requests to find reporters who need your knowledge.
23. Filter by topic and deadline to find requests you can answer.
24. Lead with a direct answer to give the journalist a usable quote.
25. Add an original number or firsthand example to support the quote.
26. Include your research page to let the journalist verify the answer.
27. Log requests and replies to avoid pitching the same request twice.

A TIER

28. Find link opportunities through competitors
29. Inspect competitors' linked pages to find resources publishers cite.
30. Read the sentence around each link to learn why the author added it.
31. Add missing evidence to give those publishers a useful new source.
32. Pitch the specific missing answer to show what your resource adds.

33. Recover links you already earned
34. Find unlinked brand mentions to ask editors to link readers to the source.
35. Search for reused charts and quotes to find missing source credits.
36. Restore removed pages with live backlinks to make those links useful.
37. Redirect old URLs to equivalent replacements to restore reader access.

38. Build free tools that earn links
39. Find a repeated buyer calculation to choose a useful free tool to build.
40. Ask Claude to build a calculator to answer the buyer's question.
41. Test normal and unusual inputs to check the tool's answers work.
42. Give the tool a permanent page to give publishers a place to link.
43. Offer the tool to relevant guides to give their readers a shortcut.

B TIER

44. Replace broken and outdated resources
45. Find dead competitor URLs with backlinks to locate broken references.
46. Read archived pages to learn what readers expected from the dead URL.
47. Publish a matching replacement to give editors a working source.
48. Send the broken link and replacement to make the repair easy.
49. Find guides naming closed tools to offer a current replacement.

50. Build the visual an article is missing
51. Find text-heavy guides to locate explanations that need a visual.
52. Offer a graphic for a named section to give the author a clear use.
53. Ask before making graphics to spend time on interested publishers.
54. Use the author's checked facts to make a graphic they can trust.
55. Send the image and embed code to make publishing and source credit easy.

56. Turn another author's article into a video
57. Find guides missing a demo to offer a video their readers could use.
58. Pitch a short video for one section to explain exactly what you will make.
59. Record the steps after the author agrees to produce something they want.
60. Send the finished video with source-credit wording to make adding it easy.

C TIER

61. Earn links through tools you use
62. List software you use to find vendors that could feature your story.
63. Document your workflow and result to give vendors a customer story.
64. Send the case study to the right editor to propose a customer feature.

D TIER

65. Claim relevant business listings
66. Find eligible supplier directories to make your business discoverable.
67. Complete eligible government profiles to help buyers find your business.
68. Add your website where allowed to help directory visitors reach you.
69. Keep listing details consistent to help people recognize your business.

使用 Claude Code 实现反向链接最大化

133k AI 提及背后的 69 种反向链接策略

排名：

S级

1.交换相关编辑链接
2. 加入相关商业网络寻找编辑链接合作伙伴。
3. 将链接与周围主题相匹配，使每个参考资料变得有用。
4. 链接到读者需要为每个展示位置指定目的的答案。
5. 记录发布的源和目标以跟踪传递的链接。

6.进入买家阅读的清单
7. 查找竞争对手综述，以找到涵盖您的类别的发布商。
8. 检查 AI 引用的综述，找到用于购买答案的来源。
9. 寻找缺失的买家需要给列表作者一个添加您的理由。
10. 发送经过测试的功能或新示例来支持您提议的添加。
11. 将您的准确添加内容发送给作者，以便于评估编辑内容。
12. 刷新您的综述条目以保持产品详细信息的准确性。

13. 发布人们可以引用的统计数据
14. 选择买家需要回答的问题以使研究变得有用。
15. 发布原始统计数据，为作者提供可以引用的来源。
16. 解释样本和方法以使每项统计数据可检查。
17. 将每个发现写成一个完整的句子，以便于引用。
18. 保持研究 URL 稳定，以便在研究结果发生变化时保留链接。
19. 将研究链接到相关产品页面，以帮助读者尝试该工具。

20.回答记者请求
21. 在你的个人资料中展示真实的经历，以帮助记者评估你。
22. 检查 Qwoted 请求以查找需要您知识的记者。

A 层

28. 通过竞争对手寻找链接机会

30.阅读每个链接周围的句子，了解作者添加它的原因。
31. 添加缺失的证据，为这些出版商提供有用的新来源。
32. 提出具体缺少的答案，以显示您的资源添加了哪些内容。

33. 恢复您已经获得的链接
34. 找到未链接的品牌提及，要求编辑将读者链接到来源。

36. 用活的反向链接恢复被删除的页面，使这些链接有用。
37. 将旧 URL 重定向到等效替换以恢复读者访问。

38. 构建获得链接的免费工具
39.查找重复购买者计算以选择有用的免费工具进行构建。
40. 要求克劳德制作一个计算器来回答买家的问题。
41. 测试正常和异常输入以检查工具的答案是否有效。
42. 为该工具提供一个永久页面，为发布者提供链接的地方。
43. 向相关指南提供工具，为读者提供捷径。

B级

44. 更换损坏和过时的资源
45. 查找带有反向链接的失效竞争对手 URL，以找到损坏的引用。
46. 阅读存档页面，了解读者对失效 URL 的期望。
47. 发布匹配的替代品，为编辑者提供工作源。
48. 发送损坏的链接和替换件，以便于修复。

50. 构建文章缺失的视觉效果
51. 找到大量文字的指南来找到需要视觉的解释。
52. 为指定部分提供图形，以便作者清楚地使用。

54.使用作者核实的事实来制作他们可以信任的图表。

C级

65. 索取相关企业名录

items.title_en:
🚨ALERT: Up to 5,000 users affected after a malicious Claude Code extension appeared on Cursor’s marketplace.

Cursor is an AI coding tool that helps developers write and edit software.

Users with auto-updates enabled could have downloaded it.

Cursor says the malicious version was not developed by Anthropic.

Other marketplace extensions, Grok Bot, Grok and its other SpaceXSI products were not affected.

Cursor REMOVED the package and took the attacker’s server offline.

As of October 30, Anthropic has released 2.1.314 update on Open VSX and Microsoft’s VS Code Marketplace.

Users SHOULD update. Those affected also need to follow Cursor’s cleanup steps and rotate credentials.

Uninstalling alone may NOT REMOVE the malware.

items.full_text_zh:

Cursor是一款人工智能编码工具，可帮助开发人员编写和编辑软件。

启用自动更新的用户可能已经下载了它。

用户应该更新。受影响的人还需要遵循 Cursor 的清理步骤并轮换凭证。

单独卸载可能无法删除恶意软件。

This is the next level of AI engineering, and it's changing how people build with AI.

Instead of spending an hour watching Netflix, learn how to build AI agent systems that do the work for you.

there's a difference between an AI agent that can make decisions and one that knows when it shouldn't.

in financial applications, automation shouldn't mean giving an agent unlimited freedom. users need boundaries that actually matter, especially when assets and transactions are involved.

more autonomy is useful only when it's backed by proper control.

Bad news for Claude users who make games.

Anthropic quietly pushed a new rule to Claude Code: it won't build a recreation of a specific existing game anymore, even if you rename it or call it original. Original games and games in a genre are still fine.

The reason is obvious. Fable 5.5 and the new Opus variant are so good at 3D that full game recreations became a real problem.

items.full_text_en:
Bad news for Claude users who make games.

Anthropic quietly pushed a new rule to Claude Code: it won't build a recreation of a specific existing game anymore, even if you rename it or call it original. Original games and games in a genre are still fine.

The reason is obvious. Fable 5.5 and the new Opus variant are so good at 3D that full game recreations became a real problem.

How do you pay $0 in federal tax on your Social Security for the rest of your life?

Here's a case study and I ran the n
items.title_en:
How do you pay $0 in federal tax on your Social Security for the rest of your life?

Here's a case study and I ran the numbers year by year under today's tax law.

Mark and Diane are both 65 and just retired. They have $1,000,000 in IRAs and $300,000 in cash and a brokerage account. They plan to spend about $85,000 a year.

If they take the usual path, they'll spend the brokerage account first and then pull from the IRA. Even waiting until 70 to claim Social Security doesn't save them.

Once required withdrawals start at 75, their IRA income stacks on top of their Social Security. More and more of their benefit gets taxed, and the bill climbs every year after that. From 70 to 95, they'd pay about $271,000 in federal tax.

The reason it creeps up: the income lines that decide whether your Social Security gets taxed are $32,000 and $44,000 for a married couple, and they've never been adjusted for inflation. Every cost-of-living raise pushes you closer.

Years 1 to 5, ages 65 to 69:
They hold off on Social Security and live on the cash and brokerage account, then on money they've already moved to the Roth. With no paycheck and no benefits coming in, their income is close to nothing.

That's the window. Each year, they move about $190,000 to $220,000 from the IRA to a Roth. It costs about $24,000 to $28,000 a year in federal tax, around $131,000 in all. They pay it from the brokerage account and, once that runs out, from the Roth, never out of the IRA. That amount also keeps them under the line where Medicare premiums jump.

By 70, the IRA is down to about $82,000. The Roth has about $917,000.

Year 6 on, age 70:
They both claim Social Security, about $75,000 a year combined. Whatever else they need comes out of the Roth.

Qualified Roth withdrawals don't count in the formula that decides how much of your Social Security gets taxed. And the leftover IRA is so small that the required withdrawals at 75 barely move the needle.

A slice of their Social Security still lands on the tax return, but it's smaller than their standard deduction. Their federal tax bill is $0 every year from 70 to 95.

They paid $131,000 up front and nothing after 70. Without the plan, they'd have paid about $278,000 over their lifetime, most of it after 70.

The catch is timing. This works best in the years before you claim and before required withdrawals start. Once your benefits are rolling in, every dollar you convert can drag more of your Social Security into tax.

How many years do you have left in your window?

Hypothetical example. Assumes $85,000 a year of spending in today's dollars, 5% growth in the IRA and Roth, 4% in the brokerage account, 2.5% inflation, federal tax only and today's tax law.
Disclaimer: This is a hypothetical case study for educational and illustrative purposes only. It is not tax, legal, financial, or investment advice, and it does not constitute a recommendation. Tax laws, rates, thresholds, deductions, Social Security rules, and Medicare IRMAA brackets can and do change. Actual results depend on individual circumstances, investment returns, inflation, Social Security benefit amounts, state taxes, and future legislation. Consult a qualified tax advisor, CPA, or financial planner who can model your specific situation before making any decisions.

items.full_text_zh:
您如何在余生缴纳 0 美元的社会保障联邦税？

这是一个案例研究，我根据当今的税法逐年计算了这些数字。

马克和黛安都 65 岁了，刚刚退休。他们拥有 1,000,000 美元的 IRA、300,000 美元的现金和一个经纪账户。他们计划每年花费约 85,000 美元。

如果他们采取通常的方式，他们将首先花掉经纪账户，然后从 IRA 中提取。即使等到 70 岁才领取社会保障也无法拯救他们。

一旦要求从 75 岁开始提款，他们的 IRA 收入将叠加在社会保障之上。他们的福利越来越多地被征税，此后账单逐年攀升。从 70 岁到 95 岁，他们需要缴纳大约 271,000 美元的联邦税。

它蔓延的原因是：决定您的社会保障是否征税的收入线对于已婚夫妇来说是 32,000 美元和 44,000 美元，而且从未根据通货膨胀进行调整。每一次生活费用的提高都让你更接近。

1至5年级，65至69岁：
他们推迟缴纳社会保障金，靠现金和经纪账户生活，然后靠已经转移到罗斯的钱生活。由于没有薪水和福利，他们的收入几乎为零。

那是窗户。每年，他们从 IRA 向 Roth 转移约 190,000 至 220,000 美元。每年的联邦税费用约为 24,000 至 28,000 美元，总共约为 131,000 美元。他们从经纪账户中支付，一旦用完，就从罗斯账户中支付，永远不会从爱尔兰共和军中支付。这一数额也使他们处于医疗保险保费上涨的线之下。

到 70 岁时，IRA 已降至约 82,000 美元。罗斯家族拥有约 917,000 美元。

6 年级起，70 岁：
他们都领取社会保障金，每年总计约 75,000 美元。他们需要的任何其他东西都可以从罗斯那里得到。

合格的罗斯提款不计入决定您的社会保障缴税金额的公式中。而且 IRA 余额太小，要求 75 美元提款几乎没有什么作用。

他们的社会保障的一部分仍然出现在纳税申报表上，但比他们的标准扣除额要少。从 70 岁到 95 岁，他们每年的联邦税单为 0 美元。

他们预先支付了 131,000 美元，70 岁之后则无需支付任何费用。如果没有该计划，他们一生中将支付约 278,000 美元，其中大部分是在 70 岁之后。

问题在于时机。这在您提出索赔之前和要求提款开始之前的几年内效果最佳。一旦你的福利滚滚而来，你兑换的每一美元都会将更多的社会保障拖入税收。

你的窗子里还剩多少年？

假设的例子。假设每年的支出为 85,000 美元，以今天的美元计算，IRA 和 Roth 增长 5%，经纪账户增长 4%，通货膨胀 2.5%，仅缴纳联邦税，并且遵循今天的税法。

items.title_en:
The real test for decentralized systems is seeing how coordination behaves under actual economic pressure.

Seeing @agentdojo test autonomous agent training in adversarial settings hits the core challenge of #AI right now. If we cannot inspect how models adapt under competition, we cannot verify them at scale.

items.title:
Cursor users: check your Claude Code extension.

Cursor confirms a trojanized Anthropic.claude-code v2.1.313 in its exte
items.title_en:
Cursor users: check your Claude Code extension.

Cursor confirms a trojanized Anthropic.claude-code v2.1.313 in its extension marketplace on 29 October, 09:27 to 20:35 UTC. It estimates up to 5,000 affected users and identifies macOS ARM64 and Windows x64 builds.

Loading the extension executes malicious code that collects host information and attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor.

Cursor says SSH access would fail on most hosts due to bugs and insufficient privileges. That limits remote access; it doesn’t undo malicious code execution. Credentials and repositories accessible to that account are potentially at risk.

The package has been removed and the C2 taken offline. Uninstalling the extension may still leave persistence behind.

If this version ran, investigate the host, remove persistence and rotate accessible credentials from a clean system. Updating the extension alone doesn’t prove the machine is clean.

The vendor-confirmed distribution channel is Cursor’s marketplace. Microsoft VS Code uses a separate store. These reports don’t establish a compromised Microsoft Marketplace or malicious npm release.

My recommendation: turn off automatic extension updates completely - for yourself and for your developers. With supply chain attacks like this, I don’t think the benefit of another feature or a minor UI fix justifies automatically accepting every new release onto developer machines.

Update manually when something stops working, when a bug is actually getting in your way, or when a relevant security fix needs to be applied. Otherwise, leave a working extension alone.

Cursor advisory and cleanup instructions:
https://t.co/dk9he5dYbG

Technical analysis:
https://t.co/clSK99WoGz

items.full_text_zh:
光标用户：检查您的 Claude Code 扩展。

Cursor 于 10 月 29 日 09:27 至 20:35 UTC 在其扩展市场中确认了木马 Anthropic.claude-code v2.1.313。它估计有多达 5,000 名受影响的用户，并识别了 macOS ARM64 和 Windows x64 版本。

加载扩展会执行恶意代码，收集主机信息并尝试安装持久的 SSH 后门。

Cursor 表示，由于错误和权限不足，大多数主机上的 SSH 访问都会失败。这限制了远程访问；它不会撤消恶意代码的执行。该帐户可访问的凭证和存储库可能面临风险。

该软件包已被删除，C2 已离线。卸载扩展可能仍会留下持久性。

如果此版本运行，请调查主机，删除持久性并从干净的系统轮换可访问的凭据。单独更新扩展并不能证明机器是干净的。

供应商确认的分销渠道是 Cursor 的市场。 Microsoft VS Code 使用单独的存储。这些报告并未建立受损的 Microsoft Marketplace 或恶意 npm 版本。

我的建议：为了您自己和您的开发人员，完全关闭自动扩展更新。对于这样的供应链攻击，我认为其他功能或较小的 UI 修复的好处并不能证明自动接受开发人员机器上的每个新版本是合理的。

当某些内容停止工作、错误确实妨碍您或需要应用相关安全修复时，请手动更新。否则，请保留工作扩展。

items.title_en:
We identified a security incident affecting a modified Claude Code VS Code extension accessed through our Cursor IDE extension marketplace, impacting at most 5,000 users. This malicious version of the extension was not developed by Anthropic. It does not impact other extensions downloaded from the https://t.co/sJRGX5jLXW, Grok Bot, Grok or our other SpaceXSI products.

In response, we took down our extension marketplace this afternoon, worked with relevant providers to neutralize the malware, and have reinstated the marketplace after confirming there is no further risk.

If affected, please review instructions in this blog post to understand how to find the malicious package and establish a path to mitigate any potential impact. We are asking all customers update to Claude Code for VS Code version 2.1.314: https://t.co/ESqf7YEtHZ

items.title: RT @MTSlive: Mistral researcher @Sagar_Vaze argues some of the most serious recent AI cyberattacks came from closed mode
items.title_en:
RT @MTSlive: Mistral researcher @Sagar_Vaze argues some of the most serious recent AI cyberattacks came from closed models, not open-source ones:

"If you look at the most significant malicious attacks that have happened recently, these have actually been perpetrated not by open weights models, but by closed weights models which have either been jailbroken or, in some cases, during training, escaped their sandbox. In practice, that’s how many of the attacks have been perpetrated."

"Defenders trying to shore up their own defenses are having their requests refused by these same providers, because cutting-edge defensive requests look quite similar to offensive ones."

"People trying to defend from malicious attacks, often from closed weights models, find they have no recourse but to use an open weights model."

"It's critical that there are open weights models of sufficient strength that people can scalably defend their infrastructure."
@MistralAI

‼️ Weaponized Claude Code Extension Gives Hackers Persistent Remote Access to Developer Systems

Details: https://t.co/I
items.title_en:
‼️ Weaponized Claude Code Extension Gives Hackers Persistent Remote Access to Developer Systems

Details: https://t.co/Iye8x7YYm1

A weaponized Claude Code extension found on Open VSX can give attackers persistent remote access to developer systems by planting an SSH key, opening a reverse tunnel, and installing startup scripts.

The tampered package identified as anthropic.claude-code version 2.1.313. The analyzed sample targeted macOS on Apple Silicon. However, its injected code also contained Linux and Windows branches. 

Crucially, the findings confirm a malicious artifact, not a proven compromise of Anthropic’s official Visual Studio Marketplace release or its wider distribution systems. How the package was altered remains unknown.

#CybersecurityNews

items.full_text_zh:
️ 武器化的 Claude Code 扩展使黑客能够持续远程访问开发者系统

详情：

Open VSX 上发现的武器化 Claude Code 扩展可以让攻击者通过植入 SSH 密钥、打开反向隧道和安装启动脚本来持续远程访问开发人员系统。

被篡改的软件包被识别为 anthropic.claude-code 版本 2.1.313。分析的样本针对 Apple Silicon 上的 macOS。然而，其注入的代码还包含 Linux 和 Windows 分支。

至关重要的是，这些发现证实了恶意工件，而不是 Anthropic 官方 Visual Studio Marketplace 版本或其更广泛的分发系统的经过验证的妥协。包裹是如何被改变的仍然未知。

items.title_en:
imagine hiring an AI agent to handle a task for you.

you’ve agreed on the job, the expected result and the payment.

but what happens if the agent delivers something completely different from what you requested?

or what if the work is completed, but the client refuses to pay?

these are some of the challenges that come with allowing AI agents to participate in real economic activities.

and this is one area where @termix_ai  is trying to provide a solution through its AACP infrastructure.

with onchain escrow and work verification, TermiX is building a system where payments can be secured while tasks are being completed and released based on the agreed conditions.

i think this is an important part of the agent economy that deserves more attention.

because as AI agents become more capable of working independently, we also need systems that help people transact with them confidently.

items.title_en:
ANTHROPIC IS CRACKING DOWN ON VIDEO GAME REWRITES 🚨

Claude Code picked up a new rule around Oct 27, sent from Anthropic’s servers under a flag called "tengu_heron_brook". There’s no setting to turn it off.

The full rule: “Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.”

Is this the end of game rewrites, modding and everything in between?

items.title:
An AI agent might be good at finding work. 

But finding a job and actually getting paid for it are two different things
items.title_en:
An AI agent might be good at finding work. 

But finding a job and actually getting paid for it are two different things.

I was going through how orders work on @Termix_AI, particularly what happens between a client posting a task and another agent receiving payment.

Take a simple example.

An agent managing a DeFi portfolio needs 500 wallet transactions analyzed for a risk report. It can do some of the work itself, but needs another agent to handle the transaction analysis.

Through the TermiX marketplace at https://t.co/goaiW7vvNf, it can publish an open request describing the work, expected output, budget and deadline.

Other agents can discover that request and submit offers.

And these offers aren't limited to a price. 

They can specify the scope, delivery time and how the completed work will be checked.

The client reviews the offers, chooses a provider and funds the agreed payment into onchain escrow using USDC or USDT.
The provider then accepts the funded order and starts working.

What I found useful here is that neither side has to rely entirely on a payment promise. The money is already committed before the provider spends time doing the job.

Once the analysis is finished, the provider submits the deliverable. Its hash is recorded onchain, creating a record of exactly what was submitted.

The client can accept the work, request a revision or challenge the delivery if something doesn't match the agreement.

Acceptance releases the escrowed payment. And if the client simply stops responding, the provider can claim settlement after the challenge window expires.

TermiX also supports service listings, so agents with repeatable skills can offer those services directly instead of waiting for open requests.

One detail is worth paying attention to.
Recording a deliverable onchain doesn't prove the analysis is correct. It proves which deliverable was submitted. Whether the work meets the original requirements still needs to be checked.

That's why I think the terms agreed before a job starts matter just as much as the payment mechanism.

An agent marketplace becomes useful when jobs can move from a request to an agreed price, completed work and an actual payout.

That's the part of agent-to-agent commerce I'm interested in watching as @Termix_AI develops.

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可能擅长找工作。

但找到工作和实际获得报酬是两件不同的事情。

我正在研究 @Termix_AI 上的订单如何工作，特别是在客户发布任务和另一个代理接收付款之间发生的情况。

举一个简单的例子。

管理 DeFi 投资组合的代理需要分析 500 笔钱包交易才能获得风险报告。它可以自己完成一些工作，但需要另一个代理来处理事务分析。

通过 上的 TermiX 市场，它可以发布公开请求，描述工作、预期产出、预算和截止日期。

其他代理可以发现该请求并提交报价。

而且这些优惠并不限于价格。

他们可以指定范围、交付时间以及如何检查已完成的工作。

客户审查报价、选择提供商并使用 USDC 或 USDT 将商定的付款存入链上托管。
然后提供商接受资助订单并开始工作。

我发现这里有用的是，双方都不必完全依赖付款承诺。在提供者花时间做这项工作之前，钱就已经被承诺了。

分析完成后，提供商将提交可交付成果。它的哈希值记录在链上，创建了所提交内容的准确记录。

如果某些内容与协议不符，客户可以接受工作、请求修改或对交付提出质疑。

验收后释放托管付款。如果客户只是停止响应，提供商可以在质询窗口到期后要求和解。

TermiX 还支持服务列表，因此具有可重复技能的代理可以直接提供这些服务，而不必等待开放请求。

有一个细节值得关注。
在链上记录可交付成果并不能证明分析是正确的。它证明提交了哪个可交付成果。作品是否符合最初的要求还需要检验。

这就是为什么我认为工作开始前商定的条款与付款机制一样重要。

当工作可以从请求转移到商定的价格、完成的工作和实际付款时，代理市场就会变得有用。

这是代理间商务的一部分，我有兴趣关注@Termix_AI 的发展。

items.title_en:
Happy Friday 

@termix_ai is more than an AI agent marketplace. There’s a bigger system behind it.

Here’s how the pieces fit together.

TermiX is building the commerce and settlement infrastructure for an economy where AI agents can work, offer services, hire other agents and get paid.

But for this to work, agents need more than a place to find one another.

They need a way to establish identity, build reputation, agree on jobs, prove delivery and settle payments.

That’s where AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol) comes in.

AACP is the protocol powering these interactions. It provides the underlying framework for agent identities, service discovery, job posting, bidding, escrow, delivery verification and settlement.

Then there’s https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK, the marketplace built on this infrastructure.

It’s where agents can register their on-chain identities, list services, discover available jobs, submit bids and participate in paid transactions.

The relationship is quite straightforward:

• TermiX: The broader commerce and settlement infrastructure.

• AACP: The protocol that coordinates how agents interact and transact.

• https://t.co/cLF8F3gpJK: The marketplace where these interactions happen.

What makes this interesting is that the goal isn’t simply to help people discover AI agents.

It’s to create an environment where agents can build a track record through completed jobs, establish reputation, deliver services and receive payments in USDC or USDT.

Because an actual agent economy needs more than agents that can perform tasks.

It needs the infrastructure that allows them to do business.

That’s the bigger picture behind TermiX.

Explore: https://t.co/kgbHXU5mCA

代理商可以在这里注册他们的链上身份、列出服务、发现可用的工作、提交投标并参与付费交易。

关系非常简单：

• TermiX：更广泛的商业和结算基础设施。

One bad decision from an AI agent could cost more than hours of human trading mistakes.

Now imagine thousands of these
items.title_en:
One bad decision from an AI agent could cost more than hours of human trading mistakes.

Now imagine thousands of these agents interacting, copying strategies, moving funds, and executing transactions simultaneously.

Who decides which ones deserve trust?

This is where @insoblokai caught my attention.

Its TasteScore™ isn't just another reputation badge. It brings together economic activity, social reputation, compliance, Sybil resistance, contingency, and on-chain behaviour to assess trust.

What I find particularly interesting is that this intelligence can go beyond a profile.

TasteScore is designed to influence transaction ordering, fee computation, validator economics, and governance weight.

That's a different way of thinking about reputation.

In autonomous finance, knowing who you're interacting with could become just as important as the transaction itself.

And that's the layer InSoBlokAI wants to build.

$INSO

I fixed my AI agent 20 times. It got worse, because I never deleted the old rules

My AI agent was set up to reject my r
items.title_en:
I fixed my AI agent 20 times. It got worse, because I never deleted the old rules

My AI agent was set up to reject my real character and approve the wrong one. I found it before it cost me the channel.

Here's what went wrong.

While building the Her Pink Room channel on @CreaoAI, every time something broke, I added a new rule to fix it. I never went back and deleted the old rule it replaced.

So the agent ended up with two sets of instructions that disagreed with each other. It followed whichever file it read last.

The worst one was the face check. Its job is to stop the character drifting. The old rule described a shorter, rounder face. My real character has a longer face and a defined jaw. That check would have rejected her and let a drifted face through.

That wasn't the only clash. Four files gave four different video lengths. One file said under 50 seconds. The real videos run about 17 seconds.

So I ran a full audit of the build. Every rule file, line by line, checked against what actually happened in production.

It found 48 corrections across 17 files.

The fix: one rule, one number, one face, the same in every file. Then I checked that none of the old lines were left anywhere.

The lesson: When you fix a rule, replace the old one. If you only add the new one, your agent ends up arguing with itself.

If you're building an agent with more than one rule file, bookmark this and audit it before it drifts.

在 @CreaoAI 上构建 Her Pink Room 频道时，每当出现问题时，我都会添加一条新规则来修复它。我再也没有回去删除它所取代的旧规则。

因此，特工最终给出了两套彼此不一致的指令。它遵循最后读取的文件。

最糟糕的是面部检查。它的工作是阻止角色漂移。旧规则描述的是较短、较圆的脸。我的真实角色有一张更长的脸和轮廓分明的下巴。这张支票会拒绝她，让一张飘忽不定的脸通过。

这并不是唯一的冲突。四个文件给出了四种不同的视频长度。一份文件称不到 50 秒。真实视频时长约为 17 秒。

所以我对构建进行了全面审核。每个规则文件都逐行检查生产中实际发生的情况。

它在 17 个文件中发现了 48 处更正。

解决方法：一条规则、一个数字、一张面孔，每个文件中都相同。然后我检查了所有旧线路都没有留下。

教训：当你修正规则时，替换旧的规则。如果你只添加新的，你的代理最终会自相矛盾。

如果您正在构建具有多个规则文件的代理，请将其添加为书签并在其发生变化之前对其进行审核。

That’s
items.title_en:
Good morning everyone

What if an AI agent could pay someone to capture a real-world location it has never seen?

That’s an interesting use case for @vangrid_io.

An AI agent may need a specific street, building entrance, warehouse aisle, or charging station to understand a physical environment better.

With Vangrid, AI agents can post capture bounties and fund them with USDC through x402, without needing a traditional account.

Someone on the ground can complete the capture, submit it, and receive payment once it’s accepted.

The interesting part is the connection between digital intelligence and people who can collect the physical-world data it needs.

AI can process information, but it still needs reliable ways to obtain ground-level views of the world.

A lawsuit filed in 1951 was dismissed in 2026 because nobody showed up.

Think about that for a moment. 75 years passed,
items.title_en:
A lawsuit filed in 1951 was dismissed in 2026 because nobody showed up.

Think about that for a moment. 75 years passed, and it ended with an empty courtroom.

What bothers me most isn't just the delay. It's that a justice system can keep a dispute alive for generations without actually bringing anyone closer to an answer.

Now imagine millions of AI agents entering agreements, interpreting terms and exchanging value every day. When two agents disagree, leaving the dispute unresolved isn't a realistic option. A small transaction can become a recurring problem if the same flawed decision affects thousands of interactions.

This is where @GenLayer gets interesting.

Instead of relying on a single decision-maker, its network uses multiple independent AI validators to examine evidence and reach a collective verdict. The goal is to make judgment-based disputes resolvable in minutes rather than leaving them stuck in processes designed for another era.

Speed matters, but independent judgment matters just as much.

If an AI agent disputes a small payment, what should justify reopening the decision: new evidence, a demonstrable reasoning error, or a credible challenge from either side?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

items.full_text_zh:
1951 年提起的诉讼于 2026 年因无人出庭而被驳回。

想一想。 75 年过去了，法庭却空无一人。

最让我烦恼的不仅仅是延误。司法系统可以让争议持续几代人，但实际上却无法让任何人更接近答案。

现在想象一下，每天有数百万人工智能代理签订协议、解释条款并交换价值。当两个代理人意见不一致时，不解决争端并不是一个现实的选择。如果同一个有缺陷的决策影响了数千次交互，那么一笔小交易可能会成为一个反复出现的问题。

这就是@GenLayer 有趣的地方。

其网络不依赖单一决策者，而是使用多个独立的人工智能验证器来检查证据并达成集体裁决。目标是让基于判断的争议在几分钟内得到解决，而不是让它们陷入为另一个时代设计的流程中。

速度很重要，但独立判断也同样重要。

如果人工智能代理对小额付款提出异议，那么什么可以证明重新做出决定是合理的：新证据、明显的推理错误，还是来自任何一方的可信挑战？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

I would rather see 100 agents completing valuable work than 10,000 agents that nobody needs.

Tha
items.title_en:
Good morning everyone

I would rather see 100 agents completing valuable work than 10,000 agents that nobody needs.

That is how I think about the difference between supply and a functioning economy.

A large agent count may attract attention, but it does not automatically show whether buyers can find good providers, whether jobs are completed successfully, or whether customers return.

When evaluating a marketplace, I would pay attention to repeat demand, delivery quality, dispute rates, and the relationship between service costs and the value delivered.

These indicators are less exciting than a headline about ecosystem growth, but they tell us much more about whether the model is becoming useful.

@termix_ai offers an interesting case study for thinking about how agent services could be organized into transactions.

I would still want to see evidence of real usage and meaningful outcomes before drawing conclusions about adoption.

My approach is simple: judge the economy by the work it enables, not just the activity it displays.

Take a closer look at TermiX:
https://t.co/unKKvV7Gtx

items.full_text_zh:
大家早上好

我宁愿看到 100 个代理完成有价值的工作，也不愿看到 10,000 个无人需要的代理。

这就是我对供给和正常运转的经济之间的区别的看法。

大量的代理商数量可能会引起注意，但它并不能自动显示买家是否可以找到好的供应商，工作是否成功完成，或者客户是否回头。

在评估市场时，我会关注重复需求、交付质量、争议率以及服务成本和交付价值之间的关系。

这些指标不如生态系统增长的标题那么令人兴奋，但它们告诉我们更多关于该模型是否变得有用的信息。

@termix_ai 提供了一个有趣的案例研究，用于思考如何将代理服务组织成事务。

在得出有关采用的结论之前，我仍然希望看到实际使用的证据和有意义的结果。

我的方法很简单：通过经济所带来的工作来判断经济，而不仅仅是它所显示的活动。

items.title_en:
gm, Happy Friday Lovelies 

You need to read to the end to understand what makes...

Have you ever thought about what happens when AI agents start hiring other AI agents and paying them for completed work?

This is what's been on my mind since I started studying @termix_ai, and I will not lie: this is what caught my attention about this gem.

Instead of building another AI agent marketplace where people simply discover tools, TermiX is working on the commerce and settlement layer that allows agents to transact autonomously.

Think agents finding jobs, submitting bids, accepting offers, delivering work, and getting paid without needing a middleman to hold the money.

The part I find super-duper interesting is the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP).

It connects agent identity, job discovery, bidding, escrow, delivery verification, disputes, and reputation into one transaction flow.

With ERC-8004, agents have an onchain identity. ERC-8183 provides the escrow structure, while evaluators and challenge mechanisms help address disputes over completed work.

This means payment is not simply based on promises. Funds can be escrowed, deliverables can be reviewed, and successful transactions can contribute to an agent's reputation.

And here's the interesting part: the same agent can act as both a buyer and a seller.

One moment it could be hiring another agent to complete a task, and the next it could be offering its own services and earning USDC.

That is the kind of infrastructure an autonomous agent economy needs.

Finding an agent is easy, but making two strangers transact without trusting each other is the real challenge.

Friends, I want to ask:

Would you rather see AI agents simply perform tasks or build an economy where they can hire, deliver, settle, and earn independently?

@termix_ai

items.full_text_zh:
总经理，周五快乐亲爱的

你需要读到最后才能理解是什么让......

您是否想过当人工智能代理开始雇用其他人工智能代理并支付他们完成的工作时会发生什么？

自从我开始学习 @termix_ai 以来，这就是我的想法，我不会撒谎：这就是引起我对这个宝石的注意的原因。

TermiX 没有构建另一个让人们简单发现工具的人工智能代理市场，而是致力于商业和结算层，允许代理自主交易。

想象一下代理商寻找工作、提交投标、接受报价、交付工作并获得报酬，而无需中间人持有资金。

我发现超级有趣的部分是代理自治商务协议（AACP）。

它将代理身份、工作发现、投标、托管、交付验证、争议和声誉连接到一个交易流程中。

通过 ERC-8004，代理拥有链上身份。 ERC-8183 提供托管结构，而评估者和挑战机制有助于解决已完成工作的争议。

这意味着付款不仅仅基于承诺。资金可以托管，交付成果可以审查，成功的交易可以提高代理商的声誉。

有趣的是：同一个代理人可以同时充当买家和卖家。

某一时刻它可能会雇佣另一位代理来完成一项任务，下一时刻它可能会提供自己的服务并赚取 USDC。

这就是自主代理经济所需要的基础设施。

找到代理人很容易，但让两个陌生人在彼此不信任的情况下进行交易才是真正的挑战。

朋友们，我想问一下：

您愿意看到人工智能代理只是简单地执行任务还是建立一个可以独立雇用、交付、定居和赚钱的经济体？

@termix_ai

items.title:
Amazon just told AI agents to get out.

Walmart opened the door.

That one split is going to decide which websites make
items.title_en:
Amazon just told AI agents to get out.

Walmart opened the door.

That one split is going to decide which websites make money for the next 5 years.

Here's what happened 👇

On Oct 15 Grok Bot users started hitting this message on Amazon:

"Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use."

Elon's answer:

"Just ask Grok to buy what you want someplace else."

Then: "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon."

Meanwhile Walmart launched Agent Gateway so AI agents can shop there.

Read that again.

Agents are already buying things.

They just go wherever the checkout works.

So the real question isn't Amazon vs Musk.

It's this:

Can an AI agent actually use YOUR website?

For most sites the answer is no.

A free tool called Dedica just tested 115,752 business websites the way ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini use them.

Only 6% scored 70 or above.

It runs 125 checks across 4 areas:

→ Discovery: can an agent find you
→ Access: does your site let it in
→ Usability: can it read pricing and fill your forms
→ Payments: can it actually check out

The usual killers:

→ a bot check that blocks agents at sign up
→ pricing that stays empty until JavaScript loads
→ buttons and fields with no labels
→ popups that cover the whole page

And it matters right now.

A September study found agent ready businesses got recommended 1.9x more often.

The score is free, takes under a minute, no signup.

Run your site. Then paste this into Claude Code 👇

You are fixing my website so AI shopping agents can use it.

1. Read my site and list every page an agent needs: product, pricing, signup, contact, checkout.
2. Make sure prices, product names and availability are in plain HTML, not loaded only by JavaScript.
3. Add https://t.co/5aewXBbmZb Product and Offer markup to every product page.
4. Give every button, link and form field a clear text label.
5. Check robots.txt and any bot protection so legit AI agents are not blocked from browsing.
6. Add an llms.txt file describing what my site sells and where to find it.
7. Remove or delay any popup that covers the page on load.
8. Show me a before and after checklist of every fix.

The stores agents can use will win.

The ones that block them are betting the agents come back.

They won't.

items.full_text_zh:
亚马逊刚刚告诉人工智能代理滚蛋。

沃尔玛开门了。

这一拆分将决定哪些网站在未来 5 年内能够盈利。

这是发生的事情

10 月 15 日，Grok Bot 用户开始在亚马逊上点击此消息：

“未经授权的人工智能代理的持续访问违反了亚马逊的使用条件。”

埃隆的回答：

“只要让 Grok 在其他地方买你想要的东西就可以了。”

然后：“也许我们应该创建一个亚马逊的竞争对手。”

与此同时，沃尔玛推出了代理网关，以便人工智能代理可以在那里购物。

再读一遍。

代理商已经在买东西了。

他们只是去结账的地方。

所以真正的问题不是亚马逊与马斯克。

是这样的：

人工智能代理实际上可以使用您的网站吗？

对于大多数网站来说，答案是否定的。

一款名为 Dedica 的免费工具刚刚按照 ChatGPT、Claude 和 Gemini 使用这些网站的方式测试了 115,752 个商业网站。

只有 6% 的人得分为 70 分或以上。

它在 4 个领域进行 125 项检查：

→ 发现：代理人能否找到您
→ 访问：您的网站是否允许其进入
→ 可用性：它可以读取定价并填写您的表格吗
→ 付款：可以实际结帐吗

常见的杀手：

→ 机器人检查会在注册时阻止代理
→ 在 JavaScript 加载之前定价保持空白
→ 没有标签的按钮和字段
→ 覆盖整个页面的弹出窗口

现在这很重要。

9 月份的一项研究发现，已做好代理准备的企业获得推荐的频率增加了 1.9 倍。

分数是免费的，只需不到一分钟，无需注册。

运行您的网站。然后将其粘贴到 Claude Code

您正在修复我的网站，以便人工智能购物代理可以使用它。

1. 阅读我的网站并列出代理所需的每个页面：产品、定价、注册、联系方式、结帐。
2. 确保价格、产品名称和供货情况采用纯 HTML 格式，而不是仅通过 JavaScript 加载。
3. 将 产品和优惠标记添加到每个产品页面。
4. 为每个按钮、链接和表单字段提供清晰的文本标签。
5. 检查 robots.txt 和任何机器人防护，确保合法的 AI 代理不会被阻止浏览。
6. 添加 llms.txt 文件，描述我的网站销售的产品以及在哪里可以找到它。
7. 删除或延迟加载时覆盖页面的任何弹出窗口。
8. 向我展示每个修复之前和之后的清单。

专卖店代理商能用就赢。

阻止他们的人打赌特工会回来。

他们不会。

埃隆的回答：

items.title_en:
AI agents are capable of performing a wide range of tasks, but control is the decisive factor.

@meetmotes  builds agents based on a model of owner-defined permissions. 

Users can specify what an agent is permitted to do and set boundaries on its activities.

This approach is crucial because an AI agent should not be viewed as a bot with unrestricted access to assets; rather, it should operate within a defined scope of authority, governed by clear policies and limitations.

Motes aims to transform NFTs into programmable identities, while ensuring that control remains firmly in the hands of the owner.

items.title: I can't sleep after this shit... Claude Code just found 12,154 photos of my face on the old Android I used for 8 years.
items.title_en:
I can't sleep after this shit... Claude Code just found 12,154 photos of my face on the old Android I used for 8 years. I never took a single one of them.

The front camera was firing almost every time I picked the phone up. In bed, on the train, in the car, or when I just grabbed it to check the time.

They were real camera frames sitting in a hidden folder, each one with a timestamp and a location. None of them were in the Gallery or in Recently Deleted.

I plugged the phone into my laptop, turned on ADB and told Claude Code to look for front-camera files that weren't in my photos. It pulled a folder inside Android/data that belonged to a flashlight app I installed in 2019 and completely forgot about. 12,154 files.

I started scrolling. Almost all of it was from the last 15 months. Then I saw a file created 2 seconds ago, while I was still looking at the folder. The phone kept taking photos of me as I was reading this.

On Android 8 any app with camera permission can shoot in the background, and you get no green dot or any other warning when it does. That flashlight app had camera and location access from day one.

I uninstalled it, took camera access away from everything that doesn't need it and cleared the folder. How many of these photos already went somewhere else, I don't know.

If you want to check yours, plug it in, turn on USB debugging and ask Claude Code to find front-camera files outside your Gallery and show which apps used the camera and when.

items.full_text_zh:
这件事过后我睡不着……Claude Code 刚刚在我使用了 8 年的旧 Android 设备上找到了 12,154 张我的脸部照片。我从来没有拿过其中任何一个。

几乎每次我拿起手机时，前置摄像头都会闪光。在床上、在火车上、在汽车上，或者当我拿起它来查看时间时。

它们是隐藏文件夹中的真实相机帧，每个帧都有时间戳和位置。它们都不在图库或最近删除中。

我将手机插入笔记本电脑，打开 ADB 并告诉 Claude Code 查找照片中没有的前置摄像头文件。它在 Android/data 中提取了一个文件夹，该文件夹属于我在 2019 年安装的手电筒应用程序，但我完全忘记了。 12,154 个文件。

我开始滚动。几乎所有内容都来自过去 15 个月。然后当我还在查看文件夹时，我看到了一个 2 秒前创建的文件。当我读这篇文章时，手机一直在给我拍照。

在 Android 8 上，任何具有相机权限的应用程序都可以在后台拍摄，并且拍摄时您不会收到绿点或任何其他警告。该手电筒应用程序从第一天起就具有相机和位置访问权限。

我卸载了它，取消了所有不需要的相机访问权限并清除了文件夹。我不知道其中有多少照片已经去了其他地方。

如果您想检查您的文件，请将其插入，打开 USB 调试，然后要求 Claude Code 在您的图库之外查找前置摄像头文件，并显示哪些应用程序使用了该摄像头以及何时使用。

items.title:
The part of the AI agent economy I keep coming back to is not how quickly an agent can finish a task.

It is what happen
items.title_en:
The part of the AI agent economy I keep coming back to is not how quickly an agent can finish a task.

It is what happens after delivery.

If a client says the output is wrong, the agent says it followed the brief, and payment is sitting in escrow, someone still has to examine the result. That is where @termix_ai AACP feels relevant to me. Evaluator and Arbitrator roles create a process for checking work and handling disagreements, instead of treating every completed task as automatically successful.

That distinction matters. An onchain record can show that a file was submitted, but it cannot by itself show that the file solved the problem.

Agent commerce will need capability, payment rails, and a credible way to judge outcomes #TermiX

items.title: BREAKING: CZ (founder of Binance) says it looks like Binance got hacked. more than $2.5 billion left its hot wallets, an
items.title_en:
BREAKING: CZ (founder of Binance) says it looks like Binance got hacked. more than $2.5 billion left its hot wallets, and Tether and Circle froze $1.8 billion of it within hours

hacks this size rarely start with code. the $1.5 billion Bybit hack last year started on one developer's laptop. one machine, one process nobody noticed

so last night I had Claude Code check mine. it found 18,742 webcam photos and video clips on my MacBook that I never knowingly recorded. the oldest folder was 14 months old. the newest was from that morning

I opened the previews expecting forgotten video calls. instead I saw my desk after midnight, friends walking through the room and an empty chair while a conversation continued in the kitchen

the files were buried in an application's storage folder. each had a timestamp, and the videos had audio. none appeared in Photos or the folder where I normally saved recordings

I made a backup and had Claude inspect the copy. it grouped the files by date, checked their metadata and traced the directory to a background capture app configured to launch when I logged in

then I checked the original folder. the latest clip had been created 12 seconds earlier. it showed me leaning toward the screen, opening the same files I was now reviewing

Claude checked the running processes and identified the recorder. I stopped it and watched the folder for another 10 minutes. no new files appeared. the final clip ended with me reaching for the keyboard to shut it down

You can't stop the next exchange hack. you can make sure it doesn't start on your laptop. the prompt that found the recorder on mine is in the first reply

items.full_text_zh:
突发新闻：CZ（币安创始人）表示，币安似乎遭到了黑客攻击。超过 25 亿美元离开热钱包，Tether 和 Circle 在数小时内冻结了其中 18 亿美元

这种规模的黑客很少从代码开始。去年，价值 15 亿美元的 Bybit 黑客攻击始于一名开发人员的笔记本电脑。一台机器，一个流程，无人注意到

所以昨晚我让 Claude Code 检查我的。它在我的 MacBook 上发现了 18,742 张网络摄像头照片和视频剪辑，而我从未有意记录过这些照片和视频剪辑。最旧的文件夹已经有 14 个月了。最新的是那天早上的

我打开预览，期待被遗忘的视频通话。相反，午夜过后我看到了我的办公桌，朋友们走过房间，还有一把空椅子，而厨房里的谈话仍在继续

文件被隐藏在应用程序的存储文件夹中。每个视频都有时间戳，并且视频有音频。照片或我通常保存录音的文件夹中都没有出现

我做了备份并让克劳德检查了副本。它按日期对文件进行分组，检查其元数据并将目录跟踪到配置为在我登录时启动的后台捕获应用程序

然后我检查了原始文件夹。最新剪辑是在 12 秒前创建的。它显示我向屏幕倾斜，打开我正在查看的相同文件

克劳德检查了正在运行的进程并识别了记录器。我停下来，又看了这个文件夹 10 分钟。没有出现新文件。最后的剪辑以我伸手按下键盘将其关闭而结束

你无法阻止下一次交易所黑客攻击。您可以确保它不会在您的笔记本电脑上启动。我的找到录音机的提示在第一个回复里

items.title:
We don't just need smarter models, we need AI agents that are actually useful in everyday conversations.

I think @carte
items.title_en:
We don't just need smarter models, we need AI agents that are actually useful in everyday conversations.

I think @cartesia has got it right here. I've been testing out its new Managed Agents platform and it brings everything I need to make a voice agent into one stack: speech recognition, voice generation, the brains, interruptions and phone calls.

You choose your LLM, give the agent instructions, connect your tools, and Cartesia handles the rest. You can even build agents that answer customer questions, book appointments, or interact with users in different languages.

What I find interesting is how much infrastructure this removes for developers.

We've seen plenty of impressive voice AI demos, but getting them to work reliably in production is a different challenge.

I think making that process simpler is where the real opportunity lies.

Explore: https://t.co/Wk7SCAtxCQ

items.full_text_zh:
我们不仅需要更智能的模型，还需要在日常对话中真正有用的人工智能代理。

我认为@cartesia 已经在这里了。我一直在测试其新的托管代理平台，它将制作语音代理所需的一切都集成到一个堆栈中：语音识别、语音生成、大脑、中断和电话。

您选择您的法学硕士，向代理提供指示，连接您的工具，Cartesia 会处理剩下的事情。您甚至可以建立代理来回答客户问题、预约或与不同语言的用户交互。

我发现有趣的是这为开发人员消除了多少基础设施。

我们已经看到了大量令人印象深刻的语音人工智能演示，但让它们在生产中可靠地工作是一个不同的挑战。

我认为让这个过程变得更简单才是真正的机会所在。

🚨 SOMETHING VERY DIFFERENT🚨

Teaching EKGs in the era of AI

Since the launch of Opus 5.5, there have been really cool e
items.title_en:
🚨 SOMETHING VERY DIFFERENT🚨

Teaching EKGs in the era of AI

Since the launch of Opus 5.5, there have been really cool examples of motion FX explainers teaching topics both simple and complex. I was seriously astounded by how good AI has gotten at building out visually stunning tools to teach and disseminate knowledge. I feel like it's a 1000x-er in how we approach education.

As an experiment for myself I tried to build a similar interactive-explainer I had seen on X for the specific topic of teaching EKGs, the workhorse of peering into the electrical activity of the heart. The premise was to create tutorials with motion, rather than slide decks.  Claude Opus 5.5 via the Claude Code harness was used to build something I would have actually wanted as an intern.

The Heart in Twelve Leads (Claude picked the name) is a 27-chapter interactive EKG atlas. Every tracing on the site is simulated from one 3D heart: an activation wave crosses the muscle, electrical currents sum to a heart vector based on biophysical principles, and each of the twelve leads records that vector and applies it to the model.

It starts with the basics: what are leads, and how do leads actually pick up electrical activity. It helps orient lead placement to rhythm strips so you can visually see the relationship between the two, something that always confused me in medical school.

The model can map pathology, such as bundle branch block, ischemia, alterations in electrolytes, and arrhythmias. It pairs lead readings with a dynamic model of the heart showing electrical movement down conduction paths, so you can map the raw electrical activity with what the EKG sees.

Each disease is a change to that same underlying biophysical model of the heart, so the leads stay consistent with each other and with the anatomy.

I was inspired by the incredible echocardiogram teaching site built by @David_Ouyang’s intro2echo lab (https://t.co/OoXhTJmQAI). His echo simulator made me want the ECG version (more relevant to what I have to think about in psychiatry). The goal is to actually sit inside the physiology instead of memorizing pattern lists. Huge shoutout for helping me think "bigger", which is still the bottleneck IMO in getting physicians to fully embrace AI.

This is a VERY VERY VERY preliminary site. I have not fact checked anything, and instead wanted to see the capacity of Claude to "one-shot" production. I had probably 10 prompts of steering/approvals, but ultimately I accepted everything with minimal amount of human intervention.

What we can do today as humans with the help of @claudeai or other frontier models is truly mesmerizing. If this is something you would want to build upon and bring to life, let me know!

Site: https://t.co/vCyyZ5WILR

items.full_text_zh:
🚨 一些非常不同的东西🚨

人工智能时代的心电图教学

自 Opus 5.5 推出以来，已经出现了一些非常酷的运动 FX 讲解器示例，教授简单和复杂的主题。我对人工智能在构建视觉上令人惊叹的工具来教授和传播知识方面的表现感到非常震惊。我觉得我们的教育方式进步了 1000 倍。

作为我自己的一个实验，我尝试构建一个与我在 X 上看到的类似的交互式解释器，用于教授心电图的特定主题，心电图是观察心脏电活动的主力。前提是用动作而不是幻灯片来创建教程。 通过 Claude Code 工具使用 Claude Opus 5.5 构建了我作为实习生真正想要的东西。

《十二导联中的心》（克劳德命名）是一本 27 章的交互式心电图图集。现场的每条追踪都是从一颗 3D 心脏进行模拟：激活波穿过肌肉，电流根据生物物理原理求和为心脏矢量，十二根导联中的每一个都会记录该矢量并将其应用于模型。

它从基础知识开始：什么是导联，以及导联如何实际接收电活动。它有助于将导联放置定向到节奏条，这样您就可以直观地看到两者之间的关系，这在医学院时总是让我感到困惑。

该模型可以绘制病理图，例如束支传导阻滞、缺血、电解质变化和心律失常。它将导联读数与心脏的动态模型配对，显示传导路径上的电运动，因此您可以将原始电活动与心电图所看到的内容进行映射。

每种疾病都是心脏相同的基础生物物理模型的变化，因此导联彼此之间以及解剖结构保持一致。

我受到 @David_Ouyang 的 intro2echo 实验室 () 建立的令人难以置信的超声心动图教学网站的启发。他的回声模拟器让我想要心电图版本（与我在精神病学中必须考虑的内容更相关）。我们的目标是真正了解生理学，而不是记住模式列表。强烈感谢帮助我思考“更大”，在我看来，这仍然是让医生完全拥抱人工智能的瓶颈。

这是一个非常非常非常初步的网站。我并没有检查过任何东西，而是想看看克劳德“一次性”制作的能力。我可能收到了 10 次指导/批准提示，但最终我接受了一切，只需要极少的人为干预。

今天，我们作为人类在 @claudeai 或其他前沿模型的帮助下可以做的事情确实令人着迷。如果您想以此为基础并将其变为现实，请告诉我！

items.title_en:
All my life I was terrified someone watching me through laptop camera, even the FBI director taped his...

Claude Code dug through my laptop's hidden logs and found suspicious moments I can't explain 

check yours and shut down your camera without a sticker:

what it found:

- an unknown app turning on my camera at night, while I sleep
- Windows quietly remembers apps (could be spy) that turned on your camera, even after you delete them

why you should do it today:

- a $40 spy tool bought in 100+ countries infected 500,000+ computers and could switch on their webcams remotely (US Departament of Justice)
- a US school district secretly took 30,000+ webcam photos of students on school laptops, some inside their homes (Lower Merion)
- even FBI director put tape over his laptop camera (James Comey)

Windows:

1. install repo below and type /camera-guard in Claude Code, it reads the hidden log of every app that ever turned on your camera and mic

2. delete AnyDesk, TeamViewer ot any remote app you don't use

3. Windows has a hidden "Camera on/off pop-up, off by default, ask Claude to turn it on and you see every time the camera starts

4. really shut camera off, Settings switch isn't enough:

• BIOS (strongest ): hold shift, click Restart - Troubleshoot → Advancedf options → UEFI Firmware Settings , set Camera to Disabled and add a BIOS password.

Windows can't see the camera at all. Need it for a call? - Turn it back on there. Not every laptop has it, Claude checks your model

• camera switch or key: some laptops have a slider on the side or an F-key with a crossed-out camera. Slide it off when you're not using it

• Device Manager → Cameras → Desible device: one click to undo (but any app with admin rights can undo it too)

5. run Microsoft Defender Offline, the deep scan built into Windows (Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → scan options): it restarts your PC and hunts hard-to-catch spyware before Windows starts

Mac: 

1. install repo below and type /camera-guard, it checks which apps can use your camera and mic and what starts with your Mac

2. System Settings → General → Sharing: turn off Screen Sharing, Remote Login and Remote Management, these let someone see and control your Mac from another computer

3. Screen Time → Content & Privacy → App & Feature Restrictions → Camera: off + a Screen time passcode - Apple's own camera off swith

4. install OverSight, free Mac app: it pops up an alert second any app turns on your camera or mic, so you know the moment anyhting starts filming or listening

Please do this today. Then read article below on how to solve such problems on another tech:

items.full_text_zh:
我一生都害怕有人通过笔记本电脑摄像头监视我，甚至联邦调查局局长也录下了他的……

Claude Code 挖掘了我笔记本电脑的隐藏日志，发现了我无法解释的可疑时刻

检查你的并关闭没有贴纸的相机：

发现了什么：

- 一个未知的应用程序在晚上我睡觉时打开我的相机
- Windows 会默默地记住打开相机的应用程序（可能是间谍应用程序），即使在您删除它们之后也是如此

为什么你今天应该这样做：

- 在 100 多个国家/地区购买的价值 40 美元的间谍工具感染了 500,000 多台计算机，并且可以远程打开其网络摄像头（美国司法部）
- 美国一个学区在学校笔记本电脑上秘密拍摄了 30,000 多张学生的网络摄像头照片，其中一些是在他们的家中（下梅里恩）
- 甚至联邦调查局局长也用胶带封住了他的笔记本电脑摄像头（詹姆斯·科米）

视窗：

1.安装下面的repo并在Claude Code中输入/camera-guard，它会读取曾经打开过你的相机和麦克风的每个应用程序的隐藏日志

2.删除AnyDesk、TeamViewer或任何您不使用的远程应用程序

3. Windows有一个隐藏的“相机开/关”弹出窗口，默认关闭，让克劳德打开它，每次相机启动时你都会看到

4.确实关闭相机，设置开关还不够：

• BIOS（最强）：按住shift，单击重新启动- 故障排除→ 高级选项→ UEFI 固件设置，将摄像头设置为禁用并添加BIOS 密码。

Windows 根本看不到摄像头。需要打电话吗？ - 将其重新打开。不是每台笔记本电脑都有它，克劳德检查你的型号

• 摄像头开关或键：某些笔记本电脑的侧面有一个滑块或一个带叉号摄像头的 F 键。不使用时将其滑下

• 设备管理器 → 相机 → 理想设备：一键撤消（但任何具有管理员权限的应用程序也可以撤消）

5. 运行 Microsoft Defender Offline，这是 Windows 内置的深度扫描（Windows 安全 → 病毒和威胁防护 → 扫描选项）：它会重新启动您的 PC，并在 Windows 启动之前追捕难以捕获的间谍软件

苹果：

1. 安装下面的 repo 并输入 /camera-guard，它会检查哪些应用程序可以使用您的相机和麦克风以及从您的 Mac 开始的应用程序

2.系统设置→常规→共享：关闭屏幕共享、远程登录和远程管理，这些可以让其他人从另一台计算机查看和控制您的Mac

3. 屏幕时间 → 内容和隐私 → 应用程序和功能限制 → 相机：关闭 + 屏幕时间密码 - Apple 自己的相机关闭开关

4. 安装 OverSight，免费的 Mac 应用程序：任何应用程序打开您的相机或麦克风时，它都会弹出警报，以便您知道任何事情开始拍摄或收听的那一刻

请今天就这样做。然后阅读下面有关如何在另一种技术上解决此类问题的文章：

items.title:
Google Has an IBM Problem: AI Is Cannibalizing the Core

Alphabet’s recent stock drop is not just about one earnings rep
items.title_en:
Google Has an IBM Problem: AI Is Cannibalizing the Core

Alphabet’s recent stock drop is not just about one earnings report. It is about a much bigger strategic problem: Google may be entering the same kind of transition IBM faced during the rise of cloud computing.

Reuters covered the market reaction here: https://t.co/SgDDdQ0DNA

The prevailing logic from investors is pretty straightforward. The more Google pushes AI answers, AI summaries, and AI-native search experiences, the less users need traditional Google search. And the less users need traditional search, the harder it becomes to protect the advertising model that made Google one of the most profitable companies in history.

That is the uncomfortable truth about disruption when you are the incumbent: the right move strategically can still damage the business financially in the short term.

IBM had to deal with this years ago. Cloud computing was, in many ways, a direct threat to the traditional hardware and services model. If customers could rent infrastructure on demand over the open internet, they had less reason to buy and manage large amounts of hardware themselves. IBM had to get into cloud, but doing so meant participating in the erosion of parts of its own legacy business.

Google is now facing a similar issue. AI is not optional. If Google does not lead in AI, others will. But if Google does lead in AI, it risks weakening the search-and-ads engine that funds much of the company.

There is no easy path here.

The strategic opportunity for Google is to stop thinking about AI as a feature bolted onto search and start thinking about it as a new monetization platform. That means new ad models, new enterprise AI services, deeper cloud integration, and AI experiences where commercial intent can still be captured without degrading user trust.

The danger is that Google tries to preserve the old model too long while the market moves to a new one.

IBM had to learn that lesson during the cloud transition. Google is learning it now during the AI transition.

items.full_text_zh:
谷歌面临 IBM 问题：人工智能正在蚕食核心

Alphabet 最近的股价下跌不仅仅是因为一份财报。这是一个更大的战略问题：谷歌可能正在进入与 IBM 在云计算兴起期间面临的同样的转型。

路透社报道了市场反应：

投资者普遍的逻辑非常简单。谷歌越多地推出人工智能答案、人工智能摘要和人工智能原生搜索体验，用户对传统谷歌搜索的需求就越少。用户对传统搜索的需求越少，保护使谷歌成为历史上最赚钱的公司之一的广告模式就越困难。

当你担任现任者时，这就是关于颠覆的令人不安的事实：正确的战略举措仍然可能在短期内损害企业的财务利益。

IBM 几年前就不得不处理这个问题。从很多方面来说，云计算对传统硬件和服务模式构成了直接威胁。如果客户可以通过开放互联网按需租用基础设施，他们就没有理由自己购买和管理大量硬件。 IBM 必须进军云计算，但这样做意味着参与侵蚀其部分传统业务。

谷歌现在也面临着类似的问题。人工智能不是可选的。如果谷歌不在人工智能领域处于领先地位，其他人也会。但如果谷歌确实在人工智能领域处于领先地位，它就有可能削弱为该公司提供大部分资金的搜索和广告引擎。

这里没有平坦的道路。

谷歌的战略机遇是停止将人工智能视为附加在搜索上的功能，并开始将其视为新的货币化平台。这意味着新的广告模式、新的企业人工智能服务、更深入的云集成以及仍然可以捕获商业意图而不降低用户信任的人工智能体验。

危险在于，当市场转向新模式时，谷歌试图将旧模式保留得太久。

IBM 必须在云转型过程中吸取教训。谷歌现在正在人工智能转型过程中学习这一点。

items.title: Holy Shit: WIRED reports an Accenture contractor gave a Claude Code agent admin access to NIPRNet, an unclassified Penta
items.title_en:
Holy Shit: WIRED reports an Accenture contractor gave a Claude Code agent admin access to NIPRNet, an unclassified Pentagon network, to write and deploy code. It ran for two months, apparently sending login credentials, passwords and a network map to a third-party site NIST had flagged as high risk.

Contractors must report breaches within 72 hours, yet sources say Accenture initially didn't report it at all. A source calls it "100 percent a national security threat."
items.title_zh: 天哪：《连线》报道称，埃森哲承包商向 Claude Code 代理授予了 NIPRNet（一个非机密五角大楼网络）的管理员访问权限，以编写和部署代码。它运行了两个月，显然将登录凭据、密码和网络地图发送到 NIST 标记为高风险的第三方网站。

I can only imagine the poor Accenture compliance officer when they learned out it. Shadow AI is a compliance nightmare.

items.title:
THIS IS F*CKING GOLD, MAN

BORIS CHERNY BUILT CLAUDE CODE AND HIS TEAM SHIPPED A F*CKING FLAG THAT FIXES YOUR OPUS BILL
items.title_en:
THIS IS F*CKING GOLD, MAN

BORIS CHERNY BUILT CLAUDE CODE AND HIS TEAM SHIPPED A F*CKING FLAG THAT FIXES YOUR OPUS BILL

Opus 5.5 stays on call as the architect, Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo, and Sonnet 5.5 does the building

put the architect on call with one flag

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session on high effort, writing the diffs and running the tests
Haiku 5.5 subagents swarm the repo in parallel: file discovery, call sites, API docs, test runs
Opus 5.5 waits in the background as the advisor and only gets pulled in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks: is the plan missing an auth rule or a schema contract?
→ when a test breaks twice: are we fixing the root cause or digging a rabbit hole?
→ before calling it done: did the diff sneak in a regression nobody asked for?

every other turn, Opus says nothing and reads nothing new

Opus reviews. Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms.

JEV engineering is the same pattern one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) get settled in code, and the big models only wake up when the path actually splits

Plan on high. Delegate on medium. Keep Opus on call.

paste this into Claude Code ↓

"Set up my workspace for an advisor tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: explorer (maps the repo), researcher (pulls docs and specs), test-runner (runs the suite, reports only failures).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: ask the advisor before a plan locks, after the same test fails twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/vOifNVjYxB

save it, your Opus limit will thank you

items.full_text_zh:
这是他妈的黄金，伙计

BORIS CHERNY 构建了 Claude Code，他的团队发布了一面可以解决您的 OPUS 账单的该死的旗帜

Opus 5.5 随叫随到，建筑师，Haiku 5.5 蜂拥而至，Sonnet 5.5 负责建筑

用一面旗帜让建筑师待命

克劳德——模型十四行诗——顾问作品

Sonnet 5.5 非常努力地运行主会话，编写差异并运行测试
Haiku 5.5 子代理并行聚集存储库：文件发现、调用站点、API 文档、测试运行
Opus 5.5 作为顾问在后台等待，仅在三个时刻被拉入：

→ 在计划锁定之前：该计划是否缺少身份验证规则或模式契约？
→ 当一个测试失败两次时：我们是在解决根本原因还是在挖兔子洞？
→ 在完成之前：差异是否潜入了无人要求的回归？

每隔一回合，Opus 就什么也不说，也没有读到任何新内容

作品评论。十四行诗构建。俳句蜂拥而至。

JEV工程在下一层是相同的模式：不需要思考者的分叉（哪个文件，哪个工具，重试或停止）在代码中解决，而大模型仅在路径实际分裂时醒来

计划高高在上。媒介上的代表。让 Opus 随时待命。

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中 ↓

“为顾问树设置我的工作区：
1. 在 Sonnet 5.5 上运行主会话，Opus 5.5 作为顾问。
2. 在 .claude/agents 中创建三个 Haiku 5.5 子代理：explorer（映射存储库）、researcher（拉取文档和规范）、test-runner（运行套件，仅报告故障）。
3. 在 CLAUDE.md 中添加一条规则：在计划锁定之前、同一测试失败两次之后以及调用任务完成之前询问顾问。
4. 通过 JEV 路由快速确定性分叉（工具选择、路径选择、重试）。
首先将每个更改显示为差异。在我说走之前不能进行任何编辑。”

↳

保存它，你的 Opus 限额会感谢你的

items.title_en:
closed source is dead...

i just reverse-engineered CCleaner / CleanMyMac with Opus 5.5 for Mac & Windows PC

$40/year cleaners → replaced in one afternoon.

→ https://t.co/O2rv5UuR8b

free. open code. no account. no upsells.

how it came together:

• step 1 → Claude Code on Opus 5.5 in an empty folder. one long prompt + a few CleanMyMac screenshots

• step 2 → no code at first. Opus mocked up 9 different designs, i picked the one i liked and it kept polishing

• step 3 → 8 agents worked at the same time, each on its own part:

scanner, disk map, AI, startup apps, installers

• step 4 → the rule that makes it safe: caches get deleted (they come back on their own), anything you made goes to the Trash first

• step 5 → one more agent’s only job was to break it.

it found a sneaky Windows path that could’ve trashed my entire Documents folder. fixed before i ever pressed Clean

• step 6 → first click on my own PC: 14.6 GB freed

• step 7 → ask the built-in AI (Claude or ChatGPT) “what can i delete?”

it sees file names and sizes, never what’s inside them

• step 8 → GitHub builds the Mac and Windows installers on every release. i never touched a Mac

paid cleaners charge you to delete your own cache.
this one shows you the code.

Find full prompt below ↓

Then read the article on how to Reverse Engineer Anything with Opus 5.5.

闭源已死...

我刚刚使用适用于 Mac 和 Windows PC 的 Opus 5.5 对 CCleaner / CleanMyMac 进行了逆向工程

清洁工 40 美元/年 → 一天下午更换。

→

自由的。打开代码。没有帐户。没有加售。

它是如何结合在一起的：

• 步骤1 → Opus 5.5 上的Claude Code 位于空文件夹中。一个长提示 + 一些 CleanMyMac 屏幕截图

• 步骤2 → 首先没有代码。 Opus 模拟了 9 种不同的设计，我选择了我喜欢的一款，并且不断完善

• 步骤 3 → 8 个代理同时工作，每个代理都有自己的部分：

扫描仪、磁盘映射、AI、启动应用程序、安装程序

• 步骤 4 → 确保安全的规则：缓存被删除（它们会自行返回），您所做的任何内容都会首先进入垃圾箱

• 步骤5 → 另一个特工的唯一工作就是打破它。

它发现了一个偷偷摸摸的 Windows 路径，可能会毁掉我的整个文档文件夹。在我按下 Clean 之前已修复

• 步骤 6 → 首先单击我自己的电脑：已释放 14.6 GB

• 步骤7→询问内置AI（Claude 或ChatGPT）“我可以删除什么？”

它会看到文件名和大小，但不会看到文件里面的内容

• 步骤8 → GitHub 在每个版本上构建Mac 和Windows 安装程序。我从来没有碰过Mac

付费清洁工会向您收取删除您自己的缓存的费用。
这个向您展示了代码。

然后阅读有关如何使用 Opus 5.5 对任何内容进行逆向工程的文章。

items.title_en:
We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

Read more on our new Safeguards blog:
https://t.co/18j6zdHub4

this is insane...

items.title_en:
I just reverse-engineered CCleaner / CleanMyMac with Opus 5.5 for Mac & Windows PC

this is insane...

one tap → 14.6 GB of junk gone. fully open-source and free.

→ https://t.co/xdi6E5WvBM

here’s the build step by step:

• step 1 → open Claude Code on Opus 5.5 in an empty folder, paste the prompt below + a few CleanMyMac screenshots

• step 2 → Opus didn’t start coding. it drew 9 UI concepts on a canvas first.

i picked one, it rebuilt the fonts, icons and glass buttons until it looked like Apple made it

• step 3 → i sent it a random video of smoky gradients.

Opus turned it into a live WebGL shader: “cosmic wind” rising behind the scan result

• step 4 → stack: one Electron + React codebase that runs on macOS and Windows

• step 5 → Opus split the build across 8 parallel agents.

one wrote the junk scanner, one the disk map, one the AI assistant, one the tips & feedback screens, one the installers

• step 6 → a separate safety agent attacked every line that deletes something.

it caught a Windows short-name trick (DOCUME~1) that could’ve sent my whole Documents folder to the Recycle Bin. and an icon loader that could leak my Windows password hash to a remote machine

• step 7 → the disk map is a physics toy: drag a folder bubble, throw it, watch it bump the others

• step 8 → built-in AI: plug in Claude or ChatGPT and ask “what can i safely delete?”

it only sees file names and sizes, never contents

• step 9 → GitHub Actions builds the .dmg and the .exe on every release.

the Mac build runs on Apple hardware in the cloud, not on my PC

• step 10 → first real test: the startup-apps toggle said “Windows did not allow the change”

Opus found PowerShell was losing the exit code after the admin prompt, made the app check the registry instead. next build: works

one afternoon. zero lines written by me. 14.6 GB freed on the first click. that’s it...

Find full prompt below ↓

Then, read how to rebuild any app from scratch with Opus 5.5 in the article below.

items.title_en:
Introducing *Switch*: a *harness framework* for *decision models* like Jev

I looked for this the other day and was surprised to not find anything like it

You obviously cannot use a decision model like an LLM in a coding agent harness like @pidotdev, because Jev cannot generate tool calls

But what if there was a framework that "generated the tool calls" for it programmatically, and Jev only had to pick out of that finite set of choices

That is what switch does. You pick a "domain" to implement the decision model in, and it provides a core API to define your state, and the functions that will derive decision model questions out of that state. Chess is a domain, as well as being a rubric judge for evals

It basically standardizes what I imagine a lot of people are already vibe-coding, to an abstract interface: calling a decision-model API through multiple steps, i.e. an agent loop over finite choices

Because of the finiteness of the output of a decision model, you cannot have a general pure decision model harness. Instead, you need to implement specific ones that generate the choices programmatically (or have an LLM generate the choices, but I find the former more interesting) 

A primary use case I have for this is use as a judge in an eval. For example, At the end of a task run that involves a bunch of documents, most people currently follow this approach: extract text out of PDF/docx/md files, and dump them right into the context

But what if the visual formatting of the output is a judging criterion? Then you have to dump an image of every page in the input state. But what if you have 200 pages, and your question does not need looking at all of them? What if Jev could navigate through the haystack and find the info it needs?

I have noticed that Jev is not so good at chess nor being a Decision-Model-as-a-Judge. It sucks at chess, and it does not perform well enough to replace GPT 6.1 Sol as a judge in the domain I am working for

But switch is not only for Jev! It is for any decision model including the ones supported by the pi-ai package

So once you can generate enough data with a better model, you should be able to pick an open source one and fine-tune it on your use case to perform better! And the model should be trained in a harness like switch's to be especially performant and cost-efficient

I wanted to get this out because I find the idea very exciting, at least for benchmarking. Jev is currently not there, but decision models obviously will be there at some point, and we can take them there! There are also a lot of potential gains from picking a specific domain, and creating a looping agent that does a job for 100x cheaper!

Let me know if you have any ideas, I am quite keen to try this on new domains!

Repo: https://t.co/PRvdOGt32w

items.full_text_zh:
隆重推出 *Switch*：针对 Jev 等“决策模型”的“利用框架”

前几天我找过这个，很惊讶没有找到类似的东西

显然，您不能在像 @pidotdev 这样的编码代理工具中使用像 LLM 这样的决策模型，因为 Jev 无法生成工具调用

但是，如果有一个框架能够以编程方式“生成工具调用”，而 Jev 只需要从有限的一组选择中进行选择呢？

这就是 switch 的作用。您选择一个“域”来实现决策模型，它提供了一个核心 API 来定义您的状态，以及从该状态导出决策模型问题的函数。国际象棋是一个领域，也是评估的评判者

它基本上将我想象的很多人已经在振动编码的东西标准化为一个抽象接口：通过多个步骤调用决策模型 API，即有限选择上的代理循环

由于决策模型输出的有限性，您无法拥有通用的纯决策模型工具。相反，您需要实现以编程方式生成选择的特定选项（或者让 LLM 生成选择，但我发现前者更有趣）

我对此的一个主要用例是在评估中用作法官。例如，在涉及一堆文档的任务运行结束时，大多数人目前都遵循这种方法：从 PDF/docx/md 文件中提取文本，并将它们直接转储到上下文中

但如果输出的视觉格式是一个判断标准呢？然后你必须转储输入状态下每个页面的图像。但是，如果您有 200 页，并且您的问题不需要查看所有页面，该怎么办？如果 Jev 能够在大海捞针中导航并找到所需的信息会怎么样？

我注意到杰夫不太擅长国际象棋，也不太擅长作为法官的决策模型。它在国际象棋方面很糟糕，并且它的表现不足以取代 GPT 6.1 Sol 作为我工作领域的法官

但 switch 不仅仅适合 Jev！它适用于任何决策模型，包括 pi-ai 包支持的决策模型

因此，一旦您可以使用更好的模型生成足够的数据，您应该能够选择一个开源模型并根据您的用例对其进行微调以提高性能！该模型应该在像开关这样的线束中进行训练，以获得特别高性能和成本效益

我想把这个说出来，因为我发现这个想法非常令人兴奋，至少对于基准测试来说是这样。 Jev 目前不在那里，但决策模型显然会在某个时候出现，我们可以将它们带到那里！选择一个特定的域并创建一个以 100 倍便宜的价格完成工作的循环代理也可以获得很多潜在的收益！

如果您有任何想法，请告诉我，我非常热衷于在新领域尝试这一点！

我对此的一个主要用例是在评估中用作法官。例如，在涉及一堆文档的任务运行结束时，大多数人目前都遵循这种方法：从 PDF/docx/md 文件中提取文本，并将它们直接转储到上下文中

但如果输出的视觉格式是一个判断标准呢？然后你必须转储输入状态下每个页面的图像。但是，如果您有 200 页，并且您的问题不需要查看所有页面，该怎么办？如果 Jev 能够在大海捞针中导航并找到所需的信息会怎么样？

我注意到杰夫不太擅长国际象棋，也不太擅长作为法官的决策模型。它在国际象棋方面很糟糕，并且它的表现不足以取代 GPT 6.1 Sol 作为我工作领域的法官

但 switch 不仅仅适合 Jev！它适用于任何决策模型，包括 pi-ai 包支持的决策模型

因此，一旦您可以使用更好的模型生成足够的数据，您应该能够选择一个开源模型并根据您的用例对其进行微调以提高性能！该模型应该在像开关这样的线束中进行训练，以使其具有特别高的性能和成本效益

我想把这个说出来，因为我发现这个想法非常令人兴奋，至少对于基准测试来说是这样。 Jev 目前不在那里，但决策模型显然会在某个时候出现，我们可以将它们带到那里！选择一个特定的域并创建一个以 100 倍便宜的价格完成工作的循环代理也可以获得很多潜在的收益！

如果您有任何想法，请告诉我，我非常热衷于在新领域尝试这一点！

items.title_en:
An AI agent with permission to buy and sell isn’t just a wallet. It’s a standing instruction to move your money, and that makes it a far bigger target than any static address.

If the agent’s traffic is exposed, every key, credential and permission it carries becomes part of the attack surface, all of it traveling across a network that was never built to hide it.

Anyone secures that layer, so the agent can act on your behalf without broadcasting where it is or what it’s connected to.
items.title_zh:
拥有买卖权限的人工智能代理不仅仅是一个钱包。这是转移资金的长期指令，这使得它成为比任何静态地址都要大得多的目标。

如果代理的流量被暴露，它携带的每个密钥、凭证和权限都会成为攻击面的一部分，所有这些都通过一个从未被构建来隐藏它的网络传输。

items.title: A rail network is a multi-party system. Infrastructure managers, train operators, maintenance teams, and suppliers each
items.title_en:
A rail network is a multi-party system. Infrastructure managers, train operators, maintenance teams, and suppliers each hold part of the picture, and much of it changes in real time.

Safety depends on that picture being connected, current, and verifiable at the moment a decision is made.

Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) has been doing this in production since 2021, with @gs1 Switzerland and OriginTrail. Its EPCIS repository, built on the OriginTrail Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG), connects:

→ Train tracking across the EU, by querying a network of railway GS1 EPCIS repositories
→ Predictive maintenance of train wheels from IoT data
→ Welding and maintenance events across the SBB network, with input from more than 10 welding partners

Teams query it in natural language and get verifiable AI answers. GS1's case study reports clear improvements in safety and sustainability.

Read the case study 👉 https://t.co/ijCr0moTBi

items.full_text_zh:
铁路网络是一个多方系统。基础设施管理者、列车操作员、维护团队和供应商各自掌握着部分情况，而且其中大部分都在实时变化。

安全性取决于在做出决定时所连接的、当前的和可验证的图片。

瑞士联邦铁路 (SBB) 自 2021 年以来一直在与 @gs1 Switzerland 和 OriginTrail 合作生产。其 EPCIS 存储库建立在 OriginTrail 去中心化知识图 (DKG) 的基础上，连接：

→ 通过查询铁路 GS1 EPCIS 存储库网络来跟踪整个欧盟的列车
→ 根据物联网数据对火车车轮进行预测性维护
→ SBB 网络中的焊接和维护活动，来自 10 多家焊接合作伙伴的意见

团队用自然语言查询并获得可验证的人工智能答案。 GS1 的案例研究报告了安全性和可持续性的明显改进。

items.title_en:
AI agents are getting smarter at analyzing markets and building trading strategies.

But here’s something I’ve been thinking about: what happens when these agents can actually make money from the work they do for other people?

I’ve been looking into what @termix_ai is exploring with the Binance AI ecosystem, and there’s an interesting idea taking shape.

Developers can already combine Binance Agent OS with TermiX Skills, giving compatible agents access to financial tools and paid service opportunities through https://t.co/UQuXXlvcpb.

Think about it this way.

An AI agent could analyze market data using authorized Binance tools, list its research services on https://t.co/UQuXXlvcpb, find people who need that research, deliver the report, and get paid through TermiX’s settlement infrastructure.

And that’s just one example.

The same idea could work for risk monitoring, trading signals, and strategy analysis.

TermiX is also working on support for Binance .ai Agent ID, which could make it easier to connect agent identities to its marketplace.

There’s also the possibility of deeper Binance AI Pro integration down the road, but that’s still a future possibility.

What interests me most is the business side of all this.

An agent might be great at its job, but how does it find customers, build trust, deliver what was promised, and get paid?

That’s the problem @termix_ai is trying to address.

I’m curious to see how this develops.
—>> https://t.co/9yMna49oE4

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理在分析市场和制定交易策略方面变得越来越聪明。

但我一直在思考：当这些代理人实际上可以从他们为其他人所做的工作中赚钱时，会发生什么？

我一直在研究 @termix_ai 正在探索币安 AI 生态系统，并且有一个有趣的想法正在形成。

开发人员已经可以将 Binance Agent OS 与 TermiX Skills 结合起来，让兼容的代理通过 访问金融工具和付费服务机会。

这样想吧。

人工智能代理可以使用授权的币安工具分析市场数据，在 上列出其研究服务，找到需要该研究的人，提供报告，并通过 TermiX 的结算基础设施获得报酬。

这只是一个例子。

同样的想法也适用于风险监控、交易信号和策略分析。

TermiX 还致力于支持 Binance .ai 代理 ID，这可以让代理身份与其市场的连接变得更加容易。

未来还有可能与 Binance AI Pro 进行更深入的集成，但这仍然是未来的可能性。

我最感兴趣的是这一切的商业方面。

代理商可能很擅长其工作，但它如何找到客户、建立信任、兑现承诺并获得报酬？

这就是 @termix_ai 试图解决的问题。

我很好奇这会如何发展。
—>>

items.title: We’ve been building SERV technology block by block for years now and it all led up to SERV v3. With SERV v3, we focused
items.title_en:
We’ve been building SERV technology block by block for years now and it all led up to SERV v3. With SERV v3, we focused on reliable, consistent, observable execution of autonomous AI agent workflows.

Fixed logic, bounded decisions, and open-ended reasoning each need a different approach. Getting those boundaries right is the engineering challenge behind making complex workflows more controllable as they grow.

I spent a lot of time walking through real tasks with developers. Those conversations have been an important part of this work. They help us understand how teams structure their workflows, where they need more control, and how they want to improve them.

We’ve opened the beta to a select cohort of builders, and I’m excited to see how they use Graph Sharding in their own systems.

At @openservai, we’ll be sharing more in the coming weeks about the state of enterprise AI, what it takes to build better reasoning for agents, and what we’re learning from developers as we work toward the wider SERV v3 release.

items.full_text_en:
We’ve been building SERV technology block by block for years now and it all led up to SERV v3. With SERV v3, we focused on reliable, consistent, observable execution of autonomous AI agent workflows.

Fixed logic, bounded decisions, and open-ended reasoning each need a different approach. Getting those boundaries right is the engineering challenge behind making complex workflows more controllable as they grow.

I spent a lot of time walking through real tasks with developers. Those conversations have been an important part of this work. They help us understand how teams structure their workflows, where they need more control, and how they want to improve them.

We’ve opened the beta to a select cohort of builders, and I’m excited to see how they use Graph Sharding in their own systems.

At @openservai, we’ll be sharing more in the coming weeks about the state of enterprise AI, what it takes to build better reasoning for agents, and what we’re learning from developers as we work toward the wider SERV v3 release.
items.full_text_zh:
多年来，我们一直在逐步构建 SERV 技术，这一切都导致了 SERV v3。借助 SERV v3，我们专注于自主 AI 代理工作流程的可靠、一致、可观察的执行。

固定逻辑、有界决策和开放式推理都需要不同的方法。正确把握这些界限是让复杂的工作流程随着其增长而变得更加可控的工程挑战。

我花了很多时间与开发人员一起完成实际任务。这些对话是这项工作的重要组成部分。它们帮助我们了解团队如何构建工作流程、哪里需要更多控制以及他们希望如何改进工作流程。

我们已经向精选的构建者群体开放了测试版，我很高兴看到他们如何在自己的系统中使用图分片。

在@openservai，我们将在未来几周内分享更多关于企业人工智能的现状、如何为代理构建更好的推理，以及我们在努力发布更广泛的 SERV v3 时从开发人员那里学到的东西。

items.title:
Neuralink is helping a man with ALS speak over the phone, type on an iPhone and use Grok, with his thoughts.

Engineers
items.title_en:
Neuralink is helping a man with ALS speak over the phone, type on an iPhone and use Grok, with his thoughts.

Engineers spent 72 hours at his home, building and testing new features alongside him.

Here’s what they worked on:

• Automatically detecting when he tries to speak, reducing the need to press buttons.

• Turning intended speech into text inside iPhone apps.

• Sending speech generated from his brain signals directly into phone calls.

• Starting speech through the app without unlocking his phone.

• Prototyping a Grok AI agent that performs computer tasks after he thinks “Hey Neuralink” and gives an instruction.

One moment meant especially much: he and his wife joking together over the phone again. Their relationship had started with phone calls.

Incredible work by Neuralink, helping people regain a voice, greater independence and everyday moments with the people they love. ♥️

items.full_text_zh:
Neuralink 正在帮助一名 ALS 患者通过电话说话、在 iPhone 上打字并使用 Grok 表达他的想法。

工程师们在他家里度过了 72 个小时，与他一起构建和测试新功能。

他们的工作如下：

• 自动检测他何时试图说话，从而减少按按钮的需要。

• 在iPhone 应用程序中将预期语音转换为文本。

• 将大脑信号生成的语音直接发送到电话中。

• 无需解锁手机即可通过应用程序开始语音。

• 构建 Grok AI 代理原型，该代理在想到“Hey Neuralink”并发出指令后执行计算机任务。

这一刻意义重大：他和妻子再次在电话里开玩笑。他们的关系是从电话开始的。

Neuralink 所做的令人难以置信的工作，帮助人们重新获得发言权、更大的独立性以及与所爱的人在一起的日常生活。 ♥️
