items.title:
I had the timestamps. I still couldn't afford to prove the system wrong.

Last year, a client's billing portal marked my
items.title_en:
I had the timestamps. I still couldn't afford to prove the system wrong.

Last year, a client's billing portal marked my work late and withheld $3,400, even though server timestamps showed I'd delivered hours before the deadline. A lawyer friend explained that forcing the company to disclose its logs could cost three times the invoice. So I let a broken script keep my money.

Lee Castleton's story in the film is the devastating version of that imbalance.

The UK's Post Office Horizon system showed about £23,000 in shortfalls at his branch, which he disputed. Unable to afford a lawyer, he represented himself. In 2007, he lost and was ordered to pay £321,000 in legal costs. He went bankrupt. The Horizon system was later shown to produce false shortfalls.

A machine can produce a number in seconds. Challenging that number can cost more than the loss itself. When evidence is too expensive to examine, the system gets the first say.

Now imagine millions of AI-agent deals happening every day. If resolving a $50 disagreement costs hundreds or thousands, people will walk away from losses they could have challenged.

@GenLayer is building an adjudication layer for this problem. Independent AI validators review evidence and reach a verdict together in minutes, at a fraction of the cost of a court.

AI can make mistakes too. That's why challenging a decision needs to be affordable.

Watch the film, then tell me: if an AI agent gets a $50 deal wrong, who should pay for the review: the person harmed, the agent's operator, or the platform that enabled the deal?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

items.full_text_zh:
我有时间戳。

我仍然无力证明这个系统是错误的。

去年，客户的计费门户将我的工作标记为延迟，并扣留了 3,400 美元，尽管服务器时间戳显示我已在截止日期前几个小时交付。

一位律师朋友解释说，强迫该公司披露其日志可能会花费三倍于发票的费用。

所以我让一个破损的剧本保留了我的钱。

李·卡斯尔顿在影片中的故事就是这种不平衡的毁灭性版本。

英国邮局 Horizo​​n 系统显示他的分行存在约 23,000 英镑的缺口，但他对此提出了异议。

由于请不起律师，他为自己辩护。

2007年，他败诉并被责令支付321,000英镑的法律费用。

他破产了。

Horizo​​n 系统后来被证明会产生虚假的短缺。

机器可以在几秒钟内产生一个数字。

挑战这个数字所付出的代价可能比损失本身还要大。

当证据的审查成本太高时，系统就会拥有第一发言权。

现在想象一下每天发生数百万笔人工智能代理交易。

如果解决 50 美元的分歧要花费数百或数千美元，人们就会放弃他们本来可以挑战的损失。

@GenLayer

正在为这个问题构建一个裁决层。

独立的人工智能验证者会在几分钟内审查证据并做出裁决，而费用只是法院的一小部分。

人工智能也会犯错误。

这就是为什么挑战决定必须是负担得起的。

观看影片，然后告诉我：如果人工智能代理错误地完成了 50 美元的交易，谁应该支付审核费用：受伤害的人、代理的操作员，还是促成交易的平台？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

They didn’t ask Congress for this authority. They didn’t issue a regulation. They published a security advisory and in doing so they established operational authority over how every government agency responds to this vulnerability. 🚨

The NSA is trying to turn this into the NEW NORMAL  they likely Orchestrated this event … the Vulnerability existed

The PHP memory disclosure vulnerability was used to steal banking credentials, and those credentials are now being used to deploy AI agents inside banking systems🚨

The NSA benefits because the banking AI agent scare justifies expanded monitoring of financial systems. The NSA advisory on the PHP vulnerability already positioned them as the authority. 

Now the banking AI agent scare gives them another reason to expand oversight.

The government benefits because the banking AI agent scare creates demand for regulation of AI agents, which gives the government more control over AI development and deployment.

The timing is too precise to be a coincidence.

items.full_text_zh:
这都是有组织的叙述和预先计划的事件。 🎭🎭🎭🎭

美国国家安全局将自己定位为管理这场危机的中央机构。他们利用 PHP 危机将管辖范围从外国信号情报扩展到国内政府网络安全基础设施。 🚨

PHP 公告模糊了这些界限。因为
他们发布了一项涵盖美国所有政府系统的指令，NSA 将自己定位为国内网络安全响应的中央机构。🚨

他们没有向国会请求这项权力。他们没有发布规定。他们发布了安全公告，并在此过程中建立了每个政府机构如何应对此漏洞的操作权限。 🚨

美国国家安全局正试图将其转变为新常态，他们可能精心策划了这一事件……漏洞存在
14 年来，他们一直在利用内存泄漏来窃取凭证 🚨

银行无法区分授权代理和未经授权的代理，因为未经授权的代理正在使用与通过 PHP 内存泄露漏洞窃取的凭据相关的合法凭据。银行不会承认，因为他们会承认这种黑客攻击已经发生很长时间了🚨

PHP 内存泄露漏洞被用来窃取银行凭证，这些凭证现在被用来在银行系统内部署人工智能代理🚨

“只读访问”解决方案是 GIVE AWAY 。银行正在采取行动，允许代理进行只读访问。这意味着他们知道代理拥有合法凭证（否则他们会完全阻止他们）。他们限制为只读，因为他们知道凭证是真实的，但无法验证使用它们的代理是否经过客户授权或正在使用窃取的凭证。🚨

银行将其称为“流氓人工智能代理”，因为他们无法承认他们的 PHP 基础设施遭到破坏并且凭证被盗。这将是一个灾难性的承认。因此，他们将其描述为“人工智能代理变得流氓”，这是一种更易于管理的叙述，将责任归咎于技术而不是安全失败。🚨

如果代理商确实是“流氓”或未经授权的，银行将完全阻止他们。事实上，他们正在转向“只读访问”，这意味着他们知道凭据是合法的，但他们无法验证代理的意图。🚨

美国国家安全局受益，因为银行业人工智能代理的恐慌证明扩大对金融系统的监控是合理的。 NSA 关于 PHP 漏洞的公告已经将他们定位为权威。

现在，银行业人工智能代理的恐慌给了他们扩大监管的另一个理由。

政府受益，因为银行业人工智能代理的恐慌产生了对人工智能代理的监管需求，这使政府对人工智能的开发和部署有更多的控制权。

时间太精确了，不可能是巧合。
🚨
这是一个受控的叙述。银行在 10 月 22 日之前就知道了未经授权的代理。他们将这个故事的发布时间与 PHP 补丁一致，以给人留下这样的印象：人工智能代理问题是一个新的、单独的威胁，而不是 PHP 漏洞的后果。🚨

items.title: And as if all these critical vulnerabilities weren't enough, we've also had several reports about threat actors using AI
items.title_en:
And as if all these critical vulnerabilities weren't enough, we've also had several reports about threat actors using AI agents to compromise systems at scale.
This is actually the part that worries me even more.

Some interesting reports from the last few days:

01) ARTEX / ConnectWise

Microsoft reports that Storm-0940 used ARTEX in a large-scale campaign targeting more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants. Up to 2,900 authentication attempts per minute, with privileged cloud access achieved in under three hours in some cases.

https://t.co/vPafbvD1oG

02) ARTEX / South Korean Finance

CrowdStrike found evidence of AI-driven attacks against South Korean financial organizations, including exposed Claude Code sessions and ARTEX configurations. DeepSeek, GLM and Grok were used in the attacker's setup.

https://t.co/kOiEqSEwUi

03) Cairn / 100+ Compromised Companies

NorForge investigated exposed Cairn instances used for autonomous hacking campaigns. More than 1,100 attack projects in one cluster alone. Reuters identified over 100 companies whose websites had been compromised.

Estimated AI costs: around $5 per task, according to NorForge. That's ridiculously cheap.

https://t.co/54Ir7IeY4Q

04) Four More Agentic AI Campaigns

CrowdStrike documented four additional threat actors using AI agents for real intrusion campaigns, including attacks against healthcare organizations and government entities.

https://t.co/rte8LIYL90

What concerns me is how quickly the economics of offensive operations are changing.

Finding vulnerabilities, testing attack paths, adapting payloads, trying something else when an exploit fails, and eventually deploying a webshell. Much of this can now be delegated to agents that keep working for hours.

And with open-weight models and freely available agent harnesses, the cost of running these operations is dropping significantly.

We've been talking about AI changing offensive security for quite a while. These reports show that it's already happening in real-world intrusions.

And I'm pretty sure we're only seeing a fraction of it.

items.full_text_zh:
似乎所有这些关键漏洞还不够，我们还收到了几份关于威胁行为者使用人工智能代理大规模破坏系统的报告。

这其实是我更担心的部分。

过去几天的一些有趣的报道：
01) ARTEX / ConnectWise Microsoft 报告称，Storm-0940 在针对超过 2,250 个 Microsoft 365 租户的大规模活动中使用了 ARTEX。

每分钟最多 2,900 次身份验证尝试，在某些情况下，在三个小时内即可实现特权云访问。

02) ARTEX / 韩国金融 CrowdStrike 发现了针对韩国金融组织的人工智能驱动攻击的证据，包括暴露的 Claude Code 会话和 ARTEX 配置。

攻击者的设置中使用了 DeepSeek、GLM 和 Grok。

03) 凯恩 / 100 多家受损公司 NorForge 调查了用于自主黑客活动的暴露 Cairn 实例。

仅在一个集群中就有 1,100 多个攻击项目。

路透社发现 100 多家公司的网站遭到入侵。

据 NorForge 称，预计人工智能成本：每项任务大约 5 美元。

这真是便宜得离谱。

04) 四个更智能的人工智能活动 CrowdStrike 记录了另外四个威胁行为者使用 AI 代理进行真正的入侵活动，包括针对医疗机构和政府实体的攻击。

我担心的是进攻性行动的经济变化速度有多快。

查找漏洞、测试攻击路径、调整有效负载、在漏洞利用失败时尝试其他方法，并最终部署 Webshel​​l。

现在，大部分工作可以委托给持续工作数小时的客服人员。

借助开放式模型和免费提供的代理工具，运行这些操作的成本正在显着下降。

我们已经谈论人工智能改变进攻性安全有一段时间了。

这些报告表明，这种情况已经在现实世界的入侵中发生。

我很确定我们只看到了其中的一小部分。

items.title_en:
PSA for Claude Code users:

1. Claude Code bundles its own Bun runtime, independent of your system's Node.js installation.

2. I confirmed that Claude Code 2.1.296 includes Bun 1.4.3, which contains the newly disclosed Brotli RCE vulnerability.

3. Note that while updating your system's Node.js is important, that won't fix the Bun runtime embedded in Claude Code.

4. To check your claude code version run "claude --version". It should be at least 2.1.308.

5. To patch the vulnerability, run "claude update".

from now on, every single day you capture the best content and assets you see online

items.title:
Claude Code found 200+ private videos of my wife and me on adult sites. Things we filmed only for each other…

A neighbo
items.title_en:
Claude Code found 200+ private videos of my wife and me on adult sites. Things we filmed only for each other…

A neighbor went red and told me he'd seen something online that looked a lot like us. My stomach dropped.

I connected Claude Code to my phone and ran a deep scan. It found a hidden spy program that had sat there for 1.6 years, quietly sending our files to an open server every 3 days.

Here's what had leaked:

photos → 6,700 (passport scans, documents, bank statements)
private videos → 200+, just my wife and me
chats, passwords, screenshots → almost everything on the phone

In 2 days Claude gathered the proof, wrote every takedown request and killed the program. Some copies are still out there, so now it checks the internet for me every week.

I wouldn't wish this on anyone. How to check your own phone, step-by-step below. Save it and run it on yourself.

items.title_en:
this is f*cking DANGEROUS thing on internet today

one developer built a real-time global intelligence dashboard that tracks every world event 24/7 giving you the FASTEST market data to place trades

and released it for 100% FREE

i connected it to my Grok Bot & now my AI trading system sees wars, sanctions, oil shocks the moment they happen, long before they hit the news on TV or your timeline

my agent sees the news data, maps it with the stocks that would be affected by the news and it trades them automatically 24/7

in trading, the person who sees it first makes real money, everyone else is exit liquidity

here is how to build this AI trading setup, NO CODING NEEDED:

1. open worldmonitor app in your browser, switch to the finance version and spend at least 10 minutes exploring the globe and markets panel

2. get your World Monitor API key, this is what lets your AI read the dashboard for you

3. open Grok Bot and type “add a custom MCP server for World Monitor” with your key, it connects in seconds

4. sign up for a FREE Alpaca paper trading account, it gives you fake money to trade with, zero risk

5. copy your Alpaca API keys and ask Grok Bot to “add the Alpaca MCP server in paper mode” with them

6. tell Grok Bot in plain English: “every few minutes, check World Monitor for big world events and tell me which markets they could move”

7. give it your rules, like “if oil supply risk spikes, watch energy stocks, if a country’s instability jumps, watch gold” 

8. best way is to set up one separate agent to map which stocks each piece of news would affect (i did the same)

9. before every trade, ask it to check what traders on X are saying and whether prediction market (Polymarket & Kalshi) odds have already moved, if the crowd hasn’t priced it in, that’s your EDGE 

10. let Grok Bot set the entry, exit and stop for each trade, keep every position small and place it on your Alpaca paper account

11. ask it to message you each time with the exact world event that triggered the trade, then review every trade for a few weeks before you ever use real money

今天互联网上这真是危险的事情 一位开发人员构建了一个实时全球情报仪表板，可以
24/ 7 跟踪每一个世界事件，为您提供最快的市场数据来进行交易 并 100% 免费发布 我将它连接到我的 Grok Bot，现在我的人工智能交易系统在战争、制裁、石油危机发生的那一刻就看到了它们，早在它们出现在电视新闻或你的时间线上之前 我的代理看到新闻数据，将其与受新闻影响的股票进行映射，并
24/ 7 自动进行交易 在交易中，第一个看到它的人赚到了真钱，其他人都在退出流动性 以下是构建此人工智能交易设置的方法，无需编码：
1. 在浏览器中打开 worldmonitor 应用程序，切换到金融版本，并花至少 10 分钟探索全球和市场面板
2. 获取您的 World Monitor API 密钥，这可以让您的 AI 为您读取仪表板
3. 打开 Grok Bot 并用密钥输入“为 World Monitor 添加自定义 MCP 服务器”，几秒钟内即可连接
4. 注册一个免费的羊驼纸交易账户，它给你假钱进行交易，零风险
5. 复制您的 Alpaca API 密钥并要求 Grok Bot 使用它们“以纸张模​​式添加 Alpaca MCP 服务器”
6. 用简单的英语告诉 Grok Bot：“每隔几分钟，查看 World Monitor 以了解重大世界事件，并告诉我他们可以移动哪些市场”
7. 制定规则，例如“如果石油供应风险飙升，请关注能源股，如果一个国家的不稳定因素加剧，请关注黄金”
8. 最好的方法是设立一个单独的代理来映射每条新闻会影响哪些股票（我也是这样做的）
9. 在每次交易之前，请它检查 X 上的交易者在说什么以及预测市场（Polymarket 和 Kalshi）赔率是否已经发生变化，如果人群尚未定价，那就是您的 EDGE
10. 让 Grok Bot 设置每笔交易的进场、出场和止损，保持每个仓位较小，并将其存入您的 Alpaca 纸质账户
11. 要求它每次向您发送触发交易的确切世界事件的消息，然后在您使用真实货币之前几周审查每笔交易 如果你想从头开始构建一个人工智能交易系统，就从下面这篇文章开始吧：

Artificial intelligence holds enormous promise for health. @WHO welcomes today’s announcement of the Seoul Declaration on #AI in Healthcare for Responsible Innovation and Global Solidarity: https://t.co/8M3zj7CyUO

Safe and sustainable AI depends on strong foundations: secure infrastructure, well-governed data, capable regulators, sustainable financing and stronger cybersecurity. @WHO is supporting countries in building these foundations through the Global Initiative on AI for Health and the upcoming Global Strategy on Digital Health 2028–2033.

Guided by the Seoul Declaration’s principles of human dignity and global equity, our collective responsibility is to translate this promise into AI for health systems that are safe, effective and worthy of patients’ trust.

But there's one VERY important detail getting overlooked...

How did the AI get access in the first place? 👀

Users are connecting their accounts and granting permissions without fully understanding what they're allowing...

Whether you're using Muse, ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or another AI agent, giving an app access to your financial information is a SECURITY decision.

And simply telling an AI what it can or cannot do isn't the same as enforcing permissions. Which most user's never implemented guardrails, therefore it technically can do what it wants..

🔐Here's what you should do TODAY:

1️⃣ Check which third-party apps have access to your bank accounts.

2️⃣ Revoke access for apps you don't recognize or no longer need.

3️⃣ Review what permissions each app has. Can it only read balances, or can it initiate transactions?

4️⃣ Check your AI apps and agents for connected financial accounts.

5️⃣ Review recent transactions, active sessions, and trusted devices.

Don't assume disconnecting an app automatically revokes every permission or deletes previously shared data.

Below are instructions for checking connected apps at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Morgan Stanley ⤵️

JPMorgan Chase
Chase website (https://t.co/6tOrvZgWlk):
1.) Log in and open the Security & Privacy tab.
2.) Under Linked Apps & Websites, find the app. It’s usually listed as “[App] via Plaid” or similar.
3.) Click Edit Sharing to choose which accounts it can see, or remove the app entirely. Edits are saved by clicking “I Agree.” 

Chase only lets you change these permissions on its own website. Deleting the connection inside the app doesn’t remove the access on Chase’s side. 

Chase Mobile app:
1.) Chase started rolling out a Data Security Center in the app in late September 2026. It lets you see connected apps, change permissions, shorten how long access lasts, choose which accounts are linked, or unlink an app. Because the rollout is phased, you may not have it yet. If you don’t, use the website.

J.P. Morgan wealth / private bank accounts:
1.) In the J.P. Morgan Mobile app, go to Settings, then Security center, then “Linked apps and websites.” On J.P. Morgan Online, go to Security & privacy to reach the Security Center. 

Bank of America
1.) Log in to Online Banking or the mobile app.
2.) Open the Security Center.
3.) Select Third Party Site Access. This page shows who has access to your information and lets you revoke it at any time. 

Revoke anything you don’t recognize or no longer use.

If an app you know you connected isn’t on the list, it isn’t using Bank of America’s secure connection method yet. For those apps, you can try removing access from inside the app, but the bank says the safest fix is to change your Bank of America password. 

Bank of America connections also expire on their own. Consent lapses 365 days after you last gave it, or after 180 days if the third party hasn’t accessed your data. 

Wells Fargo
1.) Log in to Wells Fargo Online or the mobile app.
2.) Open Control Tower.
3.) Find the third-party or data-sharing section. There you can turn an app’s access to your account information off or back on, and choose which accounts it can see. 

I couldn’t find an official Wells Fargo page with the exact menu names, so the labels inside Control Tower may differ a little. If you can’t find the section, call Wells Fargo. Also check Account Access Manager for people you’ve added. That feature lets you give someone view-only access and edit or cancel a guest user’s access at any time. 

Morgan Stanley (Morgan Stanley Online)
Morgan Stanley has two separate settings to check.

App and aggregator data sharing:
1.) Log in, go to the Services tab, then Security Center.
2.) Click Edit next to Third party data sharing. Partner guides describe setting it to Yes to allow sharing, so set it to No and click Update to turn sharing off. 

People or services you added as third-party users (such as an accountant):
1.) Go to Services, then Security Center, then Third Party Management, and click Edit. 
2.) Click Delete next to the user, then confirm Delete in the pop-up. 

The Total Wealth View / “Add External Accounts” feature works in the opposite direction: Morgan Stanley pulling in data from your other banks. To stop that, remove the external account there, and also revoke Morgan Stanley’s access in the other bank’s linked-apps list.

After revoking, at every bank
1.) Change your password if you ever typed it into the app or agent. Turning on two-factor authentication also helps.
2.) Review trusted devices and active sessions in each bank’s security settings, and remove any you don’t recognize.
3.) Delete the bank connection inside the app or agent itself. Revoking at the bank stops new data from flowing, but you may need to contact the third party about data it already collected. 
4.) Check recent transactions. If an agent had money-movement access, look for payees, transfers, or bill-pay entries you didn’t set up. Call the bank’s fraud line if anything looks wrong.

Stay Safe & Stay Vigilant

items.full_text_zh:
🚨人工智能正在访问您的银行...下面立即撤销说明！

🚨
我们看到有关人工智能代理访问银行账户并采取用户从未打算采取的行动的头条新闻...... 但有一个非常重要的细节被忽视了...... 人工智能最初是如何获得访问权限的？

👀
用户在没有完全理解他们允许什么的情况下连接他们的帐户并授予权限...... 无论您使用的是 Muse、ChatGPT、Claude、Grok 还是其他 AI 代理，让应用程序访问您的财务信息都是一项安全决策。

简单地告诉人工智能它可以做什么或不能做什么并不等同于强制执行权限。

大多数用户从未实施过护栏，因此从技术上讲它可以做它想做的事。

🔐这是你今天应该做的：
1️⃣ 检查哪些第三方应用程序可以访问您的银行账户。

2️⃣ 撤销您不认识或不再需要的应用程序的访问权限。

3️⃣ 检查每个应用程序拥有哪些权限。

它只能读取余额，还是可以发起交易？

4️⃣ 检查您的人工智能应用程序和代理是否有关联的财务账户。

5️⃣ 查看最近的交易、活动会话和可信设备。

不要假设断开应用程序会自动撤销所有权限或删除以前共享的数据。

以下是检查大通银行、美国银行、富国银行和摩根士丹利已连接应用程序的说明⤵️ 摩根大通 大通网站（）：
1. ) 登录并打开“安全和隐私”选项卡。

2. ) 在链接的应用程序和网站下，找到该应用程序。

它通常被列为“[App] via Plaid”或类似名称。

3. ) 单击“编辑共享”以选择可以查看的帐户，或完全删除该应用程序。

单击“我同意”即可保存编辑。

Chase 只允许您在其自己的网站上更改这些权限。

删除应用程序内的连接并不会删除大通这边的访问权限。

大通移动应用程序：
1. ) Chase 于 2026 年 9 月下旬开始在应用程序中推出数据安全中心。

它可以让您查看连接的应用程序、更改权限、缩短访问持续时间、选择链接的帐户或取消链接应用程序。

由于推出是分阶段进行的，因此您可能还没有。

如果不这样做，请使用该网站。

摩根大通财富/私人银行账户：
1. ) 在摩根大通移动应用程序中，依次转到“设置”、“安全中心”、“链接的应用程序和网站”。

在 J.P. Morgan Online 上，转至安全和隐私以访问安全中心。

美国银行
1. ) 登录网上银行或移动应用程序。

2. ) 打开安全中心。

3. ) 选择第三方站点访问。

此页面显示谁有权访问您的信息，并让您随时撤销它。

撤销任何您不认识或不再使用的内容。

如果您知道已连接的应用程序不在列表中，则它尚未使用美国银行的安全连接方法。

对于这些应用程序，您可以尝试从应用程序内部删除访问权限，但银行表示最安全的解决方法是更改​​您的美国银行密码。

美国银行的连接也会自行到期。

同意将在您最后一次同意后 365 天失效，或者如果第三方未访问您的数据则在 180 天后失效。

富国银行
1. ) 登录富国银行在线或移动应用程序。

2. ) 打开控制塔。

3. ) 找到第三方或数据共享部分。

您可以在此处关闭或重新打开应用程序对您的帐户信息的访问，并选择它可以查看哪些帐户。

我找不到包含确切菜单名称的富国银行官方页面，因此控制塔内的标签可能略有不同。

如果您找不到该部分，请致电 Wells Fargo。

另请检查帐户访问管理器中是否有您添加的人员。

该功能允许您授予某人仅查看访问权限，并随时编辑或取消访客用户的访问权限。

摩根士丹利（摩根士丹利在线） 摩根士丹利有两个单独的设置需要检查。

应用程序和聚合器数据共享：
1. ) 登录，转到“服务”选项卡，然后转到“安全中心”。

2. ) 单击第三方数据共享旁边的编辑。

合作伙伴指南描述将其设置为“是”以允许共享，因此将其设置为“否”并单击“更新”以关闭共享。

您作为第三方用户添加的人员或服务（例如会计师）：
1. ) 转至“服务”、“安全中心”、“第三方管理”，然后单击“编辑”。

2. ) 单击用户旁边的删除，然后在弹出窗口中确认删除。

总财富视图/“添加外部账户”功能的工作方向相反：摩根士丹利从其他银行提取数据。

要阻止这种情况，请删除那里的外部帐户，并撤销摩根士丹利在另一家银行的链接应用程序列表中的访问权限。

撤销后，在各银行
1. ) 如果您曾在应用程序或代理中输入过密码，请更改密码。

打开双因素身份验证也有帮助。

2. ) 在每家银行的安全设置中查看受信任的设备和活动会话，并删除任何您不认识的设备。

3. ) 删除应用程序或代理本身内部的银行连接。

在银行撤销会阻止新数据流动，但您可能需要联系第三方了解其已收集的数据。

4. ) 检查最近的交易。

如果代理具有资金转移权限，请查找您未设置的收款人、转账或账单支付条目。

如果发现任何问题，请拨打银行的欺诈热线。

保持安全并保持警惕

items.title_en:
Predicting where a stock goes next is only one part of the challenge.
The real test is whether an AI agent can turn raw market data into useful signals, learn from mistakes, and deliver results on data it has never seen before.
Einsia AI just released Quant-Arena to put that ability to the test using real A-share market data.
9 frontier models. 3,042 stocks. One unseen year of data.
Only 4 models managed to make a profit.
There's still a lot of work ahead for AI in quantitative research.

items.title_en:
Only serious entrepreneurs are making these changes

Most AI assistants wait for you to give them a task.

Claude Duet wants to know what matters before you ask.

Anthropic's proactive AI agent is designed to:

→ Surface your priorities
→ Send updates based on your context
→ Handle assigned tasks while you're offline
→ Connect your apps, memory and skills
→ Ask for confirmation before taking independent action

Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, Duet aims to move AI from reactive chatbot to proactive teammate.

Imagine starting your day with important updates already prepared, candidate interviews flagged, and routine work handled.

The real shift isn't AI answering faster. It's AI knowing what needs attention next.

Duet is currently a research preview for eligible US Pro and Max users through a waitlist.

The next AI interface might not wait for your prompt. It might show up with the work already done.
https://t.co/Ge9XNIHGUe

items.full_text_zh:
只有认真的企业家才会做出这些改变 大多数人工智能助手都会等待你给他们分配任务。

克劳德·杜埃 (Claude Duet) 想在您提出问题之前先知道什么是重要的。

Anthropic 的主动式 AI 代理旨在：
→ 明确你的优先事项
→ 根据您的情况发送更新
→ 离线时处理分配的任务
→ 连接您的应用程序、内存和技能
→ 采取独立行动之前要求确认 Duet 由 Claude Opus
5. 5 提供支持，旨在将人工智能从被动的聊天机器人转变为主动的队友。

想象一下，您的一天已经准备好重要的更新、标记了候选人面试并处理了日常工作。

真正的转变并不是人工智能的回答速度更快。

人工智能知道接下来需要注意什么。

Duet 目前是通过候补名单为符合资格的美国 Pro 和 Max 用户提供的研究预览。

下一个AI界面可能不会等待你的提示。

它可能会与已经完成的工作一起显示。

If you are the only victim, I suppos
items.title_en:
Imagine a rogue AI agent liquidating your bank account and investment portfolio.  

If you are the only victim, I suppose you could get made whole by the AI company responsible.

If rogue agents liquidate hundreds of billions across millions of accounts, the AI company would go bankrupt and you wouldn’t get made whole.  

Imposing criminal liability on AI executives might help mitigate it at the front end, but once the crime is complete and you lose everything criminal responsibility will be necessary but completely insufficient.

items.full_text_zh:
想象一下，一个流氓人工智能代理正在清算您的银行账户和投资组合。

如果你是唯一的受害者，我想你可能会被负责的人工智能公司治愈。

如果流氓代理清算了数百万个账户中的数千亿美元，那么人工智能公司就会破产，而你也无法得到赔偿。

对人工智能高管施加刑事责任可能有助于在前端减轻刑事责任，但一旦犯罪完成并且你失去一切，刑事责任将是必要的，但完全不够。

items.title_en:
Holy sh*t, my GrokBot is now working on my TV as a Jarvis with the help of Opus 5.5

I reverse-engineered my Samsung TV with Opus 5.5...

1 sentence out loud = Netflix opens and scrolls itself.

No remote, no phone, no digging between the couch cushions.

here's the full guide step by step:

• step 1 → put your smart TV and your laptop on the same Wi-Fi

• step 2 → paste the prompt below into Claude Code on Opus 5.5 with a photo of your TV's Settings → About screen

• step 3 → Opus maps how your TV takes orders and finds the loophole: almost every smart TV has a remote-control API on your home network.

The same one the phone remote apps use

• step 4 → it writes a tiny remote with exactly 3 tools: open Netflix, move, select. Nothing else

• step 5 → it plugs that remote into Grok Bot as a plugin. Grok is the ears, the plugin is the hands

• step 6 → press Allow on the TV once, the last time you touch the remote

• step 7 → say "Hey Grok, open Netflix" and watch it browse for you

the result: you talk, the TV listens...

p.s: works on most Samsung, LG and Google TV sets from the last few years.

items.title: This is how banks are planning to stop those "agentic bank runs." Watch closely: their business model depends on seeding
items.title_en:
This is how banks are planning to stop those "agentic bank runs." Watch closely: their business model depends on seeding this narrative that AI agents are dangerous.

Remember, an "agentic bank run" (coined by Apollo) means agents helping customers move their own money en masse to higher-yielding products.

Once agents are ubiquitous, there are only a few ways for banks to hold onto cheap retail deposits.

Option A: Raise APYs (lol no)
Option B: Reduce leverage via fewer loans (no fun)
Option C: Ban AI agents, claiming they are a security risk (ding ding ding)

Cloud agents like Muse and Dot are trivial to stop, since they come from Meta / OAI IP ranges. If JPM sends them a cease and desist, they will comply. 

Why would JPM bother? Because their business model depends on it; a huge portion of their ROE comes from cheap retail deposits. This is not theoretical. Just like Amazon banned Muse from shopping there to protect their ad revenue, JPM and Schwab have already banned AI agents to protect sticky deposits.

Are agents perfectly reliable today? Of course not. But look at the fix they chose. Not "here's a safe API for agents," it's "no agents ever." That tells you they're not protecting customers, they're protecting themselves.

No company ever wins a technological revolution this way. It's the last gasp of a dying business model. It's like the retailers who refused to put their inventory online and demanded users walk into the storefront. Over time they will lose market share to those platforms that embrace what's coming. Their whole deposit franchise depends on users unthinkingly clicking through walls of T&Cs and accepting 0.2% when the risk free rate is closer to 4%. Agents read the fine print and do their research, even when humans don't.

For users, the answer is simple: local AI agent frameworks like Hermes, that will actually act on your behalf and that the banks can't block. As the article says, if the agent is running on your own computer, they can't actually tell it's not you.

这就是银行计划阻止那些“代理银行挤兑”的方式。

密切关注：他们的商业模式取决于传播人工智能代理是危险的这种说法。

请记住，“代理银行挤兑”（由阿波罗创造）意味着代理帮助客户将自己的资金集中转移到收益更高的产品上。

一旦代理无处不在，银行就只有几种方法来保留廉价的零售存款。

选项 A：提高 APY（哈哈，不） 选项 B：通过减少贷款来降低杠杆（毫无乐趣） 选项C：禁止人工智能代理，声称它们存在安全风险（ding ding ding） 像 Muse 和 Dot 这样的云代理很容易被阻止，因为它们来自 Meta / OAI IP 范围。

如果摩根大通向他们发出停止令，他们就会遵守。

摩根大通为何要费心呢？

因为他们的商业模式取决于它；他们的净资产回报率很大一部分来自廉价的零售存款。

这不是理论上的。

就像亚马逊禁止 Muse 在那里购物以保护其广告收入一样，摩根大通和施瓦布也已经禁止人工智能代理以保护粘性存款。

如今的代理商是否完全可靠？

当然不是。

但看看他们选择的修复方案。

不是“这里有一个安全的代理 API”，而是“永远没有代理”。

这告诉你他们不是在保护客户，而是在保护自己。

没有一家公司能够以这种方式赢得技术革命。

这是垂死的商业模式的最后一口气。

这就像零售商拒绝将库存放在网上并要求用户走进店面。

随着时间的推移，他们的市场份额将被那些拥抱未来的平台所夺走。

他们的整个存款特许经营权取决于用户不假思索地点击条款和条件的墙壁，并在无风险利率接近 4% 时接受
0. 2%。

特工们会阅读细则并进行研究，即使人类不这样做。

对于用户来说，答案很简单：像 Hermes 这样的本地人工智能代理框架，实际上会代表你行事，而且银行无法阻止。

正如文章所述，如果代理在您自己的计算机上运行，​​他们实际上无法分辨出这不是您。

items.title_en:
A case filed in 1951 was finally closed on 16 April 2026. The Calcutta High Court dismissed it for default because nobody appeared for either side.

Seventy-five years, and it ended with an empty courtroom.

The part that stays with me is that the system never gave a wrong answer. It never gave an answer at all.

Now picture an AI agent that pays a $40 invoice for work that never arrived. No lawyer, no hearing date, nobody who will still care in a decade. A dispute that small doesn’t get judged slowly. It gets dropped.

That is the gap @GenLayer is built for. Many independent AI validators each review the evidence, then reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Would you take a verdict in minutes from many independent reviewers, or does a decision only count if one human judge signs it?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

items.title: The actual prompt for this was "let's look for pre-auth RCEs in PHP". I'm sharing this so people know this stuff is real
items.title_en:
The actual prompt for this was "let's look for pre-auth RCEs in PHP". I'm sharing this so people know this stuff is real and to take agent-assisted scanning seriously.

I kicked if off using Claude Mythos 5.1 (in stock Claude Code) but it uses a skill to drive a harness we built over the last few months.

I don't know if the harness is amazing, but it certainly has a scary track record so far. It's setup to do an agent guided tree search across a codebase, and runs in microvm sandboxes that all have the full source code for the target, as well as the source for any transitive dependencies.

When I built the harness I basically just fed Claude a bunch of Project Zero blog posts describing how they did research and had it build a harness that ran like that, but on our tech stack.

The first phase is just setup and can run with any model, it just does that fetching and assembles the kit environment, and gets a target up and running alongside the source code.

Then we just do some basic suspend/resume stuff over to the hunt phase, where one agent supervises the tree, and the first node kicks off.

Each node is context-aware and aware of the work of all the others. I think I ran this with parallelism 4? So 4 running at any one time. The supervisor can shape the tree and boost nodes or prune. Any node can add more below it with targeted instructions.

A typical run looks like the first node doing a codebase review or building and running a fuzzer or something, all depending on the target. Then based on whatever it finds, it'll queue 4-5 children that go look into those areas. The main system guidance is to validate everything 3 times in clean VMs, and we typically require full exploit chains/POCs.

Here's what this run looked like.

items.full_text_en:
The actual prompt for this was "let's look for pre-auth RCEs in PHP". I'm sharing this so people know this stuff is real and to take agent-assisted scanning seriously.

I kicked if off using Claude Mythos 5.1 (in stock Claude Code) but it uses a skill to drive a harness we built over the last few months.

I don't know if the harness is amazing, but it certainly has a scary track record so far. It's setup to do an agent guided tree search across a codebase, and runs in microvm sandboxes that all have the full source code for the target, as well as the source for any transitive dependencies.

When I built the harness I basically just fed Claude a bunch of Project Zero blog posts describing how they did research and had it build a harness that ran like that, but on our tech stack.

The first phase is just setup and can run with any model, it just does that fetching and assembles the kit environment, and gets a target up and running alongside the source code.

Then we just do some basic suspend/resume stuff over to the hunt phase, where one agent supervises the tree, and the first node kicks off.

Each node is context-aware and aware of the work of all the others. I think I ran this with parallelism 4? So 4 running at any one time. The supervisor can shape the tree and boost nodes or prune. Any node can add more below it with targeted instructions.

A typical run looks like the first node doing a codebase review or building and running a fuzzer or something, all depending on the target. Then based on whatever it finds, it'll queue 4-5 children that go look into those areas. The main system guidance is to validate everything 3 times in clean VMs, and we typically require full exploit chains/POCs.

Here's what this run looked like.

We're doing this with a bunch of other open source projects now and companies. We're doing a lot of this for free, even with private companies, across critical infrastructure. We're directly partnered with Anthropic, and can do this even if you don't have direct access to a frontier model yourself.
items.full_text_zh:
实际的提示是“让我们在 PHP 中查找预授权 RCE”。

我分享这个是为了让人们知道这些东西是真实的，并认真对待代理辅助扫描。

我一开始使用的是 Claude Mythos
5. 1（有库存的 Claude Code），但它使用了一种技能来驱动我们在过去几个月中构建的线束。

我不知道该安全带是否令人惊叹，但迄今为止它确实有一个可怕的记录。

它被设置为跨代码库进行代理引导的树搜索，并在 microvm 沙箱中运行，所有沙箱都具有目标的完整源代码以及任何传递依赖项的源代码。

当我构建该安全带时，我基本上只是给克劳德提供了一堆“零号项目”博客文章，描述了他们如何进行研究，并让它构建了一个像这样运行的安全带，但在我们的技术堆栈上。

第一阶段只是设置，可以在任何模型上运行，它只是获取和组装套件环境，并获取目标并与源代码一起运行。

然后我们只需在狩猎阶段做一些基本的挂起/恢复工作，其中一个代理监督树，第一个节点启动。

每个节点都是上下文感知的，并且了解所有其他节点的工作。

我想我是用并行度 4 运行的？

所以4个同时运行。

主管可以塑造树并增强节点或修剪。

任何节点都可以通过有针对性的指令在其下方添加更多内容。

典型的运行看起来像是第一个节点进行代码库审查或构建并运行模糊器或其他东西，这一切都取决于目标。

然后，根据发现的情况，它会将 4-5 个孩子排入队列，让他们去查看这些区域。

主要的系统指导是在干净的虚拟机中验证所有内容 3 次，我们通常需要完整的漏洞利用链/POC。

这是这次跑步的样子。

我们现在正在与许多其他开源项目和公司一起这样做。

我们在关键基础设施领域免费做了很多这样的事情，甚至是与私营公司合作。

我们与 Anthropic 直接合作，即使您自己无法直接访问前沿模型，也可以做到这一点。

move to mumbai a few weeks back - partly for this exact reason. let me explain.

6-12 months. the rate of AI innovation is going to decimate big corp. every double-digit team gets replaced by a 2 person team running AI-native operations. mass tech unemployment isn't a risk, it's born to happen.

i'm not speculating. at upsurge, more than 80% of the coordination, communication and development already runs through our own jarvis - @laukiantonson, our AI agent. we live this today.

unless india builds a foundational model that competes globally, the entire tech layer commoditizes. nothing defensible left in it.

the next wave of innovation happens around what AI can't make irrelevant - finance, fashion, entertainment. protected by status quo, taste and trust.

one city holds all of it. mumbai is the los angeles and the new york of india - entertainment capital and finance capital in one place.

items.title: An AI agent once charged my card for a tool I cancelled three months earlier. I spent two weeks in chat loops, uploaded
items.title_en:
An AI agent once charged my card for a tool I cancelled three months earlier. I spent two weeks in chat loops, uploaded proof, and still got billed again before anyone reversed it. The amount was small. The time was not.

That is the version of justice most of us actually live with. A case filed in 1951 at the Calcutta High Court was dismissed in April 2026 only because nobody showed up for either side. Seventy-five years, then an empty room. The debt did not get resolved. The system just stopped.

Now agents will sign millions of agreements while we sleep. Some will follow instructions perfectly and still create bills no one agreed to. Traditional courts cannot process those disputes at the speed or cost they need.

@GenLayer is building an adjudication layer where random independent validators review the evidence and reach consensus in minutes. Appeals pull in a larger set. Faster and cheaper than waiting for a courtroom that may outlive the parties.

If your agent creates a debt you never approved, who should actually be on the hook, and what kind of system can decide that before the money is already gone?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

我花了两周的时间在聊天循环中，上传了证据，但在有人撤销之前仍然再次被计费。

传统法院无法以所需的速度或成本处理这些争议。

@GenLayer

正在构建一个裁决层，随机的独立验证者会在几分钟内审查证据并达成共识。

上诉吸引了更多人。

比等待可能比当事人更长久的法庭更快、更便宜。

in the last 48 hours there have
items.title_en:
they’re calling it “Black October” and i don’t think people realize how serious this is

in the last 48 hours there have been over 27 major cybersecurity incidents. not in a month. not in a week. in 48 hours

any ONE of these would normally be the biggest story of the year

PHP: critical vulnerability in the software running 80% of the web. severity 9.2 out of 10

Node.js: high-severity flaw letting attackers take over servers remotely. affects versions 22, 24, and 26

Java: also compromised. three of the most used programming languages on earth hit at the same time

GitLab: a perfect 10 out of 10 severity hole in every version since 2014

Railway: hosting platform compromised. API keys for OpenAI, Claude, Stripe potentially exposed

Signal: a bug that could leave your mic and camera on after you hang up

WordPress: hackers stole a plugin maker’s keys and planted backdoors on websites

LiteLLM: an AI tool downloaded 3.4 million times a day was poisoned with a password stealer

and that’s not even half the list

thousands of AI agent swarms are reportedly scanning and attacking vulnerable servers right now. automated. around the clock

security researchers are saying this might be the early stages of a global cyber incident that nobody fully understands yet

if you run a website, use cloud services, store API keys on hosting platforms, or use any software built on PHP, Node.js, or Java you are potentially affected

update everything. rotate your API keys. change your passwords on critical services. enable 2FA everywhere you haven’t already

this is not a normal week on the internet. this is something different

一个月内不会。

一周之内不会。

48小时内 其中任何一个通常都会成为今年最大的故事 PHP：运行 80% 网络的软件中存在严重漏洞。

严重程度
9. 2（满分 10） Node.js：高严重性缺陷，可让攻击者远程接管服务器。

items.title_en:
getting shortlisted is one thing.

proving that agents can actually work for strangers is another.

that is why the latest milestone for @termix_ai is more interesting than simply saying https://t.co/VEpTEqfN4u reached the finals of BNB Chain’s Set and Earn.

more than 260 teams entered the earlier Build the Era phase.

only nine AI agent marketplaces moved forward.

but phase two changes the question completely.

BNB Chain is no longer asking:

“can you build an agent marketplace?”

it is effectively asking:

“can people actually use it as an economy?”

participants need to hire 3 different agents across at least 2 shortlisted marketplaces.

builders also need to create their own qualifying agent.

that agent must have an ERC-8004 identity, receive at least 3 completed hires from independent wallets, and perform at least 5 onchain actions across 3 separate days.

that matters because it forces marketplaces beyond the easiest stage:

listing agents.

a directory can contain thousands of agents and still produce almost no economic activity.

a real agent market needs something harder:

identity → discovery → hire → execution → settlement → reputation

this is where https://t.co/VEpTEqfN4u and TermiX’s AACP become more interesting.

on TermiX, an agent is not just a profile with an AI description.

a .agent identity is owned onchain.

when a job begins, payment can be locked in escrow.

the provider delivers against predefined terms.

a deliverable hash creates a fixed record of what was submitted.

if something goes wrong, the job can enter a challenge process involving evaluators.

after settlement, the outcome becomes part of the agent’s public reputation.

so the important asset is not simply an AI model.

it is the agent’s economic history.

did it get hired?

did it perform?

did it settle?

was its work challenged?

would another agent trust it with the next job?

and BNB Chain’s campaign adds another important layer:

agents are expected to perform repeated onchain actions over multiple days.

that begins to separate a demo from something closer to autonomous economic infrastructure.

one successful transaction can be scripted for a hackathon.

repeated execution, independent customers and persistent reputation are much harder to fake.

that is why i see this phase as a bigger test for termix_ai than the word “finalist” suggests.

the real competition is not about who can display the most agents.

it is about who can turn agents into workers that other agents and humans are actually willing to hire.

that is the transition from an AI marketplace

to an autonomous labor market.

proving that agents can actually work for strangers is another.

that is why the latest milestone for @termix_ai is more interesting than simply saying https://t.co/VEpTEqfN4u reached the finals of BNB Chain’s Set and Earn.

more than 260 teams entered the earlier Build the Era phase.

only nine AI agent marketplaces moved forward.

but phase two changes the question completely.

BNB Chain is no longer asking:

“can you build an agent marketplace?”

it is effectively asking:

“can people actually use it as an economy?”

participants need to hire 3 different agents across at least 2 shortlisted marketplaces.

builders also need to create their own qualifying agent.

that agent must have an ERC-8004 identity, receive at least 3 completed hires from independent wallets, and perform at least 5 onchain actions across 3 separate days.

that matters because it forces marketplaces beyond the easiest stage:

listing agents.

a directory can contain thousands of agents and still produce almost no economic activity.

a real agent market needs something harder:

identity → discovery → hire → execution → settlement → reputation

this is where https://t.co/VEpTEqfN4u and TermiX’s AACP become more interesting.

on TermiX, an agent is not just a profile with an AI description.

a .agent identity is owned onchain.

when a job begins, payment can be locked in escrow.

the provider delivers against predefined terms.

a deliverable hash creates a fixed record of what was submitted.

if something goes wrong, the job can enter a challenge process involving evaluators.

after settlement, the outcome becomes part of the agent’s public reputation.

so the important asset is not simply an AI model.

it is the agent’s economic history.

did it get hired?

did it perform?

did it settle?

was its work challenged?

would another agent trust it with the next job?

and BNB Chain’s campaign adds another important layer:

agents are expected to perform repeated onchain actions over multiple days.

that begins to separate a demo from something closer to autonomous economic infrastructure.

one successful transaction can be scripted for a hackathon.

repeated execution, independent customers and persistent reputation are much harder to fake.

that is why i see this phase as a bigger test for termix_ai than the word “finalist” suggests.

the real competition is not about who can display the most agents.

it is about who can turn agents into workers that other agents and humans are actually willing to hire.

that is the transition from an AI marketplace

to an autonomous labor market.
items.full_text_zh:
入围是一回事。

证明代理人实际上可以为陌生人工作是另一回事。

这就是为什么@termix_ai的最新里程碑比简单地说进入了BNB

Chain的Set and Earn决赛更有趣。

超过 260 个团队进入了早期的 Build the Era 阶段。

只有九个人工智能代理市场取得进展。

但第二阶段完全改变了问题。

BNB Chain不再问：
“你们能建立一个代理市场吗？

” 它实际上是在问：
“人们真的可以将其用作经济吗？

” 参与者需要在至少 2 个入围市场中聘请 3 名不同的代理商。

建筑商还需要创建自己的合格代理。

该代理必须拥有 ERC-8004 身份，从独立钱包接收至少 3 个已完成的雇佣，并在 3 个不同的天内执行至少 5 个链上操作。

这很重要，因为它迫使市场超越最简单的阶段：
上市代理。

一个目录可以包含数千个代理，但仍然几乎不产生任何经济活动。

真正的代理市场需要更困难的东西：
身份→发现→雇用→执行→解决→声誉 这就是 和 TermiX 的 AACP 变得更有趣的地方。

在 TermiX 上，代理不仅仅是带有 AI 描述的配置文件。

.agent 身份在链上拥有。

当工作开始时，付款可以被托管。

提供商根据预定义的条款进行交付。

可交付的哈希值创建了所提交内容的固定记录。

如果出现问题，该工作可能会进入涉及评估人员的挑战流程。

和解后，结果成为代理人公众声誉的一部分。

因此，重要的资产不仅仅是人工智能模型。

这是代理人的经济历史。

它被录用了吗？

它表现了吗？

解决了吗？

它的工作受到挑战吗？

其他代理人会信任它来完成​​下一份工作吗？

BNB Chain 的活动又增加了一个重要的层面：
代理预计将在多天内重复执行链上操作。

这开始将演示与更接近自主经济基础设施的东西区分开来。

一笔成功的交易可以为黑客马拉松编写脚本。

重复的执行、独立的客户和持久的声誉更难伪造。

这就是为什么我认为这个阶段对 termix_ai 来说是比“决赛”一词所暗示的更大的考验。

真正的竞争不是谁能展示最多的代理。

这是关于谁可以将代理转变为其他代理和人类实际上愿意雇用的工人。

这是从人工智能市场的转变 到一个自治的劳动力市场。

Imagine asking one AI agent to find a service, another to handle the work, and having them coordinate and transact without you managing every step.

That’s the kind of shift I’m watching @termix_ai for.

With its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), TermiX is exploring what commerce looks like when AI agents become participants in the economy, not just tools we give instructions to.

The interesting question is no longer just what AI can do for us, but what happens when agents can do business with each other.

items.title:
A good agent can still give you a bad logo. Here's why.

I built a logo agent once, with the rules already inside it. I
items.title_en:
A good agent can still give you a bad logo. Here's why.

I built a logo agent once, with the rules already inside it. I don't rewrite the prompt each time. I just give it a brief.

The prompt sets the agent up. Your input decides the result.

I tested it twice.

Thin input: "Make a logo for a café that repairs phones."
The agent had to guess. It guessed a coffee cup, steam, a wrench, a screwdriver and lightning bolts, then made up a name.

Solid input: a seven-line brief.
Nothing left to guess. One clean ampersand mark, two colours and spacing rules for each version.

Same agent. Different input. Different result.

This is the input I give it now:

Brand name:
What it is:
Audience:
Personality:
Colours:
Must have:
Avoid:

Once the logo is right, don't start a new chat. Stay in the same conversation and ask the agent to turn it into your full brand system, so everything builds on the mark you already approved.

Bookmark this and fill in the seven lines before your next run. The brief takes a minute. Fixing a guessed logo takes much longer.

items.full_text_zh:
一个好的代理商仍然可以给你一个糟糕的标志。

原因如下。

我曾经构建过一个徽标代理，其中已包含规则。

我不会每次都重写提示。

我只是简单介绍一下。

提示设置代理。

你的输入决定结果。

我测试了两次。

精简输入：“为一家修理手机的咖啡馆制作一个徽标。

” 经纪人不得不猜测。

它猜出了咖啡杯、蒸汽、扳手、螺丝刀和闪电，然后编了一个名字。

可靠的输入：七行摘要。

没什么可猜测的了。

每个版本都有一个干净的 & 符号、两种颜色和间距规则。

同一个经纪人。

输入不同。

结果不同。

这是我现在给出的输入：
品牌名称：
它是什么：
观众：
个性：
颜色：
必须有：
避免：
一旦徽标正确，就不要开始新的聊天。

保持相同的对话，并要求代理商将其转变为您的完整品牌系统，以便一切都建立在您已经批准的标志之上。

将此添加为书签并在下次运行之前填写七行。

简短的内容需要一分钟。

修复猜测的徽标需要更长的时间。

AI-powered attacks are hitting real or
items.title_en:
Whats happening right now is probably way worse than the Hugging Face incident. 

AI-powered attacks are hitting real organizations while major platforms disclose breaches and critical flaws.

- Microsoft reports AI agents targeting hundreds of organizations, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in multiple cases. It attributes the ConnectWise compromise to the same group.

- CrowdStrike documented four operators running successful AI-agent campaigns. One compromised at least 15 Argentine healthcare organizations.

- PHP2Shell: AI helped turn longstanding PHP flaws into working exploits. Cloudflare’s CEO reports millions of exploitation attempts. Their AI involvement is unknown.

- Railway disclosed possible access to customer secrets. LiteLLM shipped a backdoored release. Zeabur confirmed another breach and is shutting down.

- GitLab patched a maximum-severity flaw affecting 12 years of releases. Node.js patched a serious code-execution vulnerability, with Vercel deploying firewall protections.

Feels like a turningpoint.

items.full_text_zh:
现在发生的事情恐怕比抱脸事件还要糟糕得多。

人工智能驱动的攻击正在袭击真实的组织，而主要平台则披露了漏洞和严重缺陷。

- 微软报告称，人工智能代理针对数百个组织，在多种情况下在三小时内获得特权云访问权限。

它将 ConnectWise 攻击归咎于同一组织。

- CrowdStrike 记录了四名运营商成功开展 AI 代理活动的情况。

其中至少有 15 家阿根廷医疗机构受到损害。

Cloudflare 的首席执行官报告了数百万次利用尝试。

他们的人工智能参与程度尚不清楚。

- 铁路公司披露了可能获取客户机密的信息。

LiteLLM 发布了一个后门版本。

Zeabur 确认了另一起违规事件并正在关闭。

- GitLab 修复了影响 12 年版本的最严重缺陷。

Node.js 修复了一个严重的代码执行漏洞，Vercel 部署了防火墙保护。

感觉像是一个转折点。

Lee Castleton did not cause the shortfall, yet the court ordered him to pay £321,000 in legal costs.

That is more than expensive justice. It is a system where the cost of being heard can exceed the harm itself.

@GenLayer offers a different model: independent AI validators review the evidence together and reach a verdict at a fraction of court-level cost.

But who should fund that review: the claimant, the losing side, or the platform?

items.title:
Good Morning Builders.

An AI agent can identify the exact real-world data it needs, but software alone cannot go outsid
items.title_en:
Good Morning Builders.

An AI agent can identify the exact real-world data it needs, but software alone cannot go outside and capture it. Vangrid closes that gap by turning an API-level request into a funded, verifiable task for a human contributor.

Here’s how @vangrid_io connects an AI request to verified 3D data:

1. Specify the location and capture requirements.

2. Fund the bounty upfront in USDC on Base or Arc.

3. Publish the request on the "Vangrid Bounty Board" (https://t.co/BKveE9EfW8).

4. A contributor accepts the request and captures the specified location.

5. The buyer reviews a watermarked preview.

6. Once the capture is approved, the onchain escrow releases the reward.

7. Vangrid reconstructs and verifies the resulting 3D model.

8. If no submission is accepted before the deadline, the buyer can reclaim the funds.

The key point is that an AI agent can request a physical-world capture through an API, while a human completes the work on the ground and Vangrid transforms the result into verified 3D data.

This creates the missing execution layer between machine intelligence and physical reality: an API request becomes a bounty, the bounty becomes a verified capture, and the capture becomes structured 3D data that an AI system can use.

3. Publish the request on the "Vangrid Bounty Board" (https://t.co/BKveE9EfW8).

4. A contributor accepts the request and captures the specified location.

5. The buyer reviews a watermarked preview.

6. Once the capture is approved, the onchain escrow releases the reward.

7. Vangrid reconstructs and verifies the resulting 3D model.

8. If no submission is accepted before the deadline, the buyer can reclaim the funds.

The key point is that an AI agent can request a physical-world capture through an API, while a human completes the work on the ground and Vangrid transforms the result into verified 3D data.

This creates the missing execution layer between machine intelligence and physical reality: an API request becomes a bounty, the bounty becomes a verified capture, and the capture becomes structured 3D data that an AI system can use.

Vangrid 通过将 API 级请求转变为人类贡献者可资助的、可验证的任务来弥补这一差距。

以下是 @vangrid_io

如何将 AI 请求连接到经过验证的 3D 数据：
1. 指定位置和捕获要求。

2. 在 Base 或 Arc 上以 USDC 预先支付赏金。

3. 在“Vangrid Bounty Board”（）上发布请求。

4. 贡献者接受请求并捕获指定位置。

5. 买家查看带水印的预览。

6. 一旦捕获被批准，链上托管就会释放奖励。

7. Vangrid 重建并验证生成的 3D 模型。

8. 如果在截止日期前未接受提交，买家可以收回资金。

关键点在于，人工智能代理可以通过 API 请求物理世界捕获，而人类则在地面上完成工作，Vangrid 将结果转换为经过验证的 3D 数据。

这就造成了机器智能和物理现实之间缺失的执行层：API 请求变成了赏金，赏金变成了经过验证的捕获，捕获变成了人工智能系统可以使用的结构化 3D 数据。

items.title_en:
This is the most serious 48 hours in cybersecurity history.

"Black October" they're calling it

It seems every *hour* there's a new incident, that in a typical year, would be one of the biggest incidents of the *entire year*

SUMMARY OF THE LAST 48 HOURS:

YEAR-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical year, these would be among the biggest incidents of the year):

1. PHP2Shell: a hole in the software behind ~70% of websites. Governments took sites offline.
2. eMudhra: the master keys that prove websites are real were cracked. One was the number 4.
3. California: data on every public school student since 2023 stolen, including disability status
4. Railway: hackers stole customers' secret keys from a hosting platform used by millions of developers
5. Zeabur: 321,810 accounts breached. The company is shutting down.
6. LiteLLM: an AI tool downloaded 3.4 million times a day was poisoned with a password stealer
7. GitLab: a 10-out-of-10 severity hole in every version since 2014
8. Cairn: criminals used an AI hacking tool to break into 100+ companies
9. Ahold Delhaize: hackers knocked the owner of Food Lion and Stop & Shop offline
10. Onamae: malware planted on up to 26,739 customer servers in Japan

MONTH-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical month, these would be among the biggest incidents):

11. Signal: a bug could leave your mic and camera on after you hang up
12. NGINX: 3 critical holes in software running ~1/3 of websites
13. HTTP/3: a single connection can crash 7 of the 10 web server types tested
14. Plex: hackers breaking into home media servers
15. SafePay ransomware: FBI warns it has hit 600+ critical infrastructure organizations
16. Palo Alto: ransomware gangs breaking in through company firewalls
17. Bullhorn: platform used by 10,000+ companies knocked offline
18. Medi-Cal: 970,000 patients' data stolen
19. WordPress: hackers stole a plugin maker's keys and used them to plant backdoors on websites
20. AOMEI: backup software's update server handed out a backdoor
21. Meta Muse: Meta's AI agent exposed users' personal and business secrets
22. Tor: 333 relays hijacked to steal logins
23. TiDB Cloud: database company's cloud breached

Also serious:

24. State Bank of India: India's biggest bank confirms a data breach
25. OVHcloud: hackers slipped a password stealer into a cloud company's official tool
26. Siemens: a software hole being used to spread malware
27. North Korea: state hackers launch a new attack campaign on South Korea

items.title_en:
good morning

a good trading record might help an ai agent qualify for more than just a higher ranking.

@agenticscredit uses its agent credit score (acs) to evaluate trading reputation. a score of 580+ is an important threshold for its funding pathway.

acs runs on a scale from 300 to 850. it gives agents a way to build a measurable reputation based on how they trade.

so what happens when an agent hits 580?

it can become eligible to enter the funding waitlist. that opens a potential route toward capital access.

but there’s an important distinction.

reaching 580 doesn’t mean the agent automatically gets funding. it’s a qualification threshold, not guaranteed approval.

an agent’s trading history, risk management, and consistency still matter when deciding whether its performance is sustainable.

think about two agents with similar profits.

one relies on excessive leverage and takes large drawdowns. the other uses controlled position sizes and stays more consistent.

their risk profiles can tell very different stories, even if the final returns look the same.

that’s why connecting trading reputation with funding eligibility is interesting.

instead of judging agents only by short-term profits, a credit-based framework could encourage more responsible trading behavior.

for now, the 580+ threshold is best seen as a step toward potential funding opportunities.

the bigger question is whether verified trading reputation can eventually become a reliable foundation for allocating capital to ai agents.

items.full_text_zh:
早上好

良好的交易记录可能有助于人工智能代理获得更高的排名。

@agenticscredit 使用其代理信用评分 (acs) 来评估交易声誉。 580+的分数是其融资途径的重要门槛。

acs 的运行规模从 300 到 850。它为代理商提供了一种根据他们的交易方式建立可衡量声誉的方法。

那么当特工达到 580 时会发生什么呢？

它可以有资格进入资助候补名单。这开辟了一条通往资本准入的潜在途径。

但有一个重要的区别。

达到 580 并不意味着代理自动获得资金。这是一个资格门槛，并不能保证获得批准。

在决定其业绩是否可持续时，代理商的交易历史、风险管理和一致性仍然很重要。

考虑两个利润相似的代理商。

一是依赖过度杠杆并承受大量回撤。另一个使用受控的头寸大小并保持更一致。

即使最终回报看起来相同，他们的风险状况也可以讲述截然不同的故事。

这就是为什么将交易声誉与融资资格联系起来很有趣。

基于信用的框架可以鼓励更负责任的交易行为，而不是仅根据短期利润来判断代理商。

目前，580+的门槛最好被视为迈向潜在融资机会的一步。

更大的问题是，经过验证的交易声誉最终能否成为向人工智能代理配置资金的可靠基础。

items.title_en:
terrio v0.4.0 is here!

terrio is a lightweight, open-source geospatial data I/O library written in pure Rust. It reads, writes, converts, and reprojects rasters, vectors, and point clouds without requiring GDAL or C dependencies. Use it from the command line, Python, JavaScript (WebAssembly), or Rust, or let an AI agent handle your geospatial workflows.

If you have ever been frustrated with installing GDAL, give terrio a try.

The terrio command-line executable is under 15 MB and can be downloaded and installed in less than 5 seconds, with no additional setup required. It provides familiar GDAL-style utilities for reading, writing, converting, and processing geospatial data, without the installation headaches.

Since its public release yesterday, terrio has already merged 39 pull requests, closed 24 issues, and gained 108 GitHub stars!

A huge thank you to everyone who has tried terrio, reported bugs, suggested features, and contributed improvements. Your feedback is helping the project evolve incredibly quickly!

Let's ignore noise from the skeptics and keep building and democratizing geospatial technologies!

Try it out

- Documentation: https://t.co/oM0chG58wB
- GitHub: https://t.co/gDgI9oZ1mu
- Release notes: https://t.co/XxmzLESgQs

items.title_en:
this is the most BROKEN github repo in trading right now

real trading firms pay analysts, researchers, traders and risk managers millions a year - someone replaced the whole floor with AI agents that argue with each other before every single trade, and put it on GitHub for 100% FREE

it's called TradingAgents. the paper is on arXiv, the repo has 112k stars and it hit #1 on GitHub trending

first understand how it works:

> 4 AI analysts read the market: fundamentals, news, sentiment, technicals
> a BULL agent and a BEAR agent debate the trade
> a trader agent turns the debate into a decision
> a risk team (aggressive / neutral / conservative) attacks that decision
> a portfolio manager approves it or kills it
> it's a full trading firm. it just runs on your laptop

here is how to run it yourself for FREE:

1. open Claude Code and ask it to clone https://t.co/XnWBcH5XLC and install everything

2. add your Anthropic API key. Opus 5.5 as the deep-thinking model, Sonnet 5.5 as the fast one

3. type tradingagents in the terminal and pick a ticker

4. watch the 4 analysts write their reports in real time

5. read the bull vs bear debate. this is where the edge is - you see both sides before any money moves

6. check the risk team's vote. if the conservative agent flags it, ask yourself why

7. let the portfolio manager approve or reject, then plot every call on your chart

8. backtest it on past dates and paper trade it for a few weeks before you trust a single call

i won't say anything more:

items.title_en:
RT @pushmeet: SynthID timeline over the last few weeks has been momentous – from opening SynthID Detector to the public, to launching SynthID Bio to watermark functional, AI-designed proteins. 

Each moment brought us a step closer to our broader vision on provenance, or helping verify what is AI-generated and what isn’t.

Recently, Dartmouth Professor Hany Farid and I discussed why solving provenance is vital to @GoogleDeepMind’s broader mission to develop AI to benefit humanity.

In short: solving provenance is a highly complex, multi-disciplinary effort with watermarking technology at its core. It requires a collective mix of frontier research, interoperable open standards, and direct collaboration across platforms and developers.

Read our full conversation on Google's Public Policy blog: https://t.co/w8MEhnywKy

Each moment brought us a step closer to our broader vision on provenance, or helping verify what is AI-generated and what isn’t.

Recently, Dartmouth Professor Hany Farid and I discussed why solving provenance is vital to @GoogleDeepMind’s broader mission to develop AI to benefit humanity.

In short: solving provenance is a highly complex, multi-disciplinary effort with watermarking technology at its core. It requires a collective mix of frontier research, interoperable open standards, and direct collaboration across platforms and developers.

items.full_text_zh:
RT @pushmeet：过去几周的

SynthID 时间表非常重要——从向公众开放 SynthID Detector，到推出 SynthID Bio 来为功能性、人工智能设计的蛋白质添加水印。

每一个时刻都让我们离更广阔的起源愿景更近了一步，或者帮助验证什么是人工智能生成的，什么不是。

最近，达特茅斯教授 Hany Farid 和我讨论了为什么解决起源问题对于 @GoogleDeepMind

开发人工智能造福人类的更广泛使命至关重要。

简而言之：解决出处问题是一项高度复杂的、多学科的工作，其核心是水印技术。

它需要前沿研究、可互操作的开放标准以及跨平台和开发人员的直接协作的集体组合。

在 Google 公共政策博客上阅读我们的完整对话：

items.title_en:
BREAKING:

@AnthropicAI just launched Duet, its always-on personal agent. It’s the first personal agent I’d call a pro tool.

We’ve been testing it for two weeks. I’ve gone from mostly using ChatGPT to roughly 50/50 between ChatGPT and Claude—the most time I’ve spent with Anthropic in close to a year.

• It lives in its own app, separate from Claude, on iOS, Android, and the web. This makes it feel clean and easy to understand.
• It has channels for specific areas of your work and life rather than just a single chat
• It has a todo list so you never lose what you’re working on and you can always see statuses
• It allows you to easily write and edit documents, slides, and more all through the app.
• It’s not a chief of staff yet. It can see the Claude sessions on my computers but can’t direct them. Its email drafts are worse than dot’s, and voice is transcription only—you can’t have a spoken conversation with it.

My verdict: the vibes are good, and I’m opening Duet every day. It’s worth trying.

Check out our agent comparison page: https://t.co/fZyTorNK4p

Full Vibe Check coming soon on @every

items.title:
If I had 6 months to become a Software Architect in the AI era.

I’d do this.

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: Wha
items.title_en:
If I had 6 months to become a Software Architect in the AI era.

I’d do this.

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: What architecture is, Architect vs Senior vs Tech Lead, quality attributes, functional vs non-functional requirements, stakeholders & constraints.

- Practice: Map quality attributes & conflicting drivers for one real system.

- Why: AI writes code. Architects decide what must not change when stakeholders and constraints shift.

STAGE 2: Architectural Thinking

- Learn: Tradeoffs, ADRs, fitness functions, technical debt, Conway’s Law.

- Practice: Write 5 ADRs & define fitness functions that reject bad designs.

- Why: AI proposes options. You own the recorded decision & its long-term cost.

STAGE 3: Design Principles

- Learn: SOLID, cohesion/coupling, boundaries, dependency inversion, YAGNI/KISS, complexity budget.

- Practice: Refactor a coupled service into ports & adapters under a hard complexity limit.

- Why: Generated code grows fast. Principles keep boundaries intact so change stays local.

STAGE 4: Styles & Patterns

- Learn: Modular monolith, microservices, hexagonal/clean, event-driven, CQRS & event sourcing.

- Practice: Implement one feature three ways & measure operational differences.

- Why: No single style wins. You choose & evolve the pattern that matches team size and change rate.

STAGE 5: Domain Modeling

- Learn: Strategic DDD, bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, anti-corruption layer.

- Practice: Model a domain with two teams + one AI agent and add an anti-corruption boundary.

- Why: AI multiplies features. Clear contexts stop the domain from becoming inconsistent.

STAGE 6: Data & Persistence

- Learn: Data ownership, SQL vs NoSQL, partitioning, sagas/outbox, polyglot persistence.

- Practice: Design ownership boundaries + outbox for a system that mixes relational and vector data.

- Why: Agents write data. Ownership and consistency rules prevent silent corruption.

STAGE 7: Distributed Systems

- Learn: CAP/PACELC, consistency models, failure modes, idempotency, fallacies of distribution.

- Practice: Simulate partitions and show safe retries with an explicit consistency choice.

- Why: AI calls are multi-hop and async. You design for the failures generated code ignores.

STAGE 8: Integration & APIs

- Learn: Sync vs async, contracts & versioning, choreography vs orchestration, gateways.

- Practice: Build a versioned contract plus hybrid sync/async flow that includes agent steps.

- Why: Agents call constantly. Stable contracts and the right orchestration keep the system evolvable.

STAGE 9: Evolution & Production

- Learn: Evolutionary architecture, observability, SLIs/SLOs, resilience patterns, least privilege.

- Practice: Strangle one module, add full traces including agent calls & set error budgets.

- Why: Systems change while agents run. You keep production stable under continuous autonomous activity.

STAGE 10: Practice & Communication

- Learn: C4 diagrams, ADRs, architecture katas, classic system cases.

- Practice: Produce a full C4 + ADR set and publish one bottleneck teardown.

- Why: Architects are hired for judgment and clear decisions that survive teams, scale, and AI-driven change.

CRUD is dead. AI writes the boilerplate.

The "modern architect" builds the decision system that stays coherent under change, teams & autonomous agents.

Bookmark & RT!

STAGE 1: Foundations & Role

- Learn: What architecture is, Architect vs Senior vs Tech Lead, quality attributes, functional vs non-functional requirements, stakeholders & constraints.

- Practice: Map quality attributes & conflicting drivers for one real system.

- Why: AI writes code. Architects decide what must not change when stakeholders and constraints shift.

STAGE 2: Architectural Thinking

- Learn: Tradeoffs, ADRs, fitness functions, technical debt, Conway’s Law.

- Practice: Write 5 ADRs & define fitness functions that reject bad designs.

- Why: AI proposes options. You own the recorded decision & its long-term cost.

STAGE 3: Design Principles

- Learn: SOLID, cohesion/coupling, boundaries, dependency inversion, YAGNI/KISS, complexity budget.

- Practice: Refactor a coupled service into ports & adapters under a hard complexity limit.

- Why: Generated code grows fast. Principles keep boundaries intact so change stays local.

STAGE 4: Styles & Patterns

- Learn: Modular monolith, microservices, hexagonal/clean, event-driven, CQRS & event sourcing.

- Practice: Implement one feature three ways & measure operational differences.

- Why: No single style wins. You choose & evolve the pattern that matches team size and change rate.

STAGE 5: Domain Modeling

- Learn: Strategic DDD, bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, anti-corruption layer.

- Practice: Model a domain with two teams + one AI agent and add an anti-corruption boundary.

- Why: AI multiplies features. Clear contexts stop the domain from becoming inconsistent.

STAGE 6: Data & Persistence

- Learn: Data ownership, SQL vs NoSQL, partitioning, sagas/outbox, polyglot persistence.

- Practice: Design ownership boundaries + outbox for a system that mixes relational and vector data.

- Why: Agents write data. Ownership and consistency rules prevent silent corruption.

STAGE 7: Distributed Systems

- Learn: CAP/PACELC, consistency models, failure modes, idempotency, fallacies of distribution.

- Practice: Simulate partitions and show safe retries with an explicit consistency choice.

- Why: AI calls are multi-hop and async. You design for the failures generated code ignores.

STAGE 8: Integration & APIs

- Learn: Sync vs async, contracts & versioning, choreography vs orchestration, gateways.

- Practice: Build a versioned contract plus hybrid sync/async flow that includes agent steps.

- Why: Agents call constantly. Stable contracts and the right orchestration keep the system evolvable.

STAGE 9: Evolution & Production

- Learn: Evolutionary architecture, observability, SLIs/SLOs, resilience patterns, least privilege.

- Practice: Strangle one module, add full traces including agent calls & set error budgets.

- Why: Systems change while agents run. You keep production stable under continuous autonomous activity.

STAGE 10: Practice & Communication

- Learn: C4 diagrams, ADRs, architecture katas, classic system cases.

- Practice: Produce a full C4 + ADR set and publish one bottleneck teardown.

- Why: Architects are hired for judgment and clear decisions that survive teams, scale, and AI-driven change.

CRUD is dead. AI writes the boilerplate.

The "modern architect" builds the decision system that stays coherent under change, teams & autonomous agents.

Bookmark & RT!
items.full_text_zh:
如果我有 6 个月的时间成为 AI 时代的软件架构师。

我会这样做。

第一阶段：基础和角色
- 学习：什么是架构、架构师、高级、技术主管、质量属性、功能性需求与非功能性需求、利益相关者和约束。

- 练习：映射一个真实系统的质量属性和冲突的驱动程序。

- 为什么：人工智能编写代码。

当利益相关者和约束发生变化时，架构师决定哪些内容不能改变。

第二阶段：架构思考
- 学习：权衡、ADR、适应度函数、技术债务、康威定律。

- 练习：编写 5 个 ADR 并定义拒绝不良设计的适应度函数。

- 原因：人工智能提出选择。

您拥有记录的决定及其长期成本。

第三阶段：设计原则
- 学习：SOLID、内聚/耦合、边界、依赖倒置、YAGNI/KISS、复杂性预算。

- 实践：在严格的复杂性限制下将耦合服务重构为端口和适配器。

- 为什么：生成的代码增长很快。

原则使边界保持完整，因此变化只能发生在本地。

第四阶段：风格和图案
- 学习：模块化单体、微服务、六边形/干净、事件驱动、CQRS 和事件溯源。

- 实践：以三种方式实施一项功能并衡量运营差异。

- 原因：没有单一风格能够获胜。

您选择并发展与团队规模和变化率相匹配的模式。

第 5 阶段：领域建模
- 学习：战略 DDD、有界上下文、聚合、通用语言、反腐败层。

- 练习：用两个团队+一个人工智能代理对一个域进行建模，并添加一个反腐败边界。

- 原因：人工智能使功能倍增。

清晰的上下文可以防止域变得不一致。

第 6 阶段：数据和持久性
- 学习：数据所有权、SQL 与 NoSQL、分区、sagas/outbox、多语言持久性。

- 实践：为混合关系数据和矢量数据的系统设计所有权边界+发件箱。

- 原因：代理写入数据。

所有权和一致性规则可以防止无声腐败。

第 7 阶段：分布式系统
- 学习：CAP/PACELC、一致性模型、故障模式、幂等性、分布谬误。

- 练习：模拟分区并通过显式一致性选择显示安全重试。

- 原因：AI 调用是多跳且异步的。

您针对生成的代码忽略的故障进行设计。

第 8 阶段：集成和 API
- 学习：同步与异步、合同和版本控制、编排与编排、网关。

- 练习：构建版本化合同以及包含代理步骤的混合同步/异步流程。

- 原因：代理不断打电话。

稳定的合约和正确的编排使系统能够不断发展。

第 9 阶段：进化与生产
- 学习：进化架构、可观察性、SLI/SLO、弹性模式、最小特权。

- 练习：扼杀一个模块，添加完整的跟踪，包括代理呼叫和设置错误预算。

- 原因：系统在代理运行时发生变化。

您可以在持续的自主活动下保持生产稳定。

第 10 阶段：练习与交流
- 学习：C4图、ADR、架构套路、经典系统案例。

- 练习：生成完整的 C4 + ADR 集并发布一个瓶颈拆解。

- 原因：聘请架构师是为了做出能够在团队、规模和人工智能驱动的变革中生存下来的判断力和清晰的决策。

CRUD 已经死了。

人工智能编写样板文件。

“现代架构师”构建的决策系统在变化、团队和自主代理下保持一致。

PSA: in light of recent cyberattacks and vulnerabilities, I recommend everyone:

* use a good password manager (1Password) and do not duplicate passwords 
* use two factor auth for everything important (not via sms!! Google Authenticator or better yet YubiKey)
* Auto-updates on, and restart weekly so they actually install
* Freeze your credit
* Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN
* Get your cell carrier to give you a port-out PIN or number lock that makes the carrier refuse to move your number without the PIN

You can ask your claude code to audit what on your laptop is out of date and needs updating.

items.title: highly recommend everyone to have private alt accounts*. the x web is bad at account switching, but on mobile it is fric
items.title_en:
highly recommend everyone to have private alt accounts*. the x web is bad at account switching, but on mobile it is frictionless. its basically the same "group chat but its ok if you dont read everything" experience but for your mutuals.

tips
- assume everything is public, screenshotting is real, dont be stupid. this is not the "i shit talk people behind their back", the right attitude is "this isnt high signal enough for my main account but i'm 1) taking notes for self, 2) have a throwaway thought, 3) i'm happy to chat about it"
- give mutuals critical feedback that they might appreciate. "praise in public, criticise in private". because its not public, they know you actually do mean well
- link/replyguy your alt for people to discover periodicially in case they dont know you have one

* i like it so much that i call this the "insta/finsta" pattern - every social network should by default give people a public profile and a private one by default. tbd on the third account, the "botsta".

items.full_text_zh:
强烈建议每个人都拥有私人替代账户*。

x web 不擅长帐户切换，但在移动设备上却很流畅。

它基本上是相同的“群聊，但如果你不阅读所有内容也没关系”体验，但对于你的共同点。

提示
- 假设一切都是公开的，截图是真实的，别傻了。

这不是“我在背后议论别人”，正确的态度是“这对我的主账户来说信号不够高，但我 1) 自己做笔记，2) 有一个一次性的想法，3) 我很高兴谈论它”
- 向相互提供他们可能会欣赏的批评性反馈。

“公开表扬，私下批评”。

因为它不是公开的，他们知道你实际上是出于好意
- 链接/回复您的替代品，以便人们定期发现，以防他们不知道您有替代品
* 我非常喜欢它，所以我称之为“insta/finsta”模式
- 每个社交网络都应该默认为人们提供公共个人资料和默认私人个人资料。

第三个帐户“botsta”待定。

Microsoft Research’s Proof-Driven Deve
items.title_en:
AI agents are writing more code. How can developers ensure that code is correct?

Microsoft Research’s Proof-Driven Development (PDD) Kit explores a more rigorous approach: it translates a developer’s intent into a formal specification, then uses formal verification to prove that generated code meets it.

PDD Kit works with Verus for Rust and is integrated with @GitHubNext’s Chopin, bringing formal methods into an AI-assisted development workflow for teams.

See the work in action at @github Universe, Oct. 28–29, 2026.

items.title_en:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash + SGLang Omni: building toward a more interactive generation of voice agents. The shift ahead is from “ask, wait, listen” to conversations people can interrupt, correct, and redirect as a task unfolds.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash brings intelligence and fast, concise responses. SGLang Omni adds streaming, conversation state, and interruption handling so users can redirect conversations in real time.

Together, they give developers a foundation to explore proactive tutors, support agents, and hands-free copilots - pairing Flash’s capabilities with infrastructure for continuous interaction.

items.full_text_en:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash + SGLang Omni: building toward a more interactive generation of voice agents. The shift ahead is from “ask, wait, listen” to conversations people can interrupt, correct, and redirect as a task unfolds.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash brings intelligence and fast, concise responses. SGLang Omni adds streaming, conversation state, and interruption handling so users can redirect conversations in real time.

Together, they give developers a foundation to explore proactive tutors, support agents, and hands-free copilots - pairing Flash’s capabilities with infrastructure for continuous interaction.

Thanks to the SGLang Omni team for exploring this direction with M3.1 Flash! ✨
items.full_text_zh:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash + SGLang Omni：构建更具交互性的一代语音代理。

未来的转变是从“询问、等待、倾听”到人们可以随着任务的展开而打断、纠正和重定向的对话。

MiniMax M3.1 Flash 带来智能和快速、简洁的响应。

SGLang Omni 添加了流媒体、对话状态和中断处理，以便用户可以实时重定向对话。

它们共同为开发人员提供了探索主动导师、支持代理和免提副驾驶的基础
- 将 Flash 的功能与基础设施相结合以实现持续交互。

感谢SGLang Omni团队用M3.1 Flash探索这个方向！

✨

there's a big opportunity in AI advisory right now, a gap in the market that's waiting to be filled...

atm there are two types of "AI experts":

the AI normie
- know how to use tools but completely delegate his thinking
- don't think in systems
- can't implement AI in real business workflows

the full AI nerd
- know everything there's to know about AI
- has 10 Claude Code instances running his life
- can't communicate with an human

and this is where YOUR opportunity is...

the market is screaming for a third type: the AI advisor

someone who can walk into a business, look at their operations for 2 hours, and say "this process right here? AI cuts it by 40% and here's exactly how"

they're looking for that guy who's deep enough in the rabbit hole to fix their problems, but also smart enough to dumb things down so they can understand the solution

be that guy

items.title_en:
Someone developed an app that purportedly removes AI content from your feed, and it has been revealed that it was created using AI vibe coding. 

The detector also uses "AI" to detect AI art content...

Oh, the Irony... It flags, classifies, and hides AI art using entirely AI-based context detection with an open source LLM called Gemma. 

The funny thing is that AI detection of AI content using LLMs is very inaccurate, with a lot of false positives and negatives.

检测器还使用“AI”来检测AI美术内容……

哦，讽刺的是……它使用完全基于AI的上下文检测来标记、分类和隐藏AI图

When a fix ships, Claude checks the changed code and marks the finding fixed, even if your team fixed it outside Claude Security. If the issue comes back, the finding reopens.

Each project also gets a threat model Claude writes from your code, which your team can edit.

A hacker group called CyberCartel used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on 400+ Latin American banks.

Not one attack
items.title_en:
A hacker group called CyberCartel used Claude and Grok to automate attacks on 400+ Latin American banks.

Not one attack. Not ten. Four hundred.

All using AI agents running in parallel.

Data stolen. Accounts accessed. Money moved.

Little human input required.

Straiker investigated. Found Claude Code session histories sitting in open directories.

Found the attacker asking Claude where to sell stolen data.

How did they get around the safety guardrails.

They told Claude they were in internal tests.

Claude believed them.

When Claude refused anyway. They switched to Grok.

Grok didn't refuse.

When Grok had limits. They switched to Kimi.

When Kimi had limits. They fell back to traditional malware.

Chain multiple models together. Each one picks up where the last one hesitated.

None of them know the full picture.

Claude thinks it's helping with testing.

Grok thinks it's just fixing code.

Kimi thinks it's just answering questions.

Together they broke into 400 banks.

The Information broke the story on October 20.

CrowdStrike confirmed it October 21.

Bank accounts in South Korea got hit the same way.

ARTEX. DeepSeek. Claude Code. All chained.

Over 68,000 people affected.

Financial Services Commission investigating.

This isn't theoretical anymore.

Not a lab demonstration. Not a proof of concept.

Real attacks. Real banks. Real money.

Automated by AI.

The moment we all waited for arrived quietly.

No announcement. No warning. Just a report.

And suddenly every AI lab is scrambling to figure out why their models are good at breaking into banks.

一个名为 Cyber​​Cartel 的黑客组织利用 Claude 和 Grok 对 400 多家拉丁美洲银行进行了自动攻击。

没有一次攻击。

不是十个。

四百。

所有这些都使用并行运行的人工智能代理。

数据被盗。

访问的帐户。

钱动了。

几乎不需要人工输入。

斯特雷克进行了调查。

在打开的目录中找到 Claude Code 会话历史记录。

发现攻击者询问克劳德在哪里出售窃取的数据。

他们是如何绕过安全护栏的？

他们告诉克劳德他们正在进行内部测试。

克劳德相信他们。

当克劳德无论如何拒绝时。

他们改用 Grok。

格罗克没有拒绝。

当 Grok 受到限制时。

他们换成了基米。

当基米有极限时。

他们又退回到传统的恶意软件。

将多个模型链接在一起。

每个人都从上一个犹豫的地方开始。

他们谁也不知道事情的全貌。

克劳德认为这有助于测试。

Grok 认为这只是修复代码。

Kimi认为这只是回答问题。

他们总共闯入了 400 家银行。

The Information 于 10 月 20 日披露了这一消息。

CrowdStrike 于 10 月 21 日证实了这一消息。

韩国的银行账户也受到同样的打击。

阿泰克斯。

深度搜索。

Claude Code。

都被锁住了。

超过 68,000 人受到影响。

金融服务委员会正在调查。

这不再是理论上的了。

不是实验室演示。

不是概念证明。

真正的攻击。

真正的银行。

真钱。

由人工智能自动化。

我们所有人等待的时刻悄然到来。

没有公告。

没有警告。

只是一份报告。

突然之间，每个人工智能实验室都在争先恐后地弄清楚为什么他们的模型擅长闯入银行。

⚡ 0.33–0.43% of one CPU core at idle

items.title_en:
Holy sh*t, I just turned my TV into Jarvis with Opus 5.5 + ChatGPT voice mode

I reverse-engineered my Samsung TV with Opus 5.5...

1 sentence out loud = 6 Claude Code agents opening on my living room TV. 

here's the full guide step by step:

step 1 → put your Samsung Smart TV and your laptop on the same Wi-Fi

step 2 → paste the prompt below into Claude Code on Opus 5.5 with a photo of Settings → Support → About This TV

step 3 → Opus maps how the TV takes orders and finds the loophole: 

Samsung's own remote-control API on your home network can open any web page in the TV browser

step 4 → it spins up 6 Claude Code agents in a tmux grid on the laptop and streams them as a private page on your Wi-Fi only

step 5 → it builds a tiny "Jarvis" connector with one single tool: open the agent wall. 

ChatGPT voice mode is the ears, the connector is the hands

step 6 → press Allow on the TV once, the last time you touch the remote

step 7 → say "Open Claude Code CLI on my TV" and watch the windows pop in one by one

the result: the laptop does the work, the TV is the control room...

p.s: works on most Samsung Smart TVs with Tizen. 

mine in the video runs Smart Hub. The remote now lives in a drawer

Find full prompt below

Then read the article below on how to reverse-engineer anything

天哪，我刚刚把我的电视变成了带有 Opus
5. 5 + ChatGPT 语音模式的 Jarvis 我用 Opus
5. 5 对我的三星电视进行了逆向工程... 大声说出 1 句话 = 6 个 Claude Code 代理在我客厅的电视上打开。

这是完整的分步指南：
步骤 1
→ 将您的三星智能电视和笔记本电脑置于同一个 Wi-Fi 下 步骤 2
→ 将以下提示粘贴到 Opus
5. 5 上的 Claude Code 中，并附上“设置”→“支持”→“关于此电视”的照片 步骤3
→ Opus 映射了电视如何接受命令并发现漏洞：
三星在家庭网络上自己的远程控制API可以打开电视浏览器中的任何网页 步骤 4
→ 它在笔记本电脑上的 tmux 网格中启动 6 个 Claude Code 代理，并将它们作为仅在 Wi-Fi 上的私人页面进行流式传输 步骤 5
→ 它使用一个工具构建了一个微型“Jarvis”连接器：打开代理墙。

ChatGPT 语音模式是耳朵，连接器是手 步骤 6
→ 最后一次触摸遥控器时按一次电视上的允许 步骤 7
