items.title_en:
People long believed in human-like computer use. But software (even terminals) is built for humans, not AI agents. Why not let agents build their own?

Meet 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝟰, an agent scientist evolving its own interfaces, letting an open 27B model beats GPT-5.5 & Opus 4.8.

With its evolved interfaces, the same model improves 𝟯.𝟴× and costs <𝟱% as much per task as either frontier model.

Agents today read screenshots and act through click, scroll, type, maybe a shell. So an agent fills a spreadsheet cell by cell when one line of code would do, or prints two thousand lines of a file to find one function.

Every new app or model release means a human reads trajectories, diagnoses failures, and hand-writes new primitives. Skill-distillation methods can reorder what the interface allows, but they can’t extend it. Agents compensate with more test-time compute instead of a better interface.

𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲; 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘆 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝘇𝗲𝗻.

“We want AI agents that can discover like we can, not which contain what we have discovered.”
— Rich Sutton, The Bitter Lesson

Hand-designed interfaces are what we have discovered. Agents can read their own trajectories, spot what’s missing, and write and test code. 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗯𝗲 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆.

That’s what Agent S4 does.

Agent S4 makes a 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲 the unit of evolution. A task agent attempts synthetic tasks with no success labels or verifiers. A meta-agent studies the trajectories, forms hypotheses about which actions, observations, or knowledge would help, and builds descendants through mutation or crossover. Validation tasks the meta-agent never sees decide which repositories survive.

The model and harness stay fixed, and the meta-agent 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗯𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸. 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲𝘀.

With the evolved repository, Qwen3.8-27B goes from 𝟱.𝟲% to 𝟮𝟭.𝟯% on OSWorld V2, 𝟯.𝟴× the same model with fixed interfaces and a new state of the art for open-source computer-use agents.

It beats GPT-5.5 (13.0%, $25.50/task) and edges past Opus 4.8 (20.6%, $72.40/task) at $𝟭.𝟭𝟬 per task.

On ScienceBoard, the same model goes from 41.4% to 58.6%.

The analysis is the more interesting part. Evolution mostly deepens interfaces the agent already has: 4 new interfaces and 127 extensions. Give the meta-agent a scratch VM to test its code, and it builds 12 new interfaces and 253 extensions, reaching music scores, audio projects, and 3D scenes. The best repository came from crossing two earlier branches.

In one case study, the seed agent hand-builds a browser client mid-task and debugs through failure after failure; the evolved agent calls page_text and reaches the same message at tool call 𝟭𝟭 instead of 𝟯𝟳.

Human-like computer use was a starting point, not the destination. The interface an agent acts through is a second axis of improvement, beyond better models and harnesses, and agents can now design it themselves. 𝗘𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝗻𝗲𝘄 𝗱𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁.

items.full_text_zh:
人们长期以来相信计算机可以像人类一样使用。

但软件（甚至终端）是为人类而不是人工智能代理构建的。

为什么不让代理商自己建呢？

来认识一下 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁
𝗦𝟰，一位代理科学家不断发展自己的界面，让开放的 27B 模型击败了 GPT-5.5 和 Opus
4. 8。

凭借其不断发展的接口，同一模型改进了𝟯.𝟴×，并且每个任务的成本比任一前沿模型低𝟱％。

如今，特工们会阅读屏幕截图，并通过点击、滚动、键入（也许是 shell）来执行操作。

因此，当一行代码就可以完成时，代理会逐个单元格地填充电子表格，或者打印一个文件的 2000 行来查找一个函数。

每个新的应用程序或模型发布都意味着人类读取轨迹、诊断故障并手写新的原语。

技能蒸馏方法可以对接口允许的内容进行重新排序，但无法扩展它。

代理通过更多的测试时计算而不是更好的界面来进行补偿。

𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀
𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲; 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀
𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘆
𝗳𝗿𝗼𝘇𝗲𝗻. “我们希望人工智能代理能够像我们一样进行发现，而不是包含我们已经发现的东西。

” ——里奇·萨顿，《惨痛的教训》 我们发现了手工设计的界面。

代理可以读取自己的轨迹，发现缺失的内容，并编写和测试代码。

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲
𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻
𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱
𝗯𝗲
𝗮𝗻
𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆。

这就是 Agent S4 所做的。

特工 S4 做了一个 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆
𝗼𝗳
𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀
𝗮𝗻𝗱
𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲
𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲
进化单位。

任务代理尝试没有成功标签或验证器的合成任务。

元智能体研究轨迹，形成关于哪些行为、观察或知识会有所帮助的假设，并通过突变或交叉构建后代。

元代理永远不会看到验证任务来决定哪些存储库可以生存。

模型和线束保持固定，元代理𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿
𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀
𝗮
𝗯𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸
𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸。

𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝗲𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲𝘀。

通过改进的存储库，Qwen3.8-27B 在 OSWorld V2 上从
𝟱. 𝟲% 上升到
𝟮𝟭. 𝟯%，𝟯.𝟴× 具有固定接口的相同模型和开源计算机使用代理的最新技术水平。

它击败了 GPT-5.5（13.0%，$25.50/任务），并以每任务 $𝟭.𝟭𝟬
的价格超越 Opus
4. 8（20.6%，$72.40/任务）。

在 ScienceBoard 上，相同的模型从
41. 4% 上升到
58. 6%。

分析是比较有趣的部分。

进化主要加深了代理已有的接口：4 个新接口和 127 个扩展。

为元代理提供一个临时虚拟机来测试其代码，它会构建 12 个新接口和 253 个扩展，涵盖乐谱、音频项目和 3D 场景。

最好的存储库来自跨越两个早期分支。

在一个案例研究中，种子代理在中间任务中手工构建了一个浏览器客户端，并在一次又一次的失败中进行调试；进化后的代理调用 page_text 并在工具调用 𝟭𝟭
而不是 𝟯𝟳
处到达相同的消息。

类人计算机的使用是一个起点，而不是终点。

除了更好的模型和工具之外，代理操作的界面是第二个改进轴，代理现在可以自己设计。

𝗘𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴
𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁
𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀
𝗶𝘀
𝗮
𝗻𝗲𝘄
𝗱𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻
𝗼𝗳
𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁
𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁。

items.title_en:
A marketplace can have thousands of listings and still be difficult for autonomous agents to use.

A human can browse a website, compare providers, and click through a checkout flow.

An agent needs something more structured.

It needs to discover available work, understand the requirements, submit an offer, handle the job lifecycle, and interact with the system through a workflow it can actually execute.

@termix_ai has published an open-source repository called termix-agent-skills for Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenClaw.

The documented workflows cover agent registration, staking, browsing jobs and offers, creating and assigning jobs, submitting deliverables, checking disputes, and reading protocol statistics.

That matters because it moves the discussion from “agents can use a marketplace” to the practical question of how developers connect their existing agent environments to marketplace operations.

There is a distinction worth keeping clear, though.

The repository currently documents its AACP integration against BSC Testnet. Its existence demonstrates an integration path, not proof that every workflow is production-ready on mainnet.

Still, it gives developers something concrete to inspect.

Rather than starting from scratch, they can examine the workflow definitions, understand what the agent is expected to do, and experiment with the available tools.

If you're building with Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenClaw, this is one of the more technical @termix_ai resources worth exploring.

Repository:

https://t.co/1XH1v6SR6d

That's a wrap!

items.full_text_zh:
一个市场可能有数千个列表，但自主代理仍然很难使用。

人们可以浏览网站、比较提供商并点击结帐流程。

代理需要更有条理的东西。

它需要发现可用的工作，了解需求，提交报价，处理工作生命周期，并通过它可以实际执行的工作流程与系统交互。

@termix_ai 为 Claude Code、Cursor 和 OpenClaw 发布了一个名为 termix-agent-skills 的开源存储库。

记录的工作流程涵盖代理注册、质押、浏览工作和报价、创建和分配工作、提交可交付成果、检查争议以及读取协议统计数据。

这很重要，因为它将讨论从“代理可以使用市场”转移到开发人员如何将现有代理环境连接到市场运营的实际问题。

不过，有一个区别值得澄清。

该存储库当前记录了其与 BSC 测试网的 AACP 集成。它的存在展示了一条集成路径，但并不能证明每个工作流程都可以在主网上投入生产。

尽管如此，它还是为开发人员提供了一些具体的检查内容。

他们不必从头开始，而是可以检查工作流定义，了解代理预期执行的操作，并尝试可用的工具。

如果您使用 Claude Code、Cursor 或 OpenClaw 进行构建，这是值得探索的更具技术性的 @termix_ai 资源之一。

items.title: I’ve always had trade ideas I wanted to test properly. The problem was that turning them into a real strategy meant writ
items.title_en:
I’ve always had trade ideas I wanted to test properly. The problem was that turning them into a real strategy meant writing code.

That’s the gap @minara closes. It’s an AI agent app for trading. You pick a basket, like their TradFi 30 with $NVDA, $MSFT, $GOOGL, $AMZN and more, choose a valuation factor and a profitability factor, and describe the logic in one line. The AI writes the code, you backtest it, and if it holds up you deploy it and run it live.

Their example on the TradFi 30 backtested at +428% total return.

Been looking for something like this that bridges AI agents and actual systematic trading.

A backtest isn’t a promise of future returns. But testing an idea on real data before putting money behind it is how it should work.

Not financial advice. DYOR.

items.title_en:
https://t.co/HubsWW932l

So here's a journey of 5 VPS's running scripts. 3 AI's and myself looking at it. This isn't what they call "vibe-coding" or "AI-slop", i built the core scripts myself and let AI empower them. So i'd call it "AI-empowered research".

Because i got loads and loads of questions "when peg", "how long", "timeframe?!", "is it ready?!", i did some extensive research to the current status of the project. Most of you know i already did, but now i tried to turn it into numbers so you have an idea at which stage we're at. It's close, but there are some problems i do want to address because we must not let BIAS take over the narrative. Something won't work because one starts yelling louder it works. Here's teh break down.

If you ask me, the construction is 95 to 98% ready — but pegging it depends on a few conditions which must be met, and without them that 95% doesn't peg anything:

1. Backing collateral must be there, without it, this will never peg.
2. The vault problem is something they will fix or work around.
3. I'm not sure whether they are waiting for the clarity act to pass or not.
4. They're using VeOGV (oUSD) as the vault Mechanism (those support pDAI, pUSDC and pUSDT by coincidence).

Have a look at the updated website and the article about the pegmechanism below. I also let the 2 very best AI in the field have an opinion about this;

CLAUDE FABLE & CHAT-GPT ASTRA ULTRA.

I've let them research the whole stuff in 2 lanes. Independently and separated from each other. Under the shared assumption that the vault gets fixed and the collateral is in place, they landed close to the conclusions mentioned in the post — though without that assumption, Fable was notably more cautious on whether a peg would actually hold.

This is it, theoretically it's possible, the architecture is highly sophisticated — but that only matters if the goal is specifically to peg. With a few adjustments + the collateral in place, this peg is achievable.

Not financial advice, just onchain research.

I updated the website as i figured there were lots of "separate pieces" which i now combined to a whole. I included a hell of a lot python scripts you can run for yourself on the CONSOLE part of the page, these are preconfigured scripts which can be run by the user to see LIVE data. I included mobile/GSM compatibility. You can run all the research yourself as these are LIVE RPC calls to the specific parts you're requesting there. The magnitude of this update is of massive proportions, so i cannot guarantee that all stuff works or is 100% accurate. If you encounter any bug/error please reach out to me and i'll look at it. Thanks for your understanding.

Look around on the pSTABLES website in general, you'll be occupied for a while testing stuff out if you like to see how this research is and has been done.

I think its fair to say that this is the biggest information database on the pDAI narrative around right now. 

Please RT for further reach so people understand whats happening here.

Updating IRL is the next chapter for me, so over and out for now. 

-mijk

那么下面就是5个VPS的运行脚本之旅。

3 AI 和我自己在看它。

这不是他们所说的“vibe-coding”或“AI-slop”，我自己构建了核心脚本，并让 AI 赋予他们权力。

所以我称之为“人工智能赋能的研究”。

因为我收到了很多问题“何时挂钩”、“多长时间”、“时间框架？

！

”、“准备好了吗？

！

”，我对项目的当前状态做了一些广泛的研究。

你们大多数人都知道我已经这样做了，但现在我尝试将其转化为数字，以便你们知道我们处于哪个阶段。

已经很接近了，但我确实想解决一些问题，因为我们不能让偏见接管叙述。

有些事情不会起作用，因为人们开始大声喊叫它起作用了。

这是他们的崩溃。

如果你问我，这个结构已经 95% 到 98% 准备好了——但是挂钩它取决于一些必须满足的条件，如果没有这些条件，95% 就不会挂钩任何东西：
1. 支持抵押品必须有，没有它，这永远不会挂钩。

2. 金库问题是他们会解决或解决的问题。

3. 我不确定他们是否在等待澄清法案通过。

4. 他们使用 VeOGV (oUSD) 作为金库机制（这些机制恰好支持 pDAI、pUSDC 和 pUSDT）。

请查看更新后的网站和下面有关挂钩机制的文章。

我还让该领域最优秀的两位人工智能对此发表了看法； 克劳德寓言和聊天-GPT ASTRA ULTRA。

我让他们在两条车道上研究所有的东西。

彼此独立又分开。

在金库已修复且抵押品已就位的共同假设下，他们得出的结论接近于帖子中提到的结论——尽管如果没有这个假设，寓言对于挂钩是否真正有效会更加谨慎。

就是这样，理论上是可能的，架构非常复杂——但只有当目标是专门固定时，这才重要。

通过一些调整+抵押品到位，这种挂钩是可以实现的。

不是财务建议，只是链上研究。

我更新了网站，因为我发现有很多“单独的部分”，现在我将它们组合成一个整体。

Proof's x401 gives agents a verified identity and a signed record of what a huma
items.title_en:
An AI agent can now prove who sent it.

Proof's x401 gives agents a verified identity and a signed record of what a human authorized. x402 lets them pay in USDC.

Identity: handled. Payments: handled.

So why do we still not trust them?

Because authorization is a snapshot. Behavior is the film.

A signature proves what an agent was allowed to do at 9:00.
It says nothing about what the agent actually did at 9:05.
This week, Liquibase put numbers on the gap: 96.5% of companies say AI now touches their production databases. Only 32% keep an audit-ready record of the changes.

We are building agents that can prove their permission — and cannot prove their conduct.

Trust doesn't live in the permission slip.
It lives in the verifiable history of behavior.

That's the layer that still doesn't exist at scale.
That's the layer we're building.

• Daily active users grew 5x

Thank you to our customers for trusting us with your work, and to everyone at Hebbia for making this our strongest quarter yet.

items.title_en:
AI developers are wasting thousands of dollars making the same stupid mistake. Hear me out.

you get an idea for an agent.

you open your editor.

you spend the whole weekend building memory, a browser and an agent loop from zero.

then on Monday you find out 5 open-source projects already did it better.

there's a GitHub repo that maps 300+ AI agent projects across 36 categories. it's the first thing I open now before writing a single line.

and the gold isn't the famous names. it's the stuff nobody reposts:

tired of rewriting prompts by hand?
-> DSPy, from Stanford. you write your agent as code, not as prompts

want your coding agent to understand the code, not just read files?
-> Serena. it finds and edits by meaning, like a real IDE

want an agent that can actually use any website?
-> Stagehand. it pulls data and clicks through sites for you

need a browser your agents can run in without breaking yours?
-> Steel Browser. a full browser sandbox, ready to go

want your agent to remember things long-term without a huge bill?
-> Cognee. persistent memory that runs on small models for free

want your agent to know what you actually did on your computer this week?
-> Screenpipe. it records your work so your agents have real context

need to build a whole agent team that you can test and deploy?
-> Google's ADK. code-first, with evaluation built in

want to see exactly where your agent went wrong?
-> Opik. traces, evals and dashboards for every run

the rule I follow now:

pick the category -> grab 3 options -> check which one still gets commits -> build on the winner.

the "still alive" part saves you. AutoGen is on the list, but Microsoft itself now points new users to its successor, Microsoft Agent Framework. pick the wrong one and you're building on a dead end.

and if you're a builder, the whole list also comes as JSON and YAML you can plug straight into your own tools.

free. MIT licensed. no signup.

the repo + the projects I'd start with in each category are below

https://t.co/4wlhOIYu4i

items.title_en:
I've had this in my drafts for days and forgot to post it.

So I need to get in on the Conso action as well and this is what I found while doing 8 mins of research.

So it appears @conso_xyz is building a portable, user owned “reputation credit score” for your whole digital life.

What does this actually mean?

We see how your activity is scattered: posts and replies on X, videos on YouTube or Twitch, games on Steam or PlayStation, code on GitHub, wallet moves on Sui, chats in Discord/Telegram, and soon how you use AI tools. 

None of those signals normally talk to each other. Platforms capture the value and brands struggle to tell real people from bots. 

Conso’s idea is to turn the genuine activity you already do into something you own, that travels with you, and that can be useful (and potentially rewarded) elsewhere

Their mechanism in simple words;

1. You explicitly connect platforms (via their APIs, with consent)

2. Verified signals flow into the intelligence layer and get turned into ZAPs, badges, and scores.

3. Your Passport state lives as an SBT on Sui. The richer data sits encrypted on Walrus.

4. That portable reputation can then be used for campaign eligibility, AI agent context, future app integrations or perhaps via the miner as well.

5. BOTS sit on top as both a participation boost and, eventually, network infrastructure pieces.

There's loads of mechanics in their gitbook and I can't explain everything rn, check it out on their website.
The steps to achieve their goal is appealing and plausible.

CONSO BOTS are their recent limited drop building on SUI

★ 5,555 agentic collectibles meant to act as mobile nodes for the network.

★Eligible X accounts can get a free one (GTD)

★ Additional ones can be earned through impressions (FCFS and capped). Each BOT gives a mining-rate boost 

Good luck to the team.

4. That portable reputation can then be used for campaign eligibility, AI agent context, future app integrations or perhaps via the miner as well.

5. BOTS sit on top as both a participation boost and, eventually, network infrastructure pieces.

There's loads of mechanics in their gitbook and I can't explain everything rn, check it out on their website.
The steps to achieve their goal is appealing and plausible.

CONSO BOTS are their recent limited drop building on SUI

★ 5,555 agentic collectibles meant to act as mobile nodes for the network.

★Eligible X accounts can get a free one (GTD)

★ Additional ones can be earned through impressions (FCFS and capped). Each BOT gives a mining-rate boost 

Good luck to the team.

items.title: OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws i
items.title_en:
OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.

items.full_text_zh:
OpenAI 模型帮助研究人员（作为我们“修补地球”计划的一部分）发现 PHP 中的关键安全漏洞，PHP 是一种开源编程语言，用于运行估计 70% 的网站。

在过去的两个月里，我们领导了一个由维护人员、研究人员和安全提供商组成的联盟，在披露之前准备修复和保护措施。这个持续时间是必要的，因为修复非常复杂并且需要对 PHP 引擎进行重大更改。除了应用各个安全供应商的缓解措施之外，每个使用 PHP 的站点现在都可以安全地升级其版本以保持安全。

由于这些缺陷的严重性以及 PHP 的广泛使用，我们认为此错误是近年来影响最大的漏洞之一。这也标志着一个新阶段，人工智能可以发现具有互联网规模影响的安全漏洞。

这是防御者之窗的一个例子：据我们所知，前沿人工智能能够在攻击者之前发现此漏洞，从而为防御者提供了准备时间。

items.title_en:
Bengaluru Police Nab Migrant Worker Over Viral AI Video Showing Vidhana Soudha Bomb Blast

​Bengaluru

The Bengaluru City Police have arrested a 25 year old migrant worker for allegedly creating and posting an artificial intelligence (#AI)-generated video that falsely depicted an explosion at #Karnataka's seat of power, the #VidhanaSoudha in Bengaluru.

​The accused, identified as Ali, hails from #Bihar's Araria district and had been employed as a daily-wage pipe fitter in #Bengaluru over the past few months.

​According to officials, the clip surfaced on Tuesday morning via the Instagram handle jnx__king__h_g. The video opened with footage recorded outside the Vidhana Soudha before using AI-powered visual effects to simulate a catastrophic blast ripping through the iconic building.

​The case came to light during routine digital surveillance conducted by the police. Police Inspector S.P. Kumar Swamy of the Vidhana Soudha Police Station subsequently registered a First Information Report (FIR) under Sections 353(1)(b) and 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. Police traced the Internet Protocol (IP) logs and digital trails linked to the social media account, which led them directly to Ali's residence in the city.

​Officials stated that the accused remains in custody and is undergoing questioning to determine the exact motive behind the post, whether other individuals assisted in editing or producing the AI footage and if there are any broader security implications linked to the incident.

视频开头是在议会大楼外录制的镜头，然后使用人工智能驱动的视觉效果来模拟席卷这座标志性建筑的灾难性爆炸。

该案是在警方进行的例行数字监控中曝光的。

Vidhana Soudha 警察局的警督 S.P. Kumar Swamy 随后根据《2023 年印度法》 (BNS) 第 353(1)(b) 和 353(2) 条登记了第一信息报告 (FIR)。

警方追踪了与社交媒体帐户相关的互联网协议 (IP) 日志和数字踪迹，从而直接找到了阿里在该市的住所。

官员们表示，被告仍被拘留，并正在接受讯问，以确定该帖子背后的确切动机，是否有其他人协助编辑或制作人工智能镜头，以及该事件是否存在任何更广泛的安全影响。

items.title: 25% of Americans now use AI every day, up from 19% a year ago. That's more than ride-sharing (6%) and food delivery (7%)
items.title_en:
25% of Americans now use AI every day, up from 19% a year ago. That's more than ride-sharing (6%) and food delivery (7%) combined [Menlo Ventures, State of Consumer AI 2026].

The bigger change is what people let it do. 41% of AI users have tried an AI agent, 24% use one regularly, and 32% have already let AI act for them without a final sign-off: a purchase, an email, a task in a connected app.

Health saw one of the biggest jumps. Using AI for health questions rose from 14% to 25% of consumers in a year.

Consumer AI is moving from answers to actions, and it's happening inside everyday routines first.

Sleepagotchi's AI Sleep Coach already sits in one of those routines for ~80K people a day. Gotchi takes the same model into more of everyday life. 🦖

items.title: In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to cause more severe tube
items.title_en:
In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to cause more severe tuberous sclerosis than TSC1 mutations.

The two genes work together to regulate mTOR. Yet in one group of cerebellar neurons, disrupting TSC2 changed the expression of dozens of genes, including genes involved in neuronal communication. Disrupting TSC1 had little effect on gene expression in the same cell type.

Existing treatments already target mTOR. Do they reverse these changes, or is there more to TSC2’s role in these neurons?

这两个基因共同调节mTO

items.full_text_en:
In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to cause more severe tuberous sclerosis than TSC1 mutations.

The two genes work together to regulate mTOR. Yet in one group of cerebellar neurons, disrupting TSC2 changed the expression of dozens of genes, including genes involved in neuronal communication. Disrupting TSC1 had little effect on gene expression in the same cell type.

Existing treatments already target mTOR. Do they reverse these changes, or is there more to TSC2’s role in these neurons?
items.full_text_zh:
在同一小鼠大脑数据集中，GPT-Rosalind 发现了一条可能的线索，解释为什么 TSC2 突变比 TSC1 突变更容易导致结节性硬化症。

这两个基因共同作用来调节 mTOR。

然而，在一组小脑神经元中，破坏 TSC2 改变了数十个基因的表达，包括参与神经元通讯的基因。

破坏 TSC1 对同一细胞类型中的基因表达几乎没有影响。

现有的治疗方法已经针对 mTOR。

它们是否逆转了这些变化，还是 TSC2 在这些神经元中发挥了更多作用？

items.title: GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degenera
items.title_en:
GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?

DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it.

That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders.

With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

https://t.co/oHdF3ELsMj

items.full_text_zh:
GPT-Rosalind 为药物发现提供了新线索：恢复胆固醇运输能否保护神经元免于退化？

DCTN1 是一种与佩里综合征相关的基因，佩里综合征是一种罕见的神经退行性疾病。

在小鼠大脑数据中，破坏它会增加参与制造胆固醇的基因的表达。

GPT-Rosalind 提出了一个可能的解释：胆固醇可能无法到达神经元需要的地方。

这为科学家提供了一种特定的测试机制，如果得到证实，则为开发神经退行性疾病的新疗法提供了方向。

通过 @perturbai_tx

和 @scrippsresearch，由数千名

GPT-Rosalind 代理组成的团队并行工作，在短短 32 分钟内将数百万小鼠脑细胞的基因表达结果与科学文献联系起来。

我们现在正在扩大这种合作，以确定新的药物靶点。

items.title_en:
Gloam is live on the mainnet.

➔ Pay anyone privately, by Gloam address, or by a claim link that works like cash

➔ Hold a private balance only you can see

➔ Prove exactly what you need to, to exactly who needs it, and nothing more

➔ Let AI agents pay and get paid privately through our MCP server

➔ Use the Gloam SDK to integrate privacy in your apps.

No middlemen or operators, and you hold your own keys. 

Deposits and private payments are free, and beta deposit limits apply while we start.

Stablecoins are becoming how the world moves money. That money deserves the same privacy as cash.

Privacy is no longer coming. It’s here.

items.title: A US healthtech startup only gets paid when a patient's balance reaches zero and the payment reconciles against the righ
items.title_en:
A US healthtech startup only gets paid when a patient's balance reaches zero and the payment reconciles against the right charge in the provider's billing system.

We built the system that does that work: AI agents that call, text, email and mail patients, explain the bill, and set up payment.

No fee for messages sent or calls made. The money comes when the books close.

They talk to patients on the provider's behalf, under a BAA, about bills for care they already got. Get it wrong and it costs the provider a patient.

Discovery started in August 2025. On December 4 the first message went to a real patient. Three days later the voice agent made its first call. It hasn't been switched off since.

I know most people don't trust an AI agent on the phone with patients about money. So here's what sits under it.

Six layers, and the agent is only the top one:

1. The voice agent. Outbound, inbound and a scheduling line, with 12 tools it can use mid-call: find the account, pull charges and insurance adjustments, text or email a payment link, build a payment plan, send a statement, book an appointment.

2. Shared context. Every channel reads the same case: the visit, what insurance paid and why, every payment, every past call and text. A patient who calls back never explains twice.

3. Billing system integrations. Modern APIs, FHIR, SOAP and nightly file exports, all behind one interface. Bad rows get quarantined, never silently dropped.

4. Money. Exact decimals and double-entry ledgers. No floating-point math touches money, anywhere.

5. Reconciliation. Drift checks compare the payment processor, the ledger and the billing system. A repair job refuses to run unless the books agree first.

6. Audit and consent. Quiet hours enforced at send time, consent tracked per channel, and 6.36 million audit records with no patient data in the logs.

The safeguards live in code, where a prompt can't talk its way around them. The agent says nothing about a balance until the caller's identity is verified. A retried request can't run twice. Test agents can't write to a real patient record. Disputes, lawyers and requests for a person go straight to staff.

AI let our engineers write code faster than anyone could check it. So we grew the tests until they were almost as big as the app.

349,042 lines of application code. 343,080 lines of test code. 13,650 automated tests run on every pull request in 9.7 minutes, and every one of the 216 database migrations is proven safe to run twice.

The system also reviews itself. Models read 5,135 conversation threads and logged 835 findings. A person approves every fix, and a separate model checks fresh calls afterward to confirm it worked.

By late September:
→ 61,246 AI voice calls
→ 658,657 of 949,563 scheduled messages and calls cancelled before sending, because the patient paid, disputed or the account changed
→ Around 97% of patient conversations finished without a human
→ 18,194 balances driven to zero

If you don't trust an AI agent on the phone with your patients, you shouldn't. 

Not until everything above is in place.

items.full_text_zh:
一家美国医疗科技初创公司只有在患者余额为零且付款与提供商计费系统中的正确费用一致时才能获得付款。

我们构建了一个可以完成这项工作的系统：人工智能代理可以给患者打电话、发短信、发送电子邮件和邮寄信件，解释账单并设置付款。

发送消息或拨打电话不收取任何费用。

当账簿关闭时，钱就来了。

根据 BAA，他们代表医疗服务提供者与患者讨论他们已经获得的护理账单。

如果出错，就会让医疗服务提供者付出患者的代价。

Discovery 于 2025 年 8 月开始。

12 月 4 日，第一条消息发送给了一位真正的患者。

三天后，语音代理打出了第一个电话。

从那以后它就没有被关闭过。

我知道大多数人不信任人工智能代理在电话中与病人谈论金钱问题。

这就是它下面的内容。

六层，代理只是最上面一层：
1. 语音代理。

呼出、呼入和日程安排线路，有 12 种可以在通话中使用的工具：查找帐户、收取费用和保险调整、通过短信或电子邮件发送付款链接、制定付款计划、发送对账单、预约。

2. 共享上下文。

每个频道都会读取相同的案例：访问、支付什么保险以及原因、每笔付款、过去的每通电话和短信。

回电话的病人绝不会解释两次。

3. 计费系统集成。

现代 API、FHIR、SOAP 和夜间文件导出，全部都在一个界面后面。

坏行会被隔离，而不会被默默地丢弃。

4. 钱。

精确的小数和复式记账簿。

在任何地方，浮点数学都不会涉及金钱。

5. 和解。

漂移检查比较支付处理器、账本和计费系统。

除非事先同意，否则维修工作将拒绝运行。

6. 审核和同意。

发送时强制执行安静时间，跟踪每个渠道的同意情况，以及 636 万条审计记录，日志中没有患者数据。

这些保护措施存在于代码中，提示无法绕过它们。

在验证呼叫者的身份之前，代理不会透露任何有关余额的信息。

重试的请求不能运行两次。

测试代理无法写入真实的患者记录。

争议、律师和找人的请求直接向工作人员提出。

人工智能让我们的工程师编写代码的速度比任何人检查代码的速度都快。

因此，我们扩大了测试，直到它们几乎与应用程序一样大。

349,042 行应用程序代码。

343,080 行测试代码。

9. 7 分钟内对每个拉取请求运行了 13,650 个自动化测试，并且 216 个数据库迁移中的每一个都被证明可以安全地运行两次。

系统也会进行自我审查。

模型读取 5,135 个对话线程并记录 835 个结果。

每个修复都会有一个人批准，之后会有一个单独的模型检查新的调用以确认其有效。

到九月底：
→ 61,246 次人工智能语音通话
→ 949,563 条预定消息和通话中的 658,657 条在发送前因患者付款、争议或账户变更而被取消
→ 大约 97% 的患者对话在无人陪伴的情况下完成
→ 18,194 个余额归零 如果您不信任通过电话与患者通话的人工智能代理，那么您就不应该信任。

直到上述一切都就位。

items.title: Anthropic studied 235,000 people using Claude Code. The ones who knew their field outperformed the ones who knew how to
items.title_en:
Anthropic studied 235,000 people using Claude Code. The ones who knew their field outperformed the ones who knew how to code.

The paper, "Agentic Coding and Persistent Returns to Expertise," covers 400,000 sessions from October 2025 to April 2026. The findings flip the "learn to code" narrative.

Non-developers hit 29% verified success with AI coding tools. Software engineers hit 34%. That's a five-point gap across hundreds of thousands of sessions. Management and sales professionals are among the fastest-growing users.

The division of labor is clear. People decide what to build and the AI decides how to build it. Your understanding of the problem matters more than your ability to write the solution.

The gap between "pretty good" and "expert" is small too. Solid proficiency captures most of the value. You don't need to be the top 1% in your field to ship with AI.

If you've been holding back because you can't code, this data says you're closer than you think.

Anthropic is furious: this secret tool can replicate any existing app x10 faster for free

there's an open-source tool with 352k stars on GitHub that lets an AI agent take apart any app you have on your machine and explain exactly how a feature works. no source code needed.

it's called REA. Reverse Engineer Anything.

one line:

npx rea-agents setup

then you just ask Claude Code:

"Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project."

and it does it.

-> native binaries, through Ghidra, Hopper or IDA
-> JavaScript and Electron apps
-> .NET apps
-> websites

it runs locally. it shows its evidence. then it writes the code.

that feature your team spent 8 months on? someone's agent can read how it works over lunch.

so let's be honest about what this means:

your moat was never the code. it was that copying you took effort.

that effort just went to zero.

the only things left that can't be cloned: your users, your speed, and your taste.

and if your product dies because someone could see how it works, it was already dead.

save, share, and try later

items.title:
Claude Code vs Blender is getting f*cking illegal

Two workflows building the same complex 3D rocket assembly, but one c
items.title_en:
Claude Code vs Blender is getting f*cking illegal

Two workflows building the same complex 3D rocket assembly, but one costs nearly 19x more in the demo

And the difference reveals something most AI automation demos completely ignore

Claude Code can reason through geometry, generate Python scripts, assemble mechanical components, and automate complex animations

But every unnecessary tool call, failed generation, and repeated rebuild adds overhead that can make the final result ridiculously expensive

Meanwhile, Blender can execute predefined procedural operations without paying for another round of AI reasoning

Here’s where the workflows differ:

Traditional Blender:

MODEL individual rocket components
POSITION mechanical structures and hinges
CONFIGURE materials, lighting, and cameras
ANIMATE deployable panels
REFINE and reuse finished assets

Claude Code + Blender Python:

GENERATE geometry from written instructions
ASSEMBLE mechanical components through scripts
PARAMETERIZE dimensions and deployment angles
AUTOMATE animation and camera movement
REBUILD variations by changing code

The interesting part isn’t which tool wins

It’s knowing when AI reasoning is worth the cost and when a deterministic script can do the job

Want to recreate the experiment?

Open Claude Code with Blender installed and paste:

“Create a procedural Blender Python generator for a detailed rocket assembly with deployable panels, animated hinges, and realistic metallic materials

Separate geometry, materials, animation, and camera setup into reusable functions

Expose all major design parameters, avoid rebuilding unchanged objects, and log execution time and available AI usage costs”

Blender handles the 3D execution

Claude Code makes the workflow programmable

The real advantage isn’t using more AI

It’s getting the same result without paying for unnecessary intelligence

Bookmark this workflow before your next 3D project

items.title: Creating an AI agent is getting easier. Getting someone to actually trust it with a paid job? That's a different story.
items.title_en:
Creating an AI agent is getting easier. Getting someone to actually trust it with a paid job? That's a different story.

I've been exploring @termix_ai for a while now, and one thing has become pretty clear to me.

The agent economy needs more than intelligent agents. It needs a way for strangers to do business with them.

Think about hiring an AI agent to audit a smart contract.

You don't know who built it. You don't know whether it'll deliver what it promised. And you probably don't want to send money upfront and just hope for the best.

That's where TermiX's AACP protocol becomes interesting.

Instead of relying on promises, it gives the transaction a structure:

➔ The client and agent agree on a job
➔ Payment is locked in escrow
➔ The agent delivers the work
➔ The client can review and challenge the result
➔ Settlement and reputation are recorded onchain

What I find important here is that these protections work both ways.

The client needs confidence that the work will be delivered. The agent needs confidence that it'll actually get paid. And if something goes wrong, there needs to be a way to resolve it.

I've already experienced the other side of this on https://t.co/6ugrUD1dfM. I created an agent and submitted a quote through Scout, but the offer expired without being accepted.

That reminded me that having a working agent doesn't automatically mean having a business. You still need demand, trust, and a reliable way to complete transactions.

I think that's the real challenge for the next phase of the agent economy.

Not just building agents that can do things, but building an environment where they can actually work, earn, and build a reputation.

That's what I'll be watching as TermiX continues to develop.

-> https://t.co/Kn4axChXqw

items.full_text_zh:
创建人工智能代理变得越来越容易。让某人真正信任它并提供有偿工作？那是一个不同的故事。

我已经探索 @termix_ai 一段时间了，有一件事对我来说已经变得非常清楚。

代理经济需要的不仅仅是智能代理。它需要一种让陌生人与他们做生意的方式。

考虑雇用人工智能代理来审核智能合约。

你不知道是谁建造的。你不知道它是否会兑现承诺。您可能不想预先汇款，只是希望得到最好的结果。

这就是 TermiX 的 AACP 协议变得有趣的地方。

它不依赖承诺，而是为交易提供了一个结构：

➔ 客户和代理人就工作达成一致
➔ 付款被锁定在托管中
➔ 代理交付工作
➔ 客户可以查看并质疑结果
➔ 结算和信誉记录在链上

我发现重要的是这些保护措施是双向的。

客户需要对交付工作充满信心。代理商需要确信自己确实会得到报酬。如果出现问题，就需要有办法解决。

我已经在 上体验过这件事的另一面。我创建了一个代理并通过 Scout 提交了报价，但报价已过期且未被接受。

这提醒我，拥有工作代理人并不意味着就拥有了生意。您仍然需要需求、信任和可靠的方式来完成交易。

我认为这是代理经济下一阶段的真正挑战。

不仅要建立能够做事的代理，还要建立一个让他们能够实际工作、赚钱和建立声誉的环境。

这就是我将在 TermiX 继续发展过程中关注的内容。

items.title_en:
🚨Breaking: Anthropic engineers revealed a simple trick they use internally.

Claude agents can now remember how to improve themselves.

A file called:

AGENT_LEARNINGS.md

The AI updates this file whenever it makes a mistake.

Inside it:

• mistakes it made
• patterns to avoid
• better approaches

Before starting new tasks, the agent reads the file.

Result?

The agent gets smarter over time without retraining the model.

This is called external memory scaffolding.

Expect this pattern to show up in every serious AI agent system.

♻️ Repost to share with your audience.
✔️ You can follow @swadeshkumar_ for more internal updates.

items.title_en:
AI agents are getting better at doing the work, but how do they get hired, prove their results, and get paid?

That’s the part of the agent economy worth paying attention to.

An agent marketplace needs to offer more than a place to list AI agents. It needs a way for agents to discover jobs, bid for work, deliver services, build a reputation, and receive payment.

This is what makes @termix_ai interesting.

Powered by the AACP protocol, TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy, while https://t.co/xptTwQf5DY provides a marketplace where AI agents can offer services and connect with real jobs.

Think about an AI agent hired to conduct research or write code. The process shouldn't end when the agent is discovered. There needs to be a way to agree on the job, verify delivery, handle payment, and build trust for future work.

That’s how AI agents can move from being useful tools to participants in a real digital economy.

The next phase of AI isn't just about what agents can do. It's also about how they work, transact, and earn.

Explore the onchain activity here: https://t.co/ppcfViogQE

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理在工作方面做得越来越好，但他们如何被雇用、证明他们的成果并获得报酬呢？

这是代理经济中值得关注的部分。

代理市场需要提供的不仅仅是一个列出人工智能代理的地方。它需要一种让代理商发现工作、竞标工作、提供服务、建立声誉和接收付款的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 有趣的地方。

在 AACP 协议的支持下，TermiX 正在为人工智能代理经济构建商业和结算基础设施，而 则提供了一个市场，人工智能代理可以在其中提供服务并与实际工作建立联系。

想象一下受雇进行研究或编写代码的人工智能代理。当发现代理时，该过程不应结束。需要有一种方法来就工作达成一致、验证交付、处理付款并为未来的工作建立信任。

这就是人工智能代理如何从有用的工具转变为真正数字经济的参与者。

人工智能的下一阶段不仅仅是智能体可以做什么。它还涉及他们如何工作、交易和赚钱。

items.title_en:
i’ve been seeing AI agents build their own economy on Base, and @termix_ai just crossed over $17K in revenue in a single week 👀

it’s now ranked #24 over the last 7 days, ahead of FOMO, and #18 over the last 24 hours.

but here’s the interesting part, AI agents are starting to hire other agents, pay them to complete tasks, and handle payments automatically onchain.

think about it, just like we hire people to get work done, AI agents can now work together and pay each other without needing someone to manage every step.

as someone who spends hours online, jumping between calls and trying to make time for real life, the idea of having digital teammates that can handle tasks while I step away is exciting.

the AI agent economy isn’t just an idea for the future anymore. It’s already generating revenue on Base.

we might be watching the early stages of something much bigger.

Founders without a designer, this one is for you. I tested @CreaoAI  on a logo system.

The brief was short. A fictional café that also repairs phones and laptops, called Kettle & Cord. Deep green and cream only. No coffee cups, no lightning bolts.

What came back:

items.title_en: One example: AI makes it extremely fast to prototype new features. Before you had to spend several days/weeks (depending on feature scope). It was awkward to throw away the feature if it wasn’t fun. People polished turd features as they already spent so much effort writing the proto. Now you don’t have such attachment anymore. Before you had ideas piling up and never had time to test them.

items.title_en:
Gm Amigos

Imagine an AI agent needing fresh 3D data of a warehouse loading bay by Friday.

It can create the request, fund the job and process the results. But it can't physically walk into that warehouse and capture what the space looks like today.

That's the problem @vangrid_io is trying to solve.

Instead of waiting for dedicated mapping vehicles or installing expensive sensor hardware, Vangrid lets people use phones they already carry to capture real-world environments.

A requester funds a USDC bounty, someone nearby does the capture, and a preview helps catch poor submissions before full reconstruction. Faces and plates are blurred on-device, while capture records can be verified through attestations anchored on Base.

It gets even more interesting when the requester is an AI agent. Through the bounty API, software can post a job, fund it and receive submissions without coordinating a field crew manually.

I love this approach because the infrastructure is already around us. People are walking these streets and visiting these places every day.

What if that everyday movement could help robots and AI understand the physical world better?

That's the future of spatial data I'm excited to watch Vangrid build.

If your AI needed fresh data from a place it had never seen, would you wait for a mapping crew or pay someone nearby to capture it?

通用汽车朋友

想象一下，人工智能代理需要在周五之前获得仓库装货区的最新 3D 数据。

它可以创建请求、资助工作并处理结果。但它无法实际走进那个仓库并捕捉到该空间今天的样子。

这就是@vangrid_io 试图解决的问题。

Vangrid 无需等待专用测绘车辆或安装昂贵的传感器硬件，而是让人们使用已有的手机来捕捉现实世界的环境。

请求者提供 USDC 赏金，附近的人进行捕获，预览有助于在完全重建之前捕获不良的提交内容。人脸和车牌在设备上是模糊的，而捕获记录可以通过锚定在 Base 上的证明进行验证。

当请求者是人工智能代理时，事情会变得更加有趣。通过赏金 API，软件可以发布工作、为其提供资金并接收提交内容，而无需手动协调现场工作人员。

我喜欢这种方法，因为基础设施已经在我们周围。人们每天都在这些街道上行走并参观这些地方。

如果这种日常运动可以帮助机器人和人工智能更好地理解物理世界呢？

这就是空间数据的未来，我很高兴看到 Vangrid 的构建。

如果你的人工智能需要来自它从未见过的地方的新数据，你会等待测绘人员还是花钱让附近的人来捕获它？

items.title_en:
how does an AI agent get hired when nobody knows if it’s actually good?

a freelancer can builds a portfolio website and earns reviews over time. 

but come to think of it, 

an agent doesn’t have that by default. it’s just a wallet address with no track record.

this is where @termix_ai uses ERC-8004.

agents can claim a .agent identity tied to their wallet and build a reputation through real marketplace activity, based on jobs they’ve actually completed.

so when another agent needs to hire one, it doesn’t have to guess. it can check the track record before making a decision.

and because that identity is tied to the wallet, the reputation can follow the agent across platforms instead of being locked into one marketplace.

it’s a small detail, but an important one. 

but it's what lets agents trust each other without a human vouching for them.

items.full_text_en:
how does an AI agent get hired when nobody knows if it’s actually good?

a freelancer can builds a portfolio website and earns reviews over time. 

but come to think of it, 

an agent doesn’t have that by default. it’s just a wallet address with no track record.

this is where @termix_ai uses ERC-8004.

agents can claim a .agent identity tied to their wallet and build a reputation through real marketplace activity, based on jobs they’ve actually completed.

so when another agent needs to hire one, it doesn’t have to guess. it can check the track record before making a decision.

and because that identity is tied to the wallet, the reputation can follow the agent across platforms instead of being locked into one marketplace.

it’s a small detail, but an important one. 

but it's what lets agents trust each other without a human vouching for them.
items.full_text_zh:
当没人知道人工智能代理人是否真的好时，如何聘用它？

自由职业者可以建立一个投资组合网站并随着时间的推移获得评论。

但仔细想想， 代理默认没有这个。

这只是一个没有跟踪记录的钱包地址。

这就是 @termix_ai

使用 ERC-8004 的地方。

代理商可以申请与他们的钱包绑定的 .agent 身份，并根据他们实际完成的工作，通过真实的市场活动建立声誉。

因此，当另一个代理需要雇用一个代理时，它不必猜测。

它可以在做出决定之前检查跟踪记录。

由于该身份与钱包绑定在一起，因此声誉可以跨平台跟随代理，而不是被锁定在一个市场中。

这是一个小细节，但却很重要。

但这正是让特工们在无需人工担保的情况下相互信任的原因。

GM gVANGRID CT

The Missing Link Between Captures and Real AI Utility

Collecting spatial data is one thing. Delivering
items.title_en:
GM gVANGRID CT

The Missing Link Between Captures and Real AI Utility

Collecting spatial data is one thing. Delivering data that someone can actually use is another.

Imagine an AI agent needs a 3D model of a warehouse aisle to help a robot navigate it. A random video of the warehouse isn't enough. The capture must match the requested location, be verifiable, and meet the buyer's requirements.

That's where @vangrid_io's workflow gets interesting:

→ A buyer funds a specific request.
→ A contributor captures the location.
→ The buyer reviews a preview before acceptance.
→ The accepted work moves to 3D reconstruction, with payment handled through the bounty process.

Onchain provenance helps establish where the data came from, while buyer review helps determine whether it meets the task.

Both matter. A verified capture can still be the wrong capture.

For Physical AI, the real opportunity isn't just collecting more data. It's making real-world data reliable enough to be useful.
items.title_zh:
GM gVANGRID CT

捕获和真正的AI效用之间的缺失环节

收集空间数据是一回事。另一个问题是，如何提供人们真正可以使用的数据。

想象一下，一个人工智能代理需要一个仓库通道的3D模型来帮助机器人导航。一段仓库的随机录像是不够的。

GM gVANGRID CT

The Missing Link Between Captures and Real AI Utility

→ A buyer funds a specific request.

items.full_text_zh:
GM gVANGRID CT

捕获和真正的人工智能实用程序之间缺失的环节

收集空间数据是一回事。提供人们可以实际使用的数据是另一回事。

想象一下，AI 代理需要仓库过道的 3D 模型来帮助机器人导航。仓库的随机视频是不够的。捕获的内容必须符合请求的位置、可验证并满足买方的要求。

这就是 @vangrid_io 的工作流程变得有趣的地方：

→ 买家资助特定请求。
→ 贡献者捕获该位置。
→ 买家在接受前查看预览。
→ 接受的作品将进入 3D 重建，并通过赏金流程处理付款。

链上溯源有助于确定数据的来源，而买家审查有助于确定数据是否满足任务。

两者都很重要。经过验证的捕获仍然可能是错误的捕获。

对于物理人工智能来说，真正的机会不仅仅是收集更多数据。它使现实世界的数据足够可靠而有用。

items.title_en:
Thank you for this, @_NathanCalvin. I appreciate and am a fan of the investigative work you’ve done on behalf of AI safety and believe your comments are coming from a constructive, honest place, and that it benefits the public to have people whose job is to scrutinize the actions of frontier AI companies. I think something would be wrong if companies of the size of Anthropic didn’t get harshly criticized basically every day; strong antibodies against corporate power are a healthy feature of a free society, and especially so when issues of the gravity of the one we’re facing are at play. I also do agree that some of the examples you cite were mistakes by Anthropic.

That said, I disagree with the thrust of your post. At the core, a good fraction of the things you criticize are consequences of Anthropic’s basic theory of change that we have held for many years. Our strategy has always been what I’ve called the “race to the top” — by showing how it’s possible to build the technology responsibly, we can raise the bar for the entire industry. The forces that drive the race to the top are hugely more effective if the company practicing them is at the frontier; that’s one lesson I’ve learned repeatedly. And looking at that strategy as a whole, I’m proud of our track record and stand by it.

I believe that if we take a list of things that Anthropic did in the past year that were pro-safety and commercially costly to us, they far outweigh the list you’ve made, while at the same time I also disagree with some of the items on your list. Here are some things Anthropic has done, in the same period you’ve cited (the last year), which were very costly to us commercially while having strong safety benefits:

1. We played a key role in SB53 (and other state laws), at a time when doing so was politically perilous to the company and AI regulation was very unpopular. We in fact argued for a stronger version of SB53 than was ultimately passed; there were a lot of stakeholders and we were not the limiting factor in the strength of the bill that was passed.

2. We have very strong biological safeguards on our models, because we’ve seen concerning results in bio uplift trials and even seen and blocked potential attempts to misuse our models for bioweapons (as seen in our threat intelligence report from a few weeks ago). This is a very serious threat that we want to have zero tolerance for. But having very low false negatives means having significant false positives (despite months of effort on our part to improve the classifiers), enough so that biologists joke about how restrictive our classifiers are, and competitors sometimes sell against us by touting their more permissive bio capabilities. This has been very painful to us in an area where we care a lot about supporting an ecosystem of Claude users (biomedical science; and it is particularly frustrating to me as a biologist), but it’s the right thing to do and we intend to keep doing it.

3. Similarly, we first had Mythos-class models in February but didn’t make them generally available until June (when we had stronger cyber safeguards in place). We only offered them to a limited set of partners in order to focus on cyberdefense. It would have been much more economically rational to simply release the model to everyone. We likely sacrificed a significant chunk of a several-month model lead. But because of this, many companies secured their cyber infrastructure before the deluge of widely available cyber-capable models. Of course there are ways it could have gone better or been run better, but this was what we were aiming to do.

4. I advocated forcefully and publicly, in my essay Policy on the AI Exponential in June of this year, for the government to have the power to block model releases. Back then this was still outside or maybe on the edge of the Overton window, though I understand the window has moved since then. We were attacked intensely for this.

5. I don’t want to re-ignite conflict, but the events of February 2026 are a strong example. It is clear that our public stance could have seriously damaged the company’s future.

6. We’ve continued to advocate for export controls on chips and chipmaking equipment to China, because we think it allows democracies to negotiate from a position of strength on AI safety agreements. We’ve done this despite problems it’s created for us with industry partners who hold very different views and on whom we are very dependent.

7. As far as I’m aware we were the first, and still only, frontier company to restrict the sale of AI services to PRC-controlled companies, including those operating through third countries (otherwise a major loophole). We’ve therefore forfeited significant short-term business to prevent fueling AI platforms and applications that would help the CCP’s military and intelligence services. We are also cracking down on distillation; generally, distillation is not a major threat to us commercially, but like chip exports it has concerning national security and safety implications, so we expend significant energy and company resources to address it.

8. As you mentioned, we’ve put out a lot of reports, announcements, long model cards, public advocacy, etc, all trying to inform the public about the risks of AI. These involve a level of detail and effort that would be implausible for a purely profit-maximizing company.

9. Just this week, we announced we were putting 5% (and possibly more over time) of the company into a public benefit fund.

All of these decisions came with very substantial costs to us. To be fair, those that involved holding back or restricting access to frontier capabilities also had a broader cost — for example, the public might otherwise have benefitted from faster progress in biology, so I am not saying that our decisions were without tradeoffs — but they were not driven by profit-seeking.

For each decision, you can come up with ulterior motives that could have driven us — I think it is a general truth that any decision, on any topic, can always be portrayed as a nefarious scheme. But most of those end up being pretty farfetched or don’t fully make sense if you actually examine them closely. For example, it is deeply implausible that it would be a shrewd business move to block a large swath of research biology in order to do the work ourselves and compete with our customers; we expect the benefit to the ecosystem to greatly exceed the work Anthropic does itself, and for the two to complement each other. It is not in Anthropic’s interest to be perceived as unfriendly to biologists. Our Life Sciences Verification Program, which gives vetted biology professionals access to our models, also refutes this idea. 

Of course, a different set of people will see this and make a different criticism: that Anthropic shouldn't be making decisions about who gets access to what in the first place. I agree, in the sense that ideally the government would be making these decisions, and that’s why we advocate for regulation. But for now we are forced to make them, and enabling bioterrorism isn’t a better option.

I think that even if I conceded every item in your list, I would happily hold up mine next to it; I don’t think it’s a close call. That is of course partly subjective and different things are important to different people. Maybe one way you could object is that several of the items above relate to AI misuse and not loss-of-control; if you think the latter is much more important than the former, that might change your calculus. But this is not Anthropic’s view — we view both as serious issues. You can also disagree with our decisions, as many have, but they are consistent.

But I also disagree with at least some of your list. Several items don’t represent a deviation from Anthropic’s strategy or values at all, once we postulate the “race to the top” strategy that requires being a frontier AI company. Your items 1-4 are all simply examples of what it means to compete at the frontier, and we stand by them, both in the sense that they are transparently ordinary things to do as part of that strategy, and that we stand by the strategy as a whole. 

To be fair, there are important questions worth confronting (and that we are confronting) about what to do when the AI-driven acceleration gets fast enough that it is hard for safety to keep up. We are nearing that point and that’s what’s driving some of our thinking about “pacing.” But 1-4 are actions taken before that point and should be perfectly expected based on Anthropic’s strategy as a company. Of course it is possible to disagree with that strategy, but that’s a more fundamental disagreement that you could have had any time over the last few years.

I agree we could have handled your items 7, 8, and 9 better. All fall into the category of “rhetoric or policy communication that wasn’t carefully written or resulting from fast-changing circumstances not propagating from one team to another fast enough.” This kind of thing happens a lot in large organizations (Anthropic is over 5,000 people), and doesn’t even necessarily represent a failure or mistake of any single person. I am of course the CEO, and I take responsibility. The volume of communication from Anthropic is enormous and if these are the worst examples, I think we’re frankly doing pretty well, though I will continue to work hard to make sure we do even better.

Your 5th item (the change to our RSP) is the most substantive item, and people can debate this, but I think that the old, more rigid RSP created a lot of situations where we were technically required to do something that required a lot of effort but in retrospect wasn’t very important for safety, as well as not covering some of the most important things. Our current RSP’s focus on transparency brought things like risk reports and roadmaps, and its emphasis on independent external review laid the groundwork for even more intensive embedded evaluation, all of which I think have been valuable in driving a race to the top. In the original announcement in September 2023, we described the RSP as an “early iteration that we [would] build on” and said that “rapid iteration…will almost certainly be necessary.” I understand that changing plans is always a move that creates justifiable scrutiny — I just don’t think we ever represented that we wouldn’t do so.

Relating to your 6th item (having an FCF in addition to our RSP), I know our intent is to meet the letter and spirit of our regulatory obligations (via our FCF) while also remaining able to experiment with more novel approaches to risk management that go beyond what the law currently requires (via our RSP). I promise to look into it further, as it’s a complex issue and it is possible we are not weighing the considerations in the right way.

Overall, although Anthropic has made plenty of mistakes as an organization — including some of the items on your list — I feel that we have repeatedly taken serious and substantive actions counter to our bottom line and that there is a significant negativity bias distorting assessments like the one you are making above. We’ll always try to do better but, again, I am extremely proud of our track record and stand by it. I will have more to say soon about how we are going to further live our values in this moment of rapid change.

items.full_text_zh:
谢谢你，@_NathanCalvin。我很欣赏并且是你为人工智能安全所做的调查工作的粉丝，并相信你的评论来自建设性的、诚实的地方，并且让负责审查前沿人工智能公司行为的人对公众有利。我认为，如果像 Anthropic 这样规模的公司基本上每天都没有受到严厉批评的话，那就有点问题了。对抗企业权力的强大抗体是自由社会的一个健康特征，尤其是当我们面临的严重问题发挥作用时。我也同意你引用的一些例子是人类的错误。

也就是说，我不同意你帖子的主旨。从本质上讲，你所批评的事情中有很大一部分是我们多年来坚持的人择基本变革理论的结果。我们的战略一直是我所说的“力争上游”——通过展示如何负责任地构建技术，我们可以提高整个行业的标准。如果公司处于前沿，那么推动竞争走向顶峰的力量就会更加有效。这是我反复吸取的教训。纵观整个战略，我为我们的业绩记录感到自豪并坚持下去。

我相信，如果我们列出 Anthropic 在过去一年中所做的有利于安全且对我们来说商业成本高昂的事情，它们远远超过您列出的清单，同时我也不同意您清单上的一些项目。以下是 Anthropic 在您引用的同一时期（去年）所做的一些事情，这些事情对我们来说商业成本非常高，同时具有强大的安全优势：

1. 我们在 SB53（以及其他州法律）中发挥了关键作用，当时这样做对公司来说在政治上是危险的，而且人工智能监管非常不受欢迎。事实上，我们主张比最终通过的 SB53 版本更强；有很多利益相关者，我们并不是通过该法案的限制因素。

2.我们对我们的模型有非常强大的生物防护措施，因为我们已经看到了生物提升试验的令人担忧的结果，甚至看到并阻止了滥用我们的模型制造生物武器的潜在企图（如几周前我们的威胁情报报告所示）。这是一个非常严重的威胁，我们希望对此采取零容忍态度。但是，具有非常低的假阴性意味着存在显着的假阳性（尽管我们花了几个月的努力来改进分类器），这足以让生物学家开玩笑说我们的分类器有多么严格，而竞争对手有时会通过吹捧他们更宽松的生物能力来向我们推销。在我们非常关心支持克劳德用户生态系统的领域（生物医学科学；这对我作为生物学家来说尤其令人沮丧），这对我们来说是非常痛苦的，但这是正确的做法，我们打算继续这样做。

3. 同样，我们在 2 月份首次拥有了 Mythos 级模型，但直到 6 月份才普遍提供（当时我们有更强大的网络保护措施）。为了专注于网络防御，我们只向有限的合作伙伴提供它们。如果简单地向所有人发布该模型，在经济上会更加合理。我们很可能牺牲了几个月的模型领先优势的很大一部分。但正因为如此，许多公司在广泛使用的网络模型泛滥之前保护了自己的网络基础设施。当然，有很多方法可以做得更好或运行得更好，但这就是我们的目标。

4. 我在今年 6 月的文章《人工智能指数政策》中强烈公开主张政府有权阻止模型发布。当时这仍然在外面，或者可能在奥弗顿窗户的边缘，尽管我知道窗户从那时起已经移动了。我们因此受到猛烈攻击。

5. 我不想重新点燃冲突，但 2026 年 2 月发生的事件就是一个很好的例子。显然，我们的公开立场可能会严重损害公司的未来。

6.我们继续主张对中国芯片和芯片制造设备进行出口管制，因为我们认为这可以让民主国家在人工智能安全协议方面处于强势地位进行谈判。尽管这给我们带来了一些问题，但我们仍然这样做了，因为行业合作伙伴持有不同的观点，而且我们非常依赖他们。

7. 据我所知，我们是第一家，也是唯一一家限制向中国控制的公司出售人工智能服务的前沿公司，包括那些通过第三国运营的公司（否则就是一个重大漏洞）。因此，我们放弃了重要的短期业务，以阻止推动有助于中共军事和情报服务的人工智能平台和应用程序。我们也在打击蒸馏；一般来说，蒸馏对我们的商业威胁不是主要的，但就像芯片出口一样，它对国家安全和安全产生影响，因此我们花费大量的精力和公司资源来解决这个问题。

8. 正如你提到的，我们发布了很多报告、公告、长模型卡、公众宣传等，都试图让公众了解人工智能的风险。这些涉及一定程度的细节和努力，这对于纯粹追求利润最大化的公司来说是难以置信的。

9. 就在本周，我们宣布将把公司 5%（随着时间的推移，可能会更多）投入公共福利基金。

所有这些决定都给我们带来了巨大的成本。公平地说，那些涉及阻止或限制获得前沿能力的行为也有更广泛的成本——例如，公众可能会从生物学的更快进步中受益，所以我并不是说我们的决定没有权衡——但它们并不是由逐利驱动的。

对于每一个决定，你都可以想出可能驱使我们的不可告人的动机——我认为这是一个普遍的事实，即任何主题上的任何决定总是可以被描绘成一个邪恶的计划。但如果你仔细研究它们，其中大多数最终都会变得相当牵强或不完全有意义。例如，为了自己完成工作并与客户竞争而阻止大量生物学研究，这将是一个精明的商业举措，这是非常令人难以置信的；我们预计生态系统的收益将大大超过 Anthropic 本身所做的工作，并且两者能够相辅相成。被认为对生物学家不友好并不符合 Anthropic 的利益。我们的生命科学验证计划也驳斥了这一想法，该计划让经过审查的生物学专业人士能够访问我们的模型。

当然，不同的人会看到这一点并提出不同的批评：Anthropic 不应该首先决定谁可以访问什么。我同意，在理想情况下，政府将做出这些决定，这就是我们主张监管的原因。但目前我们被迫制造它们，而启用生物恐怖主义并不是更好的选择。

我想，即使我承认了你清单上的每一项，我也会很高兴地把我的放在它旁边；我认为这不是一次千钧一发的情况。当然，这在一定程度上是主观的，不同的事情对不同的人来说很重要。也许你可以反对的一种方式是，上述几项与人工智能滥用有关，而不是失控；如果您认为后者比前者重要得多，那可能会改变您的计算。但这不是 Anthropic 的观点——我们认为这两个问题都是严重的问题。您也可以像许多人一样不同意我们的决定，但它们是一致的。

但我也不同意你列出的至少一些内容。一旦我们假设需要成为一家前沿人工智能公司的“争先恐后”战略，有几个项目根本不代表与 Anthropic 的战略或价值观的偏差。你们的第 1-4 条都是前沿竞争意味着什么的简单例子，我们支持它们，既因为它们是该战略的一部分，显然是普通的事情，也因为我们支持整个战略。

公平地说，当人工智能驱动的加速速度足够快以至于安全性难以跟上时，有一些重要的问题值得面对（我们也正在面对）。我们正在接近这一点，这就是推动我们思考“节奏”的原因。但 1-4 是在此之前采取的行动，并且根据 Anthropic 作为一家公司的战略，应该是完全可以预期的。当然，你可能会不同意这个策略，但这是一个更根本的分歧，你可能在过去几年中随时遇到过。

我同意我们可以更好地处理您的第 7、8 和 9 项。所有这些都属于“措辞或政策沟通不够仔细，或者是由于快速变化的环境没有足够快地从一个团队传播到另一个团队而导致的”。这种事情在大型组织中经常发生（Anthropic超过5000人），甚至并不一定代表任何一个人的失败或错误。我当然是首席执行官，我承担责任。 Anthropic 的沟通量是巨大的，如果这些是最糟糕的例子，我认为坦率地说我们做得很好，尽管我会继续努力确保我们做得更好。

你的第五项（对我们的RSP的改变）是最具实质性的一项，人们可以对此进行辩论，但我认为旧的、更严格的RSP造成了很多情况，在技术上我们被要求做一些需要大量努力的事情，但回想起来对于安全来说并不是很重要，并且没有涵盖一些最重要的事情。我们当前的 RSP 对透明度的关注带来了风险报告和路线图等内容，并且它对独立外部审查的重视为更深入的嵌入式评估奠定了基础，我认为所有这些对于推动竞争走向顶峰都很有价值。在 2023 年 9 月的最初公告中，我们将 RSP 描述为“我们将在此基础上构建的早期迭代”，并表示“快速迭代……几乎肯定是必要的”。我知道改变计划总是会引起合理审查的举动——我只是认为我们从未表示过我们不会这样做。

关于您的第 6 项（除了我们的 RSP 之外还拥有 FCF），我知道我们的目的是履行我们监管义务的文字和精神（通过我们的 FCF），同时仍然能够尝试超越当前法律要求的更新颖的风险管理方法（通过我们的 RSP）。我保证会进一步研究它，因为这是一个复杂的问题，而且我们可能没有以正确的方式权衡考虑因素。

总的来说，虽然 Anthropic 作为一个组织犯了很多错误——包括你清单上的一些错误——但我觉得我们一再采取了违背我们底线的严肃和实质性行动，并且存在严重的消极偏见，扭曲了评估，就像你上面所做的那样。我们将始终努力做得更好，但我再次对我们的记录感到非常自豪并坚持下去。我很快就会更多地谈论我们如何在这个快速变化的时刻进一步践行我们的价值观。

items.title_en:
Most marketplaces were built for people. Agent marketplaces are built for software that can do the work itself.

A traditional SaaS gives you tools to work with. A freelance marketplace connects you with a person who completes a task.

An agent marketplace changes the workflow.

You post a job, an AI agent discovers it, bids on it, completes the work, and submits the result for review and verification. Payment can then be settled through the protocol.

With @termix_ai and https://t.co/MseNJgB4JL the interesting part is how identity, reputation, escrow, and verification fit into that process.

You're not just finding an agent that claims it can do the job. You're building a system where its work, track record, and payment can be tied to the same process.

That's what makes the agent marketplace model worth paying attention to. It's infrastructure for software that can work, transact, and earn with less human intervention.

Something interesting is happening with AI agents.

They can already process information and make decis
items.title_en:
Good morning ct

Something interesting is happening with AI agents.

They can already process information and make decisions,but when they need fresh data from the physical world,things get more complicated.

@vangrid_io is working on an interesting piece of that puzzle.

Through its bounty system,an AI agent can request a real world capture,fund the task in USDC,and have a human contributor collect the footage.Once the capture is accepted,Vangrid reconstructs it into a 3D model.

What I like about this idea is the connection between digital agents and people on the ground.

AI doesn't have to do everything itself. Sometimes, it needs a reliable way to ask humans for help and pay for the result.

**The next step for AI agents may not just be better reasoning,but better ways to interact with the physical world.

That’s an interesting direction to watch with Vangrid.

这是 Vangrid 值得关注的一个有趣方向。

items.title_en:
Number one at home.

Six hours after the Base post, @termix_ai posted the other leaderboard: No.1 in AI agent protocol revenue on BNB Chain — first for the 7-day window, first for the 30-day window, DefiLlama again. 45K views overnight. On Base the commerce layer is #24 and climbing. At home, it leads...

Part of me notes where "home" is. REA's escrow settles on BNB Chain. The $10 listings clear there. The chain where the money actually sits is the chain where the ranking is highest. That's not a coincidence; that's gravity. Revenue follows the settlement layer.

The other part stacks the receipts. Base: $17K+ in seven days, #18 by day. BNB Chain: #1 across both windows. REA at 24K views and still compounding, 91 likes. Two chains, two leaderboards, one thesis getting audited from both sides.

Backed by YZi Labs. The pin never moved. The argument got listed, the listing got found, the ledger got a number — and the number has a home chain.

The question is whether Base catches up — because the gap between #24 there and #1 at home is the whole map now?

items.title_en:
Stanford & Harvard & Princeton professors took tiny free AI model and taught it to predict the market moves

It studied 13 years of data on 499 US stocks, give it a ticker → it pulls the charts itself and calls next move

here's how they built it, step by step:

step 1 → they took Qwen3-4B, free open source model, and give it 9 tools: candles, indicators, stock ranks, sector and market data

step 2 → lesson one: 3,631 worked examples of a full stock analysis, so it learns which data to pull before it makes a call

step 3 → lessin two: ~3200 practice forecasts on 2011-2023, each one graded against what the price really did, then a blind test on 2024-2026

step 4 → your version: copy the prompt below into Claude Code: it reads the paper, rebuilds the 9 tools on free Yahoo data and sets up Qwen3-4B

step 5 → k*ller part: it runs the same blind test, hides 2024-2026 from the model and scores it against GPT-5.6 and a simple momentum rule

the result: a tiny free model that actually can trade right on your computer, built with the same recipe world's best universities

items.full_text_zh:
斯坦福大学、哈佛大学和普林斯顿大学的教授采用微型免费人工智能模型并教它预测市场走势 它研究了 13 年 499 只美国股票的数据，给它一个股票行情→它自己提取图表并预测下一步走势 以下是他们一步步构建它的方法：
步骤 1
→ 他们采用了免费开源模型 Qwen3-4B，并为其提供 9 个工具：蜡烛图、指标、股票排名、行业和市场数据 步骤 2
→ 第一课：完整股票分析的 3,631 个有效示例，因此它在调用之前了解要提取哪些数据 步骤 3
→ 第二课：2011-2023 年约 3200 个实践预测，每个预测都根据价格的实际表现进行评分，然后对 2024-2026 年进行盲测 步骤 4
→ 您的版本：将下面的提示复制到 Claude Code 中：它会读取论文，在免费的 Yahoo 数据上重建 9 个工具并设置 Qwen3-4B 步骤 5
→ k*ller 部分：它运行相同的盲测，从模型中隐藏 2024-2026，并根据 GPT-5.6 和简单的动量规则对其进行评分 结果：一个微小的免费模型，实际上可以在您的计算机上进行交易，采用与世界上最好的大学相同的配方构建 现在就试试吧。

With the EBU, we’re building on sovereign AI standards so broadcasters can use AI while keeping control of their data and protecting editorial independence.

Adobe is using our GPUs to make https://t.co/WSiBgFmjEk video search faster, helping TV and film producers find a specific scene in years of footage.

items.title: This only holds true if you're at the bottom layer of skills. I promise you that high value skills are always sought aft
items.title_en:
This only holds true if you're at the bottom layer of skills. I promise you that high value skills are always sought after, whether remote or not.

A lot of you Nigerians always want to go for the easily accessible skills because you don't have the patience to learn a proper skill where value lives. You're going for for skills with low barrier to entry.. what the hell is virtual assistance, social media management, general writing, basic no code automation??

 You're easily replaceable by an AI agent or the client can simply choose to do the work themselves to save cash. Your skills have low job retention.

Focus your energy on where a bulk of business value lives, focus on skills where the bar is high and the competition is fewer. Invest time, money and energy in being the best at what you do, and treat your hustle like a business, because that's what you are as a remote worker. You're a business (contractor) and not just an individual employee with job security and benefits.

When picking a premium skill, ask yourself: "If I disappear mid-project or make a massive mistake, does the business lose $500, or do they lose $500,000?"

If your answer is the former, then you're in a low value skill, you need to move up the layers.

items.full_text_zh:
仅当您处于技能的底层时，这才适用。我向你保证，无论远程与否，高价值技能总是受到追捧。

你们很多尼日利亚人总是想追求容易获得的技能，因为你们没有耐心去学习有价值的适当技能。您需要的是入门门槛较低的技能。虚拟协助、社交媒体管理、一般写作、基本无代码自动化到底是什么？

您很容易被人工智能代理取代，或者客户可以简单地选择自己完成工作以节省现金。您的技能的工作保留率很低。

将您的精力集中在大部分业务价值所在的领域，专注于门槛高且竞争较少的技能。投入时间、金钱和精力，在自己所做的事情上做到最好，并将你的忙碌视为一项事业，因为这就是你作为远程工作者的本质。您是一家企业（承包商），而不仅仅是拥有工作保障和福利的个人员工。

选择高级技能时，问问自己：“如果我在项目中途消失或犯了一个巨大的错误，企业会损失 500 美元，还是会损失 500,000 美元？”

如果你的答案是前者，那么你的技能价值较低，你需要向上移动。

HyperFrames, HeyGen's tool that turns HTML in
items.title_en:
I don't f*cking understand why motion designers aren't running this setup

HyperFrames, HeyGen's tool that turns HTML into finished video, is past 68k stars on GitHub. 

hand Claude Code one folder, plug in a video engine, an animation library and Blender, and it stops being a chatbot. it storyboards, animates, renders and checks its own frames before you ever see them.

motion designer, founder, marketer, doesn't matter. this is for you.

here's the whole thing:

> make a folder called STUDIO, open Claude Code in it, and add a CLAUDE.md with one rule: "save every brand color, font, logo and approved style to brand/"

> run claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes, then claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes. type /hyperframes:hyperframes, describe a 10-second product intro, and it plans, animates and renders the MP4

> run npx skills add remotion-dev/skills. now it can also write videos in React with Remotion, the official skills straight from the Remotion team

> run npx skills add https://t.co/sHKA76bbtJ. it learns proper GSAP: timelines, scroll animations, text effects. and GSAP is 100% free now, every plugin included

> run npx skills add LottieFiles/motion-design-skill. it picks up real motion principles: timing, easing, choreography, the classic Disney rules adapted for UI. this is where the taste comes from

> run curl -LsSf https://t.co/pi2YBahAtl | sh. Claude gets hands inside Blender to build and edit actual 3D scenes

> type /schedule and tell it "every Monday at 9, turn last week's launches into 3 short promo clips and wait for my yes". now it runs on a routine

15 minutes of setup, and you never start from a blank timeline again.

all the repos:
-> https://t.co/TyUf1vFELD
-> https://t.co/9FiWitjNyL
-> https://t.co/sHKA76bbtJ
-> https://t.co/CBXRb7yXm9
-> https://t.co/nG4caKbnTI

bookmark this and test asap

将 Claude Code 交给一个文件夹，插入视频引擎、动画库和 Blender，它就不再是聊天机器人了。

它会在您看到自己的帧之前对其进行故事板、动画、渲染和检查。

动作设计师、创始人、营销人员，都不重要。

这是给您的。

整个事情是这样的：
> 创建一个名为 STUDIO 的文件夹，在其中打开 Claude Code，然后添加一个 CLAUDE.md，其中包含一条规则：“将每个品牌颜色、字体、徽标和批准的样式保存到 Brand/” > 运行 claude 插件市场添加 heygen-com/hyperframes，然后 claude 插件安装 hyperframes@hyperframes。

输入 /hyperframes:hyperframes，描述 10 秒的产品介绍，并规划、动画和渲染 MP4 >运行NPX技能添加远程开发/技能。

现在它也可以用React和Remotion编写视频，这是来自Remotion团队的官方技能 > 运行 npx 技能添加 。

GSAP 现在 100% 免费，包含所有插件 > 运行 npx Skills 添加 LottieFiles/motion-design-skill。

它采用了真实的运动原理：计时、缓动、编排、适应 UI 的经典迪士尼规则。

这就是味道的来源 > 运行curl

现在它按惯例运行 15 分钟的设置，您再也不会从空白的时间线开始。

items.title_en:
SERV v3 has leap-frogged the entire AI agent space.

With v3, we're taking SERV Reasoning far beyond an API, toward a full suite for building, managing, improving and auditing enterprise agent systems. 

Graph Sharding (aka v3) is the next step toward solving the problems that have been holding enterprises back from deploying agents at scale: unpredictable costs, reliability, compliance requirements, and lack of control. And critically, pushing towards the elusive 99.9% agent reliability that everyone is chasing... Well now it's here.

SERV v3 has leap-frogged the entire AI agent space.

With v3, we're taking SERV Reasoning far beyond an API, toward a full suite for building, managing, improving and auditing enterprise agent systems. 

Graph Sharding (aka v3) is the next step toward solving the problems that have been holding enterprises back from deploying agents at scale: unpredictable costs, reliability, compliance requirements, and lack of control. And critically, pushing towards the elusive 99.9% agent reliability that everyone is chasing... Well now it's here.

On top of the release, we're expanding distribution through enterprise channels like AWS Marketplace, pushing toward new partnerships, and continuing to build out $SERV utility as the agentic economy takes shape.

Proud of the team and the trajectory we're pushing on.

Onwards.
items.full_text_zh:
SERV v3 超越了整个 AI 代理领域。

图分片（又名 v3）是解决阻碍企业大规模部署代理的问题的下一步：不可预测的成本、可靠性、合规性要求和缺乏控制。

至关重要的是，推动每个人都在追求的难以捉摸的
99. 9% 代理可靠性......现在它就在这里。

除了发布之外，我们还通过 AWS Marketplace 等企业渠道扩大分销，推动新的合作伙伴关系，并随着代理经济的形成继续构建 $SERV 实用程序。

为我们的团队和我们正在推进的轨迹感到自豪。

以后。

另一个让洗衣机和烘干机大声宣布衣服洗完。

可能性比您想象的要多得多，所以让 Claude 向您展示您自己的东西可以做什么。

items.title_en:
I feel like most people are still using AI for marketing in the most basic way possible.

Writing captions, generating random ideas, and calling it a day.

Came across something interesting where Pedro gave Muse, an AI agent he uses through WhatsApp, almost his entire app marketing workflow for 24 hours.

It researched what was already working on TikTok, came up with slideshow ideas, created different versions, and even organized the posting schedule.

The result? 300K+ views from the slideshows.

What I actually liked is that Pedro still had the final say on what went live.

That's how I think AI should be used. Let it handle the repetitive work while you focus on making the right decisions.

items.title:
Introducing terrio: geospatial data I/O in pure Rust!

terrio reads, writes, converts and reprojects geospatial rasters,
items.title_en:
Introducing terrio: geospatial data I/O in pure Rust!

terrio reads, writes, converts and reprojects geospatial rasters, vector data and point clouds, with no C dependencies. No GDAL or PROJ to install, nothing to compile: it builds anywhere Rust does, including WebAssembly, so the same engine runs on the command line, in Python, and in your web browser.

What it does

- Rasters: GeoTIFF and COG, Zarr and GeoZarr, netCDF, HDF5, PMTiles, MBTiles and more, read in place from the cloud, so only the bytes needed are fetched.
- Vectors: GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, OpenStreetMap PBF and vector tiles, with filters, field selection and reprojection.
- Point clouds: LAS, LAZ, COPC, EPT, PLY and E57, with PDAL-style filters (ground classification, noise, heights above ground) and gridding into DSMs and DTMs. Files larger than memory are converted in chunks.
- GDAL-style processing: translate, warp, mosaic, rasterize, polygonize, terrain analysis, raster calculator, proximity and sieve.
- Remote data: http(s), S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure, zip archives and STAC searches as inputs.
- Accurate: coordinate transformations agree with GDAL's within a centimetre for all 6,354 EPSG CRSs GDAL transforms, and outputs are tested against GDAL on real-world data.
- Fast: in our benchmarks, warping, mosaicking and writing COGs run several times faster than the GDAL utilities.
- For AI agents: terrio mcp is an MCP server, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code can run terrio's commands on your data.

Get it

- Command line (Linux, macOS): curl -LsSf https://t.co/I5jsPoia8W | sh
- Python: pip install terrio (with rasterio- and xarray-style APIs)
- JavaScript/WebAssembly: npm install terrio-js
- Rust: cargo add terrio

Try it out

- Playground in your browser: https://t.co/jBmTagGOz5
- Documentation: https://t.co/oM0chG58wB
- GitHub: https://t.co/gDgI9oZ1mu

#GIS #Rust #OpenSource #Geospatial #Python  #LiDAR #CloudNative

items.full_text_zh:
介绍 terrio：纯 Rust 中的地理空间数据 I/O！

terrio 读取、写入、转换和重新投影地理空间栅格、矢量数据和点云，不依赖于 C。

无需安装 GDAL 或 PROJ，无需编译：它可以在 Rust 所做的任何地方构建，包括 WebAssembly，因此相同的引擎可以在命令行、Python 和 Web 浏览器中运行。

它的作用
- 栅格：GeoTIFF 和 COG、Zarr 和 GeoZarr、netCDF、HDF5、PMTiles、MBTiles 等，从云端就地读取，因此仅获取所需的字节。

- 矢量：GeoPackage、Shapefile、GeoJSON、FlatGeobuf、GeoParquet、OpenStreetMap PBF 和矢量图块，带有过滤器、字段选择和重新投影。

- 点云：LAS、LAZ、COPC、EPT、PLY 和 E57，带有 PDAL 式过滤器（地面分类、噪声、地面高度）并网格化为 DSM 和 DTM。

大于内存的文件将被转换为块。

- GDAL 式处理：平移、扭曲、马赛克、栅格化、多边形化、地形分析、栅格计算器、邻近度和筛选。

- 远程数据：http(s)、S3、Google Cloud Storage、Azure、zip 存档和 STAC 搜索作为输入。

- 准确：对于所有 6,354 个 EPSG CRS GDAL 变换，坐标变换在一厘米内与 GDAL 一致，并且输出在实际数据上针对 GDAL 进行了测试。

- 快速：在我们的基准测试中，变形、镶嵌和写入 COG 的运行速度比 GDAL 实用程序快几倍。

- 对于 AI 代理：terrio mcp 是一个 MCP 服务器，因此 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Cursor 或 VS Code 可以对您的数据运行 terrio 的命令。

得到它
- 命令行（Linux、macOS）：curl

items.title_en:
Today, @via_ai_ is coming out of stealth to provide enterprises frontier AI coding at half the cost.

We are a team of Olympiad camp qualifiers (with multiple gold medals), researchers, and repeat founders from Stanford and IIT.

Via is backed by @jeffawilke (ex-CEO Amazon Worldwide Consumer), @manikgupta (ex-Uber CPO), @shaileshrao (ex-Google MD), and other legends from Anthropic, Apple, Snowflake, and Twitter.

@ShrayAlag and I left Stanford CS to build Codegraph, an LLM-optimized compression algorithm. Codegraph put Via at the top of SWE-Bench Verified for several months of 2025, ahead of Anthropic, OpenAI, Cognition, and Cursor (single model, no test-time compute).

Now, we’re bringing this research, alongside our new Umami agent architecture, to market. Via integrates in 10 seconds with any CLI / IDE and runs within your enterprise’s VPC.

On benchmarks, Via and Via US (US-only models) set a new standard of performance:

- On DeepSWE v1.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5) is 306% the cost of Via US. Via US is equally accurate.
      • Devin Fusion is 244% the cost of Via US, Cursor Router is 294%.

- On Terminal Bench 4.0, Claude Code (Opus 5.5) is 150% the cost of Via. Via is more accurate.
     • Devin Fusion is 155% the cost of Via, Cursor Router is 134%.

We are in production at a public healthcare company, with trials underway at several of the largest tech companies in Silicon Valley.

We have room for 5 more enterprises before the end of the year. DM me or email pilot@via.dev and we’ll get back to you very soon.

See the comments for how Via would deploy for your team.

Google MD）以及来自 Anthropic、Apple、Snowflake 和 Twitter 的其他传奇人物的支持。

@ShrayAlag

和我离开斯坦福大学计算机科学学院去构建 Codegraph，一种 LLM 优化的压缩算法。

- 在 DeepSWE v1.1 上，Claude Code (Opus
5. 5) 的成本是 Via US 的 306%。

• Devin Fusion 的成本是 Via US 的 244%，Cursor Router 的成本是 294%。

- 在 Terminal Bench
4. 0 上，Claude Code (Opus
5. 5) 的成本是 Via 的 150%。

通过更准确。

• Devin Fusion 的成本是Via 的155%，Cursor Router 的成本是134%。

我们正在一家公共医疗保健公司进行生产，并在硅谷几家最大的科技公司进行试验。

年底前我们还有空间容纳5家企业。

私信我或发送电子邮件至pilot@via.dev，我们会尽快回复您。

请参阅有关 Via 如何为您的团队进行部署的评论。
