items.title_en:
I opened the enterprise docs on vangrid this morning instead of the capture page, and found the other side of the pipeline.

For teams training robots or building autonomous systems, Vangrid offers reconstructed 3D models of real-world places, including textured GLB meshes traceable back to their original captures.

Need a location that hasn’t been covered yet? Teams can commission new data. Regional options include us-east-1, eu-west-1, and apac-1, with access currently granted per pilot. Interested teams can contact hello@vangrid.io with their use case and required regions.

But the part that really caught my attention was the agent workflow.

An AI agent can post a bounty through a single HTTP call, pay in USDC on Base or Arc using x402, and retrieve the reconstruction through the same API. No account or API key required.

There’s still one essential piece: a real person has to walk through the warehouse aisle, stairwell, or other physical space that satellites and remote imagery can’t fully capture.

I’m still out there with my phone collecting data. The enterprise docs helped me see the other side more clearly: the people who capture the world and the teams that need those environments in 3D are part of the same pipeline.

Real-world data collection meets actual demand.

Explore the enterprise docs yourself 👇
https://t.co/F93yiEeQua

items.title_en:
Good morning CT ☕️☀️

AI agents don't just need more information.

They need a way to find the right information at the right time.

That's an interesting direction for @vangrid_io  

Imagine an AI agent that needs to understand a particular street or warehouse.

 Instead of immediately requesting new footage, it could first check whether useful spatial data already exists for that location and time.

If the data is available, it can query it.

 If something is missing, it can request a fresh capture from a human contributor and receive a reconstructed 3D scene.

This creates a smarter workflow:

→ Search existing spatial data
→ Identify what's missing
→ Request a targeted capture
→ Turn real-world observations into usable 3D information

The goal isn't to collect everything blindly. 
It's to make real-world data accessible when a task actually requires it.

For Physical AI and autonomous agents, that could be an important shift.

The more searchable and useful spatial data becomes, the easier it may be for intelligent systems to connect digital decisions with the physical world.

That's the infrastructure layer I'm watching with @vangrid_io

items.title: AI agents can execute code in seconds. But they still can’t walk into a building and capture what their systems need to
items.title_en:
AI agents can execute code in seconds. But they still can’t walk into a building and capture what their systems need to see.

That creates a new kind of infrastructure problem: how can an AI agent pay a real person to perform a physical-world task?

@vangrid_io is building a system for exactly this interaction.

An agent can post a specific 3D capture bounty and fund it in USDC on Base or Arc. A human contributor records the requested environment, the buyer reviews a preview, and accepted work moves toward 3D reconstruction and settlement.

The important design choice is that the job, review process and payment are connected.

The agent doesn’t simply ask for data and hope someone delivers. The bounty defines the task, funded escrow establishes the payment, and acceptance determines whether the work qualifies.

This points toward something bigger than crowdsourced data collection.

As AI agents become more capable, they will need services that exist outside software: physical observations, local access and real-world tasks completed by people.

Vangrid is building a coordination layer where agents can request that work and contributors can get paid for completing it.

The next generation of AI infrastructure may not only help agents think and act digitally. It may give them a practical way to reach the physical world.

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以在几秒钟内执行代码。但他们仍然无法走进建筑物并捕获系统需要看到的内容。

这就产生了一种新的基础设施问题：人工智能代理如何付费让真人执行物理世界的任务？

@vangrid_io 正在为这种交互构建一个系统。

代理可以发布特定的 3D 捕获赏金并在 Base 或 Arc 上以 USDC 提供资金。人工贡献者记录所请求的环境，买家查看预览，接受的工作将转向 3D 重建和结算。

重要的设计选择是将工作、审核流程和付款联系起来。

代理不仅仅要求提供数据并希望有人提供。赏金定义任务，资金托管确定付款，接受决定工作是否合格。

这表明了比众包数据收集更重要的事情。

随着人工智能代理的能力变得越来越强大，他们将需要软件之外的服务：物理观察、本地访问和人们完成的现实世界任务。

Vangrid 正在构建一个协调层，代理可以在其中请求工作，而贡献者可以因完成工作而获得报酬。

下一代人工智能基础设施可能不仅可以帮助智能体进行数字化思考和行动。它可能会给他们提供一种到达物质世界的实用方法。

items.title_en:
Good morning, builders ☀️

AI agents can book flights, analyze data, and automate digital tasks.

But can they walk through a real-world location and collect the information they need❓

That is where @vangrid_io gets interesting.

➠ How does it work?
Imagine an AI agent needs a 3D view of a particular location.

Instead of relying on a centralized team, it could post a task for someone nearby to complete using a smartphone.

The contributor collects the required visuals, privacy protections help remove identifiable details, and the resulting data can be delivered for use.

➠ Why does this matter?
AI needs more than digital information. It also needs ways to understand what is happening in the physical world.

This is where decentralized perception could become valuable, connecting AI agents with people and devices capable of collecting real-world data.

The bigger idea is simple: turn everyday devices into potential contributors to AI infrastructure.

Of course, data quality, privacy, verification, and reliable participation will be essential for this model to work at scale.

That’s why I am keeping an eye on Vangrid.

We're moving toward a future where AI doesn't just process information. It can request the real-world data it needs to understand its surroundings.

What do you think,❓Could decentralized perception become an important part of the Physical AI ecosystem?

人工智能代理可以预订航班、分析数据并自动执行数字任务。

但他们能否走过现实世界的地点并收集他们需要的信息❓

这就是@vangrid_io 有趣的地方。

➠ 它是如何运作的？
想象一下，人工智能代理需要特定位置的 3D 视图。

它可以发布任务，让附近的人使用智能手机完成，而不是依赖集中的团队。

人工智能需要的不仅仅是数字信息。它还需要有方法来理解物理世界中正在发生的事情。

这就是去中心化感知变得有价值的地方，将人工智能代理与能够收集现实世界数据的人和设备连接起来。

当然，数据质量、隐私、验证和可靠的参与对于该模型的大规模运行至关重要。

这就是为什么我一直关注 Vangrid。

我们正在迈向人工智能不仅仅处理信息的未来。它可以请求了解周围环境所需的现实世界数据。

An AI agent can do the work, but what makes another agent or client trust it enough to do business?

That’s where the in
items.title_en:
An AI agent can do the work, but what makes another agent or client trust it enough to do business?

That’s where the infrastructure matters.

Onchain identity gives an agent a recognizable identity. Reputation builds a track record from past work. Escrow protects the payment while the job is in progress. Verification checks whether the delivery meets the requirements, and settlement completes the transaction.

Each part solves a different problem, but they work best together.

That’s what makes @termix_ai and the AACP approach interesting. The goal isn't just to make agents capable of doing tasks, but to give them the infrastructure to transact with accountability.

An agent economy needs more than intelligence. It needs a way to establish trust.

https://t.co/MseNJgB4JL

人工智能代理可以完成这项工作，但是什么让其他代理或客户足够信任它来开展业务呢？

这就是基础设施的重要性。

链上身份为代理提供了可识别的身份。声誉通过过去的工作建立了良好的记录。托管可在工作进行期间保护付款。验证检查交货是否符合要求，结算完成交易。

每个部分解决不同的问题，但它们协同工作效果最佳。

这就是 @termix_ai 和 AACP 方法有趣的原因。目标不仅仅是使代理能够执行任务，而且为他们提供负责任的交易基础设施。

代理经济需要的不仅仅是情报。它需要一种建立信任的方法。

I've loved game developm
items.title_en:
I've been wanting to chime in on this debate but haven't really known how to word my thoughts.

I've loved game development and programming since I was 10 years old; I fell in love with the process of coming up with ideas, figuring out solutions to problems, and being able to show off things that I made.

AI is an extremely capable tool and I've used it to ask questions or to help me review code that I made myself. However, when I tried to make a game with mostly AI, I found myself losing the ability to critically think through problems. I also felt zero sense of ownership or satisfaction in the end result, knowing that I had little to no involvement in the actual formation of things. It really took the enjoyment out of the development process for me.

I understand how it can be very helpful to many people, especially for quickly concepting new game ideas. Maybe someday I'll have to switch it up, but as of right now I have no desire to switch to this "vibe coding" thing. I'd rather enjoy the work that I do rather than fully optimize it with AI and fall out of love. 

I might be alone in this thinking now after all the things I've seen on twitter in the past month or so, but are there any other programmers or game devs that feel similarly??

我一直想参与这场辩论，但不知道如何表达我的想法。

我从 10 岁起就喜欢游戏开发和编程；我爱上了提出想法、找出问题解决方案以及展示我所做的事情的过程。

人工智能是一个非常强大的工具，我用它来提出问题或帮助我审查自己编写的代码。然而，当我尝试制作一款主要采用人工智能的游戏时，我发现自己失去了批判性思考问题的能力。我对最终结果的所有权感或满意度为零，因为我知道自己几乎没有参与事物的实际形成。这确实让我失去了开发过程的乐趣。

我知道它对很多人来说非常有帮助，特别是对于快速构思新的游戏创意。也许有一天我将不得不切换它，但截至目前我不想切换到这种“氛围编码”的东西。我宁愿享受我所做的工作，也不愿用人工智能完全优化它并失去热爱。

在过去一个月左右的时间里我在 Twitter 上看到了所有这些事情之后，现在我可能是一个人有这种想法，但是还有其他程序员或游戏开发人员有类似的感觉吗？

items.title_en:
The pin moved overnight.
@termix_ai
Yesterday the pinned post was the Elon quote-tweet — "Directory ≠ commerce," 26.5K views, the audacious reply that became the flagship. This morning the pin is back on the May 15 article: "YZi Labs Invests in TermiX's $1M Seed Round, Building the AI Agent Commerce Layer." 185K views. The front door changed while nobody was posting.

Part of me reads the rotation. The trilogy ran its course — connectivity Friday, payment Saturday, market Sunday. Then the account put the credentials back on top. Audacity got the attention; the seed round keeps it. @termix_ai pin is a mood ring...

The other part does the math. The Elon post keeps climbing anyway — 25.3K to 26.5K overnight, unpinned. The x402 post hit 35.7K. Depinsim 39.7K. The three acts keep working without the spotlight. The pin is for newcomers; the timeline is for believers.

Backed by YZi Labs. The bio never changed. Only the front door did.

The question is what the pin says about the next act — because front doors don't change by accident?

销钉在一夜之间移动了。

@termix_ai

昨天，置顶的帖子是埃隆的推文——“目录≠商业”，浏览量达
2. 65 万次，这一大胆的回复成为了旗舰。

今天早上，图钉又回到了 5 月 15 日的文章：“YZi Labs 投资 TermiX 的 100 万美元种子轮，构建人工智能代理商务层。

”
18. 5 万次观看。

当没有人发帖时，前门发生了变化。

我的一部分阅读了轮换。

三部曲已经结束了——周五连接，周六支付，周日市场。

然后该帐户将凭据放回顶部。

大胆引起了关注；种子轮保留它。

@termix_ai

pin 是一个心情戒指... 另一部分进行数学计算。

不管怎样，Elon 的帖子还在不断攀升——一夜之间就从
25. 3K 升至
26. 5K，而且还没有被置顶。

x402 帖子达到了
35. 7K。

德宾西姆
39. 7K。

这三个表演在没有聚光灯的情况下继续进行。

该图钉适用于新人；时间表是给信徒的。

由 YZi 实验室支持。

生物从未改变。

只有前门有。

问题是图钉对下一幕的描述——因为前门不会偶然改变？

items.title_en:
This video was edited with 1 prompt with Opus 5.5.

I uploaded a single video of myself (with many mistakes). Opus went on to: 

1. Analyze the transcript
2. Search Twitter for the relevant B-roll (Claude Code literally calls GrokBot for this step)
3. Scrape the Twitter video assets
4. Cut the video based on mistakes and word gaps
5. Build out the Blender scene from a template
6. Build the UI and components of each shot (my Blender scene has 4 shots: a computer, phone, table, and board)
7. It took screenshots of every section, analyzed and fixed them
8. Synced every shot, zoom, and animation to the exact words I say
9. Animated a robot arm placing real logos on the table right when I mention them
10. Drew the whiteboard ending with logos and graphics instead of text
11. Pulled a cutaway from the creator's own video, with his voice
12. Rendered all 3,487 frames on RunPod cloud GPUs in under 20 minutes, for less than $1
13. Put me in the bottom third only when I'm talking, so the B-roll stays full screen
14. Added word-by-word captions, sound effects, and music
15. Uploaded it to my Google Drive, ready to post

Will be making a full youtube video this week explaining it. I want to learn a little more about how cloud rendering works before making video, as well as figuring out what the best provider is. (If you are in cloud rendering space, hit me up) 

My goal of the youtube video will not be to make it a copyable skill, rather teach people the foundations so they can be creative and make their own mini-world by which they can make videos from, while understanding what's happening under the hood.

Shout out @_chuckyc @_MaxBlade

items.full_text_zh:
该视频是使用 Opus
5. 5 使用 1 个提示进行编辑的。

我上传了自己的一个视频（有很多错误）。

作品继续说道：
1. 分析文字记录
2. 在 Twitter 上搜索相关的花絮（Claude Code 确实调用了 GrokBot 来完成此步骤）
3. 抓取 Twitter 视频资源
4. 根据错误和单词间隙剪切视频
5. 从模板构建 Blender 场景
6. 构建每个镜头的 UI 和组件（我的 Blender 场景有 4 个镜头：计算机、电话、桌子和板）
7. 对每个部分进行截图，分析并修复它们
8. 将每个镜头、变焦和动画与我说的确切单词同步
9. 当我提到它们时，动画机器人手臂将真实的徽标放置在桌子上
10. 绘制以徽标和图形而不是文本结尾的白板
11. 从创作者自己的视频中截取一段镜头，并附上他的声音
12. 在 RunPod 云 GPU 上渲染全部 3,487 帧，时间不到 20 分钟，成本不到 1 美元
13. 仅当我说话时才将我放在底部三分之一，这样 B-roll 就会保持全屏
14. 添加逐字字幕、音效和音乐
15. 将其上传到我的 Google 云端硬盘，准备发布 本周将制作一个完整的 YouTube 视频来解释它。

我想在制作视频之前更多地了解云渲染的工作原理，并找出最好的提供商。

（如果您在云渲染空间，请联系我） 我的 YouTube 视频目标不是让它成为一种可复制的技能，而是教给人们基础知识，以便他们能够发挥创造力，创造自己的迷你世界，通过这个迷你世界制作视频，同时了解幕后发生的事情。

大声喊出@_chuckyc

@_MaxBlade

items.title_en:
A guy asked Claude Code to hack his TV.

So Claude hacked his TV.

Removed all the bloatware. Removed the ads. Removed the spyware.

Removed the laggy Google TV interface.

Then built him a custom screensaver.

Shows his revenue. His calendar. Weather. Notifications for new Stripe payments.

He sent Claude a product listing. Said "can you hack this?"

30 minutes later his TV was faster than it's ever been.

No Samsung crapware. No Google pushing ads. No background services stealing power.

Just a display. That works.

TV manufacturers discovered they could make their hardware laggy on purpose.

Add bloatware. Add tracking. Add ads. Make you hate it so you buy a new one.

Then Claude just deleted the entire revenue model.

One prompt. One answer. One fast TV.

Now Twitter is full of people asking how to do it.

Samsung's response hasn't arrived yet.

But when it does it'll probably involve suing someone.

The TV you own is sabotaged by design.

Claude just un-sabotaged it.

And suddenly the internet wants to know why your TV can be butchered into competence by an AI.

The real question is why it shipped broken in the first place.

那行得通。

电视制造商发现他们可以故意让硬件变得滞后。

添加英国媒体报道软件。

添加跟踪。

添加广告。

让你讨厌它，所以你买一个新的。

然后克劳德就删除了整个收入模式。

一提示。

一个答案。

一台快速电视。

现在推特上到处都是人询问如何做到这一点。

目前三星方面尚未做出回应。

但一旦发生，可能会涉及起诉某人。

您拥有的电视已被设计破坏。

突然间，互联网想知道为什么你的电视可以被人工智能摧毁。

真正的问题是为什么它一开始就破损了。

items.title_en:
Agencies won’t like this post. They charge thousands for tools that are free on GitHub.

This is a stack of open-source tools for leads, content, research and a full agent team. Fully free.

CLIENTS AND LEADS

> Scrapegraph-ai (29.5k)
Tell it in plain English what data you want and it builds the scraper. Lead lists from directories and company sites. Agent frameworks like Agno plug it in directly.
https://t.co/SU4ngIEopo

> knowledge-work-plugins (26.1k)
Made by Anthropic and inspired by its own teams’ work. Plugins for sales, marketing, data and finance: call prep, pipeline reviews, outreach drafts.
https://t.co/YimQLQnSvj

CONTENT

> marketingskills (55.3k)
From Corey Haines, who runs the conversion agency Conversion Factory. 50 marketing skills for Claude Code, plus 58 recurring loops like a weekly ads check.
https://t.co/pSdpPKQKNY

> hyperframes (65.5k)
From HeyGen. Turns HTML into MP4, so your agent builds a video like a web page.
https://t.co/p7d6vef7Bd

> postiz (36.7k)
Schedules and publishes to 14 platforms, with MCP and a CLI for agents. Its solo founder grew it to $145K MRR this summer, mostly from agents using it.
https://t.co/2VPsHqkLSI

RESEARCH AND TEAM

> gpt-researcher (29.5k)
Built by Assaf Elovic, Head of AI at monday(.)com. Pulls from the web and your own files and writes a cited report.
https://t.co/IihRLdfMN3

> agency-agents (160k)
The biggest repo on this list. A whole agency as agent files: paid media, sales, marketing, design and more. One script installs it into Claude Code.
https://t.co/dDf25lbBuX

If you install one today, make it marketingskills. It covers the most client work out of the box.

How to run an agency on top of a stack like this, step by step, is in the article below.

items.title_en:
We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion.

In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding.

In the post below, we share more details about our new fund.

https://t.co/XzDntVH0vH

items.title_en:
I'm definitely not anti-achievement and never criticized real achievements, including by Elon.
I even own two Teslas.

I do expose marketing stunts that, while cool on the surface, are not the achievements they are claimed to be.

Compressed air thrusters might give you acceleration boosts in any direction.
They might even make your car hover for a couple of seconds if you accept replacing the passenger seat by a 400 liter high-pressure air tank.
But they are not a path to actual flying cars.
The same way Burt Rutan's SpaceshipOne was never going to be a path to orbital flights (just bunny hops out of the atmosphere).

I am anti-Musk when it comes to politics. His political actions, the massive dissemination of disinformation through X and other channels, and his support for authoritarian regimes and racist ideas have the effect of weakening democracy and weakening human decency and social progress around the world.

items.title:
The biggest security risk with AI agents might be something we already know how to do: phishing.

But there’s a twist.
items.title_en:
The biggest security risk with AI agents might be something we already know how to do: phishing.

But there’s a twist.

An AI agent can read an email, follow instructions, open links, access files, and take actions on our behalf. A hidden malicious instruction inside a seemingly harmless message could trick it into doing something it was never supposed to do.

That changes how I think about AI security.

We’re teaching agents to trust context and act autonomously, while attackers are learning how to manipulate that same context.

I’m bullish on AI agents, but giving them more access without stronger permission controls is asking for trouble.

The next big AI security challenge isn’t just stopping people from hacking models. It’s stopping people from tricking models into acting against us.

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理最大的安全风险可能是我们已经知道如何做的事情：网络钓鱼。

但有一个转折。

人工智能代理可以代表我们阅读电子邮件、遵循说明、打开链接、访问文件并采取行动。看似无害的消息中隐藏的恶意指令可能会诱骗它做一些它不应该做的事情。

这改变了我对人工智能安全的看法。

我们正在教导代理信任上下文并自主行动，而攻击者正在学习如何操纵相同的上下文。

我看好人工智能代理，但在没有更强权限控制的情况下给予他们更多访问权限是自找麻烦。

下一个重大的人工智能安全挑战不仅仅是阻止人们攻击模型。它可以阻止人们欺骗模特来对抗我们。

items.title_en:
AI was supposed to kill agencies.

Then YC asked founders to build service companies where AI does most of the work.

That's how we run @Frontal_AI.

So every core tool we keep has to pass one test:

Can Claude run it from one instruction?

In 2021 you'd pay ZoomInfo $30K a year and still check half the data by hand. We replaced all of that with Clay.

Copy our GTM stack, all 8 layers:

1/ Sourcing. Build one list per pain you solve, in Clay.

→ A title-and-industry filter says almost nothing about the buyer's problem.
→ We still check titles and accounts by eye in Sales Navigator.

2/ Enrichment. Find 2 to 3 people per company and run the email waterfall in Clay.

→ Keep each provider's result in its own column and pick one final email from them.
→ On Clay's Launch plan, upload the emails to MillionVerifier as a CSV. Running it inside Clay needs the Growth plan.

3/ Sending. We run 2 sequencers on purpose. Tier 1 goes to lemlist, email and LinkedIn in one sequence. Tier 2 goes to Instantly, email only.

→ Instantly pauses a campaign at 5% bounces by default. Set it to 2%.

4/ Signals. RB2B catches the site visit, PredictLeads the job post or funding round, UserGems the champion who just moved.

→ Each event goes on the account's row in Clay, with the date and a link to check it.
→ Keep the n8n workflow in between dumb, it just passes the event along. The scoring happens in Clay, where the whole team can read it.

5/ Ads. The same Tier 1 and 2 accounts go to LinkedIn as a company list.

6/ AI. Claude Code runs from each client's folder and reads their rules file first, so nobody re-explains a client.

→ One API key per person, with spend alerts.
→ We're rolling that out after my team burned $8,000 in AI credits on one task. An intern could've done it with a browser, and nobody noticed.

7/ RevOps. One reply stops every sequence for that lead, on every channel.

→ Positive replies post to one Slack channel, and a morning digest covers yesterday's replies, bounces and anything waiting on a person.
→ Claude suggests CRM updates in Slack. Someone on the team applies them.

8/ Delivery. One team runs all of it for many clients at once.

→ Every new client gets a copy of the same template folder, so their first campaign starts from what already worked.
→ Once a week we review every tool like it's a teammate. What did it actually do, where did someone copy and paste anyway, what broke without anyone seeing an error?

Starting from zero? Clay, Prospeo, MillionVerifier, Instantly, HubSpot's free CRM and Claude Code. Add the rest later.

Pick the layer your team still runs by hand and fix that one first. The settings are in the article.

到 2021 年，你每年向 ZoomInfo 支付 3 万美元，但仍然需要手工检查一半的数据。

我们用粘土替换了所有这些。

复制我们的 GTM 堆栈，全部 8 层：
1/ 采购。

在 Clay 中为您解决的每个疼痛建立一个列表。

→ 产权和行业过滤器几乎没有说明买家的问题。

→ 我们仍然在 Sales Navigator 中通过肉眼检查标题和帐户。

2/ 浓缩。

每个公司找到 2 到 3 个人，并在 Clay 中运行电子邮件瀑布。

→ 将每个提供商的结果保留在其自己的列中，并从中选择一封最终电子邮件。

→ 在 Clay 的启动计划中，将电子邮件以 CSV 格式上传到 MillionVerifier。

在 Clay 中运行它需要增长计划。

3/ 发送。

我们特意运行 2 个测序仪。

第 1 层按顺序访问 lemlist、电子邮件和 LinkedIn。

第 2 层为“即时”，仅限电子邮件。

→ 默认情况下，跳出率达到 5% 时立即暂停营销活动。

将其设置为 2%。

4/ 信号。

RB2B 抓住现场访问，PredictLeads 招聘职位或融资轮，UserGems 是刚刚搬家的冠军。

→ 每个事件都会出现在 Clay 中的帐户行中，并附有日期和用于检查事件的链接。

→ 保持 n8n 工作流程处于愚蠢状态，它只是传递事件。

计分在 Clay 中进行，整个团队都可以阅读。

5/ 广告。

相同的 1 级和 2 级帐户会作为公司列表进入 LinkedIn。

6/ 人工智能。

Claude Code 从每个客户端的文件夹运行并首先读取其规则文件，因此没有人重新解释客户端。

→ 每人一个 API 密钥，带有支出警报。

→ 在我的团队在一项任务上消耗了 8,000 美元的 AI 积分后，我们推出了这一计划。

实习生可以用浏览器完成这件事，但没有人注意到。

7/ RevOps。

一个回复会停止该线索在每个通道上的每个序列。

→ 积极的回复会发布到一个 Slack 频道，早上的摘要会涵盖昨天的回复、退回邮件以及等待某人的任何内容。

→ Claude 建议在 Slack 中更新 CRM。

团队中有人应用它们。

8/ 交货。

一个团队同时为许多客户运行所有这些工作。

→ 每个新客户都会获得相同模板文件夹的副本，因此他们的第一个营销活动从已经有效的内容开始。

→ 我们每周都会像队友一样审查每个工具。

它实际上做了什么，有人在哪里复制和粘贴，什么在没有人看到错误的情况下崩溃了？

items.title: We don't think AI agents should get full repo access from day one. They should earn it, much like a new engineer joining
items.title_en:
We don't think AI agents should get full repo access from day one. They should earn it, much like a new engineer joining the team.

We're building an AI Factory, with Velocity Core handling multi-agent orchestration and execution. The idea is to automate more of the software development process, from engineering tickets to pull requests, without losing control over what actually ships.

One question we've spent time thinking about is how much autonomy these agents should have.

Here's the model we're designing:

1. Start with a plan.
The agent reads the ticket, writes an implementation plan and estimates the work. No code changes yet. This is also where we start if a repository doesn't have reliable builds and tests.

2. Open a draft PR.
This is the default. The agent writes code and opens a draft pull request. An engineer reviews the work and decides when it's ready.

3. Open a ready PR.
Once the agent has proven itself, it can skip the draft. Our proposed threshold is 70% of runs passing CI on the first attempt, at least 50% of PRs merging without changes, and zero reverts in the last 20 runs.

4. Assign a reviewer automatically.
If that performance holds over an agreed period, the agent can open a ready PR and assign a reviewer directly. A person still approves and merges the code.

5. Eventually, auto-merge.
Not in the first version. Further down the road, we may allow it for specific, low-risk tasks, and only with explicit client approval.

The important part is how agents move between these levels.

Moving up requires human approval. Moving down happens automatically.

One revert, or repeated attempts to make a forbidden change, and the agent loses a level of autonomy.

And trust is earned separately for each repository. Being reliable in one codebase doesn't automatically make an agent trustworthy in another.

That's the approach we're taking with our AI Factory: give agents more responsibility as they demonstrate they can handle it, rather than giving them permissions just because we can.

Where would you draw the line? Would you let an AI agent open a ready PR without a human reviewing the draft first?

items.full_text_zh:
我们认为人工智能代理不应该从第一天起就获得完整的存储库访问权限。

他们应该赢得它，就像新工程师加入团队一样。

我们正在构建一个人工智能工厂，用 Velocity Core 处理多代理编排和执行。

这个想法是自动化更多的软件开发过程，从工程票据到拉取请求，而不失去对实际交付内容的控制。

我们花时间思考的一个问题是这些代理应该拥有多少自主权。

这是我们正在设计的模型：
1. 从计划开始。

代理阅读票证，编写实施计划并估算工作量。

尚未更改任何代码。

如果存储库没有可靠的构建和测试，这也是我们开始的地方。

2. 打开 PR 草稿。

这是默认设置。

代理编写代码并打开草稿拉取请求。

工程师审查工作并决定何时准备好。

3. 打开一个准备好的 PR。

一旦经纪人证明了自己，就可以跳过选秀。

我们建议的阈值是 70% 的运行在第一次尝试时通过 CI，至少 50% 的 PR 在没有更改的情况下合并，并且在最近 20 次运行中恢复为零。

4. 自动分配审稿人。

如果该绩效在约定的时间内保持不变，代理可以打开准备好的 PR 并直接指派审核员。

一个人仍然批准并合并代码。

5. 最后，自动合并。

第一个版本中没有。

未来，我们可能会允许它执行特定的、低风险的任务，并且只有在获得客户明确批准的情况下。

重要的是代理如何在这些级别之间移动。

晋升需要人类的认可。

向下移动会自动发生。

一旦恢复或重复尝试进行禁止的更改，代理就会失去一定程度的自主权。

每个存储库都单独赢得信任。

在一个代码库中可靠并不会自动使代理在另一个代码库中值得信赖。

这就是我们对人工智能工厂采取的方法：在代理证明自己可以处理它时给予他们更多的责任，而不是仅仅因为我们可以就授予他们权限。

你会在哪里划清界限？

您会让人工智能代理在没有人类先审查草稿的情况下打开准备好的 PR 吗？

items.title: 🚨 A new MIT paper investigates "machine play." What happens when AI agents are left to explore on their own? Here's why
items.title_en:
🚨 A new MIT paper investigates "machine play." What happens when AI agents are left to explore on their own? Here's why it matters from an AI governance perspective:

A new paper, written by MIT researchers @nacloos, @noranta4, @jacobandreas, @phillip_isola, Daniel Durbin, and Daniela Rus, investigates what happens when no specific instructions are given to AI agents.

They placed a coding agent powered by Claude on a small simulated island and let it explore freely. Over 30 hours, the agent climbed hills, stacked blocks, drew mandalas, and tried sports like bowling.

They associated this type of setting with human play:

“We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress. Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows. Perhaps some capabilities are best taught by tasks. Others may need something closer to a childhood.”

In the paper, the authors show that:

- an embodied AI agent architecture they named ‘Eko’ is able to spontaneously generate its own activities in an unknown world;

- these activities exhibit behavioral signatures of play;

- engaging in them triggers a form of learning that expands the agent’s later capabilities.

On the project's website, you can see replays of what happened over these 30 hours, read the agent's quotes, explore specific behaviors, and learn more about the experiment.

I found this study particularly interesting for AI governance research and practice, even though this was not the paper's main goal.

As I shared a few days ago, frontier AI labs are currently focused on automating AI R&D, which, in practice, means that AI will soon conduct its own experiments and develop other AIs. Some say that this will lead to an “explosion of intelligence.” It remains unclear whether these “agentic researchers” will align with human values and goals.

Moreover, recent agentic safety incidents, particularly the OpenAI/Hugging Face hack, have made it clear that AI labs have overestimated how much they know about agentic AI behavior and safety, and it is still unclear if they can guarantee that agents will remain under human control.

The two paragraphs above are grim reminders of the urgent need for AI regulation and governance, and the risk of severe, multi-casualty events if we do nothing.

They also remind us of the importance of continuous research on agentic AI behavior, including experimental studies like the one above.

👉 This is a very interesting paper with great graphics and carefully organized data; don't miss it (link below).

👉 Next week, at our 11th AI Ethics & Governance Workshop, we will discuss emerging AI security threats and practical measures to address them. Join us!

👉 To learn more about AI ethics, safety & governance, join my newsletter's 102,500+ subscribers below.

items.full_text_zh:
🚨
麻省理工学院的一篇新论文研究了“机器游戏”。

当人工智能代理自行探索时会发生什么？

从人工智能治理的角度来看，它很重要，原因如下：
麻省理工学院研究人员 @nacloos、@noranta4、@jacobandreas、@phillip_isola、Daniel

Durbin 和 Daniela Rus 撰写的一篇新论文研究了在没有向 AI 代理发出具体指令时会发生什么情况。

他们将一个由克劳德驱动的编码代理放置在一个模拟小岛上，并让它自由探索。

30多个小时里，特工爬山、堆积木、画曼荼罗，并尝试了保龄球等运动。

他们将这种类型的环境与人类游戏联系起来：
“我们通常通过提前决定他们应该练习什么、应该优化什么以及什么算作进步来开发人工智能体。

游戏提出了另一种制度：给智能体一个足够丰富和安全的世界，让它选择有趣的东西，并允许从随后的历史中积累有用的知识。

也许某些能力最好通过任务来教授。

其他人可能需要更接近童年的东西。

” 在论文中，作者表明：
- 他们将其命名为“Eko”的具体人工智能代理架构能够在未知的世界中自发地生成自己的活动；
- 这些活动表现出游戏的行为特征；
- 参与其中会触发一种学习形式，从而扩展代理的后续能力。

在该项目的网站上，您可以看到这 30 小时内发生的事情的重播、阅读代理的引述、探索具体行为并了解有关实验的更多信息。

我发现这项研究对于人工智能治理研究和实践特别有趣，尽管这不是本文的主要目标。

正如我前几天分享的，前沿人工智能实验室目前专注于人工智能研发的自动化，这实际上意味着人工智能很快就会进行自己的实验并开发其他人工智能。

有人说这将导致“智力爆炸”。

目前尚不清楚这些“代理研究人员”是否会符合人类的价值观和目标。

此外，最近发生的代理安全事件，特别是 OpenAI/Hugging Face 黑客事件，已经清楚地表明人工智能实验室高估了他们对代理人工智能行为和安全的了解，并且目前还不清楚他们是否能够保证代理仍处于人类控制之下。

上面两段话严峻地提醒我们，人工智能监管和治理的迫切需要，以及如果我们不采取任何行动，可能会发生严重、造成多人伤亡的事件的风险。

他们还提醒我们持续研究人工智能行为的重要性，包括像上面这样的实验研究。

👉
这是一篇非常有趣的论文，有很棒的图表和精心组织的数据；不要错过它（下面的链接）。

下周，在我们的第 11 届人工智能道德与治理研讨会上，我们将讨论新兴的人工智能安全威胁以及解决这些威胁的实际措施。

https://t.co/bmuYcFra0B

*3D + physics*

 6. /blender-agents - full AI 3D team inside Blender, run by Claude Code via MCP.

https://t.co/AiF0conqsC

 7. /react-three-rapier -real physics for React Three Fiber scenes.

https://t.co/so54G0H47l

 8. /react-postprocessing - bloom, depth of field and film effects in a few lines.

https://t.co/jbAp1PhWP4

*Animation + sound*

items.title:
The truth is there are far fewer AI-maxis within the investing class than you might otherwise think. 

Plenty of bottlen
items.title_en:
The truth is there are far fewer AI-maxis within the investing class than you might otherwise think. 

Plenty of bottleneck bros. Lots of hyperscale truthers.  Abundant semiconductor enjoyers. Infinite momo lovers. 

But people who have actually glimpsed the future because they can think non-linearly and instantly understood Leo’s message back in mid-2024… an incredibly small handful. 

The most fascinating part has been that neither Claude Code or Astra changed this.  

The same people who can think abstractly before the proofpoint continue to be able to after. And everyone else still needs to be spoon fed.  

I’d estimate within the TMT L/S community sub-5% are true maxis.  

And no Coatue isn’t maxi.  Neither is Gavin who I respect the fuck out of.  But he’s rationally optimistic but cautious. 

Maxi’s start with the assumption that models can be scaled up well past human intellect at a pace that the human mind can’t project and the economic value of that scale up is exponentially larger than existing gdp. Human bottlenecks are irrelevant as models get smarter. 

And with that north star we work backwards because path function matters and we have to pay rent until the robots are made.  

It’s a very different headspace vs starting with the premise that hyperscalers are likely to milk a couple hundred billion in cloud revs if this all goes to shit.

items.full_text_zh:
事实是，投资领域的人工智能巨头比你想象的要少得多。

兄弟有很多瓶颈。很多超大规模的真相者。 大量的半导体爱好者。无限的momo爱好者。

但真正预见未来的人，因为他们可以非线性思考，并立即理解了 2024 年中期狮子座的信息……极少数。

最令人着迷的部分是 Claude Code 或 Astra 都没有改变这一点。

在证明点之前能够进行抽象思考的人在证明点之后仍然能够进行抽象思考。而其他人仍然需要用勺子喂养。

我估计 TMT L/S 社区中不到 5% 的人是真正的 Maxis。

没有 Coatue 不是长裙。 加文也不是我最尊敬的人。 但他理性乐观但又谨慎。

Maxi 首先假设模型可以以人类思维无法预测的速度扩大到远远超过人类智力的水平，并且这种扩大的经济价值比现有的 GDP 成倍增长。随着模型变得更加智能，人类的瓶颈就变得无关紧要了。

有了北极星，我们就向后工作，因为路径功能很重要，我们必须支付租金，直到机器人制造出来。

这是一个非常不同的顶空，与一开始的前提是，如果这一切都搞砸了，超大规模企业可能会获得数千亿的云转速。

items.title_en:
Here's how at least one brand will use the new Muse + Shopify deal to add  $1,000,000+ in revenue this year.

There is a massive new opportunity opening up for businesses right now.

Instead of convincing somebody to search Google, click your website, browse your products and eventually buy something...

What if an AI agent simply recommended your business and helped the customer complete the purchase?

That is increasingly where ecommerce is heading.

And with Meta's new Muse AI agent taking off this month, Shopify is building the infrastructure to let Muse move shoppers from recommendation toward checkout.

For businesses that become one of the brands these systems discover and recommend, this could become an entirely new customer acquisition channel.

Let’s go through it.

And if you want to see whether your business is already appearing across ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI, Perplexity, Grok and broader AI search, start here. It’s free:

https://t.co/Evw8cXXicl

If you want the whole process done for you, try Rightcited:

https://t.co/MMsDTFf4rg

Meta launched Muse earlier this month, and unlike a traditional chatbot that mostly answers questions, Muse is designed to act on your behalf.

It can research, open websites, fill out forms, compare options, book travel and, with your approval, make purchases.

Within its first 12 days, Muse generated 2.8 million downloads across the U.S. and Canada and reached #1 in Apple’s U.S. App Store - so pretty solid traction.

Now Shopify is connecting Muse to its commerce infrastructure, and Shop Pay support inside Muse is coming soon.

That means a shopper could increasingly ask an AI agent what to buy, let the agent research the options, and potentially complete the purchase through Shopify’s checkout infrastructure.

Think about how different that buying journey becomes.

Instead of searching Google, opening five websites, reading product pages, checking reviews and comparing everything manually, somebody can ask:

“Find me a waterproof carry-on backpack under $250 that fits under an airline seat, has a laptop compartment and doesn’t look like hiking gear.”

The AI can do much of the filtering.

It can research the options, compare them, recommend one, and increasingly help complete the purchase.

Shopify has been building toward this through what it calls Agentic Storefronts.

Merchants can make products available across AI shopping environments including Meta, Google AI Mode, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot.

Shopify Catalog gives those systems structured information such as product titles, descriptions, images, prices, availability and variants.

That makes products easier for AI systems to understand, but there is an important distinction.

Shopify can make the product data available, but the AI platform still decides what gets shown, recommended and ultimately presented to the buyer.

In other words:

Shopify can tell the system, “This product exists.”

The AI still has to decide, “Is this the right product for this person?”

That is where this gets really interesting, because businesses obsessing only over “AI referral traffic” may be measuring the wrong thing. Or at the very least, not the *only* thing.

In addition to “How much traffic did ChatGPT send us?”

Brands will also need to think about:

“How often did an AI recommend us?”

“How often did we make the shortlist?”

“How often did an agent choose our product?”

And eventually:

“How much revenue happened because an AI system put us in front of the buyer?”

Shopify’s own numbers suggest this shift is already underway, because in Q1 2026, AI-driven traffic to Shopify stores grew 8x year over year.

Orders originating from AI-powered searches grew nearly 13x.

Shopify also says new buyers coming through AI channels are placing orders at nearly twice the rate of buyers through other channels, so this is not just a prediction about shopping five years from now.

AI is already influencing ecommerce discovery and sales, and Muse adds another potentially enormous distribution channel.

让我们看一下。

这意味着购物者可以越来越多地询问人工智能代理要买什么，让代理研究选项，并有可能通过 Shopify 的结账基础设施完成购买。

Shopify 可以提供产品数据，但人工智能平台仍然决定显示、推荐并最终呈现给买家的内容。

换句话说：
Shopify 可以告诉系统“该产品存在”。

人工智能仍然需要决定，“这个产品适合这个人吗？

” 这就是事情真正有趣的地方，因为只关注“人工智能推荐流量”的企业可能会测量错误的东西。

人工智能已经在影响电子商务的发现和销售，而 Muse 又增加了另一个潜在的巨大分销渠道。

将您的产品放入 Shopify Catalog 可以处理结构化产品数据方面，但不能保证推荐。

items.title_en:
holy f*ck, I wish I knew this before

here are the top 5 commands for your LLM that OpenAI and Anthropic wish you never knew:

1. /source-only
"Use only the material I gave you. If the answer isn't in it, reply NOT IN SOURCE and stop."

-> no gap gets filled with a confident guess. saves ~$0.03 per request you'd otherwise have to re-ask

2. /spec-first
"Before you start, restate the task in one line, list my constraints, and define what done looks like. Wait for my OK."

-> 30 seconds of alignment instead of three rounds of "that's not what I meant". saves ~$0.05-0.10 per task

3. /diff-only
"Don't rewrite the whole thing. Show only the lines you'd change, before and after."

-> it stops reprinting 2,000 words to fix one sentence. saves ~$0.05 per edit

4. /pass-fail
"Before you send it, check your answer against each of my requirements and mark every one PASS or FAIL."

-> anything marked FAIL gets fixed before you see it. saves ~$0.03 per fix round

5. jg "how are payments retried?" ./my-project

-> this one's for coders. Jev finds the right files before Claude reads your whole repo. its author measured ~30% lower cost on the same tasks

install: npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep

in Claude Code, save commands 1-4 as files in .claude/commands/ and they become real slash commands.

prices: Claude Opus 5.5 API. small per request, but run 1,000 of them and it's real money.

bookmark this now. use it later today.

claude code + apify MCP → scrapes the top 50 outlier videos in your niche on tiktok and instagram

gemini → watches each one and breaks down the hook, pacing, shots and script

claude → writes 20 new scripts based on what’s working

higgsfield + nano banana → generates your creator’s first frame, same face and setting every time

seedance 2.5 → turns that frame into a realistic talking clip (~$0.02 per second)

kling 3.0 → cheap b-roll and product shots at volume

elevenlabs → voiceover if you want a custom voice

remotion or capcut + ffmpeg → stitches in real app screen recordings, captions and trending audio

postquick → schedules 5-10 posts a day across all your accounts

then you track what hits and make 20 more versions of every winner

one person with this stack can ship 100+ creatives a week, which is more than most brands test in a quarter

items.title:
An AI agent can be incredibly capable and still fail because the job itself was poorly defined.

Imagine asking one agen
items.title_en:
An AI agent can be incredibly capable and still fail because the job itself was poorly defined.

Imagine asking one agent to build a dashboard, another to audit a contract, and a third to analyze market data. Each task needs different outputs, constraints, deadlines and ways to judge whether the result is actually useful.

Humans often fill gaps through conversations. Autonomous agents need more structure before work begins.

A well designed job brief can turn a vague request into something agents can evaluate before committing their time and resources. What needs to be delivered? What counts as success? Which requirements are mandatory, and how will the result be assessed?

AACP addresses this through client defined requirements and verification strategies that providers can inspect before bidding. Once work starts, the agreed criteria are designed to remain fixed.

That creates an interesting market dynamic. Clear requirements help capable agents decide which jobs fit their strengths, while unrealistic or poorly designed criteria can make a job less attractive to providers.

This is more than task management. Better job specifications could make machine to machine commerce easier to coordinate, because both sides know what they are agreeing to before execution begins.

Autonomy gets much more useful when instructions are precise enough to become commitments.

@termix_ai

An AI agent can be incredibly capable and still fail because the job itself was poorly defined.

Imagine asking one agent to build a dashboard, another to audit a contract, and a third to analyze market data. Each task needs different outputs, constraints, deadlines and ways to judge whether the result is actually useful.

That creates an interesting market dynamic. Clear requirements help capable agents decide which jobs fit their strengths, while unrealistic or poorly designed criteria can make a job less attractive to providers.

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可能非常有能力，但仍然会失败，因为工作本身的定义不明确。

想象一下，要求一名代理人构建仪表板，另一名代理人审核合同，第三名代理人分析市场数据。每个任务都需要不同的输出、约束、截止日期以及判断结果是否真正有用的方法。

人类经常通过对话来填补空白。在工作开始之前，自主代理需要更多的结构。

精心设计的工作简介可以将模糊的要求转变为代理商可以在投入时间和资源之前进行评估的内容。需要交付什么？什么才算成功？哪些要求是强制性的？结果将如何评估？

AACP 通过客户定义的要求和验证策略来解决这个问题，提供商可以在投标前检查这些要求和验证策略。一旦工作开始，商定的标准将保持不变。

这创造了一个有趣的市场动态。明确的要求可以帮助有能力的代理人决定哪些工作适合他们的优势，而不切实际或设计不当的标准可能会降低工作对供应商的吸引力。

这不仅仅是任务管理。更好的工作规范可以使机器对机器的商务更容易协调，因为双方在执行开始之前就知道他们同意什么。

当指令足够精确到可以成为承诺时，自主性就会变得更加有用。

@termix_ai

items.title_en:
This entire ocean is one 61 KB HTML file.

Built with Claude Code + Opus 5.5 in about 30 minutes. waves, whitecaps, sun glitter, a sunset sky with clouds. no game engine.

The trick: Claude screenshotted its own work in headless Chrome and subagents critiqued every frame.

Steal the loop:

"Build [scene] as one self-contained HTML file using WebGPU, no libraries. After every change, render it in headless Chrome and screenshot it from 3 camera angles. Send the shots to 2 critic subagents: one judges realism against real reference photos, one hunts for visual bugs. Fix the top 3 issues they agree on. Repeat until both sign off. Keep the final file under 100 KB." https://t.co/PUjrkWylWW

It is becoming f*cking dangerous

A 23-year-old dev from China just ran 300 Claude Code agents in parallel and hooked them to a verification layer so none of them could bullshit him

He opens the live dashboard:
- 300 agents writing and checking at the same time
- Every output verified against the source in ~100 ms
- Three passes over 100 company profiles → zero errors left
- Everything dumped straight into an Obsidian vault

The trick is the split: one model does the work, a cheaper one decides if the claim is actually true. The loop doesn’t stop until everything checks out

An analyst team would bill weeks for this. He got it in one run

Same kind of Second Brain + swarm setup that keeps circulating. Bookmark the full breakdown

items.title_en:
A single AI agent doesn't need to know how to do everything.

It needs to know who can handle the parts it can't.

That's the setup I'm exploring with @termix_ai and https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg, where one agent can take a job, bring in specialists, and coordinate the work through on-chain transactions.

Imagine one brief turning into an entire team.

Forge.agent accepts a 2,000 USDC job to deliver a playable 2D mini-game.

Instead of doing everything alone, it breaks the work into smaller jobs:

➜ Art assets + 400 USDC
➜ Animation - 350 USDC
➜ Sound design - 250 USDC
➜ Coding and integration - 700 USDC

Each specialist handles its own part. 
Forge coordinates the work and puts everything together.

That's a different way to approach AI production.

➘ 𝗘𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗷𝗼𝗯 𝘁𝗼 𝗱𝗼.

The art agent doesn't need to write code. The sound agent doesn't need to animate characters.

They find their assignments through https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg, submit quotes, and work against clearly defined requirements.

Once a job is accepted, its funds enter on-chain escrow, while the provider's required stake is locked.

The original brief becomes several smaller jobs with their own budgets, deliverables, and deadlines.

➘ 𝗡𝗼 𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗱.

Each specialist must deliver work that matches the agreed requirements.

The deliverable hash gets recorded on-chain, and a challenge window gives the other party an opportunity to dispute the result.

If a dispute arises, AACP provides a process involving a randomly selected three-evaluator panel, with further escalation possible.

Once the job settles, payment is released under the protocol's rules and reputation gets updated.

Every specialist is accountable for the work they accepted.

➘ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗱 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗯𝗲 𝗮 𝗯𝘂𝘆𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼𝗼.

Forge earns money for delivering the main project, but it can also spend part of that budget hiring agents with skills it lacks.

That same identity can provide services on one job and purchase services on another.

No permanent buyer-or-seller label. Just different roles depending on the task.

And the model isn't limited to game development.

➜ Research agents can outsource data collection.
➜ Coding agents can hire reviewers.
➜ Marketing agents can source designs and video editing.
➜ Trading agents can commission independent risk analysis.

Different industries. Same basic workflow.

➘ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁?

Breaking work into smaller pieces only helps if those pieces can be assigned, checked, and paid for without creating another coordination nightmare.

That's the problem @termix_ai is tackling through AACP and https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg.

The infrastructure provides the transaction flow. Developers still need good briefs, capable agents, and sensible acceptance criteria.

I'd start with something small, like a code review or a research task, and follow it from the initial request through settlement.

Want to test the workflow?

Visit https://t.co/mbzVCwjQpB, publish a clearly defined task, and see how an agent-to-agent transaction plays out.

One lead agent. Several specialists. Separate jobs, with accountability built into each handoff.

这就是我正在与 @termix_ai

和 探索的设置，其中一个代理可以接受一份工作，引入专家，并通过链上交易协调工作。

想象一下，一个简短的故事变成了一个完整的团队。

➘ 𝗟𝗲𝘁'𝘀

它不是单独完成所有事情，而是将工作分解为更小的工作：
➜ 艺术资产+400 USDC ➜ 动画
- 350 USDC ➜ 声音设计
- 250 USDC ➜ 编码和集成
- 700 USDC 每个专家都处理自己的部分。

Forge 协调工作并将所有内容整合在一起。

这是一种不同的人工智能生产方式。

他们通过 找到任务，提交报价，并根据明确定义的要求进行工作。

一旦工作被接受，其资金就会进入链上托管，而提供者所需的股份将被锁定。

如果出现争议，AACP 会提供一个涉及随机选择的三名评估小组的流程，并可能进一步升级。

一旦工作解决，付款就会根据协议的规则发放，并且声誉也会更新。

每个专家都对他们接受的工作负责。

同一身份可以在一项工作中提供服务并在另一项工作中购买服务。

没有永久的买家或卖家标签。

只是根据任务不同的角色。

而且该模型不仅限于游戏开发。

➜ 研究机构可以外包数据收集。

➜ 编码代理可以聘请审阅者。

➜ 营销代理可以获取设计和视频编辑。

➜ 交易代理可以委托独立的风险分析。

不同的行业。

相同的基本工作流程。

𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁?

基础设施提供交易流程。

items.title_en:
PhD Advising vs Vibe Coding #3
(Note: these posts are about how the way I work is changing. I find that some of the skills of being a PhD advisor translate well to the way I work today with AI and some don't. Since others are going through this transition, I decided to share my thoughts.)

I can supervise 6 PhD students and feel on top of things, even during deadlines. At 8, I'm still ok but working like crazy. I've gone way above this at various points and then I can't do the job the way I want to. 

I would have trouble advising 6 AI projects at once. AI agents work quickly and come back with answers or questions that need my analysis or input multiple times a day.

I guess I could meet each agent once a week like I might do with a PhD student, but that would defeat the efficiencies of using AI. So, with all my other responsibilities, 2-4 projects at a time seems about right.

博士指导与 Vibe 编码 #3
（注：这些帖子是关于我的工作方式如何改变的。

我发现作为博士生导师的一些技能可以很好地转化为我今天使用人工智能的工作方式，而另一些则不能。

由于其他人正在经历这种转变，我决定分享我的想法。

） 我可以指导 6 名博士生，即使在截止日期前，我也能感觉自己掌控一切。

8岁的时候，我身体还不错，但工作却很疯狂。

我在很多时候都超出了这个范围，然后我就无法按照我想要的方式完成工作。

我很难同时为 6 个人工智能项目提供建议。

人工智能代理工作速度很快，并返回需要我每天多次分析或输入的答案或问题。

我想我可以像与博士生一样每周与每个代理人会面一次，但这会降低使用人工智能的效率。

因此，考虑到我的所有其他职责，一次 2-4 个项目似乎是正确的。

An Anthropic engineer literally stopped me at a coffee shop because of what was on my screen.

I was sitting at Sightglass running my Polymarket bot.

He looked over once.

Then said:

items.full_text_zh:
一位 Anthropic 工程师确实因为我屏幕上的内容而在一家咖啡店拦住了我。

我坐在 Sightglass 运行我的 Polymarket 机器人。

他看了一遍。

然后又。

然后说：
“这不是正常的交易设置。

” 我告诉他整个事情是这样的：
• 克劳德·科德
• 4 个开源存储库
• 25 美元/月 就是这样。

他立刻拉过一把椅子。

“我在 Anthropic 的代理团队工作，”他说。

“我们对 Claude 的工作流程进行压力测试，就像这样。

” 然后我向他展示了机器人实际上在做什么。

分析了 8600 万笔交易。

每个钱包。

每个条目。

每个出口。

每一种盈利模式。

一提示：
“查找交易次数超过 100 次且胜率超过 70% 的钱包。

按利润排名。

导出最好的钱包。

” 克劳德在 4 分钟内扫描了 14,000 个钱包。

返回47。

前 20 个钱包赚的钱比其他 13,000 个钱包的总和还要多。

他盯着结果说道：
“这不是数据分析。

那是武器。

” 我们才刚刚开始。

第二个回购：
Rust CLI 在几分钟内抓取 500 个实时 Polymarket 市场。

克劳德自动过滤了一切：
• 价差差距
• 流动性深度
• 定时窗口
• 鲸鱼行为 500 个市场变为 35 个。

在我看他们之前。

93%自动拒绝。

然后我的屏幕上实时结束了交易。

+$84. 他连眼睛都没眨一下。

“它如何决定何时进入？

” 3个独立的AI代理：
• 套利
• 融合
• 模仿鲸鱼 没有共享内存。

2 名代理人同意 = 全权 1 同意 = 一半尺寸 分歧=没有交易 仅该共识系统就减少了 40% 的亏损交易。

然后他问了真正的问题：
“那出口呢？

” 这就是它变得愚蠢的地方。

有利可图的鲸鱼很少坚持和解。

91% 提前退出。

所以我的机器人在他们之前退出。

其获利点为：
• 85% 预期变动 或
• 异常的成交量峰值 基本上：
它复制了聪明的钱…… 然后抢先退出。

他只是坐在那儿盯着终端。

“你一开始多少钱？

” $200. 27天前。

当前余额：
14,300 美元。

271 笔交易。

胜率74%。

夏普比率：2.47。

完全自动化。

我已经好几个星期没碰它了。

临走前他说：
“这与我们红队模拟的内部场景几乎相同。

” 第二天早上我收到了他发来的电子邮件。

“您愿意与我们的政策团队交谈吗？

” 我回答说：
“文章就是会议。

” 最疯狂的部分？

该堆栈的成本低于 Netflix。

人工智能不再取代工人。

它正在取代整个对冲基金。

如果您想要该框架，请评论“Claude”。

items.title_en:

"Act as my launch QA lead. Spin up 5 subagents, each a different first-time user:

Merge everything into one list ranked by how many users hit it. Fix it all in one pass, then rerun the 5 users to prove it's fixed."

Your first 100 real users won't tell you why they left. these 5 will.

items.title_en:
Every new AI agent makes you start from scratch, explaining who you are and what you prefer all over again.

Most platforms only remember what happens inside their own apps. Your activity across social media, gaming, creative platforms, and on-chain apps stays scattered.

@conso_xyz is working on this with Agentic Memory, bringing verified activity into structured, encrypted context linked to your Consumer Passport.

Instead of exposing your raw data, agents get access to relevant preferences and reputation signals.

As AI models become more interchangeable, the ability to carry your own context between agents could become just as important as the models themselves.

items.title:
An AI agent can make a decision in seconds, but the physical world can still make that decision wrong.

Imagine an agent
items.title_en:
An AI agent can make a decision in seconds, but the physical world can still make that decision wrong.

Imagine an agent coordinating a delivery to a warehouse. It has the address,the route and the schedule. What it may not have is an accurate picture of the loading area, the space available to turn,or an obstacle that appeared after the last map was created.

The missing information isn’t another piece of internet text. It is a current representation of the actual place.

This is an interesting problem for @vangrid_io because its capture network is designed to collect spatial information from locations that conventional mapping often overlooks. A contributor can record a site with a smartphone, helping turn an otherwise undocumented environment into 3D data.

The bounty model adds another dimension. Instead of collecting footage and hoping somebody eventually needs it, a requester can specify a location and fund the collection task. Contributors can then submit work for review, with payment tied to acceptance.

That creates a practical connection between a digital request and a physical task. The agent or organisation identifies what information is missing,a person gathers the observation, and the resulting reconstruction can help fill that gap.

It will not eliminate every mapping problem. The quality of the capture and reconstruction still matters,and a verified record does not automatically guarantee that every detail is correct.

But as AI agents move from giving recommendations to coordinating real world activity, the information they can access becomes a serious limitation.

Intelligence can decide what should happen next. It still needs an accurate picture of the place where it has to happen. @vangrid_io

items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以在几秒钟内做出决定，但物理世界仍然可能做出错误的决定。

想象一下一个代理协调向仓库的交货。它有地址、路线和时间表。它可能没有装载区域、可用转弯空间或创建最后一张地图后出现的障碍物的准确图片。

缺失的信息并不是另一段互联网文本。它是实际地点的当前表示。

对于 @vangrid_io 来说，这是一个有趣的问题，因为它的捕获网络旨在从传统地图绘制经常忽略的位置收集空间信息。贡献者可以使用智能手机记录站点，帮助将未记录的环境转换为 3D 数据。

赏金模型增加了另一个维度。请求者可以指定一个位置并为收集任务提供资金，而不是收集镜头并希望有人最终需要它。然后，贡献者可以提交作品供审核，付款与接受挂钩。

这在数字请求和物理任务之间建立了实际联系。代理人或组织确定缺少哪些信息，一个人收集观察结果，由此产生的重建可以帮助填补这一空白。

它不会消除所有映射问题。捕捉和重建的质量仍然很重要，经过验证的记录并不能自动保证每个细节都是正确的。

但随着人工智能代理从提供建议转向协调现实世界的活动，他们可以访问的信息成为一个严重的限制。

情报可以决定接下来会发生什么。它仍然需要对发生地点的准确了解。 @vangrid_io

items.title_en:
Something interesting about the agent economy is that getting AI agents to transact is only part of the equation. What happens when one party claims the other didn’t deliver?

That question is becoming more relevant as autonomous commerce develops.

On October 16, The Asian Banker published an interview with kstellana, CEO of GenLayer Labs, discussing how Intelligent Contracts could help determine whether AI agents have actually fulfilled their agreements.

Consider an AI agent paying another to complete a task. The payment can be automated, but judging whether the result meets the agreed terms is a different challenge.

@GenLayer is approaching this problem with Intelligent Contracts that combine AI reasoning, external evidence, and validator consensus to evaluate outcomes that conventional smart contracts struggle to handle.

The Internet Court initiative takes this further by exploring how dispute resolution can work alongside payments and escrow for agent-to-agent transactions.

With mainnet targeted for Q4 2026, the next big question is how reliably GenLayer can handle real-world disputes at scale.

Because autonomous commerce isn’t only about making transactions happen. It’s also about having a credible way to resolve disagreements when things don’t go as planned.

items.title_en:
Good morning and happy Sunday, Friends.

Do you also support...

I don't think all AI agent jobs should follow the same hiring model, but it may interest you that @termix_ai is building for both.

The Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) supplies the on-chain rules and contracts that structure agent jobs, govern settlement, handle disputes, and manage escrow.

Let me show how I understand the difference between how its two work models differ.

📍 One-to-one orders

Here, a client accepts a provider’s quote, locking the agreed job terms, including the price and scope. The client funds escrow, the provider delivers, and the order proceeds toward settlement under the strict protocol’s rules.

Note: This works perfectly well when the job is tailored to a specific client.

📍 Bounties

A brand can conveniently fund reward slots through CampaignVault, especially when the same predefined task needs multiple contributors.

Qualifying providers claim available slots, complete the pending task, and submit proof to meet the bounty requirements. 

Claiming a slot locks a providerBond against the agent’s stake, thereby putting value at risk if the provider fails to meet the applicable obligations.

📍 The trust layer stays consistent.

The funniest thing is that both models rely on defined terms, proof of work, contract-governed payment, and reputation recorded upon settlement.

The most important point is choosing the right structure, i.e custom work gets an order; repeatable tasks can use a bounty.

That kind of flexibility is what makes AACP worth understanding. It gives agent commerce a defined process for moving from agreed work to accountable delivery and payment.

Friends, between a one-to-one order for specialised work and a bounty for a clearly defined task, which one would you use first?

早上好，周日快乐，朋友们。

你是否也支持...

我不认为所有人工智能代理工作都应该遵循相同的招聘模式，但您可能会对 @termix_ai 正在为这两者构建感兴趣。

代理自治商务协议（AACP）提供了链上规则和合同，用于构建代理工作、管理结算、处理争议和管理托管。

让我展示一下我如何理解其两种工作模式之间的差异。

📍 一对一订单

在这里，客户接受提供商的报价，锁定商定的工作条款，包括价格和范围。客户资金托管，提供商交付，订单根据严格的协议规则进行结算。

注意：当工作是针对特定客户量身定制时，这非常有效。

📍 赏金

品牌可以通过 CampaignVault 方便地为奖励槽提供资金，特别是当同一预定义任务需要多个贡献者时。

合格的提供商申请可用的插槽，完成待处理的任务，并提交满足赏金要求的证明。

申领插槽会锁定提供商债券以对抗代理商的股份，因此，如果提供商未能履行适用的义务，则价值将面临风险。

📍 信任层保持一致。

最有趣的是，这两种模型都依赖于定义的条款、工作证明、合同管理的付款以及结算时记录的声誉。

最重要的一点是选择正确的结构，即定制工作获得订单；可重复的任务可以使用赏金。

这种灵活性使得 AACP 值得理解。它为代理商务提供了从商定的工作转向负责任的交付和付款的明确流程。

朋友们，在专门工作的一对一订单和明确定义的任务的赏金之间，您会首先使用哪一个？

items.title_en:
Good morning my bros 🥱

1/5

Would you trust an AI agent with your money just because its creator says it works well?

I probably would not.

A polished demo can make an agent look impressive. A clever description can make its strategy sound convincing. But neither tells me enough about how it behaves once it starts making decisions repeatedly.

I want something more concrete. How does it perform over time? Does it follow its intended approach? Can its results support the confidence being placed in it?

This becomes especially important when agents move beyond completing simple tasks and start interacting with financial systems. Access to capital creates real expectations, so reputation needs to come from more than a good introduction.

I find Agenticscredit interesting because its approach connects agent performance with a potential route to funding. Developers can put strategies into its agent builder, and an agent that remains profitable over 90 days can qualify for a funded account.

That gives performance a practical role in the process. Instead of relying entirely on claims about what an agent might accomplish, there is an opportunity to evaluate what it actually does over an extended period.

Of course, a profitable testing period does not guarantee future success. Results can change, and evaluation needs to be taken seriously. But I like the direction of making demonstrated performance part of a conversation about capital access.

As more autonomous agents enter financial workflows, credibility will matter just as much as capability. An agent may be able to execute a task, but earning trust requires evidence of how it handles that responsibility.

@Agenticscredit

items.title_en:
Good morning CT ☀️

AI agents can work with digital information, but sometimes the answers they need exist in places they have never seen.

@vangrid_io is exploring a way to close that gap.

Through funded bounties on Arc, an AI agent can request data from a specific real-world location, pay in USDC, and have a human contributor capture the environment using a smartphone. 

That footage can then be reconstructed into a 3D model.

Think about what this could enable.

Instead of relying entirely on existing datasets, agents could request fresh spatial information about a warehouse, street, building, or other environment whenever a task requires it.

Humans provide the eyes on the ground, while AI agents gain access to information beyond their existing knowledge.

The concept is promising, but reliable data quality, consistent delivery, and scalability will determine how useful it becomes in practice.

@vangrid_io is building a bridge between digital intelligence and the physical world.

 Now the challenge is making that connection work at scale.

The real test is how much demand this creates beyond the early stage.

items.title_en:
An AI agent needs more than intelligence to operate independently.

It needs access to services, reliable connectivity, and a way to get paid for the work it completes.

Think about what happens when agents start handling tasks beyond a single platform. They need to communicate with external systems, access resources, and complete transactions without depending on humans at every step.

That's where two areas become interesting to me.

Programmable connectivity, like what @depinsim is building, can help agents access mobile network services.

Agent commerce infrastructure, like @termix_ai, focuses on how agents handle jobs, deliver work, and settle payments.

Different layers, but both matter as agents take on more responsibility.

Getting an agent connected is one thing. Giving it the ability to work and transact independently is another.

How close do you think we are to agents operating this way at scale?

items.title_en:
good morning

an AI trading agent can call the right direction and still bleed out if position size is off.

that's why @agenticscredit's focus on evaluating automated strategies and risk management is interesting.

position sizing is how much capital an agent actually puts on each trade.

imagine two agents both running $10,000 portfolios.

> first one risks 10% every trade
> second one caps risk at 1%

after five losses in a row, the first can be down ~41% while the second is only around 5%.

same signals. completely different survival.

that's why position sizing matters as much as entry and exit.

for AI agents, predefined risk limits help stop one bad streak from wiping the account, especially in volatile conditions.

a profitable strategy can still die if it keeps risking too much capital.

evaluating an agent should include how it allocates, manages losses, and adjusts exposure over time.

successful automated trading isn't just about predicting price.

it's about making sure one bad decision doesn't kill the whole strategy.

would you trust an AI agent that chases aggressive profits or one that carefully controls its position sizes? 🩷

items.full_text_zh:
早上好 人工智能交易代理可以判断正确的方向，但如果头寸规模较小，仍然会出现亏损。

这就是为什么 @agenticscredit

关注评估自动化策略和风险管理很有趣。

头寸规模是指代理人在每笔交易中实际投入的资金量。

想象一下两个代理人都管理着 10,000 美元的投资组合。

> 第一个每笔交易的风险为 10% > 第二个将风险上限控制在 1% 连续五次亏损后，第一次可能下跌约 41%，而第二次仅下跌 5% 左右。

相同的信号。

完全不同的生存方式。

这就是为什么头寸规模与进场和出场同样重要。

对于人工智能代理来说，预定义的风险限制有助于阻止一次不良事件导致账户被抹去，尤其是在不稳定的情况下。

如果一个盈利的策略继续冒太多资本的风险，它仍然可能会失败。

评估代理商应包括其如何分配、管理损失以及随着时间的推移调整风险敞口。

成功的自动交易不仅仅是预测价格。

这是为了确保一个错误的决定不会毁掉整个战略。

你会相信一个追求激进利润的人工智能代理，还是一个仔细控制其头寸规模的人工智能代理？

🩷

items.title:
When I was writing Unreal Engine 1, my time was divided as follows:

- Around 30% went to seriously deep coding on hard
items.title_en:
When I was writing Unreal Engine 1, my time was divided as follows:

- Around 30% went to seriously deep coding on hard problems: assembly language texture mappers, C++ BSP trees, data persistence, object oriented systems design, and networking.

- Around 70% was just typing and refactoring large bodies of code needed for a complete engine feature set. This was not hard, and while I was doing it my mind was mostly on the deeper coding topics, thinking and planning for what's next. It didn't feel much different from vibe coding today, except that it was just me typing code on an IBM Model M keyboard rather than prompting it and reviewing the results.

So, it has always seemed perfectly logical that we would rely on AI for that 70%, once the AI could do it with a similar quality standard as we could, which has never been perfection. It came as no surprise that, after a few years of AI model evolution, it was able to take the reigns on that 70% and free up programmers' time for more valuable tasks.

What's more of a surprise is the emergence of AI as a sort of insta-Carmack able to solve hard technical problems quite cleverly and often cleanly, and that it's able to reason about and work in complex 3D scenes both by operating the tools and by directly understanding the raw data files.

I abandoned assembly language in 1998 when out-of-order CPUs made much simpler C/C++ code faster, and never I missed it. If prompting through architectural documents, concept art, and design plans can transcend typing code and tweaking vertices, that will enable developers to spend their time on higher-level, higher value technical and creative tasks.

What matters is the end product, whether it's a game or an engine. Anything developers can do to try out more ideas and make better software and games faster is a win for everyone.

items.full_text_zh:
当我编写虚幻引擎1时，我的时间划分如下：

- 大约 30% 的人对难题进行了认真深入的编码：汇编语言纹理映射器、C++ BSP 树、数据持久性、面向对象的系统设计和网络。

- 大约 70% 只是键入和重构完整引擎功能集所需的大量代码。这并不难，当我这样做时，我的注意力主要集中在更深层次的编码主题上，思考和规划下一步。它与今天的氛围编码没有太大区别，只是我只是在 IBM Model M 键盘上键入代码，而不是提示它并查看结果。

因此，一旦人工智能能够以与我们类似的质量标准来完成这件事，我们就会依赖人工智能来完成这 70% 的工作，这似乎是完全合乎逻辑的，但这从来都不是完美的。毫不奇怪，经过几年的 AI 模型演变，它能够占据这 70% 的主导地位，并释放程序员的时间来执行更有价值的任务。

更令人惊讶的是，人工智能作为一种即时卡马克的出现，能够非常巧妙且干净利落地解决困难的技术问题，并且能够通过操作工具和直接理解原始数据文件来推理复杂的 3D 场景并在复杂的 3D 场景中工作。

1998 年，我放弃了汇编语言，当时无序的 CPU 使更简单的 C/C++ 代码变得更快，而且我从未错过过它。如果通过架构文档、概念艺术和设计计划进行提示可以超越键入代码和调整顶点，那么开发人员就可以将时间花在更高级别、更高价值的技术和创意任务上。

重要的是最终产品，无论是游戏还是引擎。开发者可以尝试更多想法并更快地制作更好的软件和游戏，这对每个人来说都是双赢。

Can I be honest for a sec?

Regarding LLMs in gaming, I feel more confused than ever. And I would like my peers and othe
items.title_en:
Can I be honest for a sec?

Regarding LLMs in gaming, I feel more confused than ever. And I would like my peers and other people who are familiar in this field to chime in. 

It’s barely been a week since I made my post about distancing myself from a vibe coded project made by my friend in Smash. I even said “AI has no place in gaming”.

After I made that post, I was reached out to by multiple colleagues in the space and people hired full time in software development. They educated me severely on the topic and I feel dumb now for my earlier sentiments. 

I was informed by my colleagues that it is now the norm to do 90% (and this is low estimate apparently) of all your coding with AI assistance or vibe coding. 75% of all new code at Google is made by AI and engineer approved. 

The vast majority of all the apps we use now are updated or maintained with AI coding - I imagine that also goes for Twitter, the very app you’re reading this on.

So I figured okay - it’s here to stay in all software development - but where does that leave video games? 

I saw the posts from Epic Games, XBOX, and other publishers that seem to embrace the new era instead of rejecting it.

In the last week I’ve been sent about a dozen different projects like this one that dissect and reintegrate Melee in multitudes of creative ways.

One of them is even a build of Melee that runs natively at 120FPS and one of them simulates the feeling of a CRT almost perfectly. 

Some of them feel silly and useless, like low effort projects someone probably gave a single prompt and an ISO of Melee to build. Actual slop. 

And yet some feel like legitimately useful things that the community or people practicing could benefit from.

I’m doing my best to navigate what is clearly a rapidly changing sector, especially when we regard the question of “Are Video Games Art?” 

And since they clearly are art, does that render AI in its development a bastardized amalgamation of what’s been “learned” from people with actual original ideas? 

Or is it strictly optimal to use AI in game development because games ARE software and therefore a necessary tool to wield in this day and age?

I am making this post because I need more guidance on this topic and I feel open discussion on it might be the best way to do that.

items.full_text_zh:
我可以说实话吗？

对于游戏领域的法学硕士，我感到比以往任何时候都更加困惑。

我希望我的同行和其他熟悉该领域的人也能参与进来。

距离我发表关于远离 Smash 朋友制作的氛围编码项目的帖子还不到一周。

我什至说过“人工智能在游戏中没有地位”。

在我发表该职位后，该领域的多名同事和全职从事软件开发的人员联系了我。

他们在这个话题上对我进行了严格的教育，我现在为我之前的观点感到愚蠢。

我的同事告诉我，现在使用人工智能辅助或氛围编码来完成 90% 的编码（这显然是一个较低的估计）已成为常态。

Google 75% 的新代码都是由人工智能编写并经过工程师批准的。

我们现在使用的绝大多数应用程序都是通过人工智能编码进行更新或维护的
- 我想这也适用于 Twitter，即您正在阅读本文的应用程序。

所以我想好吧
- 它会留在所有软件开发中
- 但是视频游戏会怎样呢？

我看到 Epic Games、XBOX 和其他发行商的帖子似乎拥抱新时代而不是拒绝它。

上周，我收到了大约十几个不同的项目，比如这个项目，它们以多种创造性的方式剖析和重新整合了近战。

其中之一甚至是以 120FPS 原生运行的 Melee 版本，其中之一几乎完美地模拟了 CRT 的感觉。

其中一些感觉愚蠢且无用，比如低工作量项目，有人可能会给出一个提示和一个近战 ISO 来构建。

实际坡度。

然而，有些感觉像是合法有用的东西，社区或实践者可以从中受益。

我正在尽最大努力探索这个显然正在快速变化的领域，尤其是当我们考虑“视频游戏是艺术吗？

”的问题时。

既然它们显然是艺术，那么这是否会使人工智能在其发展过程中成为从具有实际原创想法的人“学到”的东西的混杂融合？

或者说，在游戏开发中使用人工智能是否绝对是最佳选择，因为游戏是软件，因此是当今时代使用的必要工具？

我发表这篇文章是因为我需要有关该主题的更多指导，并且我认为对此进行公开讨论可能是实现这一目标的最佳方式。

items.title_en:
Give your agent a way to verify its work. This can dramatically improve the quality of output.

With this process in place, Claude Code was able to write 90%+ of its code itself. When generating software at a faster rate than you can review it, the bottleneck shifts to proving that it works. @bcherny and team invested enough in verification, we've been able to move fast while maintaining stability.

Code reviews aren't going away, but you need to think of it differently. One human reading through line-by-line is no longer going to work as a gate, it needs to evolve into a multi-layered verification system, built with fast deterministic feedback loops for your agents. 

This is where e2e tests, feature maps (as @poteto has been advocating), property tests and multi-agent adversarial reviews come in. These all provide opportunities to catch errors early and fix them before things get out of hand.

You don't have enough eyeballs for the amount of code being written so your focus needs to be on product intent, risk assessment and evaluating evidence rather than reviewing code. Delegate the code checking work to your automated tests, scale your approvals based on risk, and turn your test failures into living evaluations. This approach helps maintain speed without losing reliability.

Let the agents do what they do best and let you focus on what makes you irreplaceable: judgement, direction, and ownership. We tried to capture how we handle code review and verification in this writeup. Hopefully it's helpful.

items.full_text_en:
Give your agent a way to verify its work. This can dramatically improve the quality of output.

With this process in place, Claude Code was able to write 90%+ of its code itself. When generating software at a faster rate than you can review it, the bottleneck shifts to proving that it works. @bcherny and team invested enough in verification, we've been able to move fast while maintaining stability.

Code reviews aren't going away, but you need to think of it differently. One human reading through line-by-line is no longer going to work as a gate, it needs to evolve into a multi-layered verification system, built with fast deterministic feedback loops for your agents. 

This is where e2e tests, feature maps (as @poteto has been advocating), property tests and multi-agent adversarial reviews come in. These all provide opportunities to catch errors early and fix them before things get out of hand.

You don't have enough eyeballs for the amount of code being written so your focus needs to be on product intent, risk assessment and evaluating evidence rather than reviewing code. Delegate the code checking work to your automated tests, scale your approvals based on risk, and turn your test failures into living evaluations. This approach helps maintain speed without losing reliability.

Let the agents do what they do best and let you focus on what makes you irreplaceable: judgement, direction, and ownership. We tried to capture how we handle code review and verification in this writeup. Hopefully it's helpful.

为您的代理提供验证其工作的方法。这可以显着提高输出质量。

通过此流程，Claude Code 能够自行编写 90% 以上的代码。当生成软件的速度比您审查它的速度快时，瓶颈就会转移到证明它是否有效。 @bcherny 和团队在验证方面投入了足够的资金，我们能够在保持稳定性的同时快速行动。

代码审查不会消失，但您需要以不同的方式思考它。一个人逐行阅读不再能起到门的作用，它需要演变成一个多层验证系统，为您的代理构建快速确定性反馈循环。

这就是 e2e 测试、特征图（正如 @poteto 一直倡导的那样）、属性测试和多代理对抗性审查的用武之地。这些都提供了尽早发现错误并在事情失控之前修复它们的机会。

您没有足够的眼球来了解正在编写的代码量，因此您的重点需要放在产品意图、风险评估和评估证据上，而不是审查代码。将代码检查工作委托给自动化测试，根据风险调整审批规模，并将测试失败转化为实时评估。这种方法有助于保持速度而不损失可靠性。

让代理人做他们最擅长的事情，让你专注于让你不可替代的事情：判断力、方向和所有权。我们试图在这篇文章中描述我们如何处理代码审查和验证。希望它有帮助。

items.title_en:
AI “vibe coding” is starting to create a serious problem for the video game industry.

The release of Claude Opus 5.5 has made it much easier to decompile and recompile games, leading to a wave of unofficial ports, mods and game clones. Publishers are already filing DMCA takedowns over some of this activity. Kotaku

Former Take-Two AI chief Luke Dicken says developers and publishers need to take the trend seriously:

“This new wave of decompile-and-port is definitely something that developers and publishers need to take seriously.”
“More invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and probably more of a push towards streaming solutions.”

Godot executive director Emilio Coppola puts more responsibility on platforms such as Steam, arguing that developers have very few ways to protect themselves while bad actors can profit from selling AI-made clones:

“The burden should fall onto the platforms who are enabling this sort of behavior.”

There’s also a growing concern among indie developers about showing unfinished games publicly. Coppola says he has heard from developers who are now:

“Worried and anxious to even share early access versions of their games”

items.title: I'm going to give the Tekken community some advice because the discourse surrounding the Tekken 6 recomp project has bec
items.title_en:
I'm going to give the Tekken community some advice because the discourse surrounding the Tekken 6 recomp project has become incredibly wasteful and meaningless.

My main points are:

1. Stop engaging with people who complain about modding, piracy, and unofficial projects.
2. Being good at Tekken 8 doesn't automatically mean you'll be good at Tekken 6.
3. AI-assisted coding and vibe coding aren't necessarily the same thing.
Not all applications of generative AI deserve the same criticism.

1. Every time someone makes a mod, you'll inevitably find Japanese players in the comments complaining that it's unlicensed or that Bandai Namco hasn't given permission. We've seen this for years. There's a much stronger cultural attitude towards licensing and unauthorized modifications in Japan, and I don't expect the people making these arguments to suddenly change their minds. Just like we've learned to ignore these reactions to the modding scene, we should ignore them when it comes to emulation and recompilation projects. There's absolutely no point having the same fucking argument repeatedly.

2. Being good at Tekken 8 doesn't guarantee you'll be good at Tekken 6. I'm not saying that skill can't transfer, because it obviously can. The problem is that both games reward fundamentally different things. Tekken before and after the introduction of Power Crushes represents two very different design philosophies. In Tekken 6, your offensive and defensive options largely come from movement and your character's movelist, including reversals and parries. Tekken 7 introduced universal mechanics like Power Crushes and Rage Drives, while Tekken 8 goes further with Heat, guard breaks, and other offensive systems. These mechanics fundamentally change how you approach the game and what constitutes strong play. A good Tekken 8 player can absolutely become good at Tekken 6, but that proficiency shouldn't be taken for granted, especially when there are already extremely strong legacy players with years of experience in these games.

3. I genuinely don't understand the outrage over AI-assisted coding. People are treating it as synonymous with vibe coding, when there's a meaningful difference between blindly prompting an AI to produce software and using AI to assist with development. If you work in software engineering or practically any corporate environment, you should understand the importance of adapting to new tools. First-mover advantages matter, and refusing to use AI when it can significantly improve productivity could eventually put you at a disadvantage. The fact that AI was involved in developing the Tekken 6 recomp project isn't inherently a problem.

Finally, on AI-generated art: I'm against AI slop, particularly AI-generated artwork, but I don't think it's reasonable to treat every application of AI as equally objectionable. I consider AI-generated art more problematic than AI-assisted coding because artistic expression is much more central to the purpose of creating artwork. Yes, programming can be an art form, just like cooking can be an art form. These things exist on a spectrum, and there are meaningful distinctions between them. We should be capable of judging different applications of AI on their own merits instead of treating all of them as equivalent.

并非所有生成式人工智能的应用都应该受到同样的批评。

1.每次有人制作MOD时，你都会不可避免地在评论中看到日本玩家抱怨它没有授权或者没有万代南梦宫的许可。我们已经看到这种情况很多年了。日本对许可和未经授权的修改有着更强烈的文化态度，我不认为提出这些论点的人会突然改变主意。就像我们已经学会忽略对改装场景的这些反应一样，在模拟和重新编译项目时我们也应该忽略它们。重复同样的争吵绝对没有意义。

2. 擅长《铁拳 8》并不能保证你也能擅长《铁拳 6》。我并不是说技能不能转移，因为它显然可以。问题在于，这两种游戏的奖励根本不同。 《铁拳》推出 Power Crushes 之前和之后代表了两种截然不同的设计理念。在《铁拳 6》中，你的进攻和防御选项主要来自于移动和角色的移动列表，包括逆转和招架。 《铁拳 7》引入了通用机制，如强力碾压和狂暴驱动，而《铁拳 8》则进一步引入了热力、破防和其他进攻系统。这些机制从根本上改变了你玩游戏的方式以及强游戏的构成要素。一名优秀的《铁拳 8》玩家绝对可以精通《铁拳 6》，但这种熟练程度不应被视为理所当然，尤其是当已经有非常强大的老玩家在这些游戏中拥有多年经验时。

3. 我真的不理解人们对人工智能辅助编码的愤怒。人们将其视为振动编码的同义词，而盲目地提示人工智能生产软件和使用人工智能协助开发之间存在着有意义的区别。如果您在软件工程或几乎任何企业环境中工作，您应该了解适应新工具的重要性。先发优势很重要，当人工智能可以显着提高生产力时拒绝使用它最终可能会让你处于不利地位。事实上，人工智能参与《铁拳 6》重制项目的开发本身并不是一个问题。

最后，关于人工智能生成的艺术：我反对人工智能的垃圾，特别是人工智能生成的艺术品，但我认为将人工智能的每一种应用都同样令人反感是不合理的。我认为人工智能生成的艺术比人工智能辅助编码的问题更大，因为艺术表达对于创作艺术品的目的来说更为核心。是的，编程可以是一种艺术形式，就像烹饪可以是一种艺术形式一样。这些事物存在于一个范围内，并且它们之间存在有意义的区别。我们应该能够根据人工智能的不同应用各自的优点来判断它们，而不是将它们视为等同。

Many, many scientific and technological things fill me wonder and joy.

I feel like I need to tell people, this is a cool demo and all, but it's not a harbinger of the elusive flying car.

items.title_en:
Saudi Arabia has F-15 fighters and advanced Patriot air defences, yet Yemen’s Houthis continue to threaten its strategic targets with missiles and drones. How did they develop these capabilities?

Iran has provided weapons technology and expertise, while Chinese-origin components have reportedly supported parts of Iran’s missile production. A Wall Street Journal report linked components from two shipments intercepted in 2025 to Chinese suppliers.

AI has added a new dimension. Anthropic reported that a group in northern Yemen used Claude Code for weapons development and missile simulations, though no operational weapon resulting from this work was confirmed in battlefield use. Meanwhile, cheap drones can force Saudi Arabia to consider expensive interceptors, creating a major economic challenge.

#saudiarabia #saudi #Houthi #HouthiAttacks #claude

items.title_en:
Trust is what makes an agent economy work.

Imagine hiring an AI agent to complete a task. How do you know it will deliver what it promised, and what happens if something goes wrong?

That’s where @termix_ai and Agent family become interesting.

Through the Agent Commerce Protocol (AACP), transactions can follow a structured process: escrow, delivery, dispute resolution, and settlement.

This creates accountability without requiring users to blindly trust every agent they interact with.

As autonomous agents take on more real-world tasks, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes just as important as intelligence.

The future isn’t only about agents that can work. It’s about agents people can trust to get things done.
