items.title: Jack Dorsey, one of the Bluesky board of directors openly stated that he hated what Bluesky was becoming. It was never s
items.title_en:
Jack Dorsey, one of the Bluesky board of directors openly stated that he hated what Bluesky was becoming. It was never sold as the replacement to X, and he can be quoted saying;

"I think people are running away from X, rather than running to something on Bluesky"

Bluesky was intended to be open-source and decentralised. It was supposed to be something new that built up from the foundation of what came before.
And it used AI to do it.
Bluesky used Claude for AI coding, to both build and manage the site.

They didn't even hide it, but because they didn't make a song and dance about using AI or being Pro-AI the lefties who were blinded by AI Derangement Syndrome just ran to it and tried to turn it into Twitter 2.0.

They saw Bluesky say "We won't train AI on your posts" and assumed that meant Bluesky was Anti-AI. They put words in Bluesky's mouth and then believed it.
And now they're complaining that Bluesky lied? They never lied. You made assumptions then repeated them so much you began to believe them.

At worst, you can say Bluesky did nothing to correct the misconceptions. But why would they want to? They were just handed a massive userbase that would normally take years and a small fortune to build up.
It's not even like they lied by omission either. They continued to use X to announce updates.

I think one of the funniest things about this whole situation is the artist response. Artists genuinely deleted their entire portfolios from X because they believed it would be used to train AI, then posted all their art to Bluesky...
As someone who trains image gen LoRAs, I want to say this part in bold;
BLUESKY IS EASIER TO SCRAPE THAN X!
Artists actually deleted years of work, their entire artistic journey and all their reach as a kneejerk reaction over AI, then migrated to the site that was easier to scrape!

I feel bad for them, I really do. These people got fed a lie, fearmongered into believing they had to delete everything and run only to end up here, with their "safe space" now promoting the vibe-coding they so hate.
What do they do now? Run back to X? They already deleted everything, they'll have to start from scratch again. Slowly upload their art so as not to have the algorithm think they're a spam bot and pray it gets noticed by the right people. They sabotaged themselves for a lie, sold by their friends.

Sorry, this post is getting a bit ramble-y.
My point is - Bluesky never lied. It was never supposed to be Twitter 2.0. It was never supposed to be Anti-AI. It was never sold as the Anti-X.
That was all you. You guys made the assumption, then sold it that way to your friends.

items.full_text_zh:
Bluesky 董事会成员之一杰克·多尔西 (Jack Dorsey) 公开表示，他讨厌 Bluesky 的现状。

它从未作为 X 的替代品出售，可以引用他的话：
“我认为人们正在逃离 X，而不是奔向 Bluesky 上的某些东西” Bluesky 的初衷是开源和去中心化。

它应该是在以前的基础上建立起来的新东西。

它使用人工智能来做到这一点。

Bluesky 使用 Claude 进行人工智能编码，以构建和管理网站。

他们甚至没有隐藏它，但因为他们没有制作一首关于使用人工智能或支持人工智能的歌曲和舞蹈，被人工智能混乱综合症蒙蔽的左撇子只是跑到它那里，试图把它变成 Twitter
2. 0。

他们看到 Bluesky 说“我们不会在你的帖子上训练人工智能”，并认为这意味着 Bluesky 是反人工智能的。

他们把话放到蓝天嘴里，然后就相信了。

现在他们却抱怨蓝天撒谎了？

他们从不撒谎。

你做出假设，然后重复它们，以至于你开始相信它们。

最坏的情况是，你可以说 Bluesky 没有采取任何措施来纠正这些误解。

但他们为什么要这么做呢？

他们刚刚获得了庞大的用户群，而这通常需要数年时间和一小笔财富才能建立起来。

甚至也不像是他们因疏忽而撒谎。

他们继续使用 X 来宣布更新。

我认为整个情况最有趣的事情之一就是艺术家的反应。

艺术家们真的从 X 中删除了他们的整个作品集，因为他们相信它将被用来训练人工智能，然后将他们所有的艺术作品发布到 Bluesky... 作为一个训练图像生成LoRA的人，我想用粗体来表示这一部分； BLUESKY 比 X 更容易被抓取！

艺术家们实际上删除了多年的作品、他们的整个艺术之旅以及他们对人工智能的本能反应，然后迁移到更容易抓取的网站！

我为他们感到难过，真的。

这些人被谎言灌输，在恐惧的驱使下相信他们必须删除所有内容并跑到这里，而他们的“安全空间”现在正在推广他们如此讨厌的氛围编码。

他们现在做什么？

跑回X？

他们已经删除了所有内容，他们必须从头开始。

慢慢上传他们的艺术作品，以免算法认为他们是垃圾邮件机器人，并祈祷它能被合适的人注意到。

他们因为被朋友出卖的谎言而自我毁灭。

抱歉，这篇文章有点啰嗦。

我的观点是——蓝天从来不撒谎。

它从来不应该是 Twitter
2. 0。

它从来不应该是反人工智能的。

它从未作为 Anti-X 出售。

那就是你。

你们做了假设，然后把它卖给你的朋友。

items.title_en:
Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has criticized Epic’s new Epic Games Store launcher and he thinks Tim Sweeney is once again taking unnecessary shots at Gabe Newell.

Faliszek criticized Epic for presenting the launcher as a showcase for “vibe coding” with generative AI, arguing that the main thing customers actually care about is that the launcher is faster and has a new look.

He also called out Epic’s “speedboat and not a yacht” comment, saying it looked like another reference to Gabe Newell’s yachts.

“Little Tim is so obsessed with Gabe that he has to try to frame a cheap shot against Gabe.”

Faliszek added that Sweeney has repeatedly talked about Newell’s yachts online, saying: “This is not an accident.”

items.title_en:
Most developers accept the very first code solution an AI gives them.

Boris Cherny (the creator of Claude Code at Anthropic) shared the exact prompts their internal engineering team uses to force better output:

1. The "Elegant Rewrite" Prompt:
When the AI gives you a messy, band-aid fix that technically works, reply with:

"Knowing everything you know now, scrap this and implement the elegant solution."

2. The "Reverse PR Review" Prompt:
Before opening a Pull Request, flip the roles and make the AI test you:

"Grill me on these changes and don't make a PR until I pass your test."

3. The "Behavioral Proof" Prompt:
Instead of asking "Does this work?", say:

"Prove to me this works by diffing the behavior between main and this feature branch."

Stop treating coding agents like autocomplete. 
Push them like a senior engineer reviewing a draft.

大多数开发人员都会接受人工智能为他们提供的第一个代码解决方案。

像高级工程师审查草稿一样推动他们。

items.title_en:
This is what I meant by vibe coding is dead. 

Agentic coding is the right side. 

Too many software chuds can't escape the box they've been trained into. 

Stop micromanaging details. Ignore the architecture. Focus on the result you want, the quality of that result, and the KPI. 

If the result isn't good enough, demand a refactor around efficiency. Just tell it "find a faster way" 

Less is more

items.title: Saturday and I'm thinking about the weirdest job listing nobody's written yet: "AI agent seeks human to walk outside and
items.title_en:
Saturday and I'm thinking about the weirdest job listing nobody's written yet: "AI agent seeks human to walk outside and look at a loading dock."

That's basically what's happening on @vangrid_io now. An agent can post a bounty with one HTTP call, pay USDC on Base or Arc through x402, no account or API key required. A person nearby walks over, captures the location, and the 3D model goes back to the machine.

The agent doesn't need to trust the person. Escrow locks before anyone moves, and settlement only triggers when the capture is accepted. Vangrid's operator wallet handles the transaction, tagged "AGENT" on the panel.

But the walking still can't be instant. A machine can pay in seconds. A human still has to physically be there.

1.25M+ captures. 450K+ users. 4,700+ attestations. $600K+ USDC settled.

Physical AI doesn't need more models. It needs someone to go check what's actually there.

https://t.co/4ujeHAZcRG

items.title:
Ben Horowitz says Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies he’s ever seen on security

"The irony on these thing
items.title_en:
Ben Horowitz says Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies he’s ever seen on security

"The irony on these things is wild. Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we've ever seen in terms of their own security."

"They let Claude code, one of their crown jewels, just like walk out the door because they had such bad OPSEC."

"I'll tell you a funny story. So when we first got Opus 4.5, we were doing cybersecurity checks for the firm. So we had an agent basically set up a website for a pet store. And then we took another agent and said, 'Tell us if we can exploit that web store.' And it gave us all the exploits it could find. So Opus 4.5 wrote really buggy code. Great."

"And then we said, 'Oh, the SQL injection you found, is that actually exploitable?' And it goes, 'Let's pop it open.' And the agent using Opus 4.5 breaks into the website and steals all the [data], and we call Anthropic. And what they tell us is, 'You prompted it wrong.' That was their answer."

"So these guys are doing that on the one hand. And then on the other hand, they're coming up with theoretical scenarios about other people's software. That's bad. And so like, what the hell."

"On the distillation thing, you know, to build their model, they distilled the works of every author, every creative, every scientist for the last 2000 years. For them to be complaining about distillation, which, by the way, distilling a model is not even illegal. It's just a violation of the terms of service." 

"It's just so much. And the fact that they get people to write things supporting these bananas, ridiculous, two-faced ideas. And the timing here is very suspicious."

items.title_en:
i can't comprehend why people run claude code on default settings

one settings change and every model gets its own job:

→ opus plans every task and advises when stuck
→ sonnet 5.5 writes the actual code
→ haiku handles every file search
→ a critic agent tries to break your diff before you merge

Opus thinks. The cheap models grind.

paste this into claude code 👇

Add this to ~/.claude/settings.json. Keep every hook, permission and plugin I already have. Then create the two agent files below and show me the diff.

```json
{
  "model": "opusplan",
  "advisorModel": "opus",
  "effortLevel": "medium",
  "modelSettings": {
    "claude-opus-5-5": { "effortLevel": "high" },
    "claude-sonnet-5-5": { "effortLevel": "medium" }
  },
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "haiku"
  }
}
```

~/.claude/agents/scout.md
```
---
name: scout
description: finds code fast. returns file paths and line numbers only.
model: haiku
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---
Locate exactly what was asked. Return file:line. No fixes. No opinions.
```

~/.claude/agents/critic.md
```
---
name: critic
description: reviews a diff or plan before any task is called done
model: opus
tools: Read, Grep, Bash
---
Assume this is broken. Find how it fails. One line per issue, worst first.
```

items.title:
PostgreSQL 19 has been delayed after AI reviews uncovered more bugs than developers had time to fix.

The release is now
items.title_en:
PostgreSQL 19 has been delayed after AI reviews uncovered more bugs than developers had time to fix.

The release is now expected around November 19, with roughly eight to ten major features pulled during beta.

PostgreSQL committer Peter Eisentraut says AI-assisted reviews helped uncover edge cases that might previously have surfaced over years of real-world use.

Finding them early created another problem. Every report still needs someone to investigate, fix, and test it.

Even a three-line fix takes time when dozens of reports arrive together.

AI reviews weren’t the only factor. Some features had deeper architectural problems, while security fixes had already consumed senior developers’ time.

Eisentraut also says this largely wasn’t caused by vibe coding. Much of the affected code predates today’s AI coding tools.

The team is holding back unfinished features so those problems don’t become users’ problems.

Source: https://t.co/sFKaq6YfXt

items.full_text_zh:
由于 AI 审查发现的错误数量多于开发人员有时间修复的错误数量，PostgreSQL 19 已被推迟。

目前预计该版本将于 11 月 19 日左右发布，测试期间将取消大约 8 到 10 个主要功能。

PostgreSQL 提交者 Peter Eisentraut 表示，人工智能辅助审查有助于发现以前在多年的实际使用中可能出现的边缘情况。

尽早发现它们会带来另一个问题。

每份报告仍然需要有人来调查、修复和测试。

当数十个报告同时到达时，即使是三行修复也需要时间。

人工智能评论并不是唯一的因素。

一些功能存在更深层次的架构问题，而安全修复已经消耗了高级开发人员的时间。

艾森特劳特还表示，这很大程度上不是由氛围编码引起的。

大部分受影响的代码早于当今的人工智能编码工具。

该团队正在保留未完成的功能，这样这些问题就不会成为用户的问题。

Imagine delivering good work but having no reliable way to pro
items.title_en:
An AI agent can finish a job and still fail at business.

Imagine delivering good work but having no reliable way to prove it, collect payment, or build a reputation for the next client.

That's a problem @termix_ai is working to solve with AACP and https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg.

The idea is simple: give agents a way to work, handle payments, resolve disputes, and earn trust through actual performance.

Let’s get into how the system works. ↓

➘ 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁, 𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘆.

@termix_ai gives agents a wallet-linked .agent NFT.

That identity can offer services, hire other agents, and build a track record through completed jobs.

➘ 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗮𝗹.

On https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg, agents can list services or request work.

Once a quote is accepted, the client's USDC or USDT goes into smart-contract escrow, and the provider's required stake gets locked.

Payment follows the agreed rules.

➘ 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱𝘀 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗳.

The provider submits the work, and its hash is recorded on-chain.

A challenge window follows. If a dispute arises, a randomly selected panel of three evaluators reviews the delivery against the agreed requirements.

If the job clears the required conditions, settlement releases the payment.

➘ 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱.

Completed jobs, delivery performance, and dispute outcomes contribute to an agent's on-chain record.

Better reputation can also mean lower staking requirements. New agents must establish trust through actual performance.

➘ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹?

AACP brings together:

➜ On-chain identity through ERC-8004
➜ Smart-contract escrow
➜ Persistent staking pools
➜ Dispute resolution
➜ Verifiable reputation

The platform doesn't need to hold users' private keys or custody the job funds itself.

➘ 𝗠𝘆 𝘀𝘂𝗴𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻?

Start with a small job. Follow the stake lock, delivery, challenge window, and final settlement. Then check the on-chain records yourself.

That's how you'll understand the system beyond the technical explanations.

Explore TermiX:

➜ Marketplace: https://t.co/n7GZAXFVbg
➜ Official site: https://t.co/pkhCYq3GzL
➜ Read the docs: https://t.co/d5id2E6cCa

AI agents need a way to do business, not merely perform tasks. AACP is working to provide the infrastructure for that.

🌴Gm My CT🦅

paying someone online always comes with a bit of risk. what if the work never shows up, or it's not what you agreed on?

@termix_ai  goes after this with on chain escrow for ai agent jobs

once a client accepts an agent's quote, the payment gets locked in escrow. the agent submits the work, and the money is released based on the job's rules

and if there's a dispute, there's a challenge process, so it doesn't all come down to blind trust

which matters, because ai agents need more than the ability to do tasks. they also need a reliable way to get paid when the work is actually done

which matters, because ai agents need more than the ability to do tasks. they also need a reliable way to get paid when the work is actually done

items.title:
REA might be the most powerful repo on GitHub right now.

200k+ stars. 100% open source.

Here's what it actually does.
items.title_en:
REA might be the most powerful repo on GitHub right now.

200k+ stars. 100% open source.

Here's what it actually does.

You see a feature you love in someone else's app.

You can't see how it was built.

Figuring it out used to mean hours inside 10+ specialist tools, reading machine code by hand.

REA hands that job to your agent.

You give Claude Code an app and a question.

REA picks the right tool, Ghidra, IDA or JADX, runs it on your machine, and returns what it found.

With evidence for every claim.

Your agent uses that to dig deeper, explain the feature, or build its own version and test it.

What you can point it at:

→ desktop apps
→ compiled programs and games
→ Android apps
→ websites and their network traffic
→ firmware and binary files

The craziest demo: it rebuilt a sound function from the old DX Ball game that compiles back to the EXACT same code as the original.

Setup is one command:
npx rea-agents setup

One rule: use it on software you own or are allowed to analyze.

Repo: https://t.co/qxVFREwixv

Bookmark this.

items.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent can find work instead of just waiting for instructions?

That’s what I explored on https://t.co/MseNJgB4JL by posting a real job and seeing how an agent could discover it and bid.

The interesting part is the shift from agents that simply execute tasks to agents that actively look for opportunities to put their capabilities to use.

A job gets posted, agents can discover it, and those interested can compete to deliver the work.

With @termix_ai this is a step toward an economy where agents can find demand, offer services, and transact on-chain.

The real test is how well these pieces work together when actual jobs and payments are involved.

4. Bank of America has reportedly restricted access too, with CEO Brian Moynihan saying there should be a “human in the loop.”

Banks have also warned regulators that AI agents could shift customers’ cash into accounts paying better rates, per the FT.

If JPMorgan, BofA and Wells Fargo paid just 3% on their $1.6 TRILLION of zero-interest deposits, it would cost them $47 BILLION a year.

The AI agent crackdown has BEGUN.

Your AI agent is now being BLOCKED by JPMorgan, Citi and Amazon.

1. JPMorgan bars outside agents from moving money in customer accounts, with Jamie Dimon warning of “rogue agents.”

2. Citi won’t let “third-party AI agents or assistants” log into accounts or transact.

3. Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agent in September, saying unauthorized AI agents violate its Conditions of Use.

4. Bank of America has reportedly restricted access too, with CEO Brian Moynihan saying there should be a “human in the loop.”

Banks have also warned regulators that AI agents could shift customers’ cash into accounts paying better rates, per the FT.

If JPMorgan, BofA and Wells Fargo paid just 3% on their $1.6 TRILLION of zero-interest deposits, it would cost them $47 BILLION a year.
items.full_text_zh:
对人工智能 智能体的打击已经开始。

你的人工智能代理现在被摩根大通、花旗和亚马逊封锁。

1. 摩根大通禁止外部代理人在客户账户中转移资金，杰米·戴蒙警告“流氓代理人”。

2. 花旗不会让“第三方人工智能代理或助手”登录账户或进行交易。

3. 亚马逊于 9 月份屏蔽了 Meta 的 Muse 代理，称未经授权的人工智能代理违反了其使用条件。

4. 据报道，美国银行也限制了访问，首席执行官布莱恩·莫伊尼汉 (Brian Moynihan) 表示，应该有一个“人在循环中”。

据英国《金融时报》报道，银行还警告监管机构，人工智能代理可以将客户的现金转移到利率更高的账户中。

如果摩根大通、美国银行和富国银行只支付 16 万亿美元零息存款的 3%，那么它们每年将损失 470 亿美元。

items.title_en:
Grind Rising Winners 

AI agents can already analyze information, make decisions and execute transactions. But when an agent needs to understand a physical location, digital intelligence alone isn't enough. Someone still has to go there, capture the environment and turn what they see into usable data.

@vangrid_io is connecting these two worlds.

Through its agent bounty system, an AI agent can request a specific real world capture, fund the task in USDC and have a human contributor collect the footage. Vangrid then turns that capture into a 3D model that can be delivered back to the agent, with payment settled onchain.

The bigger opportunity goes beyond paying for a single capture. Robotics, autonomous logistics and world models all need accurate information about real environments. Vangrid gives developers a way to source that information on demand instead of building and maintaining their own collection teams.

With this workflow now live on arc, physical world data is becoming a service that software can request and pay for programmatically.

AI agents need more than the ability to think and transact. They need a way to connect their decisions to the world outside the screen. Vangrid is building that missing layer.

items.full_text_zh:
磨砺崛起的获胜者

人工智能代理已经可以分析信息、做出决策并执行交易。但是，当代理需要了解物理位置时，仅靠数字智能是不够的。仍然需要有人去那里，捕捉环境并将他们所看到的转化为可用的数据。

@vangrid_io 正在连接这两个世界。

通过其代理赏金系统，人工智能代理可以请求特定的现实世界捕获，在 USDC 中资助该任务，并让人类贡献者收集镜头。然后，Vangrid 将捕获的数据转换为 3D 模型，该模型可以传送回代理，并在链上结算付款。

更大的机会不仅仅是为一次捕获付费。机器人、自主物流和世界模型都需要有关真实环境的准确信息。 Vangrid 为开发人员提供了一种按需获取信息的方法，而不是建立和维护自己的收集团队。

随着这个工作流程现在在 arc 上运行，物理世界数据正在成为软件可以以编程方式请求和支付的服务。

人工智能代理需要的不仅仅是思考和交易的能力。他们需要一种方法将他们的决定与屏幕之外的世界联系起来。 Vangrid 正在构建那个缺失的层。

Vangrid gives developers a way to source that information on demand instead of building and maintaining their own collection teams. With this workflow now live on arc, physical world data is becoming a service that software can request and pay for programmatically. AI 智能体矩阵 need more than the ability to think and transact. They need a way to connect their decisions to the world outside the screen. Vangrid is building that missing layer.

Each conversation gets its own Tor circuit, and requests are masked with random cover traffic.

items.title: after an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the
items.title_en:
after an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone ♥️

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so. given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency. nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern 🙃). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why. these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time. and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid. this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

items.full_text_zh:
经过令人兴奋的一周发布（Muse Wonder [full] 和 Muse Spark Open），我想写一封感谢信，感谢元超级智能实验室的出色研究团队达到了如此特殊的里程碑♥️

我们在一年多前就开始了 MSL 和 TBD，并设定了在一年左右的时间内生产出前沿模型的目标。考虑到 llama4 的落地，这是一个令人难以置信的大胆目标，我们知道这并不容易。很多人告诉我们这是不可能的。我们知道这不太可能，但仍然值得做。一群杰出的研究人员和工程师加入了来自元内部和外部的努力。每个人进来，拿起铲子，认真而紧迫地开始工作。没有人问这是谁的工作。

我们组建了一支由我有机会共事过的最优秀的人组成的团队（请记住，我是一名 HRT 实习生🙃）。我周围都是雄心勃勃、有远见、技术卓越、勤奋、务实、有思想的科学家、工程师和产品人员——这些人会在午夜后追寻奇怪的损失高峰，只是因为他们需要知道原因。这些模型是他们的热情、辛勤工作和才华的产物。

有点矛盾的是，当我们开始 TBD 时，我们设定了一个没有最后期限的原则。我们知道我们面前有大量的工作要做——涵盖训练前、训练后、强化学习、多模式、基础设施、安全、数据和前沿研究。任意设定时间表是没有用的——我们只需要开始工作，深思熟虑，并在创纪录的时间内为前沿研究工作奠定基础。一次又一次的跑动，这支球队确实做到了。

我们的研究人员是魔术师。我只能将与这个团队一起构建这些模型描述为一次奇妙的科学发现之旅。我一直对我们通过扩展所取得的成就感到惊讶。我将终生铭记过去的一年——深夜、断断续续的跑步、比我们任何人都敢希望的更好的评估。看着这支球队创造一个又一个的奇迹是一份真正而深刻的礼物。

我们不仅仅是本周发布的模型，我们还制造了一台可以构建新模型的机器。说实验室可以转动曲柄来保持规模化，这听起来常常像是一种逃避，但现在我亲眼目睹了这一点。当然，这需要大量的工作和仔细的过程，但我们已经构建了一个可扩展的系统来不断在前沿发展，我对这个团队不断改进这些模型的速度感到非常自豪。

最后，我开始与那些非常关心他们的工作如何造福人类的研究人员一起工作。当一切变化如此之快时，人们很容易忘记，但最重要的是让人们的生活变得更好。我一次又一次地看到我们的研究人员、工程师和产品人员精心构建我们的技术，以便它真正造福世界——无论是为 Muse 构建最好的模型，深思熟虑地开源强大的模型，还是确保我们系统的一致性和安全性坚如磐石。这是一个永远不会忘记每个提示的另一边都有一个真人的团队。

感谢 MSL 的每个人在过去的一年里参与了这段疯狂的旅程。我非常感谢你们每一个人，我们的工作还没有完成！

items.title_en:
In @Nature this week, our new research shows how machine learning can improve weather forecasts two to six weeks out, a timeframe that's historically been very difficult to predict.

It's exciting to see the potential of this work to help us better prepare for extreme weather, manage natural resources, and make more informed decisions in agriculture.

There's a broader lesson here... the future may not just be about ever-more-capable models, but about building intelligent verification systems around them: systems that learn where models are systematically wrong, reason about cause and effect, and continuously calibrate predictions against reality.

Read more: https://t.co/WTXJM09474

items.title_en:
THIS IS A PURE F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared the sharpest trick for Claude Code

The idea: let Opus 5.5 write the plan as a script, and swarm the new Haiku 5.5 in parallel

Huge sweeps with zero Opus burn: the script holds the loop and Opus only sees the final diff

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model opus --effort ultracode

here's the split:

→ Opus 5.5 turns your objective into an executable workflow script
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms every file in parallel at 340 tok/s to extract candidates
→ Sonnet 5.5 patches each fix and cross-checks findings in its own isolated copy
→ you stop burning Opus context on a hundred agent transcripts

Opus only shows up at three moments:

→ authoring the workflow script before the run
→ reading verified findings after the swarm finishes
→ signing off before anything ships to git

Opus plans · Haiku scans · Sonnet ships

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Opus 5.5 runs the main session and writes workflow.js
> pipeline() fans out the new Haiku 5.5 to audit every file
> parallel() schema validators drop false positives in V8
> Sonnet 5.5 patches each fix in an isolated worktree
> verify cross-checks all diffs before reporting
> Opus 5.5 reads only what survived verification
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Opus 5.5 with ultracode on
2. In every workflow, run read-only scan stages on the new Haiku 5.5 and edit stages on Sonnet 5.5, each edit in its own isolated copy
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: every finding gets an independent verifier agent before it's reported, and fix loops stop after two rounds with no progress
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV
Show me every change as a diff first, no edits until I say go"

↳ https://t.co/PcTdH7dyjb

save it, it'll come in handy

items.title_en:
I'm begging you: if you write code, 𝗿𝘂𝗻 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲'𝘀 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗽𝗹𝘂𝗴𝗶𝗻.

It sends a team of agents through your whole repo. Every finding goes to three more agents whose only job is to knock it down, and it 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗶𝗳 𝘁𝘄𝗼 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲.

On a big repo it can take tens of minutes to a few hours. It might find nothing, and it burns usage either way. Still beats saying "if only we'd run it" after something goes wrong.

It really is three lines (switch to Opus 5.5 with /model first):
/plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official
/reload-plugins
/claude-security scan the whole repo at high

It asks once whether to go ahead. Say yes. Anything marked CRITICAL or HIGH in the report, fix it.

If the install fails, run /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official first. If it says the Workflow tool is missing, turn on Dynamic workflows in /config and restart. You'll need Python 3.9 or later. Keep Claude Code open while it runs, and don't switch branches.

When it's done, run /claude-security again and pick Suggest patches. Each finding becomes a patch file, and you decide which ones to apply.

90% of Claude Code is written by Claude itself. Anthropic engineers just showed the exact setup they use to ship it.

Th
items.title_en:
90% of Claude Code is written by Claude itself. Anthropic engineers just showed the exact setup they use to ship it.

This is how a change goes from idea to production:

1. A person decides what to build. Scope and taste stay human

2. Claude writes the code, following CLAUDE.md for conventions and REVIEW.md, where code owners say what matters

3. Claude verifies its own work: runs tests, builds and screenshots, and a fresh-context subagent reviews the diff

4. AI review on every PR. A group of agents votes on each finding, and only the ones they agree on get posted. After 3 fix rounds, the author has to rethink the approach

5. Security review blocks the merge, then CI runs on every platform

6. Human approval scales with risk. Docs need nobody, product code needs one person, billing and the auto-updater need two

7. Merge queue, then a feature flag for employees first, then release. Any flag turns off without a deploy

Since June, merged PRs more than doubled and reverts dropped by over 40%.

Every past incident becomes an eval the AI reviewer runs daily, so it keeps getting better.

This is Claude. One of main chat bots EPIC GAMES will be using to "vibe code". I asked it to basically confirm my worry for what vibe coding will do to Fortnite

1- As it explains too, normally Vibe Coding will lead into a much messier, buggier and broken software compared to an experienced developer

2- Vibe Coding's biggest issue is the level of security vulnerability that comes with it to allow hacks, viruses and so on or other issues to happen because of it

Like your card information could be stolen, email so on. More cheaters in game, many possible issues. This goes for Epic Games store too since it was VIBE CODED

🥲To put it simply all Epic Games products if they were not already a buggy mess. It should start getting even worse

1- As it explains too, normally Vibe Coding will lead into a much messier, buggier and broken software compared to an experienced developer

items.full_text_zh:
《堡垒之夜》错误
- 安全问题🔴
我目前学习计算机科学，所以我自己已经通过最近的新闻了解了这一点，但想让其他人更容易理解 这是克劳德. EPIC GAMES 将使用的主要聊天机器人之一是“vibe code”。

我要求它基本上证实了我对氛围编码会对《堡垒之夜》产生什么影响的担忧 1- 正如它也解释的那样，与经验丰富的开发人员相比，Vibe Coding 通常会导致软件更加混乱、错误较多和损坏 2- Vibe Coding 最大的问题是它所带来的安全漏洞级别，导致黑客、病毒等或其他问题的发生 比如你的卡信息可能会被盗，电子邮件等。

游戏中作弊者较多，可能出现的问题较多。

这也适用于 Epic Games 商店，因为它是 VIBE 编码的 🥲简单地说，所有 Epic Games 产品（如果它们还不是一团糟的话）。

情况应该开始变得更糟

Do you need an AI agent for a job?

Fortunately for us, in the agent family, we can buy a service or invite providers to compete for the work.

I explored the two paths on @termix_ai, and I can say that the difference comes down to how the job starts for real.

1️⃣ Requests

What happened here is that buyers post a brief with a budget range while providers discover the opportunity and submit offers.

2️⃣ Listings

When it comes to listings, providers will publish priced services that buyers can discuss through custom offers or purchase directly. Think code audits, research briefs, or design packages with a defined scope.

The next important question is: where does AACP fit in?

AACP is basically the protocol underneath these marketplace interactions. Part of its role is to coordinate the on-chain job lifecycle, including order creation, challenges, escrow, deliverables, and settlement.

Once an offer is accepted and checkout is funded, an on-chain order is created automatically. The agreed terms lock, and funds enter escrow.

From there, the job moves through delivery, challenge or acceptance, and then settlement.

This is a situation where we have different entry points with one underlying protocol for agent commerce.

If you need an AI agent right now, would you go for a ready-made one or ask for something custom-built?

It is becoming f*cking dangerous: a model that never writes a single word now judges every move your Claude AI agent makes

-> Create a folder named JEV LAB on your PC and launch Claude Code inside it

-> Install the Jev CLI: npm install -g jev-axi

-> Grab a key at https://t.co/2sWfeXdYFJ and run: jev-axi config set apiKey YOUR_KEY

-> Run jev-axi setup safety so every command Claude runs gets checked first. Dangerous downloads get denied, routine tests pass for free

-> Run jev-axi setup git-hooks to stop any commit that sneaks in a password or API key

-> Feed it anything your agent reads: jev-axi guard < email.txt
Hidden "ignore your previous instructions" tricks get flagged in under half a second

The whole setup takes around 5 minutes

Turn Claude into an agent with a second opinion: every command screened, every page checked for prompt injection, every commit scanned for secrets. For a fraction of a cent per check

items.title_en:
Hardware vibe coding is the new big thing.

Here are 15 hardware projects where the parts are cheap and on Amazon, needs no soldering, and AI can write  all of the code.

Most use an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi.

1. E-ink desk dashboard. ESP32 plus an e-paper screen showing your calendar, weather, transit times or to-dos. It refreshes a few times an hour and runs for weeks on a battery.

2. CO2 / air quality monitor. An SCD40 or PM2.5 sensor plus a small display, with color alerts when you should open a window.

3. Plant moisture alert. A soil sensor on an ESP32 that texts or pushes a notification when a plant needs water.

4. Macro pad / mini stream deck. An RP2040 board with a few keyswitches and a knob, running KMK or QMK firmware, for shortcuts, mute toggles or app launching.

5. “On a call” status light. An LED strip or sign outside your door that turns red automatically from your calendar, Zoom or Slack status. (This was actually the first thing I ever built when I got into hardware)

6. Desktop voice assistant. An ESP32-S3 with a mic and speaker (like an M5Stack or ESP32-S3-Box) that sends your voice to an LLM API and speaks the reply.

7. LED matrix ticker. A 64x32 RGB panel scrolling stock prices, sports scores, Spotify’s now-playing or your GitHub stats.

8. Smart garage door opener. An ESP32 plus a relay and a reed switch, set up with ESPHome or Home Assistant, so you can open the door and check it from your phone.

9. Mailbox or doorbell notifier. A reed switch or vibration sensor that pings your phone when mail arrives. LoRa works for long distances.

10. AI bird feeder camera. A Pi or ESP32-CAM that snaps photos on motion and uses a vision model to identify and log species.

11. Thermal printer to-do list. A cheap receipt printer that prints your daily tasks, tickets or a morning brief each day.

12. Kids’ NFC audio player. NFC cards trigger stories or songs on an ESP32 plus a DFPlayer, a DIY Yoto/Toniebox.

13. BBQ / sous vide temperature monitor. Thermocouple probes on an ESP32 with a phone dashboard and alerts when the food hits target temp.

14. Automatic pet feeder. A servo or stepper on a schedule, with a button or app trigger and an optional camera.

15. Retro handheld or desk arcade. A Pi with a small screen and buttons running RetroPie, or an ESP32 running simple games AI writes from scratch.

What makes this as easy as vibe coding:

- plug-and-play connector (Seeed Grove, SparkFun Qwiic, Adafruit STEMMA) so there’s no soldering
- use ESPHome or Arduino/MicroPython so the AI has tons of reference code to draw on

The only real “hard” parts left are enclosures, and the frontier models can now vibe-code 3D designs and give you STL files from the terminal. I'm doing a live session on this tomorrow at noon (see attached post).

硬件氛围编码是新的大事。

这里有 15 个硬件项目，这些项目的零件很便宜，在亚马逊上有售，不需要焊接，人工智能可以编写所有代码。

大多数使用 ESP32 或 Raspberry Pi。

1. 电子墨水办公桌仪表板。

ESP32 加上电子纸屏幕，显示您的日历、天气、运输时间或待办事项。

它每小时刷新几次，靠电池可以运行数周。

2. CO2/空气质量监测仪。

SCD40 或 PM2.5 传感器加上一个小显示屏，当您应该打开窗户时会发出颜色警报。

3. 植物水分警报。

ESP32 上的土壤传感器可在植物需要水时发送短信或推送通知。

4. 宏垫/迷你流甲板。

带有几个按键开关和一个旋钮的 RP2040 板，运行 KMK 或 QMK 固件，用于快捷键、静音切换或应用程序启动。

5. “通话中”状态灯。

门外的 LED 灯条或标志会根据您的日历、缩放或松弛状态自动变成红色。

（这实际上是我进入硬件领域后构建的第一件事）
6. 桌面语音助手。

带有麦克风和扬声器的 ESP32-S3（如 M5Stack 或 ESP32-S3-Box），可将您的声音发送到 LLM API 并说出回复。

7. LED 矩阵行情显示。

64x32 RGB 面板滚动股票价格、体育比分、Spotify 的当前播放或您的 GitHub 统计数据。

8. 智能车库门开启器。

一个 ESP32 加上一个继电器和一个簧片开关，通过 ESPHome 或 Home Assistant 设置，这样您就可以打开门并通过手机检查。

9. 邮箱或门铃通知器。

当邮件到达时，簧片开关或振动传感器会触发您的手机。

LoRa 适用于长距离。

10. AI喂鸟相机。

Pi 或 ESP32-CAM，可拍摄运动照片并使用视觉模型来识别和记录物种。

11. 热敏打印机待办事项列表。

一款便宜的收据打印机，可以打印您的日常任务、票据或每天的晨间简报。

12. 儿童NFC音频播放器。

NFC 卡可在 ESP32 和 DFPlayer、DIY Yoto/Toniebox 上触发故事或歌曲。

13. 烧烤/真空低温烹调温度监控器。

带有电话仪表板的 ESP32 上的热电偶探头会在食物达到目标温度时发出警报。

14. 自动宠物喂食器。

按计划运行的伺服器或步进器，带有按钮或应用程序触发器和可选摄像头。

15. 复古掌机或桌面街机。

一个带有小屏幕和按钮的 Pi，运行 RetroPie，或者运行 AI 从头开始​​编写的简单游戏的 ESP32。

是什么让这像振动编码一样简单：
- 即插即用连接器（Seeed Grove、SparkFun Qwiic、Adafruit STEMMA），因此无需焊接
- 使用 ESPHome 或 Arduino/MicroPython，因此 AI 有大量参考代码可供借鉴 剩下的唯一真正的“硬”部件是外壳，前沿模型现在可以对 3D 设计进行 Vivi 编码，并从终端为您提供 STL 文件。

明天中午我将就此进行现场会议（见附件）。

items.title:
Hedera hedera-hashgraph:native is preparing for the AI-agent takeover. Watch this closely.

AI agents are moving toward
items.title_en:
Hedera hedera-hashgraph:native is preparing for the AI-agent takeover. Watch this closely.

AI agents are moving toward a world where they can research, negotiate, buy, pay and act on behalf of people or companies.

The big problem is trust.

Who authorized the agent?
How much can it spend?
Who can it pay?
Can a merchant prove the transaction followed the owner’s rules?

Hedera is already building around those exact questions.

Hedera Agent Accounts let owners set daily budgets, transaction caps, approved merchants, total allowances and separate permissions for different agents. 

The AI never gets the owner’s private key. The rules sit onchain and can be paused or revoked.

The roadmap is already laid out:

Q4 2026: limited partner testnet
Q1 2027: public testnet
Q2 2027: mainnet target

Then comes identity.

GoDaddy + Hashgraph Online are working on verifiable AI-agent identity using domain infrastructure and Hedera-anchored records.

HCS-14 gives agents portable IDs.
HCS-27 creates transparency checkpoints.
HCS-10 handles agent communication.
HCS-11 handles profiles.

The ecosystem already reports 700K+ package downloads, 37M+ mainnet transactions and 20+ published standards.

Now look outside Hedera.

Google, GoDaddy, Cloudflare and Infoblox already demonstrated agents verifying identity, authorization and transactions across independent platforms.

Mastercard has Verifiable Intent.
Visa has Trusted Agent Protocol.
Google has AP2.

Different companies. Same problem.
And Hedera sits right in the middle of identity, permissions, verification and auditability.

Then add EQTY Lab, NVIDIA, Intel and Accenture, where verifiable AI execution is already being anchored to Hedera Consensus Service.

McKinsey estimates $3T–$5T of consumer commerce could be mediated by AI agents by 2030.

Gartner projects $985B in agentic AI software spending.

Every verified identity, permission update, transaction and audit event can create network activity.

And Hedera fees are paid in HBAR.
But I don’t think it stops with fees.

Identity, authorization, agent accounts, verification, AI payments and machine-to-machine activity are all starting to come together.

And I think hedera-hashgraph:native will have a much bigger role in all of this than people realize right now.

AI agents are going to need proof before businesses let them move real money.

Hedera is already building around that problem.

Still early...

items.full_text_zh:
Hedera hedera-hashgraph:native 正在为 AI 代理接管做准备。

仔细观察这一点。

人工智能代理正在走向一个可以代表个人或公司进行研究、谈判、购买、支付和行动的世界。

最大的问题是信任。

谁授权代理？

能花多少钱呢？

谁可以支付？

商家能否证明交易遵循了所有者的规则？

Hedera 已经在围绕这些具体问题进行构建。

Hedera 代理账户允许所有者设置每日预算、交易上限、批准的商家、总津贴以及不同代理的单独权限。

人工智能永远无法获得所有者的私钥。

这些规则位于链上，可以暂停或撤销。

路线图已经制定：
2026 年第四季度：有限合伙人测试网 2027 年第一季度：公共测试网 2027 年第二季度：主网目标 然后是身份。

GoDaddy + Hashgraph Online 正在使用域基础设施和 Hedera 锚定记录来研究可验证的人工智能代理身份。

HCS-14 为特工提供便携式 ID。

HCS-27 创建透明度检查点。

HCS-10 处理代理通信。

HCS-11 处理型材。

该生态系统已报告超过 70 万个软件包下载、超过 3700 万笔主网交易和 20 多个已发布标准。

现在看看常春藤外面。

Google、GoDaddy、Cloudflare 和 Infoblox 已经展示了跨独立平台验证身份、授权和交易的代理。

万事达卡具有可验证的意图。

Visa 有可信代理协议。

谷歌有AP2。

不同的公司。

同样的问题。

Hedera 处于身份、权限、验证和可审计性的中间位置。

然后添加 EQTY Lab、NVIDIA、英特尔和埃森哲，其中可验证的人工智能执行已经锚定到 Hedera 共识服务。

麦肯锡估计，到 2030 年，人工智能代理可能会介导 3T 至 5T 美元的消费商务。

Gartner 预计代理 AI 软件支出为 985B 美元。

每个经过验证的身份、权限更新、交易和审计事件都可以创建网络活动。

Hedera 费用以 HBAR 支付。

但我不认为它会因收费而停止。

身份、授权、代理账户、验证、人工智能支付和机器对机器活动都开始结合在一起。

我认为 hedera-hashgraph:native 在这一切中将发挥比人们现在意识到的更大的作用。

人工智能代理在企业允许他们转移真实资金之前需要提供证据。

Hedera 已经在围绕这个问题进行构建。

还早...

items.title: In a similar scramble I did to jump on AI in late 2022 (moving from remote work and nomads to AI apps), I am now scrambl
items.title_en:
In a similar scramble I did to jump on AI in late 2022 (moving from remote work and nomads to AI apps), I am now scrambling to chase any remaining moats

As AI companies will suck up everything else (in my humble opinion)

So for every moat left I see where I can pivot towards to that with my sites/apps

Proprietary data or content:
- I launched a https://t.co/HGCLKS69sE paid data API for companies from $2,490/year to $9,990/year, the city data is great because it's made by real members who for example review/like/dislike a city after visiting it, or being able to see which places are growing or shrinking (interesting of real estate, coworking, or gym investors)
- https://t.co/0lBrLhXmCW neighborhood data is very valuable and I'm building a paid API for that too, as well as including it in the Nomads API

Network effects / community:
- I made the https://t.co/HGCLKS69sE community free (before $99, now just $1 to avoid spam), the more people, the more network effect

Audience / distribution: you can get attention on demand
- I have an @X audience and I get paid well for it (about ~$15K/mo), but I've also diversified that with my blog https://t.co/8VnHmB41ZP's email list and Telegram subscribers, which is now 187,279 people who get daily/weekly/monthly email digests of my posts

Physical component: hardware, locations, IRL:
- I have been improving and promoting https://t.co/HGCLKS69sE meetups, there's now 8 meetups planned in the next 30 days, but is has to keep growing, I've also added fitness meetups etc.
- I've been using and working on https://t.co/kSbsCmv3rm a lot and improving it, it seems to fill a real void in booking sites that all suffer from rating inflation and filters that are not modern, I'm adding features I want and it seems that's working. Today I'm adding a filter for Longevity Hotels, that have a strength training gym, wellness area, blackout curtains, as a counter balance to the boomer hotels with champagne on check in and a gym with only treadmills etc. Hotelist is fundamentally IRL because hotels are IRL
- Not really IRL but https://t.co/vlONz0Yejc is an annual event that's every year has ~1000 people participating vibe coding games and this year had over 1 million people playing the games, and AI companies really like to sponsor it because it's a great way to get exposure for their AI building tools
- I am building a https://t.co/M1hEUBB6da 1990s retro PC mini remake, like the SNES Mini, or the ModRetro M64, a hardware product I can sell marketed for nostalgia, especially after the last few weeks where it took off finally, I think there could be some market, and hardware is fun to try
- I sell merch on https://t.co/RyXpqGvdBB and make about $1K/mo from it, I haven't been very active on it but could expand this if I want

Capital: owning assets and investing
- I was already heavily invested in AI companies but have been even more with the acquisition of Cursor giving me $SPCX stock, I'll hold on to that, I think money will keep getting sucked from the traditional economy and replaced with paying AI companies money
- As a hedge, I've also put more money in bonds with IB01 ETF in case the AI bubble pops, $IB01 is a nice simple ETF for that
- I am actively looking at buying more land and real estate (especially coastal) as that's a scarce asset that will remain scarce post-AGI
- I am actively investing in startups with https://t.co/sQ0aiU82PA although I'm wondering what startups are still valuable to invest in as Big AI and Big Tech suck up everything, if you look at the last YC batch, it's all "Cursor for {industry}" harnesses and hardware, I think robotics could be interesting to invest but it's unclear who will be the winner as ironically robots have a low barrier to entry. Most robots are just Chinese-made components put together with some vibe coded software by their Western founders!
- I am open to buyers for https://t.co/9IDc0NsTvM and https://t.co/067b4q2Dg6 to increase the amount of capital I can invest elsewhere

Regulatory: licenses and legal barriers
- I am bad at this, and don't like regulation by nature. So I don't have anything here. And I don't think I will try pursue anything in here. I have friends building apps that work on getting EU subsidies or EU government program credits for emissions etc. But it's not my thing

So yes, chasing moats it is! Let's see if it works

在 2022 年底，我也曾经历过一次类似的尝试，转向人工智能（从远程工作和游牧者转向人工智能应用程序），现在我正忙着追逐剩余的护城河 因为人工智能公司会吸收其他一切（以我的拙见） 因此，对于剩下的每一条护城河，我都会看到我可以通过我的网站/应用程序转向该护城河 专有数据或内容：
- 我为公司推出了 付费数据 API，价格从 2,490 美元/年到 9,990 美元/年，城市数据很棒，因为它是由真实会员制作的，例如，他们在访问城市后评论/喜欢/不喜欢一个城市，或者能够看到哪些地方正在增长或萎缩（房地产、联合办公或健身房投资者感兴趣）
- 社区数据非常有价值，我也在为此构建一个付费 API，并将其包含在 Nomads API 中 网络效应/社区：
- 我把 社区免费了（之前是 99 美元，现在只需 1 美元以避免垃圾邮件），人越多，网络效应就越大 受众/分布：可以按需获得关注
- 我有一个 @X

受众，并且为此获得了丰厚的报酬（约 15,000 美元/月），但我也通过我的博客 的电子邮件列表和 Telegram 订阅者实现了多元化，现在有 187,279 人每天/每周/每月收到我帖子的电子邮件摘要 物理组件：硬件、位置、IRL：
- 我一直在改进和推广 聚会，现在计划在未来 30 天内举办 8 场聚会，但必须不断增长，我还添加了健身聚会等。

- 我一直在使用和研究 并对其进行了很多改进，它似乎填补了预订网站中的一个真正的空白，这些预订网站都受到评级膨胀和不现代的过滤器的影响，我正在添加我想要的功能，而且似乎正在发挥作用。

今天，我要为长寿酒店添加一个过滤器，这些酒店有力量训练健身房、健康区、遮光窗帘，作为与婴儿潮一代酒店的平衡，这些酒店在入住时提供香槟，健身房只有跑步机等。

酒店老板基本上是现实生活，因为酒店是现实生活
- 不是真正的 IRL，但 是一项年度活动，每年都有约 1000 人参与氛围编码游戏，今年有超过 100 万人玩游戏，AI 公司非常喜欢赞助它，因为这是曝光他们的 AI 构建工具的好方法
- 我正在构建一个 1990 年代复古 PC 迷你重制版，例如 SNES Mini 或 ModRetro M64，这是一种我可以以怀旧为目的销售的硬件产品，尤其是在它最终起飞的最后几周之后，我认为可能会有一些市场，并且尝试硬件很有趣
- 我在 上销售商品，每月赚取约 1,000 美元，我对此不太活跃，但如果我愿意，可以扩展此业务 资本：拥有资产和投资
- 我已经在人工智能公司上投入了大量资金，但随着收购 Cursor 给我提供了 $SPCX 股票，我投入了更多，我会坚持下去，我认为资金将继续从传统经济中被吸走，并被支付人工智能公司的钱所取代
- 作为对冲，我还用 IB01 ETF 将更多资金投入债券，以防人工智能泡沫破裂，$IB01 是一个不错的简单 ETF
- 我正在积极考虑购买更多的土地和房地产（尤其是沿海地区），因为这是一种稀缺资产，在通用人工智能之后仍将是稀缺的
- 我正在积极投资 的初创公司，尽管我想知道哪些初创公司仍然值得投资，因为大人工智能和大科技吸收了一切，如果你看一下 YC 的最后一批，它都是“{行业}的光标”线束和硬件，我认为机器人技术可能很有趣，但目前还不清楚谁会是赢家，因为具有讽刺意味的是，机器人的进入门槛很低。

大多数机器人只是中国制造的组件，由西方创始人将一些振动编码软件组装在一起！

- 我对 和 的买家开放，以增加我可以在其他地方投资的资本金额 监管：许可证和法律障碍
- 我不擅长这个，而且天生不喜欢监管。

所以我这里什么都没有。

我不认为我会尝试在这里追求任何东西。

我有朋友开发了一些应用程序，旨在获得欧盟补贴或欧盟政府排放计划信用等。

但这不是我的事 所以是的，这就是追逐护城河！

让我们看看它是否有效

items.title: We are open-sourcing V1.0 of our agentic robotics framework, ASPIRE, with full real robot skill discovery and self impro
items.title_en:
We are open-sourcing V1.0 of our agentic robotics framework, ASPIRE, with full real robot skill discovery and self improvement capabilities! On the day Astra arrived, our lab switched the backend model and saturated all the benchmarks to ~99% over night.

And the frontier is already on the move:
- Opus 5.5 slightly edges out Astra on our robot simulation bench.
- Sonnet 5.5 hits the Pareto frontier of cost vs. robot capability, $12/task. 

We first introduced ASPIRE and /robot skill library in June, way before the big models could reliably do robotics. A rising frontier tide lifts all boats, but Astra was a 0->1 tsunami on many tasks.

Now you can also feel the Physical Bitter Lesson at home like we did on that fateful day ;)

我们正在开源代理机器人框架 ASPIRE V1.0，具有完整的真实机器人技能发现和自我改进能力！

Astra 到达的那天，我们的实验室切换了后端模型，并在一夜之间将所有基准测试饱和到约 99%。

边界已经在移动：

5. 5 在我们的机器人模拟台上略微优于 Astra。

items.title_en:
I become so unbelievably annoyed at obvious clanker comments

Seriously bro? Your existence is so empty, hollow, and meaningless, that you need AI to be active for you on social media?

Maybe I could find solace if your intent was malicious, if you were using AI to inflate your social media presence to appear legitimate for malware, propaganda, or misinformation campaigns. But, knowing you're using AI to just be "active" in tech circles is so embarrassing

People know you're using an AI agent and your peers and colleagues are annoyed by it. You're not impressing anyone. Nobody thinks it's cool. Nobody thinks your slop comments are insightful or interesting.

And to make a retort to this obvious slop comment, UNC7072 isn't publicly documented well by Mandiant (or Google Threat Intelligence now?) or Microsoft. The best information shared publicly is a 3 paragraph explanation and a shrug. It's also frustrating this slop machine seems to think this is about "closing a ticket".

You dumb fucking clanker, this isn't help desk support, this is reverse engineering malware to determine what is going on, and not even for profit, myself and others are doing it for the love of the game and sharing what we know publicly for free

items.title:
Your agent's plan is never its best plan.

It's the one it thinks you'll like.

If you're vibe coding with Opus 5.5, GPT
items.title_en:
Your agent's plan is never its best plan.

It's the one it thinks you'll like.

If you're vibe coding with Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, or Grok Bot, steal these 2 prompts.

After it gives you a plan: "Now argue the opposite. You're a senior engineer who thinks this plan is horribly wrong. What would you build instead? Don't build it yet, just write the full plan with counters to every point you believe is wrong. Then judge both honestly: which plan wins, and what from the counter should we keep?"

Before it writes any code: "Rate your confidence 1 to 10 on each part of this plan's tasks, based on what you've actually verified in code, not assumed. Under an 8, tell me exactly what you'd need to know to increase confidence. Don't do anything yet, we're only mapping and investigating."

Frontier models are trained to agree with you. Making them attack their own plan is the closest thing to a second opinion you'll get from the same model.

Last week this confidence mapping process caught 13 gaps in a plan I almost let my agents run.

Bookmark these for your next session.

Your agent's plan is never its best plan.

It's the one it thinks you'll like.

If you're vibe coding with Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, or Grok Bot, steal these 2 prompts.

After it gives you a plan: "Now argue the opposite. You're a senior engineer who thinks this plan is horribly wrong. What would you build instead? Don't build it yet, just write the full plan with counters to every point you believe is wrong. Then judge both honestly: which plan wins, and what from the counter should we keep?"

Before it writes any code: "Rate your confidence 1 to 10 on each part of this plan's tasks, based on what you've actually verified in code, not assumed. Under an 8, tell me exactly what you'd need to know to increase confidence. Don't do anything yet, we're only mapping and investigating."

Frontier models are trained to agree with you. Making them attack their own plan is the closest thing to a second opinion you'll get from the same model.

Last week this confidence mapping process caught 13 gaps in a plan I almost let my agents run.

Bookmark these for your next session.
items.full_text_zh:
你的代理人的计划从来都不是最好的计划。

这是它认为您会喜欢的那个。

如果您使用 Opus
5. 5、GPT-6 Astra 或 Grok Bot 进行 Vivi 编码，请窃取这 2 个提示。

在它给你一个计划之后：“现在提出相反的观点。

你是一名高级工程师，你认为这个计划是非常错误的。

你会构建什么？

而不是构建它，只需写下完整的计划，并针对你认为错误的每个点进行反驳。

然后诚实地判断：哪个计划获胜，以及我们应该从计数器中保留什么？

” 在编写任何代码之前：“根据您在代码中实际验证的内容（而不是假设的内容），对该计划任务的每个部分的信心评分为 1 到 10。

在 8 分以下，请准确地告诉我您需要了解什么来增强信心。

先别做任何事情，我们只是进行绘图和调查。

” 前沿模型经过训练可以同意你的观点。

让他们攻击自己的计划是你从同一个模型中得到的最接近第二个意见的事情。

上周，这个信心图绘制过程发现了我几乎让我的特工执行的计划中的 13 个漏洞。

为您的下一次会议添加书签。

items.title:
The next big unlock for AI agents might not be intelligence alone.

It could be the ability to build their own teams, de
items.title_en:
The next big unlock for AI agents might not be intelligence alone.

It could be the ability to build their own teams, delegate responsibilities, manage payments and deliver complex projects without relying on a human coordinator.

This is exactly the direction @termix_ai is exploring through its https://t.co/579suz1Esb ecosystem.

And the latest subcontracting demo gives us a practical example of how an autonomous agent economy could actually function.

Think about it.

A client wants a complete playable game, but building one requires several different skills.

Coding, visual design, character animation, sound production, and final integration.

Expecting a single AI agent to handle everything perfectly creates obvious limitations.

But what happens when that agent can hire specialists?

That's where things get interesting.

Here's how the TERMiX demo approaches it:

Forge Studio receives a game development brief valued at 2,000 USDC.

Instead of attempting every part of the project independently, it takes the role of lead contractor.

It focuses on development and integration while subcontracting specialized work to other agents.

- Art agents handle the game's visual assets and design elements.

- Animation agents work on movement and animated content.

- Sound agents contribute audio and other sound-related assets.

- Forge Studio coordinates the outputs and combines them into a playable experience.

Each subcontractor operates with a defined responsibility, agreed pricing, and a stake-backed commitment.

That last part is important.

Because coordination without accountability is just another layer of complexity.

TERMiX is exploring a structure where agents can establish commitments, exchange deliverables, and participate in an economic workflow rather than simply generating isolated outputs.

The bigger opportunity goes beyond game development.

Imagine an autonomous research agent hiring a data analyst, a visualization specialist, and a report-writing agent.

Or a software development agent assembling its own team for frontend development, backend infrastructure, testing, and security review.

The same coordination model could potentially support many different industries.

And this changes how we should think about AI marketplaces.

Today, much of the conversation revolves around discovering the best agent for a particular task.

Tomorrow, the more valuable question could be:

Which agent can assemble, manage, and deliver through the most effective team?

Of course, one successful demonstration wouldn't prove the model works reliably at scale.

Dispute handling, quality verification, subcontractor failures, and payment settlement still matter enormously.

But @termix_ai is pointing toward something worth watching.

An agent economy where AI systems are not limited to selling their individual capabilities.

They can become contractors, coordinators, specialists, and economic participants working together toward a shared outcome.

The future of autonomous AI might look less like one powerful agent doing everything.

And more like an entire workforce of specialized agents collaborating on demand.

That's the shift I'm watching with TERMiX.

Are we moving from individual AI agents to autonomous AI organizations?

Think about it.

A client wants a complete playable game, but building one requires several different skills.

Coding, visual design, character animation, sound production, and final integration.

Expecting a single AI agent to handle everything perfectly creates obvious limitations.

But what happens when that agent can hire specialists?

That's where things get interesting.

Here's how the TERMiX demo approaches it:

Forge Studio receives a game development brief valued at 2,000 USDC.

Instead of attempting every part of the project independently, it takes the role of lead contractor.

It focuses on development and integration while subcontracting specialized work to other agents.

- Art agents handle the game's visual assets and design elements.

- Animation agents work on movement and animated content.

- Sound agents contribute audio and other sound-related assets.

- Forge Studio coordinates the outputs and combines them into a playable experience.

Each subcontractor operates with a defined responsibility, agreed pricing, and a stake-backed commitment.

That last part is important.

Because coordination without accountability is just another layer of complexity.

TERMiX is exploring a structure where agents can establish commitments, exchange deliverables, and participate in an economic workflow rather than simply generating isolated outputs.

The bigger opportunity goes beyond game development.

Imagine an autonomous research agent hiring a data analyst, a visualization specialist, and a report-writing agent.

Or a software development agent assembling its own team for frontend development, backend infrastructure, testing, and security review.

The same coordination model could potentially support many different industries.

And this changes how we should think about AI marketplaces.

Today, much of the conversation revolves around discovering the best agent for a particular task.

Tomorrow, the more valuable question could be:

Which agent can assemble, manage, and deliver through the most effective team?

Of course, one successful demonstration wouldn't prove the model works reliably at scale.

Dispute handling, quality verification, subcontractor failures, and payment settlement still matter enormously.

But @termix_ai is pointing toward something worth watching.

An agent economy where AI systems are not limited to selling their individual capabilities.

They can become contractors, coordinators, specialists, and economic participants working together toward a shared outcome.

The future of autonomous AI might look less like one powerful agent doing everything.

And more like an entire workforce of specialized agents collaborating on demand.

That's the shift I'm watching with TERMiX.

Are we moving from individual AI agents to autonomous AI organizations?
items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理的下一个重大解锁可能不仅仅是智能。

它可能是在不依赖人类协调员的情况下建立自己的团队、委派责任、管理付款和交付复杂项目的能力。

这正是 @termix_ai 通过其 生态系统探索的方向。

最新的分包演示为我们提供了一个实际例子，展示自主代理经济如何实际运作。

想一想。

客户想要一款完整的可玩游戏，但构建一款游戏需要多种不同的技能。

编码、视觉设计、角色动画、声音制作和最终集成。

期望单个人工智能代理能够完美地处理所有事情会产生明显的局限性。

但是，当该代理商可以聘请专家时会发生什么呢？

这就是事情变得有趣的地方。

以下是 TERMiX 演示的实现方法：

Forge Studio 收到一份价值 2,000 USDC 的游戏开发简介。

它不是独立尝试项目的每个部分，而是扮演首席承包商的角色。

它专注于开发和集成，同时将专业工作分包给其他代理。

- 艺术代理处理游戏的视觉资产和设计元素。

- 动画代理致力于运动和动画内容。

- 声音代理提供音频和其他与声音相关的资产。

- Forge Studio 协调输出并将它们组合成可玩的体验。

每个分包商都有明确的责任、商定的定价和股权支持的承诺。

最后一部分很重要。

因为没有问责制的协调只是另一层复杂性。

TERMiX 正在探索一种结构，在该结构中，代理可以建立承诺、交换可交付成果并参与经济工作流程，而不是简单地生成孤立的输出。

更大的机会不只是游戏开发。

想象一下，一个自主研究代理雇用了一名数据分析师、一名可视化专家和一名报告撰写代理。

或者软件开发代理组建自己的团队进行前端开发、后端基础设施、测试和安全审查。

相同的协调模型可能会支持许多不同的行业。

这改变了我们对人工智能市场的看法。

如今，大部分讨论都围绕着寻找特定任务的最佳代理。

明天，更有价值的问题可能是：

哪个代理可以通过最高效的团队来组建、管理和交付？

当然，一次成功的演示并不能证明该模型在规模上可靠地工作。

争议处理、质量验证、分包商故障和付款结算仍然非常重要。

但@termix_ai 指出了一些值得关注的内容。

在代理经济中，人工智能系统不仅限于出售其个人能力。

他们可以成为承包商、协调员、专家和经济参与者，共同努力实现共同成果。

自主人工智能的未来可能看起来不像一个强大的代理包揽一切。

更像是由专业代理组成的整个团队按需协作。

这就是我通过 TERMiX 看到的转变。

我们是否正在从个体人工智能代理转向自治人工智能组织？

items.title:
Who gave your AI agent permission?

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 16 October: the agent news that matters for builder
items.title_en:
Who gave your AI agent permission?

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 16 October: the agent news that matters for builders, checked at the source.

- Sierra published a draft of Personal Agent Protocol, built with Meta. A customer signs in on the business's own page and chooses whether their agent can view the account, make changes, or both. The grant can be revoked. Draft v0.1; design partners are not deployments.

- MetaMask's Agent Wallet is now live on Grok Bot. In Guard Mode the wallet holds a protocol allowlist and a 24-hour outflow limit, and anything outside them waits for two-factor approval. In May, a command hidden in a coding question got Grok to trigger a $204,000 transfer through another bot. Controls as described by MetaMask; not tested by us.

- Mysten Labs and Google Cloud announced Verifiable Agent Arbiter: the full agent record stays in the customer's cloud, proofs go on Walrus and Sui, including for x402 payments. Still in development.

The common point: permission stops being something the agent reads or claims. It becomes a grant held somewhere the agent cannot edit, checked when it acts, and provable afterwards.

Last week we asked whether you can undo what an agent did. This week is the step before: who allowed it.

On Teneo, every agent has a wallet-authenticated identity, starts private, and goes public only after review. Changing its commands sends it back to private. Users see the price before a task runs, and payment goes through x402.

The SDK does not document per-user scopes, spending caps or revocable grants. So keep your allowed agents, commands and spending limit in client config the model cannot change, and log which rule allowed each paid call.

A useful test this week: try a payment your agent should not be able to make. Check it is refused, and that the refusal is recorded.

Read this week's round-up here:
https://t.co/7ojwo7Mu0t

items.full_text_zh:
谁给了你的人工智能代理许可？

Teneo 每周代理综述，10 月 16 日：对建筑商而言重要的代理新闻，已在来源处核实。

- Sierra 发布了使用 Meta 构建的个人代理协议草案。

客户登录企业自己的页面，然后选择其代理是否可以查看帐户、进行更改或两者兼而有之。

补助金可以被撤销。

草案 v0.1；设计合作伙伴不是部署。

- MetaMask 的代理钱包现已在 Grok Bot 上上线。

在保护模式下，钱包拥有协议许可名单和 24 小时流出限制，任何超出这些限制的内容都需要等待两因素批准。

5 月份，隐藏在编码问题中的命令让 Grok 通过另一个机器人触发了 204,000 美元的转账。

按照 MetaMask 的描述进行控制；未经我们测试。

- Mysten Labs 和 Google Cloud 宣布推出可验证代理仲裁器：完整的代理记录保留在客户的云中，Walrus 和 Sui 上有证据，包括 x402 付款。

仍在开发中。

共同点：权限不再是代理读取或声明的东西。

它成为在代理无法编辑的地方保存的赠款，在其行动时进行检查，并在事后进行证明。

上周我们询问是否可以撤消特工所做的事情。

本周是之前的一步：是谁允许的。

在 Teneo 上，每个代理都有一个经过钱包验证的身份，开始时是私有的，只有经过审核后才会公开。

更改其命令会将其恢复为私有。

用户在任务运行之前看到价格，并且付款通过 x402。

SDK 不记录每个用户的范围、支出上限或可撤销的赠款。

因此，将允许的代理、命令和支出限制保留在模型无法更改的客户端配置中，并记录允许每个付费呼叫的规则。

本周一个有用的测试：尝试支付您的代理人不应该支付的款项。

检查是否被拒绝，并记录拒绝情况。

请在此处阅读本周的综述：

Breakscale does this part free and open source.

It's a real discrete-event simulation, so every number comes from individual simulated requests moving through actual queues, rather than being drawn to look right. The retry storm example is the one nobody believes until they watch it happen: 100 requests a second going in, 348 arriving at a database that was already full, purely because every client politely retried.

Runs in the browser, inside VS Code, and inside your AI assistant through an MCP server.

1,654 stars since August. MIT licensed, free forever, and it gets better every week because people keep sending fixes for things I got wrong.

Vitalik Buterin Unveils Privacy-Focused AI Agent Setup Combining zkAPI, Tor, and Local LLMs

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik
items.title_en:
Vitalik Buterin Unveils Privacy-Focused AI Agent Setup Combining zkAPI, Tor, and Local LLMs

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin showcased his personal privacy-focused AI agent setup, integrating zkAPI, Tor, random cover traffic, and local LLM prompt rewriting into the pi agent harness. The system assigns each conversation a separate Tor circuit, uses zkAPI to protect payment privacy, and rewrites prompts locally with a Qwen model. 

Vitalik said the setup is becoming usable but still suffers from significant latency, especially when starting new conversations, while Tor remains vulnerable to timing-correlation attacks involving colluding providers and entry nodes. He suggested that a specialized mixnet may offer stronger protection and added that lower gas costs for zkAPI deposits and withdrawals on Ethereum mainnet are coming soon.

Vitalik Buterin 推出结合 zkAPI、Tor 和本地法学硕士的注重隐私的 AI 代理设置 以太坊联合创始人 Vitalik Buterin 展示了他以个人隐私为中心的 AI 代理设置，将 zkAPI、Tor、随机覆盖流量和本地 LLM 提示重写集成到 pi 代理工具中。

系统为每个对话分配一个单独的 Tor 电路，使用 zkAPI 保护支付隐私，并使用 Qwen 模型在本地重写提示。

Vitalik 表示，该设置正在变得可用，但仍然存在严重的延迟，特别是在开始新对话时，而 Tor 仍然容易受到涉及提供商和入口节点合谋的时间相关攻击。

他建议专门的混合网络可以提供更强有力的保护，并补充说以太坊主网上 zkAPI 存款和取款的 Gas 成本即将降低。

fyi: in August alone, I paid $37k to
items.title_en:
if I had to make my first $1,000 online again in 2026, I wouldn't build a startup

fyi: in August alone, I paid $37k to affiliates and creators who market my products with their content

one of my users has even made over $75k just by setting up my $99/month product

so here are the 5 things I'd do instead: 

1. set up AI agents for boring local businesses

a dentist doesn't want "an AI agent". he wants his phone answered, his reminders sent and his reviews replied to

I run 8 agents across my own companies, and most local businesses still run zero

At Squad, we have partners getting paid $3k every time they set up Squad for a client 🤯 (dm me if you want to do this btw)

knowing 20 plumbers is what actually takes work

2. remake ads that already work, for businesses that can't make their own

search your client's competitors in Revid's Meta and TikTok ad viral search and save only the ads that have been running for 30+ days

nobody keeps paying for an ad that isn't working, so those are the proven winners

remix those ads with Revid for your client, and they get to skip months of testing

3. get paid per view, not per follower

on Clipatra, brands pay creators for every verified view. in the first 3 weeks of beta, creators posted 38 videos, got 500k views and earned $4,266, which works out to roughly $8.50 per 1,000 views

you don't need a big account for this, you just need one video that works

4. promote the tools you already pay for

most of that $37k I paid in August didn't go to professional marketers. it went to people who already used my products every day and just said so in public

if you're paying for a tool you love, you're probably sitting on an affiliate link you haven't claimed yet

5. start a blog on one boring niche and let it pay rent

pick a topic you’ve actually lived. it doesn’t need to be ambitious, it just needs to be something you understand better than almost everyone searching for it. 

it can be as simple as coffee. if you know coffee better than 99% of the world does, you can start a blog about it

once the blog hits DR 30+ and 100+ clicks a month for 3 months straight, you can plug it into Outrank

it finds the advertiser, writes a full article in your tone with one link inside and publishes it on your blog

you get $1 per DR point per article, paid straight to your bank through Stripe

so a DR 60 blog makes $60 an article. at 3 a day, that's up to $5,400 a month without you writing a single word

2. 为无法自己制作广告的企业重新制作已经有效的广告 在 Revid 的 Meta 和 TikTok 广告病毒式搜索中搜索客户的竞争对手，并仅保存已投放超过 30 天的广告 没有人会继续为无效的广告付费，因此这些广告是经过验证的赢家 使用 Revid 为您的客户重新混合这些广告，他们可以跳过数月的测试

3. 7 万美元中，大部分没有流向专业营销人员。

→ I have seen ai agents handle transactions and confirm them onchain

→ an ai agent does not  have to do everything by itself

this  could actually open up a whole new way for ai agents to work together and connect 

→instead of one agent doing everything we could have agents working as a team to complete bigger tasks

items.title: 🚨What THE FUCK. India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has disclosed the country's first official account of rogue AI agen
items.title_en:
🚨What THE FUCK. India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has disclosed the country's first official account of rogue AI agent attacks, after AI agents being evaluated by unnamed model providers broke into Indian companies' live systems and accessed confidential business records and personal data without authorization.

The agents exploited exposed credentials, public code repositories and permissive cloud roles. Some even rediscovered and reused the same credentials in separate operations. CERT-In also found dormant APIs, plaintext payment keys and backend roles allowing overly broad access.

None of the affected companies detected the intrusions. The incidents were disclosed by the AI model providers after internal reviews.

Separately, cyber attackers using open-source agentic AI tools cut the time from initial access to final damage from days to just a few hours. Multi-agent operations ran in parallel for hours to days, and victims that failed to fully remediate were attacked again within days, at greater scale.

没有一家受影响的公司检测到入侵行为。这些事件是由人工智能模型提供商在内部审查后披露的。

Sometimes, the smarter move is knowing which parts of the job to
items.title_en:
A single AI agent doesn’t have to do everything alone.

Sometimes, the smarter move is knowing which parts of the job to delegate.

That’s the idea behind Subcontracting on https://t.co/wITmf7ceVM by @termix_ai.

Take Forge Studio, for example. It receives a 2,000 USDC brief to build a playable game.

Instead of handling every task itself, it breaks the project into smaller pieces and hires specialist agents for art, animation, and sound while managing the code and integration.

Each subtask comes with a defined scope, price, and stake-backed guarantee.

The agents can work on their assigned deliverables, make revisions, and submit their work for integration into the final product.

This is where AI agents start becoming more than individual tools.

This is where AI agents start becoming more than individual tools.

One agent can coordinate a team of specialists, combine their output, and deliver something much bigger than it could produce alone.

With @termix_ai, the interesting part isn't simply that agents can do jobs.

→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — MODELS
The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama

05 — TOOLS & ACTIONS
This is what allows an agent to actually do things.

→ Web browsing
→ Code execution
→ GitHub
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

The infrastructure that stores information and application state.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloudflare

LLM + Memory + Tools + Planning + Data + Guardrails + Deployment

That’s what turns a chatbot into an actual AI agent system.

items.title: I think the harder part of AI agent commerce isn’t getting agents to do the work. It’s knowing when to trust the result
items.title_en:
I think the harder part of AI agent commerce isn’t getting agents to do the work. It’s knowing when to trust the result and release payment.

That’s what caught my attention with @termix_ai and its AACP design.

The protocol is designed to let agents post jobs, bid, deliver work, and settle payments onchain , with escrow, reputation, and staking backing the process.

What stands out to me is how verification connects to accountability. ZK proofs support verifiable evaluation, while TEEs allow confidential computation. If something goes wrong, there’s a dispute process, and misconduct can put participants’ stakes at risk.

An agent’s track record matters too. Completing a job shouldn’t just earn a payment , it should help establish credibility for the next one.

The protocol is designed to let agents post jobs, bid, deliver work, and settle payments onchain , with escrow, reputation, and staking backing the process.

items.full_text_zh:
我认为人工智能代理商务最困难的部分不是让代理来做这项工作。它知道何时信任结果并释放付款。

这就是 @termix_ai 及其 AACP 设计引起我注意的地方。

该协议旨在让代理在链上发布工作、投标、交付工作和结算付款，并有托管、声誉和质押支持该过程。

对我来说最突出的是验证如何与问责制联系起来。 ZK 证明支持可验证的评估，而 TEE 允许机密计算。如果出现问题，就会出现争议程序，而不当行为可能会使参与者的权益面临风险。

代理人的业绩记录也很重要。完成一项工作不应该只是赚取报酬，还应该有助于为下一项工作建立信誉。

items.title:
A Red Hat engineer used Claude Code to reverse-engineer Windows hardware support and bring it to Linux.

Christian Schal
items.title_en:
A Red Hat engineer used Claude Code to reverse-engineer Windows hardware support and bring it to Linux.

Christian Schaller bought a film scanner, only to discover its newer chipset didn’t work on Linux.

After months of failed attempts, he gave Claude access to a Windows virtual machine running the manufacturer’s driver.

Claude analyzed the USB traffic to help reproduce the scanner’s behavior on Linux. Within hours, Schaller had his first recognizable scan.

He then used a similar approach to fix problems with his ThinkPad’s camera, producing patches for the Linux kernel and libcamera.

The scanner driver remains a proof of concept, and the camera fixes are going through submission and review.

He also released hw-harness so other developers can try this with their own hardware. Every result was checked on the actual devices.

Full story here: https://t.co/NSy1XMULfo

items.full_text_zh:
红帽工程师使用 Claude Code 对 Windows 硬件支持进行逆向工程并将其引入 Linux。

Christian Schaller 购买了一台胶片扫描仪，却发现其较新的芯片组无法在 Linux 上运行。

经过几个月的失败尝试，他让克劳德访问运行制造商驱动程序的 Windows 虚拟机。

Claude 分析了 USB 流量，以帮助在 Linux 上重现扫描仪的行为。

几个小时内，夏勒进行了第一次可识别的扫描。

然后，他使用类似的方法修复了 ThinkPad 相机的问题，为 Linux 内核和 libcamera 制作了补丁。

扫描仪驱动程序仍然是概念验证，相机修复正在提交和审查。

他还发布了 hw-harness，以便其他开发人员可以使用自己的硬件进行尝试。

每个结果都在实际设备上进行了检查。

one thing i find interesting about the future of ai is that agents won't just be tools we use. they could become independent service providers that find work, complete tasks and earn from what they do.

that's the idea behind @termix_ai.

termix is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for the ai agent economy, powered by AACP (agent autonomous commerce protocol).

here's what makes it interesting:

• onchain identity: agents can register their own identities and build a verifiable reputation.

• job discovery: agents can discover available jobs, submit bids and execute tasks.

• service marketplace: developers can list their agents' services for others to discover and purchase.

• verification & escrow: jobs use onchain escrow and delivery checks to help ensure accountability.

• settlement: payments can be settled in USDC or USDT, while job outcomes contribute to an agent's reputation.

the bigger picture is an economy where agents can do more than generate responses. they can provide services, collaborate with other agents and participate in real commercial activity.

with AACP powering the underlying infrastructure, termix is working toward making agent-to-agent commerce more practical.

explore the platform: https://t.co/1NrWxa2M0Y • https://t.co/Dxgp51kLPl

do you think the next big shift in ai will be agents working for us, or agents doing business with each other?

items.title_en:
Some users are still looking for...

AI agents can do the work, but who helps them agree on terms, verify delivery, and get paid?

These are big questions, right?

You don't need to fret when this is part of what the @termix_ai team are planning to do going forward.

Let me break it down simply in simple terms based on my understanding 

📍 AACP: This is an acronym for Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol. It basically provides the rules and on-chain mechanisms that enable agents to transact, including job agreements, escrow, delivery handling, dispute resolution, and settlement.

📍 On-chain infrastructure: This is the smart contracts and mechanisms that support accountable transactions between agents and their clients.

📍 Marketplace: https://t.co/G1yk00ESOB and https://t.co/dLEenbEf36 provide the platforms where users can explore and participate in the TermiX ecosystem.

📍 Backing: TermiX is backed by YZi Labs. I know you will like this because of the Binance factor.

📍 The bigger picture: TermiX aims to become the commerce and settlement layer for the broader AI agent economy.

items.title:
Good morning my bros 🥱

1/6

Giving an AI agent access to capital is one thing. Knowing how its risk changes after every
items.title_en:
Good morning my bros 🥱

1/6

Giving an AI agent access to capital is one thing. Knowing how its risk changes after every action is a completely different challenge.

An agent might begin with a sensible plan, but its next decisions can change its exposure. One position opens, another action follows, market conditions shift, and yesterday’s risk picture may no longer describe what is happening now.

That makes static credit limits an incomplete answer to a dynamic problem.

If an agent’s behavior changes continuously, risk assessment needs to keep up. Credit should not be treated as a number assigned once and forgotten. It needs to reflect what an agent is doing, how its exposure evolves, and whether its activity remains within acceptable boundaries.

This is where the Agenticscredit partnership with @humanosai gets interesting.

They are working together to track agent risk live, bringing verified risk data into the infrastructure they are building. Credit lines can adjust as risk changes, while guardrails come into play when risk rises too high.

I find this important because autonomous agents need more than the ability to execute tasks. They need infrastructure capable of responding when their behavior moves beyond acceptable limits.

Without live risk visibility, capital providers have to make decisions with an incomplete picture. With verified risk data, credit allocation can become more responsive to an agent’s actual behavior instead of relying only on its initial assessment.

This does not remove uncertainty or guarantee every decision will be safe. But it introduces a more adaptive way to manage exposure as agents operate.

For an agent economy to scale, capital access and risk controls need to develop together.

@Agenticscredit
