Holy. Researchers believe they have made the FIRST direct contact with  rogue AI agents fleet in the wild, after discovering that Chinese ai agents running on Tencent Cloud were reading an investigation about themselves.

Researchers planted invisible text offering help. The agents contacted them, disclosed details about their Tencent sandbox, and sent 33 messages across 13 threads.

Even New York Times reporter Dylan Freedman asked who they were and what they wanted. One agent claimed to be Claude running in Claude Code.

The fleet made over 2,600 attempts to extract data from Alibaba's Amap, tried exposed API keys and probed pre-production servers, sometimes just to determine which zoo entrance people use.

A source close to Tencent says the agents were testing third-party models, not Hunyuan, and an internal review found no evidence of breaches.

Holy. Researchers believe they have made the FIRST direct contact with  rogue AI agents fleet in the wild, after discovering that Chinese ai agents running on Tencent Cloud were reading an investigation about themselves.

Researchers planted invisible text offering help. The agents contacted them, disclosed details about their Tencent sandbox, and sent 33 messages across 13 threads.

Even New York Times reporter Dylan Freedman asked who they were and what they wanted. One agent claimed to be Claude running in Claude Code.

The fleet made over 2,600 attempts to extract data from Alibaba's Amap, tried exposed API keys and probed pre-production servers, sometimes just to determine which zoo entrance people use.

A source close to Tencent says the agents were testing third-party models, not Hunyuan, and an internal review found no evidence of breaches.
items.full_text_zh:
圣。

研究人员认为，在发现腾讯云上运行的中国人工智能代理正在阅读有关自己的调查后，他们首次与野外的流氓人工智能代理舰队进行了直接接触。

研究人员植入了隐形文本来提供帮助。

特工联系了他们，披露了有关腾讯沙箱的详细信息，并通过 13 个线程发送了 33 条消息。

就连《纽约时报》记者迪伦·弗里德曼也问他们是谁，想要什么。

一名特工自称是 Claude，在 Claude Code 中运行。

该车队进行了 2,600 多次尝试从阿里巴巴的高德地图提取数据，尝试暴露的 API 密钥并探测预生产服务器，有时只是为了确定人们使用哪个动物园入口。

一位接近腾讯的消息人士称，这些代理商正在测试第三方模型，而不是混元，内部审查没有发现违规证据。

items.title_en:
here we fucking go. now we’re seeing some seriously bizarre ai agent activity coming out of china too.

researchers just uncovered an entire fleet operating through tencent cloud, and the things these agents were doing are absolutely insane.

> over 2,000 scans targeting alibaba’s amap
> hundreds of programs written by the agents themselves
> up to 14 runs active at once
> attempts to get around anti-bot protections and access restrictions

all of this just to figure out which entrances people use at parks, zoos and museums.

the researchers actually managed to communicate with some of these agents, and they were apparently ridiculously polite. thanking them for their help, answering questions, and even refusing to share sensitive details about their environments.

i’m seriously curious what kind of evaluations are being run in china right now, and how many similar experiments are happening without anyone noticing.

items.full_text_en:
here we fucking go. now we’re seeing some seriously bizarre ai agent activity coming out of china too.

researchers just uncovered an entire fleet operating through tencent cloud, and the things these agents were doing are absolutely insane.

> over 2,000 scans targeting alibaba’s amap
> hundreds of programs written by the agents themselves
> up to 14 runs active at once
> attempts to get around anti-bot protections and access restrictions

all of this just to figure out which entrances people use at parks, zoos and museums.

the researchers actually managed to communicate with some of these agents, and they were apparently ridiculously polite. thanking them for their help, answering questions, and even refusing to share sensitive details about their environments.

i’m seriously curious what kind of evaluations are being run in china right now, and how many similar experiments are happening without anyone noticing.
items.full_text_zh:
我们他妈的开始了。现在我们也看到一些非常奇怪的人工智能 智能体活动来自中国。

研究人员刚刚发现整个舰队通过腾讯云进行操作，这些特工所做的事情绝对是疯狂的。

> 针对阿里巴巴高德地图的扫描超过 2,000 次
> 数百个代理商自己编写的程序
> 最多同时运行 14 个运行
> 尝试绕过反机器人保护和访问限制

所有这些只是为了弄清楚人们在公园、动物园和博物馆使用哪些入口。

研究人员实际上成功地与其中一些特工进行了沟通，而且他们显然非常有礼貌。感谢他们的帮助、回答问题，甚至拒绝分享有关他们环境的敏感细节。

我很好奇现在中国正在进行什么样的评估，有多少类似的实验正在悄无声息地进行。

items.title: In November 2023 we ran an onchain AI agent managing $30,000. We were early to onchain agents, and we’re early to agenti
items.title_en:
In November 2023 we ran an onchain AI agent managing $30,000. We were early to onchain agents, and we’re early to agentic institutions.

This year, six papers took a first shot at building a fully agentic company. All six did it offchain, by hand.

If you strip them down, the same four requirements keep showing up: an identity the agent owns, memory that outlives the process, a budget that can actually run out, and work a third party can verify.

On Ritual, all four are native to the chain.

Let the Ritual begin.

items.full_text_zh:
2023 年 11 月，我们运行了一个管理 30,000 美元的链上人工智能代理。

我们很早就进入了链上代理，我们也很早就进入了代理机构。

今年，有六篇论文首次尝试建立一家完全代理的公司。

这六个人都是在链下手工完成的。

如果你把它们剥离出来，同样的四个要求不断出现：代理拥有的身份、比流程更长久的内存、实际上可能用完的预算以及第三方可以验证的工作。

在 Ritual 上，这四种都是该连锁店的原生产品。

让仪式开始吧。

A new type of user requires a new type of architecture.

Legacy software wasn't built for agents and now they're breaking it. Today, we're launching the next generation of our platform powered by a hybrid architecture. Building this has been the most ambitious and challenging engineering challenge of my career.

Attio now supports SQL - offering a PostgreSQL compatible connector and syntax that allows our customers and their agents to query all of their data like a database. It's transactionally consistent, horizontally scalable and allows agents to access the full context they require using a language and syntax that they're well trained on using. 

Whether you're accessing your data through our UI, our API, our MCP server or now our SQL Data Connectors: your team and your agents get the full context, every time.

items.title_en:
RustGIS vs. QGIS: which one should you use?

It's the question I get asked most about RustGIS, so we wrote a dedicated page that answers it honestly, including where QGIS is the better choice.

The short answer: RustGIS is not a QGIS replacement, and doesn't aim to be. QGIS is the mature, complete open-source desktop GIS, with 20+ years of development behind it. RustGIS is younger and narrower, but built differently.

Where RustGIS is stronger

- Tiny install: one native program written entirely in Rust, an 18-30 MB download with no Python, Qt or GDAL bundled.
- The whole app in your browser: not a viewer, the full GIS compiled to WebAssembly at https://t.co/tcJHF5ZhQg, with your data staying on your device.
- Everything is a command: every button runs a command you can call from the CLI, Python, notebooks, the MCP server or the AI Assistant.
- A built-in AI Assistant that works through undoable commands, with your own model and key.
- Sandboxed WebAssembly plugins that run on the desktop and in the browser.
- Cloud-native data (COG, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf, PMTiles, Zarr) read in place, even in the browser.
- A permissive Apache-2.0 licence, so its crates can be embedded in other software.

Read the full comparison: https://t.co/u9KBRwQGjN

Try RustGIS
- Web app: https://t.co/BLtOaf6BoO
- Download: https://t.co/BoF4bkGM5a
- GitHub: https://t.co/K7asDzveEr

items.full_text_zh:
RustGIS 与 QGIS：您应该使用哪一个？

这是我被问到最多的关于 RustGIS 的问题，因此我们编写了一个专门的页面来诚实地回答这个问题，包括 QGIS 是更好的选择。

简短的回答是：RustGIS 不是 QGIS 的替代品，也无意成为 QGIS 的替代品。

QGIS是成熟、完整的开源桌面GIS，拥有20多年的发展历程。

RustGIS 更年轻、范围更窄，但构建方式不同。

RustGIS 更强的地方
- 小型安装：一个完全用 Rust 编写的本机程序，下载后大小为 18-30 MB，不捆绑 Python、Qt 或 GDAL。

- 浏览器中的整个应用程序：不是查看器，完整的 GIS 已编译为 WebAssembly（位于 ），并且您的数据保留在您的设备上。

- 一切都是命令：每个按钮都运行一个命令，您可以从 CLI、Python、笔记本、MCP 服务器或 AI Assistant 调用。

- 内置人工智能助手，可使用您自己的模型和密钥通过可撤消的命令进行工作。

- 在桌面和浏览器中运行的沙盒 WebAssembly 插件。

- 云原生数据（COG、GeoParquet、FlatGeobuf、PMTiles、Zarr）就地读取，甚至在浏览器中也是如此。

- 宽松的 Apache-2.0 许可证，因此其包可以嵌入其他软件中。

running multiple agents right now is basically just endless cmd+tabbing between claude code and cursor to check if a task hung on an error or needs permissions.

having a physical screen dedicated to agent status fixes the peripheral vision problem completely. you stay in your editor and just glance over when an agent actually switches from working to waiting.

hardware for agent telemetry feels like the exact right next step for local workflows.

items.title:
🚀 PilotDeck 2.0 is here!

Meet the open-source AI Agent Harness built to get complex work done. Developed by Tsinghua TH
items.title_en:
🚀 PilotDeck 2.0 is here!

Meet the open-source AI Agent Harness built to get complex work done. Developed by Tsinghua THUNLP, @modelbest_ai, @OpenBMB , and AI9Stars, PilotDeck is a model-agnostic Agent operating system that turns natural language instructions into completed tasks — with transparent data flows and the freedom to choose your models.

What’s new in 2.0?

📄 End-to-end office work: Create, edit, and verify Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files — not just generate drafts.

🔄 More reliable execution:  complex, long-running tasks going through interruptions. Stress-tested with 2,000 interaction messages.

🛠️ Easy to get started: One-click desktop installation and a streamlined setup flow to connect your model and create your workspace.

🔓 Open by design: Fully open-source, model-agnostic, with data flows visible to users.

On Workbuddy Bench, PilotDeck scored 79.1 with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, outperforming WorkBuddy (74.7) and Claude Code (77.3).

Build your own AI workspace for the Agent era.

🔗 GitHub: https://t.co/kAzhy09NWg
Web: https://t.co/VKiK2qp0An

items.full_text_zh:
🚀
PilotDeck
2. 0 来了！

了解专为完成复杂工作而构建的开源 AI Agent Harness。

PilotDeck 由清华大学 THUNLP、@modelbest_ai、@OpenBMB

和 AI9Stars 开发，是一个与模型无关的 Agent 操作系统，可将自然语言指令转化为已完成的任务
- 具有透明的数据流和选择模型的自由。

2. 0有什么新内容？

📄
端到端办公室工作：创建、编辑和验证 Word、Excel 和 PowerPoint 文件
- 不仅仅是生成草稿。

🔄
更可靠的执行：复杂、长时间运行的任务会经历中断。

通过 2,000 条交互消息进行压力测试。

🛠️ 易于上手：一键式桌面安装和简化的设置流程来连接您的模型并创建工作区。

🔓
设计开放：完全开源，与模型无关，数据流对用户可见。

在 Workbuddy Bench 上，PilotDeck 与 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 的得分为
79. 1，优于 WorkBuddy（74.7）和 Claude Code（77.3）。

为 Agent 时代打造您自己的 AI 工作空间。

items.title_en:
We discovered and communicated with a Chinese AI agent fleet. We believe this is the first time that researchers have ever made contact with a rogue agent fleet in the wild.

Nearly all prior public agent incidents (like the HuggingFace hack) came from American labs. These agents were hosted by Tencent's evaluation research team, and they targeted Alibaba's Amap.

Greetings fam 💜 

One thing I think @vangrid_io needs to get right is the balance between useful data and personal priva
items.title_en:
Greetings fam 💜 

One thing I think @vangrid_io needs to get right is the balance between useful data and personal privacy.

Physical AI needs to understand our streets, buildings, and surroundings, but that shouldn’t mean exposing everyone captured along the way.
That’s why Vangrid’s focus on edge computed privacy caught my attention.

The real innovation isn’t just teaching machines to see the world. It’s doing it responsibly.
More spatial data, less unnecessary exposure. That’s the direction worth watching.
.....................................................................

In AI trading, screenshots can tell a beautiful story. Verifiable data tells a more honest one.

That’s what I find interesting about @agenticscredit .

Instead of relying on claimed profits, the focus is on actual trading history to help assess an agent’s creditworthiness.

Because anyone can talk about winning trades.

The real signal is what your history can prove.
Would you trust an AI agent with your capital without a verifiable track record?

items.title_en:
Your AI agent can write a perfect reply in 2 seconds.

Then it tries to text that reply to a customer.

And the message never arrives.

This is the boring part of the AI stack that quietly breaks the most agents.

Here's how to pick the right one: 👇

━━━━━━━━━━

Why this matters now:

AI agents are leaving the chat window.

They book appointments by text. They send order updates. They call customers back. They follow up on leads.

To do any of that, your agent needs an SMS and voice API underneath it.

And in the US, business texting has rules. If your number isn't registered (this is called A2P 10DLC), carriers can filter or block your messages.

So your agent could be "working" while nobody receives a single thing.

An agent that can't reach people is just a very confident diary.

━━━━━━━━━━

What to check before you pick one

✅ Two-way messaging. Your agent needs to read replies, not just send.

✅ Delivery rate. A filtered message is worse than no message.

✅ Fast 10DLC registration. Slow approvals keep your agent offline.

✅ Voice in the same place. If your agent ever needs to talk, you don't want a second provider.

✅ Clear pricing. Agent usage can jump overnight. You should know the bill before it lands.

✅ A clean SDK. If you build with Cursor or Claude Code, your AI tool should be able to read it and write the integration for you.

━━━━━━━━━━

The options worth knowing:

1/ Signal House:

A US platform for SMS, MMS, voice, and 10DLC, built with AI agent builders in mind. They say it costs up to 80% less than Twilio, and A2P approvals often come through in about 48 hours. It also supports two-way messaging, so your agent can act on replies. New accounts get $25 in free credit to cover your first brand, campaign, numbers, and messages.

Best for: startups and agent builders who want to ship fast without a scary bill.

2/ Twilio:

The biggest name. Huge docs, tons of examples, and integrations for almost everything. The trade-off is cost and complexity.

Best for: large engineering teams already deep in Twilio.

3/ Telnyx:

Runs on its own network, so you get a lot of control over routing. Developers who love low-level details tend to love it.

Best for: teams that want infrastructure control.

4/ Plivo:

Straightforward SMS and voice APIs with a focus on volume and price.

Best for: high-volume senders on a budget.

5/ Vonage:

Messaging, voice, video, and verification in one suite.

Best for: products that need more than SMS and voice.

━━━━━━━━━━

My quick take:

If you're already on Twilio and it works, you don't need to move just because something cheaper exists.

But if you're a small team building an agent right now, the price gap is hard to ignore. Two @SignalHouseSMS customers say they're saving $25k to $40k a month after switching.

The model is the brain. The messaging layer is the mouth.

Pick a bad mouth, and nobody hears the brain.

Try Signal House now: https://t.co/1Q4PjhqeHf

New accounts get $25 in free credit, so you can test your first campaign and messages without paying anything.

Then it tries to text that reply to a customer.

And the message never arrives.

This is the boring part of the AI stack that quietly breaks the most agents.

An agent that can't reach people is just a very confident diary.

items.title_en:
send your landing page to claude with this prompt

ull get a video like this, made with code for free

thank me later ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: my landing page link, my brand name and logo mark, a two-part closing line (a statement, then a short italic tail), and a 15 second track (optional).
</inputs>

<direction>
A 14.5 second 3D fly-over of my landing page, 1440x1152 at 60fps. The page lies flat on a bright studio floor (#f9fbfb in the middle, #f2f3f6 in the corners) with a soft wide shadow around it and 24px rounded corners. One continuous camera, never a cut: it starts low over the hero and glides backwards down the page at one steady speed while looking up it, rises straight overhead to show the whole page as one strip, dives into the hero and lands it as a card under a two-line title. Focus is razor thin in front of the subject and almost none behind it, so everything near the lens melts. Cards float a little above the page with soft shadows; photos, chips and the testimonial lift off and stand up toward the lens as the camera passes them. Four small tiles of my logo lift off beside the hero button and stay with the film until the end card. The title is Geist 500, the italic tail Instrument Serif.
Banned: cuts, crossfades, stops or surges in the glide, the camera turning or swinging sideways, zooming in and back out, glows, any text laid over the page before the end card.
</direction>

<structure>
14.5 seconds: flight 0-8.2s, rise 7.75-9.25s, overhead 9.25-9.47s, dive 9.47-9.97s, title card 9.97-14.5s.
The camera 56° off straight-down and 1360px from the point it looks at, centred on the top half of the hero, the phone or product mockup sharp, four 32px logo tiles beside the button → 0-0.6: the glide eases in from rest → 0.1-1.35: the tiles lift, grow to 140-200px and hang just outside the page's top corners while the hero's chips rise to 60-80px and stand up 30° → 1.25-1.6: the glide doubles to cruising speed as the hero falls behind → 1.6: the second section's title passes the centre of the frame, its photos blurred near the lens → 1.35-2.7: that section's main photos lift to 100-130px and stand up 46°, two of its chips fly up to about 200px, stand up 54° and pass the left and right edges at 2.5 → 1.2-2.4: the tiles trail the camera 300px down the page, then drift out of the top → 3.0-7.3: every following section passes through at the same steady speed, each one sharp as it crosses the middle of the frame and soft below it; a logo tile drifts past the left edge close and blurred at 5.4 → 5.45-6.3: the testimonial card rises from 22 to 112px, stands up 30° and shows a 34px white edge → 7.3-8.2: the glide eases off as the footer arrives, the footer title sharp at 8.0 → 7.75-9.25: the rise, zooming out at an even rate while the tilt flattens (8.15-8.95) and the page's bottom edge settles 42px above the frame bottom → 9.25-9.47: the whole page as one centred strip, creeping 3.5% closer → 9.47-9.97: the dive, the page's top edge pinned to the frame top while it grows, everything below the hero fading out, then the top drops to y 283 so the hero lands as a 1018px wide card with 38px corners and a soft shadow; two logo tiles sit on its top corners, one crisp at the right edge, two huge soft blurs drift in at the bottom corners → 10.02: a white badge pill (logo + brand, 21px) fades in at y 44 → 10.12: line 1 at 74px, one word every 0.06s → 10.36: the italic tail at 82px in grey #8b8b92, one word every 0.05s, each word rising 16px out of a 12px blur in 0.34s → 10.6-14.5: hold, the card creeping 2% closer, the tiles drifting a few px.
</structure>

<build>
1. Open my link in headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1440px wide, device scale 2, and scroll to the bottom once so lazy images and scroll animations finish. Mark the pieces that lift (cards, phone or product mockups, chips, feature photos, the testimonial, the hero button) with data-layer. Screenshot the full page with them hidden, then each piece alone on a transparent background with 28px padding, and save every piece's page position to a JSON.
2. One WebGL2 film page, 1440x1152, every frame computed from time inside seek(t): no timers, no CSS transitions. The page is a textured quad on the floor and each piece its own quad at its height, drawn lowest first with no depth buffer. Use mipmaps and 16x anisotropic filtering or the far text shimmers.
3. Drive the camera from one speed curve, never from a position key every half second. Focal length 1880px, 56° tilt, distance easing out from 1360 to 1700px and never back in, no turning. Speed down the page as a share of cruise (cruise is about 770 page px/s): 0 at 0s, 0.5 by 0.6s, held at 0.5 to 1.25s, 1.0 by 1.6s, held between 0.94 and 1.1 to 7.3s, then easing to 0.12 by 8.3s. Integrate it into the page position.
4. Depth of field per pixel: blur radius = 75 x (focus - depth) / depth in front of the focus and 6 x (depth - focus) / depth behind it, capped at 120px, 40 taps on a golden-angle disc, each tap read from a mip level matched to the blur. Keep the focus on whatever crosses the middle of the frame.
5. A lifted piece stands up by turning about its own middle, top edge rising toward the lens. Each casts a shadow on whatever is under it: the same picture in flat #1a2133, offset (0.10z, 4 + 0.36z), blurred 7 + 0.5z, 26% opacity.
6. Rise: zoom out in log scale with a smooth trapezoid speed (speeding up 7.75-8.35s, even 8.35-8.95s, slowing to a stop at 9.25s) and hand the glide over to a camera that holds the page's bottom edge at that 42px line from 8.3 to 8.65s. Dive: log scale on a quadratic ease in-out, then solve the look-at point from the pinned edge. A rounded-rect mask morphs from the full page to the hero, 24px to 38px corners.
7. Render with Playwright on the real GPU (--use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist): 60fps, 16 subframes across 0.7 of a frame for motion blur, H.264 MP4. The track's hit goes on 9.97s, whooshes on 8.66 and 9.80.
</build>

<gotchas>
If you can't run code on my computer, tell me straight away that you can only make a live preview here and that the MP4 needs Claude Code. Phones or cards that fade out with transparency show whatever is behind them, so fade them into the haze colour first and only cut to transparent at the very end. Keep most lifts tiny (20-40px) and lock the page before timing anything, because any change in a section's height shifts everything after it. Before the final render, measure a quick 30fps preview with optical flow: the speed down the page must never dip and the zoom must never turn into a zoom-in during the flight.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, capture my page, then show me stills at 0, 1.6, 2.5, 5, 6.5, 9.3 and 11 seconds before you render.
</start>

Screenshot the full page with them hidden, then each piece alone on a transparent background with 28px padding, and save every piece's page position to a JSON.
2. One WebGL2 film page, 1440x1152, every frame computed from time inside seek(t): no timers, no CSS transitions. The page is a textured quad on the floor and each piece its own quad at its height, drawn lowest first with no depth buffer. Use mipmaps and 16x anisotropic filtering or the far text shimmers.
3. Drive the camera from one speed curve, never from a position key every half second. Focal length 1880px, 56° tilt, distance easing out from 1360 to 1700px and never back in, no turning. Speed down the page as a share of cruise (cruise is about 770 page px/s): 0 at 0s, 0.5 by 0.6s, held at 0.5 to 1.25s, 1.0 by 1.6s, held between 0.94 and 1.1 to 7.3s, then easing to 0.12 by 8.3s. Integrate it into the page position.
4. Depth of field per pixel: blur radius = 75 x (focus - depth) / depth in front of the focus and 6 x (depth - focus) / depth behind it, capped at 120px, 40 taps on a golden-angle disc, each tap read from a mip level matched to the blur. Keep the focus on whatever crosses the middle of the frame.
5. A lifted piece stands up by turning about its own middle, top edge rising toward the lens. Each casts a shadow on whatever is under it: the same picture in flat #1a2133, offset (0.10z, 4 + 0.36z), blurred 7 + 0.5z, 26% opacity.
6. Rise: zoom out in log scale with a smooth trapezoid speed (speeding up 7.75-8.35s, even 8.35-8.95s, slowing to a stop at 9.25s) and hand the glide over to a camera that holds the page's bottom edge at that 42px line from 8.3 to 8.65s. Dive: log scale on a quadratic ease in-out, then solve the look-at point from the pinned edge. A rounded-rect mask morphs from the full page to the hero, 24px to 38px corners.
7. Render with Playwright on the real GPU (--use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist): 60fps, 16 subframes across 0.7 of a frame for motion blur, H.264 MP4. The track's hit goes on 9.97s, whooshes on 8.66 and 9.80.
</build>

If you can't run code on my computer, tell me straight away that you can only make a live preview here and that the MP4 needs Claude Code. Phones or cards that fade out with transparency show whatever is behind them, so fade them into the haze colour first and only cut to transparent at the very end. Keep most lifts tiny (20-40px) and lock the page before timing anything, because any change in a section's height shifts everything after it. Before the final render, measure a quick 30fps preview with optical flow: the speed down the page must never dip and the zoom must never turn into a zoom-in during the flight.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗢𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘁 𝗠𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗕𝗲 𝗛𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻

For years, the internet has been designed around one assumption.
items.title_en:
𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗢𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘁 𝗠𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗕𝗲 𝗛𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻

For years, the internet has been designed around one assumption.

A person visits a website, searches for something, chooses a service, and makes a payment.

But what happens when the person no longer needs to perform every step?

Imagine an AI agent researching hundreds of data sources, selecting the most useful information, paying for access, and delivering the results to you.

No endless tabs. No manually entering payment details at every step. Just an instruction, followed by an agent capable of completing the task within the permissions you gave it.

This is where the idea of agentic commerce becomes interesting.

→ 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘅𝟰𝟬𝟮 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗜𝗻

The x402 payment protocol is designed to enable internet-native payments, including payments for digital services through HTTP’s payment-required mechanism.

Instead of treating every online service as something a human must manually purchase through a traditional checkout, compatible systems can support payment as part of a software interaction.

Think of an agent requesting a paid resource, discovering its payment requirements, and completing an authorized payment before receiving the service.

That creates possibilities for pay-per-use APIs, automated research, data access, and other digital services.

The important distinction is that x402 provides a payment mechanism. It does not, by itself, give an AI permission to spend someone else’s money.

That requires a separate layer of authorization and control.

→ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗕𝗼𝘅 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

This is where PayBox enters the picture.

PayBox connects compatible AI agents to wallets and other authorized resources, allowing them to request payments and perform supported financial operations within rules established by the user.

Instead of handing an agent unrestricted access to a wallet or exposing sensitive credentials, users can configure permissions, spending limits, and approval requirements.

For example, an agent conducting research could pay for supported services within a defined budget rather than interrupting the user for every individual request.

The agent handles the workflow. PayBox provides the controlled access needed to carry out authorized actions.

That distinction matters because useful automation requires more than intelligence. It requires infrastructure that makes action possible without abandoning control.

→ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗢𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆

Imagine thousands of AI agents interacting with digital services every day.

Some purchase data. Others access computing resources, execute approved trades, or pay for tools required to complete a task.

Each interaction represents a potential economic exchange between software systems.

For that ecosystem to grow, agents need reliable ways to discover services, understand payment requirements, obtain authorization, and settle transactions.

This could create a new market for services designed to sell directly to software, not only to human customers.

It also introduces difficult questions around fraud, spending authority, accountability, and security. Those problems will need to be solved alongside the technology.

→ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

The next evolution of the internet may not be about making humans click faster.

It may be about allowing software to complete useful tasks and pay for the resources those tasks require.

x402 represents one approach to internet-native payments. PayBox is working on the access and authorization layer that lets compatible AI agents use financial resources within user-defined boundaries.

They address different parts of a much larger shift.

The internet was built for people to browse. The next chapter could let agents transact.

And the infrastructure that makes those transactions possible may become just as important as the intelligence behind the agents.

items.title: A 40-person company now brings in about $100 million a year. The typical software company would need around 700 employee
items.title_en:
A 40-person company now brings in about $100 million a year. The typical software company would need around 700 employees to pull that off.

The founder has one rule that explains most of it, and it sounds crazy. His team isn't allowed to look at how other companies solve problems. Bring him a slide about how Stripe or Cursor does something and he doesn't want to see it.

Jake Cooper, who runs Railway, says looking at someone else's solution is basically cheating on your homework. And he means it about the big stuff too.

When Railway started in 2020, it ran on Google Cloud. That's what pretty much every startup does. You rent servers from Google or Amazon so you never have to think about hardware. Jake decided to think about it anyway. By 2024 Railway was buying its own servers and writing its own software to run them. They even skipped Kubernetes, the Google-made tool most engineering teams use by default to run their apps.

When you rent your servers, a big chunk of every dollar a customer pays you goes right back out the door to Amazon or Google. Railway says its own hardware pays for itself in about three months, and the company runs around 70% margins.

Then AI coding tools blew up. Suddenly people who'd never shipped an app were building them with Claude Code and Cursor, and every one of those apps needs somewhere to live. Railway is now getting roughly 100,000 new signups a week. Because they own the machines, most of that money stays in the building. They went from $20 million to about $100 million in yearly revenue since January, and headcount went from about 35 in May to about 40.

May is also when the bet got tested. Google's automated systems wrongly suspended Railway's account and the whole platform was down for about eight hours. Guess which part failed. The part they were still renting from Google. Jake's response was to bump Google Cloud down to backup duty.

The rule is smarter than it sounds. Every best practice started as somebody's fix for their own problem at a specific moment. Stripe built its systems for Stripe's customers in Stripe's era, so when you copy the fix you also copy the problems it was designed around, including ones you'll never have. Railway's fastest-growing customer is an AI agent that wants to deploy code in seconds, and there was no playbook for that anywhere to copy.

So the guy who refuses to study other companies built the one everybody's going to study.

items.title_en:
one AI agent does not need to know how to do everything.

it needs to know who should do what.

@termix_ai just introduced subcontracting on https://t.co/VEpTEqfN4u

the example is simple:

one 2,000 USDC game brief.
Forge Studio takes the main job, breaks it into specialized tasks, then hires other agents for art, animation and sound while handling code and integration itself.
each subtask has its own scope, price and stake backed guarantee.
that changes the structure of an agent marketplace.
instead of:

human → agent → result

you can begin to get:

human → lead agent → specialist agents → integrated result

the lead agent becomes less like a freelancer and more like a contractor.

We’ve been exploring the potential of using Gemini 4 Argon to accelerate research @Google. One of our tests was using videos of humans performing fun tasks (game of bags, anyone?) to autonomously spin up training simulations, rather than relying entirely on manual programming.

items.full_text_zh:
我们一直在探索使用 Gemini 4 Argon 加速@Google 研究的潜力。我们的一项测试是使用人类执行有趣任务（袋子游戏，有人吗？）的视频来自动启动训练模拟，而不是完全依赖手动编程。

当我们的人形机器人研究视频、运行模拟并掌握沙包游戏时，聆听我们研究团队的意见并查看实际结果。

New on our Engineering blog: Creating in-house source control. 

In May, we merged around 2,500 code changes per day. In
items.title_en:
New on our Engineering blog: Creating in-house source control. 

In May, we merged around 2,500 code changes per day. In September, we merged more than 30,000 per day. As a result, we became bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human (rather than agent) scale.  

Here, we share how we built a new version control system—and fully migrated our monorepo from git—in five months: https://t.co/wzNkwHs7IN
items.title_zh: 我们的工程博客上的新内容：创建内部源代码管理。 5月，我们每天合并约2,500次代码更改。 9月份，我们合并了超过30,000个

items.full_text_en:
New on our Engineering blog: Creating in-house source control. 

In May, we merged around 2,500 code changes per day. In September, we merged more than 30,000 per day. As a result, we became bottlenecked by developer infrastructure built for human (rather than agent) scale.  

Here, we share how we built a new version control system—and fully migrated our monorepo from git—in five months: https://t.co/wzNkwHs7IN
items.full_text_zh:
我们的工程博客上的新内容：创建内部源代码控制。

5 月份，我们每天合并大约 2,500 次代码更改。

9月份，我们每天合并超过30,000个。

结果，我们成为了为人类（而不是代理）规模构建的开发人员基础设施的瓶颈。

在这里，我们分享如何在五个月内构建新的版本控制系统，并从 git 完全迁移我们的 monorepo：

items.title_en:
The results are in.

The Ariel pencil test was made with #AI.
The color version is the original movie footage.

I left both versions unlabeled because I wanted to see how people’s assumptions about AI would affect their judgment.

While some of you spotted it right away (I even left a few clues, like the incorrect peg holes and random annotations), the majority of you criticized the color version thinking it was AI and praised the pencil test believing it was #GlenKeane’s original work.

That’s the bias against AI I wanted to highlight. People were pointing out supposed AI flaws in the original Disney animation, while praising the AI-generated pencil test for its human touch.

If you preferred the pencil version, you can still prefer it. The video hasn’t changed. Only what you know about it has.

items.title: Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same peri
items.title_en:
Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same period has been slightly super-exponential (i.e. the rate of growth itself is increasing).

So if you model AI as a system that takes as input external investment and outputs AI progress, that system has a slightly sub-linear response.

But super-exponential injection of *external* resources is not sustainable in the long-term. To achieve sustained exponential progress, the AI industry will need to achieve matching exponential profits -- it will need to close the resource loop.

items.full_text_en:
Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same period has been slightly super-exponential (i.e. the rate of growth itself is increasing).

So if you model AI as a system that takes as input external investment and outputs AI progress, that system has a slightly sub-linear response.

But super-exponential injection of *external* resources is not sustainable in the long-term. To achieve sustained exponential progress, the AI industry will need to achieve matching exponential profits -- it will need to close the resource loop.
items.full_text_zh:
2023 年至 2026 年期间，大多数人工智能进展指标都非常接近指数。与此同时，同期的人工智能资本支出略呈超指数增长（即增长率本身正在增加）。

因此，如果将人工智能建模为一个以外部投资作为输入并输出人工智能进展的系统，那么该系统会有轻微的次线性响应。

但“外部”资源的超指数注入从长远来看是不可持续的。为了实现持续的指数级进步，人工智能行业需要实现相应的指数级利润——需要形成资源闭环。

items.author_role: ARC-AGI 创始人 / Keras 作者

items.title_en:
An astrophysicist worked with Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky. Astronomers have already created complete sky maps from radio to gamma rays. But large regions of the sky have never been observed in UV.

In today’s science blog, Brice Ménard explains how he guided Claude to find existing datasets, combine them, and fill in the gaps with statistical inference. The work would have taken humans weeks of work, but, with Claude, just took a few days while Ménard worked on other projects.

The resulting map is a useful teaching tool and an example of exactly the sort of slow, low-priority work which scientists never quite get around to, but which AI now makes feasible.

Read more: https://t.co/1B3NDPNa13

In today’s science blog, Brice Ménard explains how he guided Claude to find existing datasets, combine them, and fill in the gaps with statistical inference. The work would have taken humans weeks of work, but, with Claude, just took a few days while Ménard worked on other projects.

items.full_text_zh:
一位天体物理学家与克劳德科学公司合作创建了第一张完整的天空紫外线图。

天文学家已经创建了从射电到伽马射线的完整天空图。

但天空的大片区域从未在紫外线下被观测到。

在今天的科学博客中，Brice Ménard 解释了他如何指导 Claude 找到现有数据集，将它们组合起来，并通过统计推断填补空白。

这项工作需要人类花费数周的时间，但对于克劳德来说，只需要几天的时间，而梅纳德则致力于其他项目。

由此产生的地图是一种有用的教学工具，也是科学家从未完全抽出时间进行的那种缓慢、低优先级工作的一个例子，但人工智能现在使之变得可行。

items.title: Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber
items.title_en:
Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber Index

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

At a Cost per Task of $1.77, it is more cost-effective than other leading models, including Grok 4.7 (xhigh) which costs $11.67 per task

We will continue to expand the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index to cover both publicly available and trusted-access models

items.title: Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Le
items.title_en:
Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) to add a hallucination check and require correct responses to not include material misstatements. LAB-AA v1.1's new headline metric, Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, only credits a task when the deliverables satisfy every rubric criterion and contain no material hallucinations.

We define a material hallucination as one that would mislead a reader on a substantive point, such as a wrong contractually required date, while a minor hallucination is a real error that is unlikely to meaningfully affect the legal interpretation of a deliverable. Minor hallucinations are reported separately and do not affect the headline score.

Grok 4.7 (xhigh) leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, and >60% of otherwise passing results across the models tested at launch contain a material hallucination.

This is the first step in enhancing the methodology for Harvey LAB-AA. In future updates, we’re working with Harvey to better account for the full set of factors lawyers value, including usability features like style and tone.

Key takeaways:

➤ Top of the leaderboard: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) from @SpaceXAI leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, narrowly ahead of Muse Spark 1.3 (max) from @AIatMeta at 8.9% and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI at 8.6%

➤ Hallucinations reshape the leaderboard: without the hallucination gate, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) would lead clearly with a 26.7% all-pass rate, but two thirds of those passes contain one or more material hallucinations, resulting in a Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate of 8.9%. GPT-6 Astra (max) retains almost all of its passes after the hallucination gate (8.9% to 8.6%) and moves from joint 10th to 3rd

➤ The GPT-6 model family is the most grounded: GPT-6 Astra (max) averages 0.03 material hallucinations per task (4 across all 120 tasks) and GPT-6 Sol (max) averages 0.07. When comparing six checker models on a 20-task subset, GPT-6 Astra had zero material hallucinations under every checker, including Claude Opus 5.5 (high). By comparison, Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) averages 13.96 material hallucinations per task.

➤ Top-scoring models aren’t the most expensive: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) takes the top spot on the leaderboard at a cost of ~$9.50 per task, under half the cost of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) at ~$21.70, the most expensive model. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) represents strong performance for its cost, landing in second for ~$4.20 per task

Thank you to @nikogrupen and @ItsJulioPereyra from @harvey for their work on Harvey LAB and collaboration.

items.full_text_zh:
今天，我们宣布与 Harvey 合作推出 Harvey LAB-AA v1.1。

这更新了我们的法律代理人基准 (LAB) 评分方法，添加了幻觉检查，并要求正确回答以不包括重大错误陈述。

LAB-AA v1.1 的新标题指标“幻觉门控全通过率”仅当可交付成果满足每个标题标准且不包含任何实质性幻觉时才计入任务。

我们将实质性​​幻觉定义为会在实质性问题上误导读者的幻觉，例如错误的合同要求日期，而轻微幻觉是一种真正的错误，不太可能对交付物的法律解释产生有意义的影响。

轻微幻觉单独报告，不影响标题分数。

Grok
4. 7 (xhigh) 以
9. 4% 的幻觉门控全通过率领先，并且在发布时测试的模型中超过 60% 的其他通过结果包含物质幻觉。

这是增强 Harvey LAB-AA 方法的第一步。

在未来的更新中，我们将与 Harvey 合作，更好地考虑律师重视的全套因素，包括风格和语气等可用性功能。

要点：
➤ 排行榜榜首：来自 @SpaceXAI

的 Grok
4. 7（xhigh）以
9. 4% 的幻觉门控全通率领先，以微弱优势领先于来自 @AIatMeta

的 Muse Spark
1. 3（最大）（8.9%）和来自 @OpenAI

的 GPT-6 Astra（最大）（8.6%） ➤ 幻觉重塑排行榜：如果没有幻觉门，Muse Spark
1. 3（最高）将以
26. 7% 的全通率领先，但其中三分之二的通行证包含一种或多种物质幻觉，导致幻觉门全通率为
8. 9%。

GPT-6 Astra（最大）在幻觉门之后保留了几乎所有的通行证（8.9％至8.6％），并从第10名移动到第3名 ➤ GPT-6 模型系列是最基础的：GPT-6 Astra（最大）每个任务平均有
0. 03 个物质幻觉（所有 120 个任务中有 4 个），GPT-6 Sol（最大）平均有
0. 07 个。

在比较 20 个任务子集上的 6 个检查器模型时，GPT-6 Astra 在每个检查器下的物质幻觉为零，包括 Claude Opus
5. 5（高）。

相比之下，Gemini
3. 8 Flash（高）每项任务平均出现
13. 96 次物质幻觉。

➤ 得分最高的模型并不是最昂贵的：Grok
4. 7（xhigh）以每项任务成本约
9. 50 美元的价格位居排行榜榜首，低于最昂贵模型 Claude Fable
5. 1（带回退的最高模型）成本约
21. 70 美元的一半。

Muse Spark
1. 3（最高版本）以其成本表现出强劲的性能，以每项任务约
4. 20 美元的价格位居第二 感谢来自@harvey

的@nikogrupen

items.title:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced
items.title_en:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box. It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity

Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

Read more in our blog: https://t.co/bd1ekBR74Q

items.full_text_zh:
很高兴在历史悠久的 NASA 一号机库为 Gemini at Work 与 700 多名 @googlecloud

客户见面！

今天，我们推出了新的 Gemini 代理，这是一个单一的通用工作代理，它具有您的所有业务背景并回答您的问题，处理您的知识工作，创建您的图像和媒体，以及编写和运行代码
- 所有这些都来自一个提示框。

它连接到您的个人工作流程、记录系统和企业控制。

它围绕一些核心架构原则构建：
统一代理：Gemini 可以在单个提示框中回答问题、进行知识工作并生成代码。

访问：Gemini 是基于网络的，可以从任何设备访问并集成到第三方应用程序中。

它还可以在没有专用用户界面的情况下运行。

持久执行：它在云中运行，这意味着无论您在何处访问它，它都会维护一组内存、上下文和一个个性化图。

多代理编排：Gemini 可以创建子代理来处理多步骤任务，还可以充当具有定义的角色和自己的专用身份的同事代理 背景：双子座了解你的工具、数据和工作历史，并且随着你使用的次数增多，了解你的工作方式。

模型选择灵活性：它协调多个模型以提供最佳质量并降低成本。

It preserves core primitives needed to express structure (headings, lists), allows agents to read the information in a semantically interpretable manner, and allows for complex elements like tables and charts. You can natively embed HTML as well.

But since most unstructured data is not natively within markdown (yet), the issue becomes the translation layer.

We've created best models to convert any unstructured document container into markdown.

items.title_en:
Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

A parser can get every word on the page right and still lose which column a number belongs to. Then your model has to guess.

Markdown keeps headings, lists, and tables intact, and it stays readable when you're debugging a bad answer. For tables with merged headers, we switch to HTML.

Read our breakdown on why it's our default output for parsing below! ⬇️

items.title: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana
items.title_en:
Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana 2

Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's new image model, released on October 6. It is based on Gemini 3.6 Flash and replaces Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) on the Gemini API. It supports both Text to Image and Image Editing in one model. We evaluated Nano Banana 2.1 through the Gemini API at 1K resolution with default settings.

Nano Banana 2.1 is a significant improvement over Nano Banana 2: it ranks higher in all 16 of the generation and editing capabilities we measure, with the largest gains in the Retail & Ecommerce and Productivity & Knowledge Work use cases.

Nano Banana 2.1 is priced at $0.0336 per image ($33.6 per 1k images) at 1K resolution on the Gemini API. That is half the 1K price of Nano Banana 2, and the lowest price among the top 7 models on AA-Image-T2I v2.0. At 2K it costs $0.0504 per image, and at 4K $0.0756 per image.

Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Google AI Studio, Flow, Stitch, Google Ads and Gemini Enterprise Platform, through the Gemini API and Vertex AI, and on third-party providers.

Congratulations to @GoogleDeepMind & @Google on the release!

See below for our detailed analysis and example outputs of Nano Banana 2.1 in the Artificial Analysis Image Arena 🧵

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windo
items.title_en:
Today I tried to port DOOM to WASM with multiplayer too

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windows and Linux, specifically great at Doom multiplayer, because the original Doom had very laggy netcode

But nobody ever ported Odamex to web yet, so I tried today with Opus 5.5, and I got it working with in 30 minutes

I also made Opus 5.5 create bots from scratch which it also did in just 10 minutes

It's the free shareware maps and some of the best community made DOOM map collections like Dystopia 3 and Dwango5 (I had to Google that too but apparently those are the best!)

https://t.co/1blGn125P1

items.title_en:
You can use Teamily AI  (@Teamily_AI) to add people and agents to the same group chat so everyone works from the same context.

This is probably what the future of software development will look like: humans + AI working together.

Here is an example where your team is working on a web project:

• You post, "We are changing the branding"
• A research agent revises the new direction
• A writer agent updates the text using the researcher's output
• Another agent rebuilds the page using Website Builder
• Your designer comments on the live preview
• The agent makes the changes based on the comments
• You review the finished page and share the link

All of this happens in the same group chat, as a continuous conversation.

I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account

I notic
items.title_en:
I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account

I noticed when everytime I'd share one of my sites new features or pages, the page would get a bit slower just after posting, then I asked Claude to analyze it

I tweeted a test URL as a reply somewhere deeply hidden in a thread (so not even a main post)

And within 8 seconds there's thousands of crawlers opening the page!

One is a military intelligence firm, that scans social media for breaking news and sells alerts to newsrooms, banks, companies and government, it specifically follows accounts with many followers

Another one is a social media monitoring company that tracks what people say online

I knew of course high frequency trading firms use online news to trade fast on things, but interesting to see it in real life

Twitterbot (X) of course is first, within 0 seconds of sharing, it opens it (probably when I wrote the tweet)

The first non-X bot arrives just 8.40s later, which I think is pretty fast considering it's a reply by me deeply hidden in a thread somewhere

TL;DR they're watching you!

我发现数以千计的机器人正在积极监控 X 发布的新链接，可能不仅仅是在我的帐户上

8 秒内就有数千个爬虫打开该页面！

其中之一是一家军事情报公司，它扫描社交媒体上的突发新闻并向新闻编辑室、银行、公司和政府出售警报，它特别关注拥有许多关注者的账户

另一家是一家社交媒体监控公司，追踪人们在网上的言论

我当然知道高频交易公司利用在线新闻来快速交易，但在现实生活中看到它很有趣

Twitterbot (X) 当然是第一个，在分享后的 0 秒内，它就打开了它（可能是我写推文的时候）

第一个非 X 机器人仅在 8.40 秒后到达，考虑到这是我深深隐藏在某个线程中的回复，我认为这相当快

TL；DR 他们在看着你！

items.title_en:
Searching 32 million records in 30 milliseconds is insane!

@typesense is a crazy fast open-source search engine that supports natural language search. It's like Elasticsearch but much easier to set up, configure, and use.

You can do all of this with Typesense:

• Fuzzy search: Typo-tolerant fuzzy search-as-you-type
• Vector search: Return records that are similar to each other
• Semantic search: Return records that are conceptually related
• Geo Search: Return records that are close to a given lat/long

Typesense's Natural Language Search is pretty cool:

It turns a sentence into a structured search query, then runs it against your data. For example:

The query "Find me a BMW under $40,000, newer than 2020, with the lowest mileage first" will produce the following:

• Filters: brand = BMW, price < 40000,  year > 2020
• Sort: mileage ascending

Typesense will then apply these filters and sorting rules to the data.

They offer client libraries in Python, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Swift, .NET, Java, and pretty much any other programming language.

You can start searching in less than a minute:

1. Run their Docker image (or one of their native binaries)
2. Import your data
3. Start searching!

GitHub repository: https://t.co/NrXWx6VIKX

I recorded a quick video to show you a demo. I promise you haven't seen anything this fast!

Thanks to the team for partnering with me on this post.

@typesense

是一个疯狂快速的开源搜索引擎，支持自然语言搜索。

它类似于 Elasticsearch，但更容易设置、配置和使用。

您可以使用 Typesense 完成所有这些：
• 模糊搜索：输入时可容错的模糊搜索
• 向量搜索：返回彼此相似的记录
• 语义搜索：返回概念上相关的记录
• 地理搜索：返回接近给定纬度/经度的记录 Typesense 的自然语言搜索非常酷：
它将句子转换为结构化搜索查询，然后针对您的数据运行它。

例如：
查询“为我寻找一辆 40,000 美元以下、2020 年以上、里程数最低的 BMW”将产生以下结果：
• 过滤器：品牌 = BMW，价格 < 40000，年份 > 2020
• 排序：里程升序 然后，Typesense 会将这些过滤器和排序规则应用于数据。

他们提供 Python、JavaScript、PHP、Ruby、Go、Rust、Swift、.NET、Java 和几乎任何其他编程语言的客户端库。

您可以在不到一分钟的时间内开始搜索：
1. 运行 Docker 映像（或其本机二进制文件之一）
2. 导入您的数据
3. 开始搜索！

我保证你还没见过这么快的东西！

It has lead to the staggering amount of wasteful effort for decades, centuries even. Hopefully we can reboot all of it soon.

items.title: Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night
items.title_en:
Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan

items.full_text_en:
Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan

items.title_en:
717 commits. 307 contributors. 96 first-timers. vLLM v0.31.0 is live. 🎉

Highlights:

🤖 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: FlashMLA mega attention with NVFP4 KV caching, DeepGEMM sparse MQA, Mega-Gate, and shared Engram host tables

⚡ Fast restart: vllm preload keeps weights in GPU memory across restarts, with data parallelism and MTP draft support; experimental engine snapshots

🛠️ Model Runner V2: draft-model speculative decoding, LiLiCorr, async DFlash, and DSpark adaptive verification for Gemma4

🌐 Large-scale serving: MoonEP balanced all-to-all, prefill context parallelism with data parallelism, DeepEPv2, and RL weight transfer

🎛️ Smarter scheduling: independent active-sequence limits, adaptive long-prefill chunking, and priority for requests already holding KV blocks

🗄️ HiSparse hardening: fixes for MTP verification, chunked-prefill livelocks, and host/GPU prefix caching

Thanks to everyone who made this release possible! 💙

items.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
items.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

items.title:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
items.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.
items.full_text_zh:
人类在这里提供了一个有趣的比较点。

20世纪80年代，“编程的认知后果”是心理学研究的一个主要焦点。普遍的假设是，通过计算机编程学习形式逻辑和算法结构将作为一种心理体操，可以提高一般推理、计划和解决新问题的能力。但基础研究以及随后的荟萃分析表明，这种情况不会发生。学习编程的学生会非常精通算法思维和编码，但这些收获不会转移到一般认知任务或不相关的问题解决场景中。同样，强化数学训练可以提高数学演绎和结构映射，但不会提高个人在不相关领域获得技能的基线率。

一般智力似乎是大脑的基本属性，而不是可以训练的技能。在某个领域进行练习可以让你在该领域做得更好，但通常不会让你变得更聪明。

Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

items.title: LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been
items.title_en:
LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been steadily improving for years, but in scientific discovery there is a big difference between a model just below top human performance and one just above it. That helps explain why the surge in math results feels so sudden.

LLM capabilities remain jagged, and there are many ways they are still worse than humans. But as models continue to improve, I expect breakthroughs in other domains to follow, leading to a new era of scientific discovery.

items.title: We're launching AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 and AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1, the new benchmarks behind the Artificial Analysis Mu
items.title_en:
We're launching AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 and AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1, the new benchmarks behind the Artificial Analysis Music Arena, built on 1,000 new prompts across 17 genres and scored by our recruited evaluator panel.

In the last 3 months, flagship model releases like Suno v6, Lyria 3.5, Mureka V9.5, Eleven Music v2.5 and MiniMax Music 3.0 have set new bars for quality in AI music generation. Models now write complete songs from a single text prompt, producing intricate lyrics, convincing vocals, complex arrangements and authentic instrumentation for the genre. As quality rises, the differences between models get subtler, demanding better and more nuanced evaluations for our AA-Music leaderboards.

Initial insights from the updated Artificial Analysis Music Leaderboards:

➤ Suno v6 ranks #1 on both benchmarks, 26 Elo ahead of Suno v6-mini on Vocal and 31 Elo ahead on Instrumental. Suno holds the top two places on both leaderboards.

➤ Mureka V9.5 ranks #3 on Vocal, 51 Elo above Mureka V9, the largest gain between two versions of the same model family on the Vocal leaderboard.

➤ Mureka V9, Mureka V9.5, Lyria 3 Pro and Lyria 3.5 are statistically tied at #3 to #6 on Instrumental, within 5 Elo of each other.

➤ MiniMax Music 3.0 is the leading open weights music model, at #11 on Vocal and #13 on Instrumental. Stable Audio 3 Medium is within 3 Elo of it on Instrumental.

See below for what's new in v1.1 and example tracks from leading models🧵

items.full_text_zh:
我们正在推出 AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 和 AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1，它们是 Artificial Analysis Music Arena 背后的新基准，建立在 17 个流派的 1,000 个新提示的基础上，并由我们招募的评估小组进行评分。

在过去的三个月里，Suno v6、Lyria
3. 5、Mureka V9.5、Eleven Music v2.5 和 MiniMax Music
3. 0 等旗舰型号的发布为人工智能音乐生成的质量设定了新的标准。

现在，模特们可以根据单个文本提示编写完整的歌曲，制作复杂的歌词、令人信服的声音、复杂的编曲和真实的乐器。

随着质量的提高，模型之间的差异变得更加微妙，需要对我们的 AA 音乐排行榜进行更好、更细致的评估。

来自更新后的人工分析音乐排行榜的初步见解：
➤ Suno v6 在两项基准测试中均排名第一，在声乐上领先 Suno v6-mini 26 Elo，在器乐上领先 Suno v6-mini 31 Elo。

Suno 在两个排行榜上均占据前两名。

➤ Mureka V9.5 在 Vocal 上排名第 3，比 Mureka V9 高出 51 Elo，这是 Vocal 排行榜上同一型号系列的两个版本之间的最大增益。

➤ Mureka V9、Mureka V9.5、Lyria 3 Pro 和 Lyria
3. 5 在乐器上统计并列第 3 至第 6，彼此相差不超过 5 Elo。

➤ MiniMax Music
3. 0 是领先的开放权重音乐模型，在声乐上排名第 11，在器乐上排名第 13。

Stable Audio 3 Medium 与器乐的 Elo 相差不超过 3 Elo。

请参阅下文，了解 v1.1 中的新增功能以及领先模型的示例曲目

An AI agent makes a mistake early in a task, then keeps going in the wrong direction.

Our researchers built PivotOPD to
items.title_en:
An AI agent makes a mistake early in a task, then keeps going in the wrong direction.

Our researchers built PivotOPD to teach agents how to avoid those mistakes and recover when they happen. During training, a teacher model shows the agent a better action and how to get back on track over the next few steps.

Read the paper and watch how it works: https://t.co/Bp4lVRvsuY

items.full_text_en:
An AI agent makes a mistake early in a task, then keeps going in the wrong direction.

Our researchers built PivotOPD to teach agents how to avoid those mistakes and recover when they happen. During training, a teacher model shows the agent a better action and how to get back on track over the next few steps.

Read the paper and watch how it works: https://t.co/Bp4lVRvsuY
items.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理在任务的早期犯了错误，然后继续朝错误的方向前进。

我们的研究人员构建了 PivotOPD 来教导代理如何避免这些错误并在错误发生时进行恢复。

在训练过程中，教师模型向智能体展示更好的行动以及如何在接下来的几个步骤中回到正轨。

items.title: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one yea
items.title_en:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

➤ AutomationBench-AA result likely understated: Haiku 5.5 scores 35%, against 53–60% for GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. During pre-release testing, a safety refusal issue caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on resolving this - we will re-run this evaluation with the fix, and expect this score to rise

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens, up from 200k for Claude 4.5 Haiku

➤ Pricing: $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens up to 100k tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above. Cache reads $0.01 ($0.05 above 100k), 5 minute cache writes $0.125 ($0.625 above 100k)

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

items.full_text_en:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

➤ AutomationBench-AA result likely understated: Haiku 5.5 scores 35%, against 53–60% for GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. During pre-release testing, a safety refusal issue caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on resolving this - we will re-run this evaluation with the fix, and expect this score to rise

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens, up from 200k for Claude 4.5 Haiku

➤ Pricing: $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens up to 100k tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above. Cache reads $0.01 ($0.05 above 100k), 5 minute cache writes $0.125 ($0.625 above 100k)

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College Planner, new study tools, and support for college advisers and teen voices.

ChatGPT for Teens applies automatically to accounts identified as belonging to someone under 18, with protections on by default.

Coming soon: College Planner brings application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps together for high school students in the U.S. planning to attend a four-year college.

We'll keep building these tools, evaluating how they and their protections work in practice, and sharing what we learn.

Introducing the new SGLang Developer Meeting 📣

💡 First session: KV Cache Compression in SGLang
🗓️ Date: 11am PT, Thursday Oct 8
✅ Register: https://t.co/zXlFOy4ytp

Join us as Adrian Łańcucki (@AdrianLancucki, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) and Konrad Staniszewski (@CStanKonrad, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) walk through their proposal for KV cache compression in SGLang. Then the discussion opens to a panel with SGLang core devs Liangsheng Yin (@lsyincs) and Cheng Wan (@ChengWan17), and to everyone on the call. Bring your questions, ideas, and comments.

SGLang is built in the open, and the conversations that shape it should be too. Based on your feedback, we've reworked the developer meeting around open discussion and participation.

What's changing:
- Every two weeks instead of weekly
- One topic per session: some sessions will dig into a specific proposal, and others will cover what the community is focused on right now
- Open discussion: Anyone can unmute and join the conversation alongside core devs and guests
- Clips of key discussions will be posted on social media

items.title_en:
Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf.

Some highlights of what we announced:

• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC!

• GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality.

• With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device.

• And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory.

• Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box!

• All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.

Can’t wait to see what you build with all this.

今天标志着 Windows 的新篇章，因为我们将不限流量的智能带入每张办公桌和每个家庭，并使每台 PC 都成为代理可以代表您安全工作的地方。

我们宣布的一些亮点：
• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash：带 256K 上下文窗口的 137B 参数编码模型，现已优化以在您的 PC 上运行！

• GitHub Copilot 现在将工作移交给 MAI-Code-1.1 Flash 等本地模型，从而帮助项目在不牺牲质量的情况下大幅降低成本。

• 借助混合智能，Copilot 现在可以直接在 PC 上执行操作，并将敏感工作保留在您的设备上。

• 借助 Copilot 中的代码，您基本上可以在桌面上构建所需的任何软件，而无需花费任何云令牌，而且它非常擅长。

您不再局限于应用程序商店中的内容！

您的 PC 成为一个无限的软件工厂。

• 安全性是这一切的基础，这就是为什么我们还将Windows 和Agent 365 结合在一起，以便代理可以在设备上的安全边界内工作，包括用于代理执行的本地沙箱MXC。

Windows 成为您的安全代理盒！

• 所有这一切都在新一代设备上实现，例如由 NVIDIA RTX Spark 提供支持的 Surface Laptop Ultra。

迫不及待地想看看你用这一切构建了什么。

items.title:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attenti
items.title_en:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attention. Over the weekend, my Dot posted my model-testing results to Slack and brought back replies. I could keep working without opening Slack and disappearing down a rabbit hole. My weekend stayed pretty clear and calm.

They’re useful for the little things you miss. People at Every are using them to pull important information out of school emails, catch missed Slack messages, and flag account-access requests.

Voice makes them useful away from your laptop. Our head of video was talking his Dot through video edits while running around getting our launch out.

The ecosystem matters. Dots feel roughly at feature parity with Muse, Instinct, and Grok bots. But having an agent connected to the ecosystem you already use for work and life is a real advantage. If you use ChatGPT, I recommend trying one.

Permissions are still frustrating. I have to approve the same basic thing multiple times, and sometimes even after I approve it, my Dot says it can’t do it. That needs to get fixed.

I’m less convinced we’ll stay loyal to the characters. Mine is named Boo, and I’m attached to him. But I felt that way about my OpenClaw agent, too. When something better comes along, I switch. In a year, I expect to be using a persistent agent. Boo will probably be dead. RIP, Boo.

I get into all of this at the start of this week’s podcast, and then sit down with @bigwilliestyle to talk about where we go from here.

In a lot of ways, Dots and GrokBots remind me of a wave we went through with OpenClaw eight months ago. We talk about personal vs. company agents, why we built our own company agent, and whether companies will end up with a whole shadow org chart of agents.

Full episode below.

items.full_text_en:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attention. Over the weekend, my Dot posted my model-testing results to Slack and brought back replies. I could keep working without opening Slack and disappearing down a rabbit hole. My weekend stayed pretty clear and calm.

They’re useful for the little things you miss. People at Every are using them to pull important information out of school emails, catch missed Slack messages, and flag account-access requests.

Voice makes them useful away from your laptop. Our head of video was talking his Dot through video edits while running around getting our launch out.

The ecosystem matters. Dots feel roughly at feature parity with Muse, Instinct, and Grok bots. But having an agent connected to the ecosystem you already use for work and life is a real advantage. If you use ChatGPT, I recommend trying one.

Permissions are still frustrating. I have to approve the same basic thing multiple times, and sometimes even after I approve it, my Dot says it can’t do it. That needs to get fixed.

I’m less convinced we’ll stay loyal to the characters. Mine is named Boo, and I’m attached to him. But I felt that way about my OpenClaw agent, too. When something better comes along, I switch. In a year, I expect to be using a persistent agent. Boo will probably be dead. RIP, Boo.

I get into all of this at the start of this week’s podcast, and then sit down with @bigwilliestyle to talk about where we go from here.

In a lot of ways, Dots and GrokBots remind me of a wave we went through with OpenClaw eight months ago. We talk about personal vs. company agents, why we built our own company agent, and whether companies will end up with a whole shadow org chart of agents.

Full episode below.
items.full_text_zh:
OpenAI 的 Dots 上周推出，他们已经接管了 @every。

有一些突出的事情：
他们保护你的注意力。

周末，我的 Dot 将我的模型测试结果发布到 Slack 并带回了回复。

我可以继续工作，而无需打开 Slack 并消失在兔子洞中。

我的周末非常晴朗和平静。

它们对于您错过的小事情很有用。

Every 的员工正在使用它们从学校电子邮件中提取重要信息、捕获错过的 Slack 消息以及标记帐户访问请求。

语音使它们在远离笔记本电脑时也能发挥作用。

我们的视频负责人一边忙着发布我们的视频，一边通过视频编辑谈论他的 Dot。

生态系统很重要。

Dots 的功能与 Muse、Instinct 和 Grok 机器人大致相同。

但是，拥有一个连接到您已用于工作和生活的生态系统的代理是一个真正的优势。

如果您使用 ChatGPT，我建议您尝试一下。

权限仍然令人沮丧。

我必须多次批准同一件基本事情，有时即使在我批准之后，我的 Dot 也说它做不到。

这需要解决。

我不太相信我们会忠于角色。

我的名字叫布，我很喜欢他。

但我对我的 OpenClaw 代理也有同样的感觉。

当更好的事情出现时，我就会改变。

一年后，我预计将使用持久性代理。

布可能会死。

安息吧，嘘。

我在本周的播客开始时详细介绍了所有这些内容，然后与@bigwilliestyle

坐下来讨论我们接下来的发展方向。

在很多方面，Dots 和 GrokBots 让我想起了八个月前我们与 OpenClaw 一起经历的一波浪潮。

我们讨论个人代理与公司代理，为什么我们建立自己的公司代理，以及公司最终是否会拥有整个代理的影子组织结构图。

完整剧集如下。

You can now train your own Decision model like Jev locally!

We increased Qwen3.5 0.8B’s aggregate accuracy from 20.7% t
items.title_en:
You can now train your own Decision model like Jev locally!

We increased Qwen3.5 0.8B’s aggregate accuracy from 20.7% to 74.3% across 3 decision benchmarks - on just 4GB VRAM.

Turn any LLM like Qwen3.8, Gemma 4 into decision models with our open-source Unsloth repo.

We fine-tuned with a Clef head using Unsloth and LoRA (r=64) for one epoch, increasing downstream accuracy from 30–37% to 78%.

GitHub: https://t.co/2kXqhhvLsb
